features.name: trailing-selector-grammar
features.what: Parses a trailing `:<sel>` off a path string: `:raw`, `:conflicts`, `:N`/`:LN`/`:N-`/`:N..` (open-ended from 1-indexed N), `:A-B`/`:LA-LB`/`:A..B` (inclusive; `..` normalized to `-`), `:A+C` (C lines from A, converted to end A+C-1), comma multi-range `:5-16,960-973` (sorted+merged before read), and combined `:range:raw`/`:raw:range`; `:0` throws `Line selector 0 is invalid; lines are 1-indexed. Use :1.`, `+` counts must be >=1, `-` end must be >= start; unrecognized trailing `:...` falls through as part of the path.

features.name: path-resolution-and-recovery
features.what: Resolves a path argument: expands `file://` and `~`, resolves relative to session cwd, maps bare `/` to session cwd (not filesystem root), retries macOS screenshot-timestamp / NFD-normalized / curly-apostrophe filename variants, and on miss attempts a workspace-wide unique-suffix glob match (5000 ms timeout, skipped for remote mounts) prefixing the first text block with `[Path '...' not found; resolved to '...' via suffix match]`; also recovers a cwd-root filename matching the active `local://` plan basename and, as a guarded last resort, a mistakenly delimited list of existing paths.

features.name: multi-root-scope-resolution
features.what: Splits a `;`-delimited `path` into roots (default `.`), keeps existing delimiter-containing paths literal, normalizes each entry, splits each into (basePath, glob, hasGlob), and either collapses roots into a common base + brace-union glob or fans out per-target when the common ancestor is not itself a requested scope (or a plain-file entry would be demoted into a directory walk); missing roots are skipped non-fatally with `missingPaths`/`Skipped missing paths: ...`, a single missing root hard-fails, and all-missing errors `Path not found: ...`.

features.name: read-text-streaming
features.what: Streams local text by line rather than loading the file: open-ended reads use `read.defaultLimit` (300) clamped to [1, 3000]; a single bounded non-raw range adds 1 leading and 3 trailing context lines on constrained sides while raw and multi-range reads are exact; 8 KiB chunk size; byte budget max(50 KiB, lines*512); out-of-bounds ranges return explanatory text (`Use :1 ...` / `Use :<last line> ...`) instead of throwing.

features.name: structural-code-summary
features.what: When no selector is given and the file is eligible, returns declarations only with elided bodies: enabled by `read.summarize.enabled` (true), prose (`.md*`, `.txt`) excluded unless `read.summarize.prose` (false), files under `read.summarize.minTotalLines` (100) verbatim, hard guards file <= 2 MiB and <= 20000 lines; elided spans render as `…` or a merged brace-pair line `{ … }`, and when anything is elided the text ends with a footer naming concrete recovery ranges, e.g. `[…NNln elided; re-read needed ranges, e.g. <path>:5-16,40-80]`.

features.name: file-display-mode-and-hashline-anchors
features.what: Chooses output prefixing per read: hashline numbered output (`[src/foo.ts#0A1B]` header then `41:text`) when edit mode is hashline, the read is not raw, the source is mutable and the `edit` tool exists; otherwise optional bare line numbers when `readLineNumbers === true`; `:raw` and immutable internal resources suppress both. The 4-uppercase-hex tag is a content hash of the whole normalized file, not of the shown range.

features.name: file-snapshot-store
features.what: Records whole-file snapshots on hashline-eligible reads and grep renders, holding 30 paths x 4 versions with files over 4 MiB skipped; snapshots mint the `#TAG` anchor, track which line ranges the model has actually seen, and back stale-tag verification/recovery for `edit` — it is explicitly not a read cache.

features.name: read-directory-listing
features.what: Renders a directory as a tree with maxDepth 2, per-directory child limit 12, no root limit, siblings sorted by recency with file sizes and relative ages, `(empty directory)` for empties, `limits.resultLimit` marked on truncation; a line selector slices the rendered entries without context padding and multi-range selectors on listings error.

features.name: archive-member-read
features.what: Reads `archive.ext`, `archive.ext:inner/path`, and `archive.ext:inner/path:50-60` for `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, `.zip` plus ZIP aliases `.jar`/`.war`/`.ear`/`.apk`; tar/tgz are loaded whole in memory (<=256 MiB) and indexed via Bun.Archive while ZIP is indexed by ranged central-directory reads and inflated on demand (member <=64 MiB); inner paths normalize `/`, drop `.` segments and reject `..`; directory reads list immediate children (default 500 entries) with ` (size)` when >0; non-UTF-8 entries return `[Cannot read binary archive entry '...' (...)]` rather than throwing.

features.name: sqlite-read
features.what: Detects SQLite only when extension (`.sqlite`,`.sqlite3`,`.db`,`.db3`) AND file magic header match, then dispatches: bare path lists non-`sqlite_%` tables with row counts (cap 500); `:table` returns `sqlite_master.sql` plus 5 sample rows; `:table:key` resolves by single-column PK else rowid (no query params allowed); `:table?limit=&offset=&order=&where=` defaults limit 20/offset 0 with limit capped at 500, `order` as `column[:asc|desc]` validated against real columns and `where` validated to reject comments, semicolons and LIMIT/OFFSET/UNION/ATTACH/PRAGMA; `?q=SELECT ...` runs raw SQL with no bound parameters, capped at 1000 rows; opens readonly+strict with `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 3000` and renders an ASCII table (width 120, column width 40).

features.name: document-conversion-read
features.what: Converts `.pdf`, `.doc`, `.docx`, `.ppt`, `.pptx`, `.xls`, `.xlsx`, `.rtf`, `.epub` to text/markdown via markit, then applies line-range and `:raw` selectors to the converted output; conversion failure returns a text notice `[Cannot read .pdf file: ...]` rather than throwing.

features.name: pdf-embedded-image-handles
features.what: Rewrites markit's `<!-- image: <id> (page N, WxHpt) -->` regions into inline-code `read <pdf>:<id>.png` hints; `doc.pdf:` lists extractable members, an unknown member errors with the available list, and reading `doc.pdf:p11-img0.png` extracts through a session artifact cache `<artifacts>/pdf-assets/<key>/` keyed by size+mtime (converted once per file) with requests matched against extracted basenames so separators/`..` cannot escape.

features.name: image-read
features.what: Detects images by metadata; rejects files over 20 MiB; when effective `inspect_image` state is active (mode `on`, or `auto` with a model lacking native image input) returns metadata only (MIME, bytes, dimensions, channels, alpha) plus a suggestion to call `inspect_image`, otherwise returns a text note plus an inline image content block; unsupported/undecodable formats throw ToolError.

features.name: profiler-report-summary
features.what: Renders recognized macOS `sample` call-tree files (`*.sample.txt`) and V8 `.cpuprofile` JSON as bottleneck summaries when valid and <= 32 MiB; line selectors page the rendered summary, `:raw` bypasses rendering, and a file with a matching name that fails to parse falls through to ordinary text handling.

features.name: notebook-editable-text
features.what: Converts `.ipynb` to editable text with `# %% [code|markdown|raw] cell:N` markers (unless `:raw`) and round-trips back to notebook JSON: source arrays joined on read and re-split preserving per-line `\n`; source lines that look like markers gain one `%` on render and lose it on parse; `cell:N` pointing at an unused original cell clones it preserving unrelated fields, `execution_count`/`outputs` for code cells, stripping them for markdown/raw; text before the first marker is rejected; a missing notebook starts from empty nbformat 4.5.

features.name: binary-and-oversize-guards
features.what: Probable binary local files return a text notice instead of bytes unless `:raw` was explicitly requested; an unbounded `artifact://<id>:raw` read over 50 KiB is refused with a workflow notice directing a bounded `:raw:N-M` range.

features.name: internal-url-router-reads
features.what: Delegates registered schemes (`agent://`, `artifact://`, `history://`, `issue://`, `local://`, `mcp://`, `memory://`, `omp://`, `pr://`, `rule://`, `security://`, `skill://`, `ssh://`, `vault://`, `xd://`, plus MCP-advertised) to a process-global router: `local://` file-backed resources are promoted onto the local-file path so images/selectors/snapshots work; `agent://` `/path` or `?q=` extraction bypasses pagination (and rejects combination with line selectors); `artifact://` uses a bounded file-backed reader; `skill://` sets `ignoreResultLimits`; others paginate in memory with `immutable` passed through to suppress anchors; `ssh://host/<path>` reads remote UTF-8 files/dirs up to 1 MiB (bare `ssh://` lists hosts, literal `:`/`?`/`#` must be percent-encoded).

features.name: url-read-and-render
features.what: Accepts `http://`, `https://`, `www.` targets; renders through a fixed ladder (scheme normalize -> site handlers unless raw -> loadPage -> binary/markit/image -> JSON/feed/plain-text -> markdown alternates, `URL.md`, content negotiation, feed alternates, HTML-to-text, linked docs, `llms.txt` -> raw body) and emits a `URL:/Content-Type:/Method:/Notes:` header block with `method` naming the winning path; `:raw` selects the raw HTML/body path; line/multi-range selectors page cached output without refetching; result shown to the model is capped at 300 lines / 50 KiB with the full body attachable as an artifact; inline images cap at 20 MiB source and 300 KiB post-resize; an HTTP response with `ok === false` returns `method: "failed"` rather than throwing.

features.name: merge-conflict-scan-and-resolve
features.what: `<path>:conflicts` scans a local file for unresolved Git conflict regions, registers session-stable ids and renders a compact `#N Lx-Ly` index; `conflict://<N>` reads one block and `/ours`, `/theirs`, `/base`, `/both` select a side (read-only scopes); writing `conflict://<N>` replaces only that recorded marker block after revalidating it on disk, where a line exactly `@ours`/`@theirs`/`@base`/`@both` expands to the recorded side (`@both` = ours then theirs, `@base` requires diff3) and other content is literal; `conflict://*` bulk-resolves every registered conflict or accepts per-id directives (`1: @ours`) with no repeated ids, applied bottom-up and all-or-nothing per file — partial cross-file success returns `isError: true`, an all-failed pass throws, successful ids are invalidated and failed-file ids stay registered.

features.name: write-plain-file
features.what: Creates or overwrites a file from full `content`, auto-creating missing parent directories, returning `Successfully wrote <chars> bytes to <relative-path>` (count is `cleanContent.length`, i.e. UTF-16 code units), emitting `Writing <chars> bytes to <path>...` via `onUpdate`, preferring an ACP bridge `writeTextFile` when available; a leading shebang may add execute bits (reported via `details.madeExecutable`), and the tool is `strict`, `loadMode: "essential"`, `concurrency: "exclusive"`, wrapped in `untilAborted`.

features.name: write-hashline-prefix-stripping-and-resnapshot
features.what: When session display mode has hashLines enabled, strips pasted `[PATH#HASH]` headers and `LINE:` prefixes from `content` before writing (adding a note to the first text block) and prepends a freshly-minted `[<relative-path>#TAG]` header to plain-file and conflict-resolution results so the next `edit` has a current tag without re-reading; bulk conflict resolutions append a `Snapshots:` block with one header per successfully written file.

features.name: archive-entry-write
features.what: Writes one entry via `archive.ext:inner/path` for tar/tgz/zip/jar/war/ear/apk: candidate archive files are checked longest-first and the shortest candidate is used when creating a new container; the inner path normalizes `/`, strips empty and `.` segments, rejects `..` and directory targets ending in `/`; the parent directory is created recursively, existing entries are read, the target replaced in the entry map, and the whole archive re-serialized to a sibling temp file and renamed over the destination with existing symlinks resolved first; ZIP aliases stay ZIP, `.tar.gz`/`.tgz` stay gzip, and ZIP output must fit non-ZIP64 32-bit entry/count/offset limits.

features.name: sqlite-row-write
features.what: `db.sqlite:table` inserts (JSON5 object; empty object becomes `INSERT INTO <table> DEFAULT VALUES`) and `db.sqlite:table:key` updates with non-empty content or deletes when content is empty/whitespace-only; opens with `{ create: false, strict: true }` and `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 3000` so a missing DB errors `SQLite database '<path>' not found` (never created); key lookup uses single-column PK else rowid and rejects composite PKs and `WITHOUT ROWID` tables; query parameters are rejected; results are `Inserted row into <table>` / `Updated row '<key>' in <table>` / `No row updated ...` / `Deleted row ...` / `No row deleted ...`.

features.name: write-uri-dispatch-and-guards
features.what: Validates URI-like targets before touching the filesystem: an internal URL whose handler exposes `write` is delegated to (a valid read selector is peeled so read and write address the same resource; malformed or range selectors on writable URLs are rejected), `local://` falls through to the session-local filesystem path, unknown schemes and common `xd://` misspellings fail rather than becoming local filenames (`./scheme://...` is the deliberate escape hatch), and a copied `[path#TAG]` wrapper argument is unwrapped; additionally rejects high-confidence read/write mis-dispatches — a missing selector-shaped filename with empty content, and a missing semicolon-joined list of selector paths.

features.name: xdev-tool-devices
features.what: `xd://` mounts tool devices behind `read`/`write`: `read xd://` lists mounted devices, `read xd://<name>` returns that device's generated input documentation, and `write xd://<name>` with a JSON object body dispatches the mounted tool while preserving its schema validation, streaming updates, result content blocks, `isError` flag, renderer metadata, and approval tier, exposing `details.xdev` for consumers to recover the inner result.

features.name: auto-generated-file-guard
features.what: Refuses to overwrite existing files that look generated/lockfile-like, inspecting at most 1024 bytes and 40 header lines; controlled by `edit.blockAutoGenerated` (default true) and applied to existing plain files on both `write` and `edit`.

features.name: plan-mode-write-guard
features.what: Resolves the target path and enforces plan-mode write policy before any mutation, receiving the operation kind (`create` vs `update`) so archive/file creation and updates can be gated differently; plan approval itself is submitted by writing a plan slug to `xd://propose` while plan mode is active.

features.name: fs-scan-cache-invalidation
features.what: Every successful mutation calls `invalidateFsScanAfterWrite/Delete/Rename` (both sides on rename), which removes every cached walk entry whose canonical root is a prefix of the target, canonicalizing the parent and reattaching the filename when the path no longer exists; the underlying process-local scan cache is keyed by canonical root plus complete effective walk options with TTL `FS_SCAN_CACHE_TTL_MS` (1000 ms), empty-recheck `FS_SCAN_EMPTY_RECHECK_MS` (200 ms), max `FS_SCAN_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES` (16), and worker pool `PI_WALK_WORKERS` (4).

features.name: edit-mode-selection
features.what: Resolves the active edit wire contract in strict order: model-specific configured variant, then `PI_EDIT_VARIANT`, then `edit.mode`, then default `hashline`; supported modes are `hashline`, `apply_patch`, `patch`, `replace`, and unless `PI_STRICT_EDIT_MODE` is set a short model exclusion list downgrades hashline to `replace`; the schema, prompt, examples, renderer and optional custom Lark grammar all switch with the mode, and in `apply_patch` custom-tool mode the wire name is `apply_patch` while dispatch reaches the same internal tool.

features.name: hashline-patch-language
features.what: Applies one `input` string of `[PATH#TAG]` sections, each editing one existing file: `PUT N.=M:` replaces inclusive original lines, `PUT <N:`/`PUT >N:`/`PUT >$:` insert before/after/at tail, `CUT N.=M` deletes-and-captures, `REM` deletes the file, `MV DEST` moves it after preceding edits in that section (quote destinations with spaces); body-bearing `PUT ...:` headers take `+TEXT` rows only (bare `+` is a blank line, literal leading `-`/`+` written as `+-`/`++`), bodies are final content not diff pairs, and `CUT`/register-`PUT`/`REM`/`MV` take no body; all line numbers refer to the original tagged snapshot, operations run top-to-bottom across sections, and a strict custom-tool grammar wraps sections in `*** Begin Patch`/`*** End Patch` while the normal parser also accepts unwrapped payloads.

features.name: hashline-registers
features.what: `CUT ... @name` writes a named register and bare `CUT` fills the anonymous register (batch-local, empty at the start of every call); `PUT <N`/`PUT >N`/`PUT >$` paste the anonymous register into a gap, `PUT <N @name`/`PUT >N @name`/`PUT >$ @name` paste a named register, and `PUT N.=M @name`/`PUT N* @name` replace a range/block (span and block paste require a named register); register names are ASCII letters/digits/`_`/`-`, named registers persist for the session and are published only after their writes land, repeating a paste does not consume the register, and a cut in an earlier section can feed a paste in a later one.

features.name: hashline-block-anchors
features.what: `PUT N*:`, `PUT >N*:`, `CUT N*`, and `PUT N* @name` resolve from an opening line through the tree-sitter node's end; anchors must be the construct opener (never a closing delimiter, last visible line, blank line, or inner statement), a single-line node is rejected with guidance to use the explicit-line form, `PUT >N*:` lowers to plain `PUT >N:` with a warning when no block resolves while replace/cut block forms fail instead of guessing; leading decorators/attributes/doc-comments may be separate nodes (anchor the first decorator when grouped), standalone line comments are not swept, and in Markdown a heading's block spans its body and deeper subsections up to the next heading of equal or higher level.

features.name: hashline-validation-and-recovery
features.what: Rejects missing/malformed `[PATH#TAG]`, unknown tags, untagged anchored edits, reversed/overlapping ranges, multiple operations on the same original anchor, empty bodies for body-backed PUTs, bodies under bodyless ops, unknown registers, anonymous paste before an unambiguous anonymous cut, edits targeting lines outside recorded visible read/grep ranges, and byte-identical no-op patches (with a three-strike no-op loop guard); ranges are bounded by a 100000-expanded-line parser amplification limit before real file bounds are checked; same-path sections are merged so their original anchors apply together (rejecting clipboard ops when interleaving makes register order ambiguous); stale tags attempt snapshot-chain recovery and apply only when a unique safe result is proven, otherwise returning a context mismatch; the parser has bounded recovery for common model slips (optional envelope, benign header noise, some bare rows and range spellings) and surfaces `Warnings:`.

features.name: edit-result-and-streaming-preview
features.what: A successful section returns a fresh `[path#TAG]` header, optional block-resolution and move lines, a compact post-edit preview, and a `Warnings:` block; `EditToolDetails` carries the unified `diff`, `firstChangedLine`, diagnostics/format results, operation (`update`/`delete`), path/move metadata, snapshots, and per-file results, with multi-section input returning one aggregate result; the streaming renderer parses complete portions of an in-flight payload and computes read-only diffs, skipping transient unresolved blocks, stale tags, and empty pastes rather than presenting partial input as failure (`edit.streamingAbort`, default false, aborts on streaming mismatch).

features.name: glob-tool
features.what: Finds paths by glob with defaults path `.`, `hidden: true`, `gitignore: true`, `limit` 200 (floored then clamped to 1..200, so it can only lower), and a fixed 5000 ms internal timeout; exact-file inputs return that one path, directory inputs search with implicit `**/*`, results are merged across concurrent per-target walks, deduplicated, sorted mtime-descending in JS and formatted by `formatGroupedPaths()` into a prefix-folded multi-level tree (one `#` per level, single-child chains folded, directories with trailing `/`, root matches headerless); empty results return `No files found matching pattern`, a timeout returns a successful partial result with `glob timed out after <s>s; returning <N> partial matches — narrow the pattern instead of retrying blindly`, and `onUpdate` emits newline-delimited snapshots throttled to 200 ms.

features.name: glob-pattern-recursion-rules
features.what: `parseFindPattern()` derives (basePath, globPattern, hasGlob): no glob chars (`*`, `?`, `[`, `{`) searches that path with implicit `**/*`; a glob in the first segment searches from `.` and is prefixed with `**/` unless it already starts with `**/`; a glob later in the path splits at the first glob-bearing segment — so `*.ts` becomes base `.` + `**/*.ts`, `src/*.ts` stays non-recursive under `src`, and `src/**/*.ts` preserves explicit recursion; a resolved base of `/` is rejected with `Searching from root directory '/' is not allowed`.

features.name: grep-tool
features.what: Searches file contents by regex with `case` default true, `gitignore` default true, hard-coded `hidden: true`, `skip` as a file-page offset (floored; negatives/non-finite fail), and context from `grep.contextBefore` (1) / `grep.contextAfter` (3); native call uses maxColumns 512, internal total cap 2000, per-file cap+1, `cache: false`, and `timeoutMs` 30000; JS shaping caps output to 20 files per page, 20 matches per file for multi-file scopes and 200 for single-file, round-robins per-file matches so one file cannot monopolize a page, emits `*LINE:content` for matches and ` LINE:content` for context (plain mode `*5|content`) under `[PATH#TAG]` headers grouped into a prefix-folded directory tree, and reports `Use skip=<N> for the next page`; no-match text is `No matches found` (or `No more results (...)`).

features.name: regex-engine-fallback-ladder
features.what: Native matcher construction sanitizes non-quantifier braces (escaping `{`/`}` that cannot form `{N}`/`{N,}`/`{N,M}` so `${platform}` works while `a{2,4}` stays a quantifier), tries the Rust regex engine first, retries with PCRE2 for lookaround/backreferences, retries once with unescaped parentheses escaped on group-balance errors, and finally searches the whole original pattern literally rather than erroring; multiline is enabled only when the pattern contains a literal newline or the two-character sequence `\n`; virtual in-memory resources instead use JavaScript `RegExp` and can report `Invalid regex: ...`.

features.name: grep-nonfilesystem-sources
features.what: Searches beyond plain files: archive members (`bundle.zip:src/foo.ts`) are materialized to temporary UTF-8 scratch files before native grep and remapped back to `archive.ext:member` for display (binary/non-UTF-8 members reported as skipped, all-unreadable errors `Cannot search archive member(s): ...`); internal URLs resolve first (glob metacharacters rejected), file-backed resources search their `sourcePath`, virtual resources search resolved content in memory, `omp://` expands to every embedded documentation file, and immutable/virtual sources suppress editable hashline anchors; line-range selectors are allowed only for single files, archive members, or virtual resources.
features.surface: `grep path` with archive selectors and internal URLs

features.name: search-output-truncation-model
features.what: Search/list tools pass final text through `truncateHead()` with `maxLines: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, so the effective cap is the 50 KiB `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES` byte budget rather than the generic 3000-line cap; per-line content is capped at 512 chars plus `…` with `linesTruncated` reported, files over the native 4 MiB per-file limit are skipped and surfaced as partial coverage (names for explicit files, a count for directory scans), and `details.meta.limits`/`meta.truncation` carry structured shown-range, total, next-offset and optional `artifactId` metadata for renderers.

features.name: ast-grep-tool
features.what: Structural search over one AST pattern (`pat`, trimmed, non-empty) with `path` roots and `skip` offset: metavariables `$NAME` (capture one node), `$_` (one node unbound), `$$$NAME` (zero or more, lazy), `$$$` (unbound), names must be uppercase and stand for whole nodes, reused names require identical code, and the pattern must parse as one valid node in the inferred language; language is inferred per candidate file from extension across a 58-language catalog and the pattern is compiled separately per discovered language; results sort by path then source position, page at 50 (`DEFAULT_AST_LIMIT`; multi-target fetches skip+51 per target then re-pages after global sort), render as `*LINE:text` under `[PATH#HASH]` with continuation lines space-prefixed and an optional `meta: NAME=value, …` line, and append `Result limit reached; narrow paths or increase limit.`; parse issues are non-fatal, deduplicated, and capped at 20 displayed entries with `parseErrorsTotal` holding the pre-cap count.

features.name: ast-edit-tool
features.what: Structural rewrite with `ops: {pat, out}[]` (non-empty `pat`, duplicate `pat` rejected, empty `out` deletes the matched node, captures substituted 1:1 into `out`) over `paths`: always runs native `astEdit` with `dryRun: true`, `failOnParseError: false` first, returning a preview beginning `Staged as a proposal — files NOT modified yet...` that names the resolve/reject device paths and renders each change as `-LINE:before`/`+LINE:after` under `[PATH#TAG]` (plain mode `-LINE:COLUMN before`) with only the first line of each snippet, truncated to 120 chars; `PI_MAX_AST_FILES` (default 1000) caps touched files; apply happens only via `write xd://resolve`, which reruns the rewrite with `dryRun: false`, stages every changed file in memory, verifies the full pass before writing, compares replacement totals and per-file counts against the preview and errors on `stalePreview`, returning `Applied N replacements in M files.` plus fresh `[path#tag]` headers; `write xd://reject` discards without mutating.

features.name: resolution-devices
features.what: Pending previews and plan approval finalize through plain-text `write` calls to virtual devices — `xd://resolve` (apply, body = one-sentence reason), `xd://reject` (discard, body = reason), `xd://propose` (plan slug for `local://<slug>-plan.md`, valid only in plan mode); producers register `apply`/`reject` callbacks through `queueResolveHandler(...)` receiving a unique pending-invoker ID so stacked previews do not overwrite one another, while pending the session returns a soft requirement (`toolName: "write"`, `satisfies: isPreviewResolutionToolCall`, reminder text) that forces `write` only on non-compliance; a successful apply or discard consumes the invoker exactly once, an apply throw re-registers the same preview, rejecting with nothing pending succeeds with `Nothing to reject; no pending action remains.` while resolving with nothing pending throws, and an ordinary apply error becomes `ToolError("Apply failed: ...")` (an existing ToolError is preserved); reading these URIs returns a one-line usage hint and completed dispatches carry `details.xdev`.

features.name: lsp-diagnostics
features.what: `action: "diagnostics"` runs per file, glob (expanded up to 20 targets with a leading truncation warning), or workspace (`file: "*"`): workspace mode picks the first matching project type in Rust -> TypeScript -> Go -> Python order and spawns `cargo check --message-format=short`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `go build` (`./...` for go.mod; `go work edit -json` Use[].DiskPath patterns for go.work), or `pyright`, capping output at 50 lines; per-file mode queries every matching server including custom linter clients, waits for project load, captures `diagnosticsVersion`, refreshes the file and waits for fresh `publishDiagnostics` (3000 ms single / 400 ms batch), deduplicates by range+message, sorts by severity, caps at 50 messages, and prints `OK` for a clean single target.

features.name: lsp-navigation-and-symbols
features.what: `definition`, `type_definition`, `implementation`, `references`, `hover`, and `symbols`: position comes from `line` (1-indexed, default 1) plus `symbol` resolved by `resolveSymbolColumn()` (exact match first, then case-insensitive, honoring `name#N` 1-indexed occurrence selectors, never scanning other lines; first non-whitespace column when `symbol` is omitted); `definition`/`references`/`rename` reject an omitted `symbol` when `line` is given on project-aware servers while `type_definition`/`implementation` fall back; location results normalize `Location`/`Location[]`/`LocationLink[]` (using `targetSelectionRange ?? targetRange`) and print `file:line:col` with one context line above/below; `references` sends `includeDeclaration: true`, retries twice with 250 ms backoff when only the declaration matched, and gives context to the first 50 hits; `symbols` needs `file: "*"` plus `query` for workspace mode (filtered, deduplicated, capped at 200) and formats hierarchical `DocumentSymbol`s or flat `SymbolInformation`s for document mode.

features.name: lsp-refactors
features.what: `rename` sends `textDocument/rename` and applies the returned `WorkspaceEdit` unless `apply === false` (preview); `rename_file` resolves absolute source/destination, rejects identical paths, missing source, existing destination, empty rename sets, and directories over 1000 file pairs, sends `workspace/willRenameFiles` to every non-custom server whose `fileTypes` match source, destination, or any enumerated pair, then in apply mode coalesces returned text edits per URI (project-aware server wins on overlap, other overlapping edits discarded with a note), applies each URI once from a single snapshot, creates the destination parent, renames on disk, sends `textDocument/didClose` for renamed open files, drops those `openFiles` entries, and sends `workspace/didRenameFiles`; `code_actions` reads cached diagnostics for the open URI, requests a zero-width range at the resolved position, uses `query` as server-side `context.only` in list mode and as a client-side zero-based index or case-insensitive title substring when `apply === true`, and applies via optional `codeAction/resolve` then `applyWorkspaceEdit` then optional `workspace/executeCommand`.

features.name: lsp-introspection-actions
features.what: `status` cross-references configured servers with `getActiveClients()` labelling each `(configured, not started)` or with live status and appends lspmux state; `reload` in workspace mode (`file: "*"` or omitted) invalidates the per-cwd config cache, reloads config from disk and restarts every newly configured non-custom server while single-file mode keeps the cached config and reloads that file's primary server — both clear matching init-failure backoff, try `rust-analyzer/reloadWorkspace` only for rust-analyzer, then fall back to `workspace/didChangeConfiguration {settings:{}}` and finally client teardown (notifying the mux first for shared clients) with cold restart on next request; `capabilities` dumps `serverCapabilities` as pretty JSON per server; `request` sends an arbitrary method with params built by precedence `payload` JSON > `{textDocument,position}` when file+line > `{textDocument}` when file > `{}`, and errors as `LSP error from <server> on <method>: ...` plus a 400-char params preview.

features.name: lsp-client-lifecycle
features.what: Caches one client per `command:cwd`, starts a message reader that parses LSP frames, resolves pending requests, caches `publishDiagnostics`, tracks `$/progress` project-load tokens, answers `workspace/configuration` and applies server-initiated `workspace/applyEdit`; requests get incrementing JSON-RPC ids with abort+timeout handling that sends `$/cancelRequest` on abort and rejects on timeout or process exit; timeouts/caps are tool timeout default 20 s clamped to 5..300 (after the positive `tools.maxTimeout` ceiling, so the 5 s floor still wins), request timeout 30000 ms, warmup 5000 ms, project-load fallback 15000 ms, idle sweep 60000 ms, and init-failure backoff 180000 ms; files are opened via `ensureFileOpen()` before file-scoped requests.

features.name: lsp-shared-mux-transport
features.what: With `lsp.shared` (default true) the client first asks the broker-managed per-project LSP mux for a shared transport over a Unix socket / Windows named pipe and silently falls back to a private `ptree.spawn()` subprocess when unreachable; an external `lspmux` wrapper takes precedence over broker sharing, with `detectLspmux()` caching state for 5 minutes and using a 1000 ms liveness check, disableable via `PI_DISABLE_LSPMUX=1` and supporting only `rust-analyzer` by default.

features.name: lsp-config-loading
features.what: Merges LSP config lowest-to-highest from `~/lsp.*` and `~/.lsp.*`, plugin LSP configs, user config dirs (active native agent dir, `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.gemini`), cwd config dirs (`<cwd>/.omp`, `.claude`, `.codex`, `.gemini`), and cwd root `<cwd>/lsp.*`/`.lsp.*`, each accepting `.json`/`.yaml`/`.yml` with in-location precedence `lsp.json > .lsp.json > lsp.yaml > .lsp.yaml > lsp.yml > .lsp.yml`; accepts a `servers` wrapper or flat map plus top-level `idleTimeoutMs`; merging is shallow per server with object-valued fields (`settings`, `initOptions`, `capabilities`, `workspaceReadyTimings`) replaced wholesale; `ServerConfig` requires `command`, `fileTypes`, `rootMarkers` for genuinely new servers and supports `args`, `languageId`, `initOptions`, `settings`, `disabled`, `warmupTimeoutMs`, `isLinter`, `capabilities`, `workspaceReadyTimings`; when no config contributes a non-empty server map, built-in `defaults.json` servers auto-detect by cwd-only root markers (one-level wildcards like `*.cabal`, no ancestor walk) intersected with binary availability checked in project-local bin dirs then `$PATH`; config is cached per cwd and only workspace `reload` invalidates it.

features.name: lsp-custom-linter-clients
features.what: Supports non-LSP diagnostic providers through `createClient` adapters cached by `serverName:cwd` — `BiomeClient` and `SwiftLintClient` spawn CLI tools and `LspLinterClient` adapts an LSP server as a linter; they participate only in `diagnostics` (via `lint(file)`) and are filtered out of navigation, refactor, `capabilities`, and `request` paths, with `isLinter` servers sorted after primary servers in file routing.

features.name: lsp-writethrough
features.what: After a successful plain-file `write` (and optionally `edit`), formats the file, synchronizes it to matching servers and collects diagnostics, returning `details.diagnostics` plus `details.meta.diagnostics`; governed by `lsp.formatOnWrite` (false), `lsp.diagnosticsOnWrite` (true), and `lsp.diagnosticsOnEdit` (false), bounded by a 5000 ms operation timeout with a deferred diagnostics fetch scheduled under `AbortSignal.timeout(25000)`; the file write always completes even when no server matches or LSP times out.

features.name: tool-result-envelope
features.what: All file tools return a single-shot `AgentToolResult` built via `toolResult()` with `content` normally one text block (image reads return `[text, image]`), plus `details` carrying `resolvedPath`, `suffixResolution`, `isDirectory`, `kind`, `displayContent` (TUI-only rendering with `│` gutters or unprefixed text plus starting line), `summary` (`lines`, `elidedSpans`, `elidedLines`), `conflictCount`, `scopePath`, `fileCount`/`matchCount`/`files`/`fileMatches`, `missingPaths`, `truncated`/`resultLimitReached`/`fileLimitReached`/`perFileLimitReached`/`linesTruncated`, and `meta` with `source` set to the backing path/URL/internal URL; empty LSP navigation results are additionally marked `useless: true` so compaction may elide them while clean diagnostics are retained as evidence.

features.name: bash tool core execution
features.what: `bash({command, env?, timeout?, cwd?, pty?, async?})` runs a shell command in session cwd, merges stdout+stderr into one text block, returns `(no output)` when empty, marks non-zero exits `isError` with `details.exitCode` and a trailing `Command exited with code <n>` line, and reports `details.wallTimeMs`.
features.surface: tool `bash`; setting `bash.enabled` (default true removes only the model-facing tool, not `!` / RPC bash)

features.name: cd-prefix normalization

features.name: per-tool timeout clamp registry

features.name: timeout-disable semantics (timeout: 0)

features.name: internal-URL expansion for exec inputs
features.what: Before execution, `skill://`, `local://`, `artifact://`, `memory://`, `agent://` etc. inside `command`, each `env` value, and protocol-looking `cwd` are rewritten to filesystem paths; command replacements are shell-escaped while env/cwd replacements are raw; `local://` parents are created (`ensureLocalParentDirs`); unknown scheme/skill, traversal, or router failure throws `ToolError`.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: bash.patterns approval policy
features.what: Ordered glob rules (`match` with `*`, `approval: allow|prompt|deny`); first match wins. `deny` blocks before execute even in yolo mode; `prompt` requires accepted approval; `allow` must match the ENTIRE command and never approves shell-control/compound syntax; `deny`/`prompt` also match each tokenized compound segment. A fixed set of destructive / fetch-and-execute patterns always forces exec approval regardless of user `allow`.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: bash interceptor (dedicated-tool routing)
features.what: Opt-in (`bashInterceptor.enabled`, default false) regex rules `{pattern, flags?, tool, message}` that abort the bash call with `ToolError("Blocked: <message>")` naming the replacement tool. Matching order: whole original command, whole cd-stripped command, then flat fragments split on unquoted/unescaped `&&`/`||`/`;`/`|`/`|&`/`&`/newline, then those fragments with leading `NAME=value` assignments removed. Defaults route cat/head/tail/less/more→read, grep/rg/ag/ack→grep, find/fd/locate→glob, `sed -i`/`perl -i`/`awk -i inplace`→edit, echo/printf/heredoc redirection→write, unmanaged services→hub.

features.name: non-PTY shell executor with persistent session reuse

features.name: native shell engine (one-shot + persistent)

features.name: shell snapshot and command prefix

Unallowed `.envrc` is never executed. Non-PTY runs it inside the executor; PTY and client-terminal routes run the same preflight in the tool before dispatch.

Enabled only when `pty===true` && `PI_NO_PTY!=="1"` && `ctx.hasUI`; otherwise it silently falls back to non-PTY and appends a `pty requested but unavailable in this environment; ran without a terminal` notice.

features.name: explicit background bash jobs
features.what: `async: true` (only when `async.enabled`) registers a job with `session.asyncJobManager` and returns immediately with `details.async = {state:"running", jobId, type:"bash"}` and text `Backgrounded as job <id>; result will be delivered automatically.`; running/completed/failed updates arrive through the job manager, with non-zero exit or timeout recorded as `failed`. Requesting it while disabled or without a job manager throws `ToolError`.

features.name: auto-backgrounding of slow bash calls
features.what: For non-PTY, non-client-terminal foreground calls with `bash.autoBackground.enabled` and an async manager below its running-job cap, the run starts managed, waits `min(thresholdMs (default 60000), timeoutMs - 1000)` (uncapped when the deadline is disabled), then either returns the completed result or converts to a background job with a preview tail; at capacity it falls back to plain foreground execution, and a queued steering message can background a still-running candidate early.

features.name: client-terminal bridge execution
features.what: When the session client advertises `clientBridge.capabilities.terminal` + `createTerminal` and `pty` is false, the command runs on the remote editor terminal: the tool emits `details.terminalId` updates, polls current output until exit/timeout/abort, maps a signal kill to exit code `137`, and always releases the terminal handle in `finally`. This route wins over auto-backgrounding.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: shell output minimizer + original artifact
features.what: Non-PTY execution passes minimizer settings into the native shell; when output is rewritten the visible text is replaced with the minimized text and, when persistence succeeds, the raw capture is saved as a separate `bash-original` artifact referenced by a `[raw output: artifact://<id>]` footer. Minimizer/artifact save failures are swallowed.

features.name: bundled uutils/jq builtins
features.what: Unless `PI_DISABLE_UUTILS_BUILTINS` is truthy, the non-PTY native shell registers an in-process command set including a `jq` backed by vendored jaq (not system jq); jaq errors (exit 5) on chained access through a null/missing intermediate where jq returns null, so `[.a.b?][0]` is the required guard.

features.name: gh cache invalidation on mutating commands
features.what: Before executing a command containing a mutating `gh issue` / `gh pr` subcommand, matching `github-cache` rows are dropped so later `issue://` / `pr://` reads observe post-mutation state.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: bash concurrency policy
features.what: `BashTool` is `strict` and resolves concurrency per call: `pty: true` → `"exclusive"` (owns the terminal UI), everything else → `"shared"`, so multiple non-PTY bash calls in one assistant message run in parallel.
depends_on: non-PTY shell executor with persistent session reuse

features.name: user bang-shell surface
features.what: Interactive `!cmd` input and the RPC `bash` command call `AgentSession.executeBash()` directly — no interception, no PTY, no managed background jobs — rendered by a dedicated streaming component (last 20 logical lines collapsed, 4000-char per-line clamp, cancel/error/exit states), with an `abort_bash` RPC counterpart.
depends_on: non-PTY shell executor with persistent session reuse
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: bash tool renderer
features.what: Merged call/result renderer: collapsed preview capped at 10 visual lines (`BASH_DEFAULT_PREVIEW_LINES`), expanded shows all text present in the result, a warning line states the truncation reason plus `artifact://<id>`, and footer metadata shows the timeout from args; partial-JSON parsing recovers `env` assignments for early streaming previews.

features.name: eval tool single-cell contract
features.what: `eval({language: "py"|"js"|"rb"|"jl", code, title?, timeout?=30, reset?})` executes exactly one cell in a retained per-language runtime; state survives across calls, `reset: true` recreates only that language's runtime, and the tool is `essential`, `strict`, approval `exec`, and `concurrency: "exclusive"` per session. No `cells` array, no header parser, no language sniffing, no cross-language fallback.

features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: eval backend availability + dynamic schema
features.what: `resolveEvalBackends()` combines settings `eval.py`/`eval.js` (default true) and `eval.rb`/`eval.jl` (default false) with independent boolean env overrides `PI_PY`/`PI_JS`/`PI_RB`/`PI_JL` and a usable-runtime prerequisite check; the session-scoped wire schema and prompt list only enabled tokens, and requesting an unavailable runtime raises `ToolError` naming enabled alternatives instead of substituting a language.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: Python kernel backend (NDJSON runner)
features.what: Spawns `<resolved-python> -u runner.py` (bundled, written once per script hash to an `omp-python-runner` temp cache) speaking one JSON object per line: host→runner `{id, code, silent, storeHistory, cwd?, env?}` / `{type:"exit"}`; runner→host `started|stdout|stderr|display|result|error|done`. Init runs `os.chdir(cwd)`, injects env, adds cwd to `sys.path`, then runs an idempotent prelude. Requires Python 3.10+; no Jupyter, no pip deps.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: kernel session modes and dead-kernel recovery
features.what: `python.kernelMode: "session"` (default) caches kernels by (namespaced eval session id, normalized cwd, interpreter), replaces a dead subprocess before execution, retries the call once if the subprocess dies mid-run, and coalesces concurrent resets (a reset already in flight is awaited and queued runs proceed on the fresh kernel); `"per-call"` spawns and shuts down a subprocess per invocation with no persistence. Shutdown is `exit` → `SIGTERM` → `SIGKILL` after `SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS`.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: kernel interrupt/timeout escalation
features.what: Abort or timeout sends `SIGINT` to the runner, whose exec-time handler raises `KeyboardInterrupt`; between requests the runner installs `SIG_IGN` so a stray cancel cannot tear down the kernel. If `done` does not arrive within `INTERRUPT_ESCALATION_MS` (5s) the host shuts down (`exit`→SIGTERM→SIGKILL), annotates the cell as kernel-killed, and recreates on next call. A timeout is annotated `eval cell timed out after <n>s; kernel interrupted but remains running. Reset the kernel via { reset: true } if state appears corrupted.`
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: IPython-style magics
features.what: The runner source-transforms magics before parsing: line `%pip` (streams `python -m pip`, evicts installed packages from `sys.modules`), `%cd`, `%pwd`, `%ls`, `%env`, `%set_env`, `%time`, `%timeit`, `%who`, `%whos`, `%reset`, `%load`, `%run`; cell `%%bash`, `%%sh`, `%%capture [name]`, `%%timeit`, `%%writefile`; shell escape `!cmd` and `var = !cmd` returning an SList with `.n`/`.s`; assignment form `var = %name args`. Unknown magic names raise `NameError: UsageError: ...`.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: Python interpreter resolution + env filtering
features.what: Interpreter order (skipped entirely when `python.interpreter` names an executable): active/located venv (`VIRTUAL_ENV`, `CONDA_PREFIX`, `<cwd>/.venv`, `<cwd>/venv`) → managed venv `~/.omp/python-env` → `python`/`python3` on PATH, with the selected venv's bin/Scripts prepended to PATH. Child env is allowlisted (PATH, HOME, locale, VIRTUAL_ENV, PYTHONPATH, prefixes `LC_`/`XDG_`/`PI_`) with a denylist stripping provider API keys, plus `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1` and `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8`.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: matplotlib figure auto-capture
features.what: The runner sets `MPLBACKEND=Agg` as an environ default and, after every cell, iterates `pyplot.get_fignums()`, saving each figure to PNG, emitting it as an `image/png` display, and closing it.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: JavaScript eval backend (worker VM)
features.what: Persistent Bun worker VM keyed `js:${sessionId}` exposing host globals (`Bun`, `Buffer`, `fetch`, `process`, `require`, `createRequire`, `fs`, Web Crypto); supports top-level `await` and bare `return` via async wrapping; static and dynamic imports are rewritten through a local module loader that cache-busts local filesystem imports between cells while bare-package and scheme/URL imports keep normal cache identity; cancellation terminates the worker.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: Ruby and Julia eval backends
features.what: Opt-in retained kernels keyed by (`ruby:`/`julia:` session id, normalized cwd, interpreter). Ruby evaluates in persistent `TOPLEVEL_BINDING` and IRB-displays a trailing value unless it is nil / an assignment / a definition, honoring OMP and IRuby MIME hooks; Julia evaluates in persistent `Main` and displays a value-bearing trailing expression unless statement form suppresses it, bridging Julia's display stack into the same MIME pipeline.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: eval prelude helper API
features.what: Every enabled runtime exposes equivalent helpers: `display(value)`, `print`, `read(path, offset?, limit?)`, `write(path, content)`, `env(...)`, `output(...)`, `tool.<name>(args)`, `completion(...)`, `agent(...)`, `parallel(...)`, `pipeline(...)`, `log(message)`, `phase(title)`, `budget`. JS helpers are async; Python/Ruby/Julia are synchronous. `read()` delegates non-`local://` schemes to the registered read tool, resolves `local://` via injected roots, and reads plain paths relative to cwd; `write()` accepts plain and `local://` paths and rejects other protocol URLs.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: in-cell completion() bridge
features.what: Stateless, tool-free one-shot model call: `completion(prompt, {model?, system?, schema?})` where `model` is tier `"smol"|"default"|"slow"` (default = active tier) and `schema` becomes a synthetic `respond` tool whose successful structured call returns parsed data; unresolved tier, missing credentials, error/abort, empty output, and invalid structured output raise inside the cell.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: in-cell agent() subagent bridge
features.what: `agent(prompt, {agent?, label?, schema?, schemaMode?, isolated?, apply?, merge?, handle?})` runs one subagent via `runStructuredSubagent()`; the selected agent's frontmatter model/settings always apply (no per-call `model`), `schema` overrides agent/session schemas, `schemaMode` chooses permissive/strict, `isolated`/`apply`/`merge` control worktree integration (`merge=false` = patch mode), and `handle: true` returns `{text, output, handle (agent://<id>), id, agent}` plus optional `data`. Children are one-shot (`keepAlive=false`), disposed after completion, and never share the caller's eval executor.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: in-cell parallel()/pipeline() fan-out
features.what: `parallel(thunks)` runs zero-argument callables in a bounded pool preserving input order; `pipeline(items, ...stages)` applies each stage as a barriered wave; pool width read live from `task.maxConcurrency` (default 32, `0` = unbounded); the lowest-index failure is the one propagated.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: bridge timeout pause/resume
features.what: `agent()`, `parallel()`, and `completion()` emit reference-counted pause/resume status operations through `withBridgeTimeoutPause`, so host-bridge wall time does not consume the cell's runtime-work budget and a fresh timeout window starts when control returns; compute, stdout/stderr, `log()`/`phase()`, and ordinary `tool.*` calls DO consume it.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: rich display MIME pipeline
features.what: Display/result bundles are demultiplexed into channels: text with precedence `text/markdown` > `text/plain` > `text/html` (converted to basic markdown); `application/json` → JSON tree (`details.jsonOutputs`, each value capped at 8000 chars in model-visible text); `image/png`/`image/jpeg` → image content blocks with dimension notes; `application/x-omp-status` → deduplicated status events. Image-only success reports `(displayed N image(s); no text output)`; nothing visible reports `(no output)`.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: eval tool-bridge environment injection
features.what: Kernel startup and per-execution env patching supply `PI_SESSION_FILE`, `PI_ARTIFACTS_DIR`, `PI_TOOL_BRIDGE_URL`, `PI_TOOL_BRIDGE_TOKEN`, `PI_TOOL_BRIDGE_SESSION`, and `PI_EVAL_LOCAL_ROOTS` so in-kernel prelude helpers can call back into the owning session's tools and artifact storage.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: eval renderer
features.what: Merged call/result renderer showing per-cell code blocks with status transitions (`pending`/`running`/`complete`/`error`), syntax highlighting from the declared language, special markdown and JSON-tree rendering, 10-line collapsed preview (20 lines and 4000-char line clamp for the interactive user-triggered renderer), and timeout/truncation notices.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: .ipynb virtual-cell representation
features.what: `read` renders `.ipynb` (unless selector `:raw`) as editable text with `# %% [code|markdown|raw] cell:N` markers over which line/multi-range selectors operate; the edit pipeline round-trips through `serializeEditedNotebookText()`. Source arrays are joined for display and re-split preserving per-line `\n` entries; a source line that looks like a marker gains one extra `%` on render and loses it on parse. This subsystem NEVER executes cells — execution goes through `eval` with `language: "py"`.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: notebook round-trip metadata preservation
features.what: A `cell:N` marker pointing at an unused existing cell clones that cell, updating only `cell_type`/`source` and preserving unrelated fields (code cells keep `execution_count` and `outputs`, initializing missing ones to `null`/`[]`; markdown/raw cells drop them); otherwise a fresh empty-metadata cell is created. Notebook-level metadata, format fields, and unrelated top-level keys survive because serialization clones the original document and replaces only `cells`; a missing notebook starts from an empty nbformat 4.5 document. Hard errors: missing notebook, invalid JSON, missing/non-array `cells`, invalid cell object/type, text before the first marker.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: debug tool DAP action surface
features.what: One tool with 28 actions — `launch`, `attach`, `set_breakpoint`, `remove_breakpoint`, `set_instruction_breakpoint`, `remove_instruction_breakpoint`, `data_breakpoint_info`, `set_data_breakpoint`, `remove_data_breakpoint`, `continue`, `step_over`, `step_in`, `step_out`, `pause`, `evaluate`, `stack_trace`, `threads`, `scopes`, `variables`, `disassemble`, `read_memory`, `write_memory`, `modules`, `loaded_sources`, `custom_request`, `output`, `terminate`, `sessions` — each returning human-readable text plus action-specific `details` and a `DapSessionSummary` snapshot; registration is gated on `debug.enabled` (default true) with `exclusive` concurrency.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: DAP client transports
features.what: `DapClient.spawn()` starts adapters detached with `NON_INTERACTIVE_ENV` in one of three modes: `stdio` (adapter pipes), `socket` (Unix domain socket on Linux, adapter callback to a local TCP listener elsewhere, 10s readiness), and `tcp` (reserve a loopback port, substitute `${port}` into adapter args, wait for listen, connect). Requests default to `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` 30000 with a 5s adapter heartbeat, and failures surface as `DAP request <cmd> timed out after <ms>ms`, `DAP adapter <name> is not running`, `DAP adapter exited (code N): <stderr>`.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: DAP adapter registry and auto-selection
features.what: Built-in adapters `gdb`, `lldb-dap`, `codelldb`, `debugpy`, `dlv`, `js-debug-adapter`, `netcoredbg`, `kotlin-debug-adapter`, `rdbg`, `php-debug-adapter`, `bash-debug-adapter`, `dart-debug-adapter`, `flutter-debug-adapter`, `elixir-ls-debugger`; launch auto-selection ranks resolvable adapters by file-extension match, then root-marker match, then native-debugger preference for extensionless binaries; attach prefers `debugpy` when `port` is set, then native debuggers, then first available. User adapters merge from `dap.{json,yaml,yml}` (and dot-prefixed variants) discovered project-root → project config dirs (`.omp/`, `.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.gemini/`) → user config dirs (`~/.omp/agent/`, `~/.claude/`, `~/.codex/`, `~/.gemini/`) → plugin roots → home fallback, lowest priority first, shaped as `{adapters: {...}}` or a top-level map with fields `command`, `args`, `languages`, `fileTypes`, `rootMarkers`, `launchDefaults`, `attachDefaults`, `connectMode`, `acceptsDirectoryProgram`.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: DAP session manager and reverse requests
features.what: Enforces one root session (`Debug session <id> is still active...`), performs the `initialize` → `launch|attach` → `initialized` → `configurationDone` handshake (and lazily sends `configurationDone` before later requests if incomplete), caches capabilities/breakpoints/threads/frames/stop location/output, synchronizes desired breakpoint sets across the whole root/child tree, handles reverse requests `runInTerminal` (spawns the debuggee detached via `ptree.spawn()` and returns `{processId}`) and `startDebugging` (connects a child client to the root TCP server, binds root breakpoints before its `configurationDone`, recursively installs the same handlers), tracks `parentSessionId`/`childSessionIds`, makes a stopped child the active target, keeps a 128KiB output ring with front-dropping and `outputTruncated`, and reaps idle sessions (10 min idle, checked every 30s).
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: debug execution-state semantics
features.what: `continue`/`step_*` clear cached stop state, subscribe for a stop/termination event anywhere in the session tree BEFORE sending the DAP request, then report stopped location, termination, or (non-fatally) `details.timedOut: true` with `state: "running"`; `pause` reuses cached stop state when already stopped; `stack_trace`/`scopes`/`variables`/`evaluate` default to the current stopped child/thread/frame when ids are omitted; `evaluate` defaults `context: "repl"` so raw debugger commands pass through; `terminate` walks root→children with best-effort `terminate`/`disconnect` and disposes the whole tree even on adapter timeout.

features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: interactive debug/diagnostics selector
features.what: UI-only (not model-callable) menu with fixed routes `open-artifacts`, `performance`, `work`, `dump`, `memory`, `logs`, `system`, `terminal`, `protocols`, `raw-sse`, `remote-debugger`, `transcript`, `clear-cache`: CPU profile via `node:inspector/promises` + 30s work profile + report bundle, heap snapshot via `Bun.generateHeapSnapshot("v8")`, `omp-report-<timestamp>.tar.gz` bundling (last 1000 log lines, ≤10 recent subagent JSONLs, 2MiB/5000-line log read ceilings), `/tmp/work-profile-<ts>.svg` flamegraph export, daily-log viewer (50-line initial/older chunks, pid filter, copy), bounded raw-SSE viewer (1000 events / 512000 chars / 64000 chars per event with tool-schema compaction then head+tail elision markers), system/terminal info dumps with env redaction, terminal protocol probe with a test notification, loopback JavaScriptCore remote inspector (idempotent, unstoppable, 127.0.0.1 only), and 30-day artifact-cache pruning behind a confirmation.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: computer tool scriptable desktop runtime
features.what: `computer({code, read_only?, timeout?})` executes a JS body with top-level `await` against the real host desktop in a persistent runtime; default timeout 120s clamped to 1..300; unknown fields rejected; `essential` load mode, `exclusive` concurrency; registration gated on `computer.enabled` (default false) with `/computer`, `/computer on|off|status` toggling the current session without persisting config. The model always receives an ordinary JSON-schema function declaration, never a provider-native computer-use tool.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: computer worker supervisor lifecycle
features.what: One lazy `ComputerSupervisor` per agent session starts one crash-isolated Bun worker (10s startup deadline) that lazily creates one native `DesktopSession` and one persistent `JsRuntime`; handles, screenshot coordinate frames, runtime variables, and recent AX refs survive successful calls; a run timeout grants a 750ms grace before the worker is terminated with `computer worker restarted; captures and ax refs were reset`; session cleanup sends `close`, waits 1.5s, then force-terminates; each run installs a run-scoped `desktop`/`wait`/`assert` facade under AsyncLocalStorage so leaked async work cannot borrow a later run's signal or read-only policy.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: desktop discovery and capability introspection
features.what: `desktop.windows({app?, title?})` (case-insensitive substring), `desktop.window(id | filter)` (zero matches throw; multiple throw listing candidates), `desktop.focusedWindow()`, `desktop.displays()`, and `desktop.capabilities()` reporting capture/input/AX availability, permission states, delivery modes, display server, backend, and display count. Window facades expose immutable `id`, `app`, `title`, `pid?`, `bounds`, `focused`.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: desktop screenshot capture with coordinate frames
features.what: `screenshot({silent?})` on a window or the desktop composite writes a PNG under the OS temp dir and returns `{path, width, height}`; unless `silent` it emits a status text block plus an image block, and details record displayed vs source dimensions and target. Capture size is bounded by `computer.maxWidth` (3840) / `computer.maxHeight` (2400), reduced to an effective `1280×896` for transports that do not preserve original detail and as a Claude-family fallback; `computer.display` selects `all` (composite) or one native display id (Wayland portal id `wayland-portal-0`).
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: native desktop input
features.what: `click(x, y, {button?, count?, modifiers?, delivery?})`, `doubleClick`, `move`, `drag([[x,y],...])`, `scroll(x, y, {dx?, dy?})`, `type(text)`, `press(chord | string[])` on either a window or the desktop composite, plus window `raise()`. Delivery defaults to `"background"` (preserves focus/pointer/window order) and throws `BackgroundUnavailable` when the OS/app cannot target it safely; `"foreground"` briefly activates the target and restores focus.
depends_on: desktop screenshot capture with coordinate frames

AX actions need no screenshot and use global logical desktop coordinates.

features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: computer error taxonomy and platform backends
features.what: Native failures surface as `ToolError` text prefixed by a stable code: `PermissionDenied`, `CaptureFailed`, `InputFailed`, `BackgroundUnavailable`, `WindowNotFound`, `InvalidTarget`, `InvalidKey`, `InvalidCoordinateFrame`, `StaleRef`, `AxUnsupported`, `AxFailed`, `Timeout`, `Closed`, `Internal`; tool/worker errors add `Computer session is closed`, `Computer worker is busy`, `Timed out starting computer worker`, `Computer code execution timed out after <ms>ms`. Backends: macOS ScreenCapture/Quartz+AX, Linux X11 (RandR/XTEST + AT-SPI), Linux Wayland (RemoteDesktop portal/`LIBEI_SOCKET` input, ScreenCast capture only in `wayland-pipewire` builds), Windows (native capture, Win32 input, UI Automation).

features.name: browser tool action dispatch
features.what: `browser({action: "open"|"close"|"run", name?="main", timeout?=30, ...})`; `open` returns `Opened`/`Reused` + browser description + URL + optional title, `close` returns `Closed ...` or `No tab named ...`, `run` returns ordered content (structured displays in execution order → JSON-stringified return value → fallback `Ran code on tab "..."`). Tabs live in a process-global map shared with in-process subagents until closed.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: browser kind resolution
features.what: Strict precedence: explicit `app.cdp_url` → `connected`; `app.path` → `spawned`; `app.relay: true` → relay (unless `PI_BROWSER_RELAY=0`); otherwise unless `app.relay === false`, setting `browser.relay` (env `PI_BROWSER_RELAY` overrides) → relay at `browser.relayUrl` (default `http://127.0.0.1:9224`); else non-empty `browser.cdpUrl` → connected; else cmux when `CMUX_SOCKET_PATH` is set and `browser.cmux`/`PI_BROWSER_CMUX` enabled; else headless per `browser.headless`.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: headless shared Chromium daemon
features.what: Headless mode attaches to one project-shared broker-owned Chromium (`omp.browser.headless` / `omp.browser.headed` in `hub ps`) that stops with the last project client; in CLI hosts a broker failure is fatal, while non-CLI hosts (bun test, SDK embedding) launch a private local Chromium. Executable resolution: `PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` always wins; on macOS isolated Chrome for Testing is preferred over system Chrome (downloaded on first use); elsewhere system Chrome/Chromium first, then downloaded Chrome for Testing. Launch always passes `--no-sandbox`, `--disable-setuid-sandbox`, `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled`, and `--window-size` matching the initial viewport (default `1365x768` @ `deviceScaleFactor 1.25`), and ignores Puppeteer's `--disable-extensions`, `--disable-default-apps`, `--disable-component-extensions-with-background-pages`.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: stealth patch injection
features.what: Headless-only injection of 14 ordered scripts (`00_stealth_tampering` … `13_stealth_worker`) masking patched natives, synthesizing visibility/focus/scroll activity, fixing Modernizr hairline, spoofing `navigator.webdriver`/`window.chrome`, iframe `contentWindow`/`srcdoc`, WebGL vendor/renderer, screen/DPR, fonts + canvas text perturbation, audio latency/sample-rate, locale/timezone, plugins/mimeTypes, `hardwareConcurrency`, codecs, and Worker/SharedWorker UA carry-over; it also strips Puppeteer's `//# sourceURL=__puppeteer_evaluation_script__` from `Runtime.evaluate`/`callFunctionOn`. Spawned, connected, relay, and cmux browsers are intentionally left untouched.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: CDP attach, spawn, relay, and cmux backends
features.what: `connected` waits ≤5s for `${cdpUrl}/json/version` then `puppeteer.connect()` (the URL must be the HTTP discovery endpoint, not `ws://`); `spawned` reuses an existing CDP process for that executable, else kills same-path processes, allocates a free loopback port, spawns with `--remote-debugging-port=<port>`, and waits ≤30s (poll 150ms); `relay` auto-starts the machine-global broker-owned relay for loopback endpoints in CLI hosts (readiness 15s) and waits ≤35s for the MV3 extension handshake before attaching; `cmux` connects a `CmuxSocketClient` JSON-RPC unix socket and reuses existing handles without a liveness recheck. Puppeteer protocol timeout for launch/connect is 60s.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: browser tab supervisor and workers
features.what: Each tab is a dedicated Bun `Worker` (falling back to inline main-thread execution when spawn fails, losing sync-infinite-loop protection) tracked in a process-global `Map<name, TabSession>` with refcounted browser handles. Reuse requires same name + same browser handle + alive + unchanged `dialogs`; a different browser handle, dead state, or changed dialog policy forces release and recreation, and reuse with a new `url` issues `tab.goto(...)`. `run` rejects dead tabs (`Tab "..." is not alive. Reopen it.`) and concurrent runs (`Tab "..." is busy`), races the result against `timeoutMs + 750ms`, and force-kills the worker (closing orphaned headless page targets) on timeout.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: tab helper API
features.what: In-cell `tab` object: `name`, `page`, `signal?`, `url()`, `title()`, `goto(url, {waitUntil?})`, `observe({includeAll?, viewportOnly?})`, `ariaSnapshot(selector?, {depth?, boxes?})`, `ref(id)`, `id(n)`, `screenshot({selector?, fullPage?, silent?})`, `extract(format="markdown")`, `click`, `type`, `fill`, `press`, `scroll`, `drag` (12 mouse-move steps), `select`, `uploadFile`, `scrollIntoView`, `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `waitForSelector`, `waitForUrl` (200ms poll), `waitForResponse`, `waitForNavigation` — alongside `page`, `browser`, `assert`, `wait`, and the shared `JsRuntime` prelude helpers.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: selector normalization
features.what: Accepts plain CSS and Puppeteer query handlers, rewrites legacy Playwright-style prefixes `p-text/`, `p-xpath/`, `p-pierce/`, `p-aria/`, and throws `ToolError` for other `p-*` prefixes; Playwright-only engines/pseudos (`:has-text()`, `:text()`, `:visible`, `:nth-match()`, `:near()`/`:above()`/…) on a CSS selector throw immediately pointing at `text/`/`aria/` equivalents rather than stalling until the action timeout. `aria-ref=eN`, `aria-ref/eN`, `ariaref/eN`, bare `eN`, and `@eN` resolve ARIA refs.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: ARIA snapshot + element reference resolution
features.what: `tab.ariaSnapshot()` resolves the optional root selector then runs the committed Playwright ARIA-snapshot bundle (wrapped in a worker-side `new Function` and serialized into a main-world `page.evaluate`, so page CSP never applies), always in `ai` mode: every node gets `[ref=eN]`, clickables get `[cursor=pointer]`, matched DOM nodes are tagged with `_ariaRef`. Existing `_ariaRef` expandos are cleared first so ids renumber deterministically from `e1` each call. `tab.ref(id)` resolves via `page.evaluateHandle` walking document + shadow roots. `tab.observe()` maintains a separate numeric-id `ElementHandle` cache validated with `el.isConnected`; the cmux backend uses `buildAriaSnapshotScript()` over `browser.eval` with CSS-only roots and its own id namespace.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: browser per-op fail-fast deadlines
features.what: Every helper except `goto`/`evaluate` runs under a per-op deadline threaded into both the Puppeteer `signal` and `.setTimeout()`: quick page reads (`observe`/`screenshot`/`extract`/`ariaSnapshot`) `min(cellBudget − 1s, 20s)`, interactive actions and default waits `min(cellBudget − 1s, 15s)`, an explicit `{timeout}` on `waitFor*` clamped to `cellBudget − 1s` (`0`/`Infinity` → that bound). A stalled helper rejects with `tab.<op>(...) timed out after <ms>ms` leaving cell budget, instead of the opaque `Browser code execution timed out after <ms>ms (stalled on <op>)`.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: browser screenshot persistence and model attachment
features.what: `tab.screenshot()` captures page or selected element as PNG, saves full resolution under `browser.screenshotDir` (timestamped) or the OS temp dir, returns the path, records `details.screenshots[] = {dest, mimeType, bytes, width, height}`, and unless `silent: true` appends text plus a resized model copy capped at 1024×1024 / 150KB / JPEG quality 70.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: page content extraction
features.what: `tab.extract(format="markdown")` reads `page.content()`, runs Readability first, then falls back to the first non-empty of `[data-pagefind-body]`, `main article`, `article`, `main`, `[role='main']`, `body`, returning `null` when neither path yields content.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: browser display-to-content mapping
features.what: `display(value)` maps `{type:"image", data, mimeType}` with decodable base64 to image content, any other object/array to pretty JSON text (`JSON.stringify(v, null, 2)`), helper side effects to compact JSON status events, while primitives, `console.*`, and non-structured-cloneable values are dropped to debug logs rather than tool content (`undefined` ignored). Combined run text is subject to `enforceInlineByteCap()`, with over-cap text saved via `saveBrowserOutputArtifact()` and replaced in both `content` and `details.result`.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: browser teardown semantics
features.what: `close({name?, all?, kill?})` aborts pending runs, asks the worker to clean up, waits ≤750ms for a `closed` ack, terminates the worker, decrements the browser refcount, and disposes the handle at zero. Headless workers close their tool-owned page and cmux closes owned surfaces (never the workspace's last surface); spawned, connected, and relay pages stay open — `kill: true` only additionally terminates a spawned-app process tree at refcount 0. Headless orphan cleanup searches browser targets by `targetId` best-effort.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: dialog policy and run-scoped interception cleanup
features.what: `dialogs: "accept"|"dismiss"` installs a page `dialog` handler (omitted = no handler); raw request interception installed by user code is run-scoped — at run end the worker removes user `request` handlers, disables interception, and releases held requests, marking the tab for recovery if cleanup fails.
features.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)

features.name: task-tool-wire-schema
features.what: `task` accepts a shape that swaps on `task.batch` (default on): batch `{context: string (required, non-empty, shared), tasks: item[]}` or flat `{...item}` where item = `{name?, agent?, task (required, non-empty-after-trim), effort?, outputSchema?, schemaMode?, isolated?}`; `effort` appears only when `task.enableEffort=true` (default false), `isolated` only when `task.isolation.mode!="none"` AND plan mode off; a legacy `schema` param is always rejected; validation failures return normal tool text with `results: []`, never a throw.

features.name: agent-id-allocation
features.what: A session-scoped `AgentOutputManager` allocates each spawn a unique id before any job is registered: caller `name` or a generated AdjectiveNoun; repeats get `-2`/`-3` suffixes; a subagent's children are dot-qualified `<parent>.<child>`; ids double as registry ids, IRC peer ids, job ids, and `agent://`/`history://` keys.

features.name: subagent-background-jobs
features.what: With `async.enabled=true` and a job manager, each non-blocking item registers one `type:"task"` job (job id = agent id, `queued:true`, `ownerId` = caller) and the call returns immediately with ``Spawned agent `<id>` (job `<jobId>`)`` (batch: `Spawned N background agents using <deduped agent types>` plus per-agent lines); `details.async.jobId` is the first started job and `details.async.state` aggregates (running until all settle, failed if any failed).

features.name: subagent-sync-execution
features.what: The call runs inline when `async.enabled=false`, the session has no `AsyncJobManager`, or the item's agent declares `blocking: true`; mode is per item, so a mixed call registers async jobs first, then runs blocking items inline and returns once they settle, combining inline summaries with the spawned-job listing.

features.name: spawn-concurrency-semaphore
features.what: One `Semaphore` per `TaskTool` instance bounds concurrent subagents across all parallel task calls; it is resized in place from the live `task.maxConcurrency` setting before every acquire and every release, so mid-session changes affect both new spawns and work already queued; both async job bodies and the sync path acquire it.

features.name: agent-definition-discovery
