features.what: `discoverAgents(cwd, home)` merges agent markdown with first-wins dedup by exact case-sensitive name in this order: nearest project `.omp/agents` → user `~/.omp/agent/agents` → `<ext-root>/agents` for each enabled OMP extension (CLI `--extension`, project `extensions:`, user `extensions:`, installed npm/link plugins) → Claude marketplace plugin `agents/` (project before user, gated on `claude-plugins` provider) → bundled; within a directory files load in lexicographic order; `.claude/agents`, `.codex/agents`, `.gemini/agents` are intentionally skipped; unreadable dirs are empty and a single bad file is warned-and-skipped without aborting discovery.

features.name: agent-frontmatter-parsing
features.what: Parses markdown frontmatter into `AgentDefinition{name, description, systemPrompt, tools?, spawns?, model?, thinkingLevel?, output?, blocking?, autoloadSkills?, readSummarize?, prewalk?, advisor?, source, filePath}`: missing `name`/`description` is invalid; `tools` takes CSV or array and auto-adds `yield`; `spawns` takes `*`/CSV/array and defaults to `*` when absent but `tools` includes `task`; `model` takes one/CSV/array tried in order after `@role` alias expansion; `read-summarize: false` forces verbatim `read` output; malformed frontmatter falls back to a naive `key: value` line parser before failing.

features.name: bundled-agent-library
features.what: Ships build-time embedded agents `scout`, `designer`, `reviewer`, `security-reviewer`, `librarian`, `task`, `sonic` (the last two share one prompt body with injected frontmatter); parsed at `level:"fatal"` and cached in memory; `scout`/`librarian` ship with `read-summarize: false`; `scout`/`sonic` configure `medium` effort while `task` configures `auto`; read-only agents are tagged in the model-facing prompt.

features.name: spawn-policy-and-depth-gating
features.what: Before allocating anything, a shared resolver enforces: parent `spawns` policy (`*`/true/null/absent = any with omitted agent defaulting to `task`; `""`/false = deny all; CSV = allow-list with omitted agent defaulting to the first name → `Cannot spawn '...'. Allowed: ...`), `PI_BLOCKED_AGENT` self-recursion rejection, `task.maxRecursionDepth` (default 2, negative disables) which both hides the `task` tool at depth and strips it from the child, `task.disabledAgents`, and unknown names → `Unknown agent "...". Available: ...`; no subprocess runs on failure.

features.name: subagent-model-resolution
features.what: Model priority is `task.agentModelOverrides[agentName]` → agent frontmatter prioritized `model` list (tried in order) → parent active model / configured task-role fallback; `@role` aliases in either of the first two resolve through `modelRoles.<role>`, whose values may carry a `:level` thinking suffix; `resolvedModelIsFallback` is reported per spawn.

features.name: per-spawn-effort-mapping
features.what: When `task.enableEffort=true`, a spawn's coarse `effort` (`lo`|`med`|`hi`) maps onto the resolved model's lowest/middle/highest supported effort level, overrides the agent's configured selector including `auto`, is clamped by `task.maxEffort` (default `max`), and the ceiling is carried across retry-fallback model switches; a model with no supported effort at or below the ceiling fails the spawn, while models with no controllable effort fall back to their normal selector.

features.name: structured-output-schema-chain
features.what: Effective output schema resolves per spawn as item `outputSchema` → agent frontmatter `output` → inherited parent session schema; the item's `schemaMode` (`permissive` default | `strict`) overrides the parent mode; the result carries `structuredOutput` with schema source, mode, validation status, parsed `data`, and validation error.

features.name: yield-completion-protocol
features.what: Every child must terminate through a hidden `yield` tool that is auto-added to any explicit `tools` list; if it does not, up to `MAX_YIELD_RETRIES=3` internal reminder prompts are injected and the final one sets `toolChoice = yield` where supported; `finalizeSubprocessOutput` then reconciles raw text, `yield` payloads, structured schema validation, and abort state, injecting `SYSTEM WARNING: Subagent exited without calling yield tool after 3 reminders.` when it still fails.

features.name: child-session-construction
features.what: `runSubprocess` creates a child `AgentSession` with an isolated settings snapshot: parent settings inherited including `async.enabled` and `bash.autoBackground.enabled`; `tier.openai`/`tier.anthropic`/`tier.google` re-resolved through `tier.subagent`; `tools.approvalMode` forced to `yolo` (headless children have no UI to confirm against); `advisor.enabled` forced off unless opted in; child `agentId` = allocated id, own internal-URL router and `AgentOutputManager`, shared parent `local://` root and `ArtifactManager`, batch `context` rendered into the system prompt's `CONTEXT` section, IRC peer roster in the system prompt, approved-plan reference when executing a plan; conversation history is NOT inherited.

features.name: child-tool-set-derivation
features.what: Child tool list = explicit `agent.tools` if declared, else the default set; then auto-add `task` when the agent declares `spawns` and depth allows; strip `task` at `task.maxRecursionDepth` (and empty the child spawn policy); always ensure `hub` is present unless the session explicitly restricts tool names; expand `exec` into `eval` + `bash`; strip parent-owned `todo` — except for prewalk-armed spawns, whose plan nudge and todo gate require the child to commit its own todo list first.

features.name: plan-mode-subagent-restriction
features.what: With parent plan mode on, an `effectiveAgent` is built before launch: plan-mode subagent prompt prepended, tools restricted to `read`, `grep`, `glob`, `web_search` (plus `ast_grep` only if the agent's own list declares it), child `spawns` cleared, `prewalk` cleared; per-spawn `isolated`/apply/merge controls are rejected; the same `effectiveAgent` drives model, thinking, and output-schema selection.
features.surface: plan mode; task item `isolated` removed from schema

features.name: isolated-workspace-execution
features.what: `isolated: true` requires a git repo (else `Isolated task execution requires a git repository. ...`), captures a baseline, maps `task.isolation.mode` (`none`|`auto`|`apfs`|`btrfs`|`zfs`|`reflink`|`overlayfs`|`projfs`|`block-clone`|`rcopy`, plus legacy `worktree`/`fuse-overlay`/`fuse-projfs`) to a backend hint, and materializes the workspace through a native PAL (`isoResolve`/`isoStart`/`isoStop`) that walks a candidate list on unavailability, reporting `fellBack`/`fallbackReason`; the workspace is always cleaned up, and isolated agents are torn down and NOT revivable.

features.name: isolation-merge-strategies
features.what: Patch mode diffs the isolated root, writes `<id>.patch`, and applies the combined patch only when a can-apply-text check passes (failures leave the artifact for manual handling); branch mode commits to `omp/task/<id>` in a temporary worktree and cherry-picks into the parent after temporarily stashing it; nested git repos are diffed and merged independently via `applyNestedPatches`.

features.name: agent-output-artifacts
features.what: Every subagent with an artifacts dir writes `<id>.md` (full raw output) and `<id>.jsonl` (session history) under the parent session artifacts dir or a temp task dir; `agent://<id>` resolves the saved output, `agent://<id>/<child>` reads a nested subagent's output, and when the path names no nested output and the file is JSON, `agent://<id>/<path>` or `agent://<id>?q=<query>` performs JSON extraction; `history://<id>` renders the JSONL as a concise transcript for live and parked agents.

features.name: subagent-output-truncation
features.what: Returned subagent output is capped at `MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES=500_000` and `MAX_OUTPUT_LINES=5000` (overridable via `PI_TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES`/`PI_TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES`) with a `truncated` flag, while the full raw text still lands in `<id>.md`; the final inline summary preview is additionally capped at 5000 chars with `agent://<id>` pointing at the full artifact.

features.name: subagent-progress-streaming
features.what: Live progress streams into the same tool block via `onUpdate` with a shared `progress[]` snapshot across the call; updates are coalesced at `PROGRESS_COALESCE_MS=150` and carry a recent-output tail of `RECENT_OUTPUT_TAIL_BYTES=8*1024` (last 8 non-empty lines); parent event bus emits `task:subagent:event`, `task:subagent:progress`, `task:subagent:lifecycle`.

features.name: agent-registry-and-lifecycle
features.what: A process-global `AgentRegistry` tracks every agent as `running | idle | parked | aborted`; end-of-run mapping is: caller signal / wall-clock timeout / hard abort → `aborted` + disposed (terminal), soft-request-budget abort on a non-isolated kept-alive agent → `idle` (resumable), isolated run → `parked` with no reviver, everything else (success and failure alike) → `idle` with live session; `AgentLifecycleManager.adopt(id, {idleTtlMs, revive})` parks idle agents after `task.agentIdleTtlMs` (default 420_000 ms; `<=0` disables) by disposing the session while retaining the `AgentRef` + session file, and messaging or the Agent Hub revives them by reopening the JSONL; `"Main"` is never parked and park timers are unref'd.

features.name: subagent-budget-and-timeout
features.what: `task.softRequestBudget` (default 200 requests, `0` disables) injects a wrap-up notice at the budget when `task.softRequestBudgetNotice` is on and force-stops the run at 1.5× to yield partial findings; `task.maxRuntimeMs` (default `0` = disabled) is a hard wall clock per spawn; bundled `scout`/`sonic` may impose lower built-in caps.

features.name: prewalk-model-handoff
features.what: `prewalk: true`/`"@smol"`/model-pattern in frontmatter, or `task.agentPrewalk[agentName]` (`on`/`off`/pattern, editable from the `/agents` hub prewalk strip), starts the subagent on its resolved model and hands off to a cheaper target at its first edit/write; `task.prewalk` (default off) arms this for the bundled generic `task` agent; unavailable/unconfigured targets are skipped instead of failing, and a target is skipped only when both model identity and effective thinking mode match after clamping (a same-model effort downgrade still hands off).

features.name: subagent-advisor-pairing
features.what: `advisor: true`/model pattern (optional `:level` suffix) in frontmatter, or `task.agentAdvisor[agentName]` (`on`/`off`/pattern from the `/agents` advisor strip), pairs the spawned session with an advisor by setting the child's `modelRoles.advisor`; subagents default to no advisor and the effective opt-in is persisted in `session_init` so cold revival restores it.

features.name: auto-generated-agent-label
features.what: There is no wire `label` field: the one-line UI label shown in the TUI and registry is generated fire-and-forget from the `task` text by the tiny/title model.

features.name: async-result-delivery
features.what: Each finished background spawn injects its result into the parent conversation as an async-result message whose text appends ``<id> is now idle — message it via `hub` to follow up; transcript at history://<id>`` (aborted variant points at the transcript only); a `jobs`/`wait` snapshot that observes a settled job first counts as the delivery and suppresses the duplicate injection.

features.name: task-result-summary-rendering
features.what: Settled calls render a summary from a `task-summary.md` template with a 5000-char preview and per-spawn `SingleResult` records carrying identity (`index`,`id`,`agent`,`agentSource`,`task`,`description`), status (`exitCode`,`error`,`aborted`,`abortReason`,`retryFailure`), output metrics (`output`,`stderr`,`truncated`,`durationMs`,`tokens`,`requests`,`contextTokens`,`contextWindow`,`usage`), model info, structured result, artifact paths (`outputPath`,`patchPath`,`branchName`,`branchBaseSha`,`nestedPatches`), and `extractedToolData`; a sync batch concatenates per-spawn summaries and aggregates usage.

features.name: hub-tool-dispatch
features.what: One always-registered (`loadMode:"essential"`) `hub` tool exposes 12 ops — `send`, `wait`, `inbox`, `list`, `jobs`, `cancel`, `start`, `ps`, `logs`, `stop`, `restart`, `describe` — routing by presence of `to` vs `name`: `send` with both is rejected as ambiguous, `wait` with `name` goes to the process broker and otherwise to the unified coordination wait; unavailable families return specific text (`Peer messaging is unavailable in this session.`, `Async execution is disabled; no background jobs are available.`, `Process supervision is disabled (launch.enabled=false).`).

features.name: peer-message-bus
features.what: A process-global `IrcBus` gives every registered agent a mailbox capped at `MAILBOX_CAP=100` messages (oldest dropped), supports direct `to:<id>` and `to:"all"` broadcast, rejects empty-after-trim `message` and self-send (`Cannot send a message to yourself.`), carries optional `replyTo`, and is available exactly when the session can spawn subagents or is itself a subagent (`isIrcEnabled` is derived, never configured).

features.name: message-delivery-semantics
features.what: Fire-and-forget sends return per-recipient receipts (`injected`/`woken`/`revived`/`failed`) and never block; a running recipient gets the message injected as a non-interrupting aside while replies are real turns; a direct send to a parked agent revives it (the only resume primitive — there is no `resume` parameter anywhere), whereas broadcasts target only visible live peers and do not revive parked agents; a busy recipient with async execution disabled may auto-reply rather than strand an awaiting sender; `send` is `isError` only when nothing was delivered.

features.name: await-reply-and-inbox
features.what: `send` with `await: true` blocks after delivery until the next message from that peer arrives (invalid with `to:"all"`, bounded by `timeoutMs` defaulting to `irc.timeoutMs`, `0` = indefinite); `inbox` drains queued messages without blocking, and `peek: true` leaves them in the process-global mailbox; `list` returns the peer roster with status for discovering idle/parked candidates.

features.name: unified-wait-primitive
features.what: One blocking `wait` resolves job legs (explicit `ids` filtered to owner-visible, or all running jobs the caller owns), parks a bus waiter when messaging is available, and races: every watched job's promise, the first matching incoming message (`from`-filtered), the wait window (explicit `timeoutMs`, `0` = none; else the smart/fixed poll window), and the tool-call abort signal — returning a message result (`details.waited`, jobs keep running and still self-deliver), a job snapshot (`details.jobs`, `## Completed`/`## Still Running`, all-running flagged `useless` and rendered displaceable), `No running background jobs to wait for.` when there is nothing to watch, or `No matching jobs found for IDs: ...` with per-id `history://<id>` hints; a timeout is always a normal result, never an error.

features.name: background-job-manager
features.what: Registers, tracks, and cancels background jobs with owner-scoped visibility, watch/unwatch delivery suppression, `acknowledgeDeliveries` on returned completions, 500 ms `onUpdate` snapshots while waiting, 5-minute retention after settlement, a max-running fallback of 15, and `async.maxJobs` clamped 1..100; `cancel` requires `ids` and returns immediately; `jobs` returns the snapshot plus the roster of running subagents that have no running job entry.

features.name: poll-wait-window-ladder
features.what: `async.pollWaitDuration` selects the default wait window from `5s`/`10s`/`30s`/`1m`/`5m`/`smart` (default `smart`); the smart ladder climbs `[5s..5m]` per back-to-back wait and resets after 60 s without a wait, and its bookkeeping (`recordPollWaitEnd`) runs only when the smart window was actually used — an explicit `timeoutMs` bypasses it.

features.name: process-supervision-ops
features.what: `start` launches `application` + `args[]` directly (no shell quoting) under a stable project-scoped `name` (1-48 chars) with defaults `cwd`=session dir, `args:[]`, `env:{}`, `pty:true`, `restart:"no"`, `persist:false`, `detached:false`; `ps` lists, `describe` shows the retained spec, `stop` does graceful tree termination before hard-kill (default 5 s), `restart` reuses the retained launch spec; names are unique per project directory — a live name must be stopped or restarted, and starting a completed name creates a new launch and rotates its prior log.

features.name: process-readiness-detection
features.what: `ready.log` is a regex over captured output and `ready.port` probes TCP at `ready.host` (default `127.0.0.1`, port 1..65535); when both are supplied BOTH must pass; `ready.timeout` defaults to 30 s and a readiness timeout leaves the process running while reporting its state; `hub wait` with `name` and `for: "ready"|"exit"` or a `pattern` regex (pattern takes precedence) blocks on the same conditions.

features.name: process-log-buffer
features.what: The broker keeps a 25 MiB current log plus one rotated log per process; `logs` defaults to the last 100 lines (max 1000), supports `head: true` to read from the beginning, a `grep` regex filter, and returns a byte `cursor`; `follow: true` waits until output advances past `cursor`, the process exits, or `timeout` (default 30 s, capped at one hour) elapses.

features.name: process-input-and-signals
features.what: `send` with `name` writes stdin `text` (`enter` defaults true), sends terminal `keys` (`ENTER`, `TAB`, `ESCAPE`, `CTRL_C`, `CTRL_D`, arrows), or delivers a process-tree `signal` (`SIGINT`, `SIGTERM`, `SIGHUP`, `SIGQUIT`, `SIGKILL`); input is one shared serialized stream across all project clients, and `detached: true` disables stdin entirely.

features.name: cross-instance-launch-broker
features.what: The first process op starts a detached broker on a private socket under `~/.omp/run/daemons/<project-hash>/` so every harness instance in the same project directory shares names, logs, and state; after the last client exits the broker stops non-persistent processes and exits; `persist: true` opts out of that teardown, `detached: true` implies persist and survives broker shutdown, and restart policies `no`/`on-failure`/`always` use bounded exponential backoff up to 30 s.

features.name: hub-approval-classification
features.what: Per-call approval tier is computed from the op: `start`, `stop`, `restart`, and `send`-to-process are `exec`; all messaging, job control, `ps`, `logs`, `describe`, and `wait` are `read`.

features.name: agent-hub-tui
features.what: An interactive roster opened with `Alt+A` (`app.agents.hub`), `Ctrl+S` (`app.session.observe`), or double-tap `←` from an empty main editor, showing per-agent status, identity, parent, unread message count, model role and resolved model, age, assigned task/current activity, cost, active time, request/tool-call counts and tokens, with a status+usage aggregate header; the main agent is never listed and missing metrics render as `usage —` rather than an estimate; `t` toggles flat vs parent/child tree; navigation is `j`/`k`/arrows/wheel, `Enter`/click opens, `r` revives a parked agent only, `x` aborts+kills+releases immediately, `Esc` closes.

features.name: agent-hub-inspector
features.what: A side inspector (auto on wide terminals, `Tab`-toggled on narrow ones, `PageUp`/`PageDown` to scroll) shows the selected agent's current tool and arguments, last intent, retry state, context-window use, parent/child lineage, output and patch paths, and isolated-worktree branch metadata.

features.name: agent-hub-focus-and-steer
features.what: `Enter` on a normal local subagent focuses the main TUI transcript/status/editor on that session (reviving it if parked) so typed messages steer a running turn or prompt an idle one through the normal prompt path and are persisted to that subagent's history; `Esc` on an empty editor or double-`←` returns to the main session without interrupting the subagent; contexts with no local focusable session (collab guests, advisor rows) instead use a full-screen transcript viewer that incrementally tails the file-backed JSONL and shows an input line only when the agent can be messaged.

features.name: persisted-agent-rehydration
features.what: Opening the Hub on a resumed session scans that session's artifact tree: historical subagent JSONL files become `parked` rows, killed agents' tombstones stay `aborted`, nested subagents retain parent/child lineage, and output/patch artifacts attach to the inspector row; `__advisor*.jsonl` files become read-only `advisor`-kind rows that can be opened and followed but never messaged, revived, or killed — and are excluded from the agent-facing `hub`, `history://`, and `agent://` workflows.

features.name: jobs-command
features.what: `/jobs` prints a snapshot of running and recently settled asynchronous tool jobs; it is a summary surface only and does not replace the per-agent transcript or control views.

features.name: todo-tool-ops
features.what: `todo` applies exactly one op per call with the discriminator at the top level (no `ops[]` wrapper): `init` (full replacement from `list[{phase,items[]}]` or flat `items` synthesizing a phase defaulting to `Tasks`), `start` (one task `in_progress`, demoting any other), `done`/`drop`/`rm` (target one exact-content `task`, else all tasks in one exact-name `phase`, else everything), `block`/`unblock` (require a task-or-phase target; `block` takes an optional `reason` collapsed to one line and only affects pending/in_progress/blocked, `unblock` returns blocked→pending and clears notes), `append` (`phase`+`items`, the only op that lazily creates a phase, rejecting globally duplicate task content), and read-only `view`; runs `concurrency:"exclusive"`, `strict:true`, `loadMode:"discoverable"`.

features.name: todo-normalization-invariant
features.what: After a successful mutation (never after `view`, never mid-op) normalization enforces exactly one active task: if several are `in_progress` only the first survives and the rest become `pending`; if none is, the first `pending` task in phase/task order is auto-promoted; blocked tasks are skipped, so a fully blocked list legitimately has no active task.

features.name: todo-markdown-roundtrip
features.what: Phases serialize to headings plus checklist items `[ ]` pending, `[/]` in_progress, `[x]` completed, `[-]` abandoned, `[!]` blocked with the blocker preserved as a trailing `<!-- blocker: ... -->` comment; the parser round-trips that format, also accepts `>` for in_progress and `~` for abandoned, defaults orphan tasks into a `Todos` phase, restores blocker notes, and re-runs normalization.

features.name: todo-session-integration
features.what: Successful todo results write the phase cache (`storage: "session"` when a session file exists, else `"memory"`), refresh the visible todo panel from `result.details.phases`, and report `details.completedTasks` transitions; failed results leave the panel stale, show `Todo update failed...`, and enqueue a hidden next-turn reminder (`customType: "todo-error-reminder"`); on session resume `completed` and `abandoned` tasks are stripped before restore, while `/todo` edits also append `customType: "user_todo_edit"` entries plus a model-visible `<system-reminder>` and read back full history; the TUI widget separately clears closed entries after `tasks.todoClearDelay` (default 60 s, `<0` disables, `0` immediate) as a display-only effect.

features.name: ask-tool-questions
features.what: `ask` takes a non-empty `questions[]` of `{id, question, options[{label, description?, preview?}], header?, multi?, recommended?}` and returns plain text (single question: the answer plus optional `User added note: ...`; multiple: `User answers:` with one line per `id`) plus `details` that are flattened for one question and `{results: QuestionResult[]}` for many; `recommended` is a zero-based hint only and invalid indexes are ignored; it is registered only when the session has a UI and runs `concurrency:"exclusive"` because the dialog surface is shared.

features.name: ask-rich-dialog-and-fallback
features.what: When the UI provides `askDialog` a single rich multi-question form is opened supporting per-question headers, option descriptions/previews, answer notes, and a `Chat about this` redirect that returns `{chatRedirect: true, questions: string[]}`; otherwise a selector/editor fallback runs per question with a single-select list plus `Other (type your own)`, a multi-select checkbox loop plus `Done selecting`, left/right arrow back/forward navigation preserving prior answers, and auto-advance on the final question — the fallback supports neither headers, previews, notes, nor chat redirect.
features.surface: `context.ui.askDialog(...)`; reserved labels `Other (type your own)`, `Chat about this`, `Next →`

features.name: ask-timeout-and-cancellation
features.what: `ask.timeout` (seconds, default `0` = disabled) is converted to ms and forced off entirely in plan mode; on timeout the fallback auto-selects the valid recommended option or the first option, appends ` (auto-selected after timeout)` and sets `details.timedOut`, and the timeout applies only to the option picker (the `Other` editor is untimed); user cancellation aborts the context and throws `ToolAbortError("Ask tool was cancelled by the user")`, headless use throws `ToolAbortError("Ask tool requires interactive mode")`, and abort mid-input becomes `ToolAbortError("Ask input was cancelled")`; `ask.notify != off` sends a terminal `Waiting for input` notification and `speech.enabled` vocalizes the questions first.

features.name: web-search-tool
features.what: `web_search` takes `{query (required), recency?: day|week|month|year, limit?, max_tokens?, temperature?, num_search_results?}`, is gated behind `web_search.enabled`, never throws on provider failure (returns `content[0].text = "Error: ..."` with `details.error` and `details.response.provider` set to the last attempted provider or `"none"`), and forwards its `AbortSignal` into every provider so a genuine cancellation is rethrown rather than converted to an error string.

features.name: search-query-directive-parsing
features.what: The orchestrator parses the raw query once for Google-style directives (`site:`/`-site:`, `after:`/`before:` `YYYY-MM-DD`, `inurl:`, `intitle:`, `filetype:`, quoted phrases, `-term` exclusions, `OR`), hands the structured form to adapters that map them to native filters or provider syntax, keeps the original string available, and then leniently post-filters returned sources per dimension — relaxing any dimension that would eliminate every remaining result and emitting a leading `Note: no results matched ...` while never rewriting answer or citation text.

features.name: search-provider-chain
features.what: Candidate providers are resolved lazily without importing modules: an internal non-`auto` forced `provider` is the sole candidate (via `isExplicitlyAvailable()`), otherwise `providers.webSearchOrder` first-occurrences lead (also `isExplicitlyAvailable()`, unlocking keyless/anonymous paths) followed by unlisted providers in the built-in 23-entry order, minus `providers.webSearchExclude`; the chain is strictly sequential with no fan-out, each transport bounded by `providers.webSearchTimeoutSeconds` (default 60, max 300, per provider not per chain), a non-renderable response is treated as a `204` provider error that advances the chain, and after exhaustion errors are normalized (Anthropic 404, `401`/`403` auth messages) into a single message or `All web search providers failed: <provider/error>; ...`.

features.name: search-provider-adapters
features.what: Implements 23 adapters in default auto order `perplexity, gemini, anthropic, codex, xai, zai, exa, tinyfish, jina, kagi, tavily, firecrawl, brave, kimi, parallel, synthetic, searxng, startpage, duckduckgo, ecosia, google, mojeek, public`, each with its own availability probe (env var, stored credential, OAuth, endpoint setting), transport (JSON GET/POST, SSE, JSON-RPC/MCP, HTML scrape), recency mapping, and result-count clamp — collapsing `numSearchResults ?? limit` in most cases and normalizing all of them into one `SearchResponse{answer?, sources, citations?, relatedQuestions?, searchQueries?, usage?, model?, requestId?, authMode?}`.

features.name: search-result-formatting
features.what: `formatForLLM()` emits, in fixed order: relaxation notes, the answer if present, then one source entry per result (`[n] <title> (<age or published date>)` / indented URL / optional snippet truncated to 240 chars) under a `## Sources` header with count that appears only when an answer was also produced, then `## Citations` (cited text truncated to 240 chars), then a `## Related` bullet list, then `Search queries: <n>` capped at the first 3 queries of 120 chars each.

features.name: public-web-aggregator
features.what: The explicit-only `public` provider (`isAvailable()` false so the auto chain never fans out to it) queries the five credential-free engines `startpage`, `google`, `duckduckgo`, `ecosia`, `mojeek` minus excluded ones, deduplicates URLs on a canonical key (host without `www.`, normalized trailing slash, query preserved, fragment removed), ranks by cross-engine consensus then best per-engine rank, keeps the longest snippet, and returns at the earliest of all-settled, a 5 s soft deadline with ≥1 success, or a 30 s hard cap, aborting stragglers and failing only if every engine fails (default 15 results, max 30).

features.name: scraper-browser-escalation
features.what: `browserFetch` tries a browser-profiled plain fetch first and escalates fetch failures, non-2xx statuses, and challenge bodies to a shared stealth headless browser (an injected test `fetch` never escalates); Google seeds cookies from its homepage before loading the rendered SERP, Startpage GETs the homepage for the `sc` anti-bot token before POSTing `/sp/search` with a tokenless GET fallback, Mojeek's ALTCHA proof-of-work wall is auto-solved in the browser, and detected challenges (DuckDuckGo `anomaly-modal`, Google `unusual traffic`, Ecosia Firewall, Mojeek ALTCHA/403, Startpage consent) raise provider-tagged `SearchProviderError(429)` so the chain advances.

features.name: github-tool-ops
features.what: A discoverable, strict-schema `github` tool dispatching solely on `op` ∈ `repo_view | file_read | pr_create | pr_checkout | pr_push | search_issues | search_prs | search_code | search_commits | search_repos | run_watch`, gated behind `github.enabled` (default false) and created only when `gh` is on `PATH`; reads and `run_watch` request `read` approval while `pr_create`/`pr_checkout`/`pr_push` request `exec`; results are one text block with optional `sourceUrl` and renderer `details`, multi-item ops joined by blank lines and `---`.

features.name: github-pr-worktree-checkout
features.what: `pr_checkout` accepts a PR number, branch, URL, or an array of them (resolved in parallel with `Promise.allSettled` so partial failures produce a `# <n>/<total> ... (<k> failed)` header plus a `## Failed` list), always names the local branch `pr-<number>`, places the worktree at `<worktrees-base>/<number>-<repo-hash>` (base = valid `OMP_WORKTREE_DIR` → `worktree.base` → `~/.omp/wt`, with `-2`/`-3` suffixes on collision), reuses an existing worktree reporting `reused: true`, requires `force: true` to reset an existing `refs/heads/pr-<number>` at a different commit, resolves cross-repo head remotes as `fork-<owner>[-n]`, and serializes all git mutation under a repo lock keyed by the primary repo root.

features.name: github-pr-push
features.what: `pr_push` uses git only (never `gh`), reading the `branch.pr-<number>.{remote,merge,pushRemote,ompPrHeadRef,ompPrUrl,ompPrIsCrossRepository,ompPrMaintainerCanModify}` config keys written by `pr_checkout` into the shared `.git/config`, deriving the refspec `HEAD:refs/heads/<headRef>` when the branch is checked out or `refs/heads/<branch>:refs/heads/<headRef>` otherwise, honoring `forceWithLease`, and invalidating cached `pr://` rows for that PR afterwards; a branch without `ompPrHeadRef` metadata is a hard error with no alternate source.

features.name: github-actions-run-watch
features.what: `run_watch` polls a run ID/URL or, without `run`, all runs for the current branch's head commit, at 3 s for the first 60 s then 15 s, tolerating 5 consecutive rate-limited failures, giving up in commit mode after 90 s with no runs; on any failed job it emits a note, waits one 5 s grace period, refetches, then collects logs, showing only the last `tail` lines (default 15, max 200) inline while persisting full logs to `session.allocateOutputArtifact("github")` as `<id>.github.log` with a `Full failed-job logs: artifact://<id>` trailer; commit-mode success additionally requires that after one more poll interval the set of run IDs is unchanged; it is the only streaming op (`onUpdate` snapshots then one final text result).

features.name: github-search-ops
features.what: Five search ops compose `gh api -X GET /search/{issues,code,commits,repositories}` with `-F per_page=<limit>` (default 10, floored, clamped to 50, must be >0); `search_issues`/`search_prs` append `is:issue`/`is:pr`; `since`/`until` accept relative durations (`3d`,`12h`,`2w`,`2mo`,`1y`), `YYYY-MM-DD`, or ISO datetimes and become `created:`/`updated:` (repo search maps `updated`→`pushed:`, commit search always uses `committer-date:`) and are rejected outright for `search_code`; `repo` defaults to the current checkout's `owner/repo` for issues/PRs/code/commits — suppressed when the query already leads with `repo:`/`org:`/`user:`/`owner:` or resolution fails — and `search_repos` never forwards `repo` at all.

features.name: github-cli-bridge
features.what: All GitHub access shells `gh` via `Bun.spawn(['gh', ...])` with the abort signal forwarded, trimming stdout/stderr unless `trimOutput:false`, rejecting empty or invalid JSON in `json()`, and mapping common failures to model-facing messages (`GitHub CLI is not authenticated. Run \`gh auth login\`.`, `GitHub repository context is unavailable. Pass \`repo\` explicitly...`, `GitHub CLI (gh) is not installed...`); `--repo` is deliberately omitted when the identifier argument is already a full GitHub URL so `gh` derives repo/number itself.

features.name: security-scan-actions
features.what: A discoverable, strict, `exec`-classified `security_scan` tool with `action` ∈ `preflight | start | status | cancel | validate | cloud_scans | cloud_start | cloud_status | cloud_pull`, gated behind `security.enabled` (default false, rechecked on every action → `Security is disabled. Enable security.enabled before using security_scan.`); every action returns one text block plus `details{action, ...}` and never streams — `start` returns a queued operation immediately and callers poll `status`, whose phases run `queued → preparing → reviewing → publishing → completed` with terminal alternatives `partial`, `cancelled`, `failed`.

features.name: security-plan-fingerprint
features.what: `preflight` persists an immutable plan pinning canonical repo root, normalized/deduplicated/sorted include-exclude scope (exclusion wins, paths must be repo-relative and resolve inside the repo), target snapshot digest (tracked+untracked paths, contents, exec bits, symlink targets, HEAD or `unborn` — or for `ref_diff` the resolved base/head commits and raw tree diff), provider/model and thinking level, the exact OAuth credential row and recorded account/workspace identity, knowledge-base files by SHA-256+size, output policy, the security setting snapshot, and coordinator prompt/workflow fingerprints; `start` recomputes the fingerprint and refuses on mismatch with `Security scan plan is stale: expected <old>, got <new>. Run security preflight again.`

features.name: security-scan-session
features.what: Execution spawns a restricted, auto-approved scan session with read-only repository inspection tools, read-only LSP, and only `security-reviewer` task workers, with extension discovery, MCP, IRC, model fallback, and account rotation all disabled; `ref_diff` targets get a detached temporary worktree at the pinned head revision plus the pinned diff, cleaned up afterwards; a process restart marks persisted `running`/`planned` scans `failed` with `Security scan was interrupted by a process restart` and cleans that worktree; `cancel` routes through the job manager or the local controller and only reaches terminal `cancelled` after the background run handles the abort and persists its terminal bundle.

features.name: security-publication-store
features.what: An internal strict write-tier `security_publish` tool, available only inside the restricted scan session, must be called exactly once with deduplicated findings (rule, title, summary, severity, confidence, category, ≥1 in-scope location, optional evidence/remediation/CWE, validation state), honest coverage (completeness, reviewed surfaces, exclusions, deferred work, open questions), and the final Markdown report — rejecting absolute, parent-traversing, or out-of-scope paths, deduplicating identical canonical fingerprints, and failing a second call; no publication yields a `partial` scan, and the completed output dir contains `findings.json`, `report.md`, `results.sarif`, `provenance.json` (redacted), and `scan.json` written LAST as the commit marker, with dirs `0700` and files `0600` on non-Windows; `validate` separately updates a stored finding's `validation_status` and appends evidence records.

features.name: security-url-namespace
features.what: An immutable, project-scoped, strictly read-only `security://` namespace exposes `security://`, `/scans`, `/scans/<id>`, `/scans/<id>/{manifest,findings,findings/<finding-id>,coverage,report,sarif,provenance}`; reads never validate, import, cancel, or otherwise mutate state, and fail with an enablement message when `security.enabled` is false.

features.name: security-cloud-integration
features.what: `cloud_scans`/`cloud_start`/`cloud_status`/`cloud_pull` talk to ChatGPT's Codex Security cloud control plane (not the public OpenAI API) using an `openai-codex` ChatGPT OAuth credential, are never a fallback from a native scan, retry once on HTTP 401 with a forced refresh then fail; `cloud_start` requires `repository_id`+`repository_url`+`environment_id` with `lookback_days` defaulting to 30 (or `"all"`) and consumes the account's separate allowance; `cloud_pull` converts attributed findings to the canonical schema, generates report+SARIF, records coverage as `unknown`, and fails closed unless the project's `origin` remote identity matches the cloud configuration URL.

features.name: generate-image-tool
features.what: A custom tool registered only when `generate_image.enabled=true` (default false) and the session's tool filter allows it, taking structured prompt fields (`subject` required, plus `action`/`scene`/`composition`/`lighting`/`style`/`text`/`changes[]`), `aspect_ratio`, `image_size`, `input[{path|data, mime_type?}]`, and `provider`; provider order is concrete `provider` → `providers.imageOrder` → the active session model's image provider → built-in `openai, openai-codex, antigravity, xai, openrouter, gemini` deduped (`auto` adds nothing), skipping uncredentialed providers and advancing ONLY on credentialed HTTP failures (validation/parse/IO/cancel/timeout never fall through); inline result images are written to `omp-image-<snowflake>.<ext>` under the OS temp dir and a response with no image data returns a normal `imageCount: 0` result.

features.name: inspect-image-tool
features.what: Sends one local image or current-turn attachment plus a `question` to a vision model, selecting it via `@vision` → `@default` → active session model → `availableModels[0]` and requiring `input.includes("image")`; resolves `Image #N` labels, `attachment://N`, and `image://N` as 1-based current-turn references, otherwise a cwd-relative path; detects format from file bytes (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP only, sniffing at most 256 KiB) and rejects >20 MiB; sends exactly two content parts in order `[image, text]` with a dedicated system prompt, bounded by `inspect_image.timeoutMs` (default 300000, `0` disables), returning concatenated assistant text plus `{model, imagePath, mimeType}`; availability is `inspect_image.mode` (`auto`|`on`|`off`, default `auto`) where `auto` registers only when the active model lacks native image input.

features.name: image-resize-ladder
features.what: When `images.autoResize` is on (or WebP must be re-encoded for a model that cannot decode it), images are downscaled toward `maxWidth/maxHeight 1568` and `maxBytes 500 KiB` at `jpegQuality 80`: a fast path returns originals already within 1568² and `maxBytes/4`, the first pass encodes PNG+JPEG+WebP keeping the smallest, retries walk qualities `[70,60,50,40]` then dimension scales `[1.0,0.75,0.5,0.35,0.25]` stopping before either dimension drops below 100 px, and fallback passes encode JPEG+WebP only; WebP is excluded when `OMP_NO_WEBP=1`/`true` or `excludeWebP` is set, and any resize failure silently keeps the original bytes.

features.name: tts-tool
features.what: A write-approved custom tool registered only when `speechgen.enabled=true` (default false) taking `{text: 1..15000 chars, voice_id?, language?, output_path (required), sample_rate?, bit_rate?}`, inferring the codec from `output_path`'s case-insensitive suffix (`.wav` → WAV, anything else → MP3) and routing by `providers.tts` (default `auto`): `local` always uses on-device Kokoro-82M through the shared ONNX tiny-model worker with `tts.localModel`/`tts.localVoice` (ignoring per-call voice/language/rates, always emitting PCM16 WAV to a sibling `.wav` path), `xai` always uses Grok Voice `<baseURL>/tts` with a 60 s timeout, and `auto` prefers local but routes MP3 requests to xAI when credentials exist; missing credentials, xAI HTTP failures (detail truncated to 300 chars), and a null local worker response return `isError` text results while cancellation, timeout, and write errors propagate.

features.name: session-jsonl-format
features.what: Persist a session as JSONL: a fixed-width 256-byte `{"type":"title"}` slot line, then the `type:"session"` header line, then one `SessionEntry` object per line; loaders strip the physical title slot and fold its title/titleSource into the logical header, and accept legacy header-first files with no slot.

features.name: session-header-schema
features.what: Header carries `type:"session"`, `version` (current 3), `id`, `timestamp`, `cwd`, optional `title`, `titleSource` (`auto`|`user`), `additionalDirectories` (normalized+deduped extra roots), `previousSessionFiles` (prior absolute paths after successful moves), `providerPromptCacheKey`, and opaque `parentSession` lineage string.

features.name: entry-taxonomy
features.what: Every non-header entry has `{type,id(8-char),parentId(string|null),timestamp}`; the union is exactly: message, thinking_level_change, model_change, service_tier_change, compaction, branch_summary, reset_boundary, custom, custom_message, label, title_change, ttsr_injection, credential_pin, session_init, mode_change — each with the documented payload shape.

features.name: session-version-migrations
features.what: On load, run v1→v2 (synthesize `id`/`parentId` from file order into a linear chain; rename compaction `firstKeptEntryIndex`→`firstKeptEntryId`) and v2→v3 (rewrite `message.role==="hookMessage"` to `"custom"`), setting header version; if any migration ran, mark the session for a full rewrite that must complete before further incremental appends.

features.name: session-loader
features.what: `loadEntriesFromFile(path)` returns [] on ENOENT; uses a streaming JSONL reader for files ≥8 MiB and a full text read otherwise; tolerates non-parseable lines via a lenient parser; strips the title slot; returns [] when the first logical entry is not a valid header (`type!=="session"` or non-string `id`).

features.name: session-path-layout
features.what: Derive the session bucket from the canonicalized cwd (symlink aliases share a bucket): `-<relative>` under home, `-tmp-<relative>` under temp root, `--<encoded-absolute>--` otherwise, with separators replaced by `-`; blobs at ~/.omp/agent/blobs/<sha256>; on access, best-effort migrate legacy hashed buckets (`<scope>-<basename>-<sha256(cwd)>`) and older `--<home-encoded>-*--` spellings back to path-encoded names.

features.name: terminal-breadcrumb
features.what: Write ~/.omp/agent/terminal-sessions/<terminal-id> containing original cwd + session file path + optional third line `fresh`; terminal id prefers TTY path then ZELLIJ_PANE_ID/TMUX_PANE/CMUX_SURFACE_ID/KITTY_WINDOW_ID/WEZTERM_PANE/TERM_SESSION_ID/WT_SESSION; writes are synchronous, ordered, best-effort, non-fatal.

features.name: lazy-materialization-gate
features.what: A new ordinary session stays memory-only until it contains an assistant message or a caller invokes `ensureOnDisk()`; crossing the gate writes title slot + header + all accumulated entries, after which appends are incremental. Saving an editor draft forces a discoverable header plus `draft.txt` with a marker, and close deletes a draft-only session whose draft vanished (explicit ensureOnDisk sessions stay resumable).

features.name: append-write-pipeline
features.what: Each completed entry updates memory and is handed to storage synchronously inside the append call once the file gate is crossed; streaming partial text is never persisted until the completed message is appended; concurrent completed appends supersede an in-flight atomic rewrite with an authoritative full-body rewrite.

features.name: atomic-rewrite-and-error-model
features.what: Full rewrites use storage `writeTextAtomic` with a commit guard (file storage stages then renames, with an EPERM-safe move-aside `.bak` fallback); persistence errors are latched and rethrown by later flush/close/write, logged once with session-file context; unprovable publication raises `SessionPersistenceIndeterminateError` carrying original + recovery errors.

features.name: flush-durability-ops
features.what: `flush()` drains async disk/storage queues and the open writer; `flushSync()` performs synchronous draining/full rewrite where supported; neither performs fsync, so the guarantee covers software crashes only; writer close propagates the first meaningful error.

features.name: persistence-truncation
features.what: Before writing an entry: truncate strings >500,000 chars with suffix `[Session persistence truncated large content]`; clear (not truncate) `thinkingSignature`/`thoughtSignature`/`textSignature`; strip transient `partialJson` and `jsonlEvents`; recompute `lineCount` when an object has both string `content` and numeric `lineCount`; omit redundant OpenAI Responses `thinkingSignature` copies when the authoritative reasoning item exists in `providerPayload`.

features.name: image-blob-externalization
features.what: Always content-address `image_url` data URLs starting `data:image/` and containing `;base64,`; externalize other image content/data payloads and image-generation results at ≥1024 base64 chars (BLOB_EXTERNALIZE_THRESHOLD); store image-block data as decoded bytes and provider data URLs as the original UTF-8 string; replace the persisted value with `blob:sha256:<hash>`.

features.name: blob-store
features.what: Content-addressed store: `put/putSync` SHA-256 the bytes and return `{hash,path:<blobsDir>/<hash>,displayPath,ref:"blob:sha256:<hash>"}`; canonical file has no extension, and a typed sidecar `<hash>.<ext>` is hardlinked/copied for image MIME types; `get` returns null on ENOENT; writes are idempotent per content and blobs are global (survive individual sessions).

features.name: blob-rehydration-on-load
features.what: After migrations, `resolveBlobRefsInEntries()` rewrites `blob:sha256:` refs back to inline shapes: image-block bytes → base64, provider `image_url` → original data-URL string; a missing blob logs a warning, keeps the ref string in memory, and never fails the load.

features.name: storage-abstraction
features.what: `SessionStorage` provides sync dir/exists/write/stat/list plus async read, sliced read, write, guarded atomic write, rename, unlink, artifact-aware delete, title-slot update, writer creation, and backend drain; implementations are `FileSessionStorage` (local files) and `MemorySessionStorage` (map/chunk-backed, used for non-persistent sessions and tests).

features.name: indexed-remote-storage
features.what: `IndexedSessionStorage` adapter layers a shared local index over ordered remote publication for Redis/SQL-backed session storage while satisfying the same `SessionStorage` contract.

features.name: session-entry-index
features.what: Maintain runtime indices in lockstep with the entry journal: `entriesById` map, `children` parent→children adjacency (including a null-parent bucket), resolved `labels` map, current `leaf` pointer, and running usage totals; expose `getEntries()` in insertion order, `getBranch(fromId?)` (root→node path), `getTree()` (SessionTreeNode{entry,children,label} with children sorted oldest→newest, orphan/self-parent/null-parent entries as roots), `getChildren(parentId)`, `getLabel(id)`.

features.name: leaf-movement-primitives
features.what: Exactly three primitives: `branch(entryId)` validates existence and moves `leafId` only (no entry written, cannot take null); `resetLeaf()` sets leafId=null so the next append is a root with parentId=null; `branchWithSummary(branchFromId|null, summary, details?, fromExtension?)` sets the leaf then appends a `branch_summary` child, persisting `fromId:"root"` when the target was null.

features.name: build-session-context
features.what: `buildSessionContext(entries, leafId?, byId?, options?)` returns the LLM context: null leaf → empty; explicit leaf else last entry; walk parentId to root stopping on a repeated id (cycle bound) then reverse; derive resolved+configured thinking, per-family service tier, role→model map (`role ?? "default"`; assistant-message inference is legacy fallback only until an explicit default), deduped injectedTtsrRules, and mode/modeData (default `"none"`); pick the emission boundary (latest reset_boundary wins, else latest compaction emits summary + kept/post-compaction messages); convert message, custom_message and branch_summary entries into messages while other types only affect replay state.

features.name: transcript-context-mode
features.what: `options.transcript:true` builds a display transcript instead of model context: full mode preserves compactions inline chronologically and retains pre-reset history; `collapseCompactedHistory` renders only the current compacted tail; `keepDanglingToolCalls` preserves running tool calls during a mid-turn UI rebuild.

features.name: dangling-toolcall-sanitization
features.what: When rebuilding model context, remove tool calls with no paired result (unless explicitly retained for a mid-turn transcript), neutralize protected reasoning metadata on rewritten turns, and drop unsafe aborted/error assistant turns together with their paired tool results.

features.name: runtime-state-entries-and-restore
features.what: Persist and replay runtime settings as entries: `model_change{model,role?}`, `thinking_level_change{thinkingLevel,configured?}`, `service_tier_change{serviceTier: per-family map openai|anthropic|google → auto|default|flex|scale|priority, or null}` (legacy single-string tiers normalized on read), `mode_change{mode,data}`, `ttsr_injection{injectedRules[]}`; on resume/switch restore the first available recorded model in role/default fallback order, restore configured thinking (`auto` survives as auto), and fall back to current settings when the branch has no entry.
features.surface: model_change / thinking_level_change / service_tier_change / mode_change / ttsr_injection entries

features.name: reset-boundary-clear
features.what: `/clear` appends a payload-free `reset_boundary`; the collapsed live transcript and rebuilt model context begin after the latest boundary while the JSONL and full-transcript export retain pre-reset history. It is TUI-only, rejected while streaming or while a foreground bash/python execution runs, aborts and awaits active compaction, drops live messages/queues/pending tool calls/error+checkpoint/deferred-tool/stop-continuation state, cancels queued continuation and async bash/task jobs, rotates provider session state, re-primes advisors, invalidates append-only context, resets memory promotion, and keeps session id/title/cwd/model/settings/plan path/transcript file.

features.name: entry-labels
features.what: `appendLabelChange(targetId,label?)` writes append-only `label` entries on the current leaf chain and immediately sets/deletes the resolved label in the index; `label:undefined` clears; tree nodes display resolved label state, not raw label history.
features.surface: label entry; Shift+L in tree selector

features.name: create-branched-session
features.what: `createBranchedSession(leafId)` builds the root→leaf path via `getBranch`, throws if missing, excludes existing `label` entries from the copy, rebuilds fresh label entries from `labelsInEffect()` for surviving entries, then in persistent mode writes a new JSONL file, switches the manager to it and returns its path; in-memory mode replaces the entries and returns undefined.

features.name: tree-selector-ui
features.what: Interactive tree navigator showing max(5, floor(terminalHeight/2)) recentered rows, active branch ordered first and bullet-marked, labels as `[label]`; keys: Up/Down (wrap), Alt+Up/Down (prev/next user-or-assistant turn), PgUp/PgDn or Left/Right (page), Home/End, Enter, Shift+Enter (summarize+switch directly), Esc (clear search else close), Ctrl+C, typing appends to search, Backspace deletes, Shift+L labels when search empty, Ctrl+O / Shift+Ctrl+O cycle filters, Alt+D/T/U/L/A jump to filter.

features.name: tree-filters-and-search
features.what: Filter modes cycle default→no-tools→user-only→labeled-only→all (initial from `treeFilterMode`, default `default`): `default` hides label/custom/model_change/thinking_level_change; `no-tools` also hides toolResult; `user-only` shows only role=user messages; `labeled-only` shows currently-labeled entries; `all` shows everything. Assistant messages containing only tool calls are hidden in every mode unless stopReason is neither stop nor toolUse, or the node is the current leaf. Search tokenizes on spaces and requires all tokens to fuzzy (subsequence, case-insensitive) match label/role/type-specific rendered text.

features.name: navigate-tree
features.what: `AgentSession.navigateTree(targetId,{summarize,customInstructions})` flushes pending bash output, validates the target, collects abandoned entries from old leaf to common ancestor, emits cancellable `session_before_tree` with TreePreparation{targetId,oldLeafId,commonAncestorId,entriesToSummarize,userWantsSummary,signal}, optionally summarizes, computes the new leaf (user message or ordinary custom_message → its parentId with text+image draft prefill; skill-prompt custom message or anything else → the entry id, no prefill), applies branchWithSummary/branch/resetLeaf, rebuilds model+display context, resets branch-scoped todo/advisor/checkpoint state, closes provider sessions whose history was rewritten, emits `session_tree`, and rebuilds again if handlers appended entries.

features.name: ask-result-reanswer
features.what: Selecting a past `ask` tool result in the interactive tree returns a `reopenAsk` request without mutating the tree; the selector reopens the original question UI and calls navigateTree again with the replacement result, which is appended as a new sibling toolResult at the original answer's parent (old answer branch preserved); cancel leaves the tree unchanged and unrecoverable/legacy question data falls back to a plain leaf move. This is the only case where selecting the current leaf is not a no-op.
features.surface: /tree selection on an ask tool result

features.name: branch-summary-generation
features.what: `generateBranchSummary` budgets `model.contextWindow - branchSummary.reserveTokens` (default 16384), collects cumulative file ops from summarized entries including prior pi-generated branch_summary details, walks newest→oldest adding messages until budget (preferring recent context, admitting large summary entries at the edge), serializes into `<conversation>`, uses custom instructions or `branch-summary.md` with SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT, prepends `branch-summary-preamble.md`, appends file-op tags, and stores a `BranchSummaryEntry{fromId,summary,details?,fromExtension?}`; requires an active model + credential and is abortable (abort cancels navigation, leaf unchanged).

features.name: summary-on-switch-prompt
features.what: When `branchSummary.enabled`, ordinary Enter in the tree selector offers `No summary` / `Summarize` / `Summarize with custom prompt`; Escape in the prompt reopens the tree selector, custom-prompt cancel returns to the choice, summarization shows a loader with Esc bound to `abortBranchSummary()`, and an abort reopens the selector applying no move; Shift+Enter bypasses the prompt. If summary was requested but nothing needs summarizing, navigation proceeds with no summary entry.

features.name: branch-command
features.what: `/branch` opens the user-message selector and creates a NEW session file: branch source must be a user message; selected text and image attachments restore into the editor draft; a root user message (parentId===null) starts `newSession({parentSession: previousSessionFile})` carrying the prior title and titleSource, otherwise `createBranchedSession(selectedEntry.parentId)` forks history up to that prompt boundary; in-memory mode replaces entries and returns no path.

features.name: new-session
features.what: `/new` starts an empty conversation, switching session identity and assigning a new transcript path in persistent mode; the `/new` boundary is preserved across `--continue` by writing a `fresh` breadcrumb whose lazily-created JSONL does not yet exist.

features.name: fresh-provider-state
features.what: `/fresh` resets provider-facing stream state only: rejected while streaming; closes every cached provider-session state entry (server-side conversation / prompt-cache handles) and reports how many were pruned; mints a fresh provider session id, re-keys hindsight/mnemopi memory to it, and invalidates the append-only context so the next turn re-sends the full local transcript; leaves transcript, session file, header, and identity untouched.

features.name: drop-session
features.what: `/drop` best-effort deletes the current persisted session JSONL and its artifact directory, logs any failure, then creates and switches to a new session regardless of deletion success.

features.name: fork-session
features.what: `/fork` (persistent mode only, rejected while streaming) emits cancellable `session_before_switch{reason:"fork"}`, flushes, calls `SessionManager.fork()` which writes a new session id + JSONL path with a rewritten header (new id, new timestamp, unchanged cwd, `parentSession`=previous session id, `providerPromptCacheKey`=previous inherited key or previous session id) and all non-header entries unchanged, recursively copies the old artifact directory into the new namespace (ENOENT tolerated, other copy errors logged non-fatally), updates agent.sessionId, inherits the prompt-cache key unless one is pinned, then emits `session_switch{reason:"fork"}`; in-memory returns undefined/false with `Fork failed (session not persisted or cancelled)`.

features.name: cli-fork
features.what: `--fork <id|path>` resolves before normal session creation, is rejected with `--no-session`, treats values containing `/`, `\` or ending `.jsonl` as paths (`forkFrom(path,cwd,sessionDir)`) and otherwise resolves via `resolveResumableSession`, creates the forked file in the current cwd/session-dir scope, and makes it the startup session manager.

features.name: prompt-cache-key-inheritance
features.what: Full-context forks seed `providerPromptCacheKey` from the source header's inherited key, falling back to the source session id; startup drops that automatic inheritance when `--model`, `--thinking`, `--system-prompt`, `--append-system-prompt`, `--tools`, or `--no-tools` changes the provider route or prompt/tool shape; `--prompt-cache-key <key>` pins it explicitly, independent of the OMP session id and `--provider-session-id` (which controls provider routing headers and sticky credential selection).

features.name: switch-session-runtime
features.what: `AgentSession.switchSession(path)` is the guarded in-process transition: emit cancellable `session_before_switch{reason:"resume",targetSessionFile}` → disconnect agent events, abort in-flight work, run pre-switch reconciler → flush bash/session writes and snapshot rollback state (manager, messages+all queues, model/thinking/tier, tools/prompts, provider/cache ids, memory promotion, checkpoint/rewind) → clear queues, drain/detach advisor recorders for a different file → `setSessionFile()` → sync ids/memory keys/display context/checkpoint → emit `session_switch` → replace messages, reset advisors, sync todos, close provider sessions → restore model, synthetic abort for interrupted turns, restore thinking/tiers → reset memory/tool state → reconnect events, run session-switch reconciler, refresh workspace-root prompt block (errors logged, not rolled back) → restore advisor cost, finish bash transition, notify session-change callbacks, return true. Any throw before commit restores every snapshotted field, reconnects and re-reconciles, then rethrows. It never creates a session file.

features.name: set-session-file-recovery
features.what: `setSessionFile(path)` updates the breadcrumb, loads/migrates/blob-resolves/indexes entries, and adopts the recorded cwd; an empty loader result (ENOENT, malformed header, or unreadable entries) is treated as an empty session and a brand-new initialized session is materialized at that exact path — recovery, not failure; genuine I/O errors still propagate.

features.name: session-listing-discovery
features.what: Two scan pipelines over the cwd bucket: `getRecentSessions(dir,limit=4)` reads only a 4 KiB prefix and returns `{path,name,timeAgo}` sorted by mtime desc; `list(cwd,sessionDir?)`/`listAll()` read a 4 KiB prefix plus a bounded 32 KiB tail and return `SessionInfo{path,id,cwd,title/parent metadata,dates,size,message previews/count,status}` sorted by modified desc, where status ∈ complete|interrupted|aborted|error|pending|unknown. Scans are stat-keyed and cached, large sets use bounded parallel workers, `listSessionsReadOnly` is the non-mutating variant, and normal per-directory scans recover the newest orphaned EPERM `.bak` when its primary JSONL is missing.

features.name: session-display-naming
features.what: `sessionDisplayName` prefers `title` → first user message → `Untitled · <time>` and never falls back to the raw id; `sanitizeSessionName` keeps only the first line and strips control characters; the welcome screen truncates to available column width. `SessionInfo.title` prefers the fixed title slot, then `header.title`, then the last compaction `shortSummary` visible in the prefix; `firstMessage` falls back to `(no messages)`.

features.name: resume-key-resolution
features.what: `resolveResumableSession(...)` searches local scope first, then global (`listAll()`) only when no explicit `sessionDir` was provided; matching is case-insensitive `startsWith` against the session id, the full JSONL filename, and the id suffix after the timestamp in `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl`; the first match in modified-desc order wins with no ambiguity prompt; no match throws `Session "..." not found.`

features.name: session-pickers
features.what: Fullscreen CLI picker (`selectSession`) resolves exactly once — selection→SessionInfo, Esc→null, Ctrl+C→stop TUI and exit — and the in-session picker mounts in the editor area; both support Up/Down and PgUp/PgDn (clamped, not wrapping), Enter, Tab to toggle current-folder ↔ all-projects (all-projects loaded lazily/preloaded and cached), Delete or Backspace-on-empty-search to delete the JSONL + artifacts after confirmation, and multi-token search across id/title/cwd/first message/prefix text/path where literal matches lead by recency, then strong fuzzy matches, with debounced `history.db` prompt matches promoted; the fullscreen picker also supports mouse wheel/click; empty folder scope renders `No sessions in current folder. Press Tab to view all.` and global empty renders `No sessions found`.

features.name: resume-command
features.what: `/resume` with no argument opens the picker in current-folder scope and on selection calls `switchSession`, resets UI (stop loader, clear status/pending message/tool map/streaming refs), clears and rerenders chat from session context, reloads todos, re-points process cwd and cwd-derived caches via `applyCwdChange` for a cross-project resume, and reports `Resumed session` / `Resumed session in <dir>`; `/resume <id>` resolves local-then-global and switches directly, reporting `Session "<value>" not found` otherwise.

features.name: cli-resume-startup
features.what: `--resume <path-like>` opens directly; `--resume <key>` resolves and, when the matched session's recorded directory no longer exists, prompts `Session's directory no longer exists (...). Move (re-root) it into the current directory? [Y/n]` (yes → open + `moveTo(cwd)`, no → cancel startup, non-TTY → SessionResolutionError); an existing recorded directory is opened in place (never implicitly forked) and startup switches process cwd, reloads project-scoped settings/plugins and re-resolves enabled models. Bare `--resume` lists current-folder sessions, probes `listAll()` only to detect a globally empty state and preload the Tab scope (never auto-switching scope), prints `No sessions found` and exits when both are empty, and `No session selected` on cancel.

features.name: continue-recent
features.what: `continueRecent(cwd,sessionDir?)` resolves the session directory, reads the terminal breadcrumb, treats a materialized target as usable and a missing target as usable only when the third line is `fresh` (a missing fresh target starts a new session instead of resurrecting the previous transcript), walks stale subagent/artifact breadcrumbs up to the top-level interactive parent (≤8 levels), re-roots a breadcrumb session whose different cwd no longer exists when the current directory has no sessions of its own, else uses a cwd-matching breadcrumb, else the newest file by mtime, else creates a new session. `--continue <full-UUID>` normalizes to `--resume <UUID>` when the UUID is the sole positional; the `autoResume` setting invokes the same path when no explicit session flag/dir is supplied and restores model/thinking state.

features.name: move-to-cwd
features.what: `SessionManager.moveTo(cwd)` renames both the session JSONL and its artifact directory into the new default session directory with rollback if a later step fails, appends the prior absolute location to header `previousSessionFiles`, and preserves artifact identity while relocating session scope.

features.name: session-title-management
features.what: `setSessionName(name, source)` refuses to overwrite a `titleSource:"user"` title with an automatic rename; a title change patches the fixed-width 256-byte title slot in place and appends a `title_change{title,source,previousTitle?,trigger?}` audit entry instead of rewriting the body, so listing never needs a full-file read. Plan approval seeds an unnamed session from the plan title via `humanizePlanTitle` (runs of `-`/`_`→single space, trim, capitalize first char, `""` for separator-only input), then refreshes terminal title and editor border color.
features.surface: setSessionName(); title slot; title_change entry; humanizePlanTitle()

features.name: foreign-session-import
features.what: `/resume @claude` and `/resume @codex` open read-only foreign-session pickers (no delete, no history augmentation, no all-projects scope); the selected foreign transcript is converted and persisted under a fresh OMP session identity, then switched to.

features.name: session-exit-records
features.what: Write a `custom` entry `session_exit{reason,kind:normal|signal|fatal|process_exit,recordedAt,pendingToolCalls?}` on normal disposal and postmortem teardown when the session has assistant history or pending tool calls, immediately calling `flushSync()` (flush failure logged); pair it with `tool_execution_start{toolCallId,toolName,startedAt,args?{command?,path?},intent?}` markers written immediately before each tool implementation starts so exit diagnostics can reconstruct calls left pending.

features.name: interrupted-turn-recovery
features.what: On resume, a valid latest `session_exit` after a non-terminal conversation tail causes the loader to append a synthetic assistant message with `stopReason:"aborted"` and rebuild display/agent context; a `normal` exit triggers this only when it recorded pending tool calls, while abnormal kinds trigger it without that list.

features.name: custom-entry-replay-registry
features.what: `custom` entries are opaque non-LLM records keyed by `customType` and consumed by subsystem replay code; core reserves `tool_execution_start`, `session_exit`, `user_todo_edit{phases}` (todo restoration scans backward for the latest snapshot or successful `todo` tool result), `vibe-session-lifecycle` (v1 spawn/turn/tombstone/tombstone-revoked events replayed to recover owned child sessions), and `autoresearch-control{mode:on|off|clear,goal?}` (replayed by `reconstructControlState()`); extensions must use namespaced reverse-domain/package-qualified identifiers and unknown values stay opaque to context reconstruction.

features.name: custom-message-injection
features.what: `custom_message{customType,content(string|text/image blocks),display,details?,attribution:"user"|"agent"}` entries DO participate in LLM context and are converted to developer-role `custom` messages via `convertMessageToLlm`; they are also valid compaction cut points and user-turn boundaries.

features.name: credential-pin-replay
features.what: Persist a `credential_pin` entry recording the provider plus a pseudonymous SHA-256 account/scope hash (never the raw account identity) so resumed OAuth traffic re-pins to the serving account and preserves account-scoped prompt-cache reuse.

features.name: session-init-entry
features.what: Persist a `session_init{systemPrompt,task,tools[],outputSchema?,outputSchemaMode?,restrictToolNames?,spawns?,readSummarize?}` entry capturing the spawn contract of a (sub)agent session.

features.name: export-html
features.what: `/export [--themes] [path]` parses args with `parseExportArgs` (after removing `--themes`, at most one whitespace-delimited path; extras → `Usage: /export [--themes] [path]`; `--copy`/`clipboard`/`copy` rejected with a pointer to `/dump`), embeds header+entries+leafId plus the current systemPrompt and tool descriptions, recursively embeds sibling subagent transcripts as `subSessions`, renders tool calls through the `<omp-tool-view>` web component, appends no session entries, opens the file in a browser in the TUI and only prints the path headlessly; `--export <session.jsonl> [out]` runs before session startup via `SessionManager.open` and prints `Exported to: ...` (`File not found: <path>` when missing); in-memory sessions fail with `Cannot export in-memory session to HTML`.

features.name: dump-transcript
features.what: `/dump` returns `formatSessionAsText()` (system prompt, active model/thinking level, tool definitions+parameters, user/assistant messages, thinking blocks, tool calls, tool results and execution blocks except `excludeFromContext` bash/python entries, custom/hook/file-mention/branch-summary/compaction-summary entries), reports `No messages to dump yet.` when empty, and best-effort writes a sidecar `omp-llm-request-<id>.json` in the OS temp dir containing model, thinking level, service tier, system prompt, wire tool schemas, and LLM-converted messages; the TUI copies the combined text to the clipboard while headless/ACP returns it as command output. No entries are appended and a sidecar failure never suppresses the transcript.

features.name: share-encrypted
features.what: `/share` builds a snapshot (header, entries, leafId, systemPrompt, tool descriptions), optionally applies typed per-field secret redaction when `share.redactSecrets` (default on) — dropping opaque provider replay fields and untyped extension payloads (`details`,`data`,`outputSchema`, compaction preserveData) rather than traversing them — gzips and seals it with a fresh AES-256-GCM key laid out `[12B IV][ciphertext+tag]`, uploads per `share.store`: `blob` (default) POSTs to `share.serverUrl` (default https://my.omp.sh/s) capped at 1 MB with progressive trimming (inline images → long strings at 32 KB→8 KB→2 KB→512 B → oldest entries), or `gist` pushing base64 `session.ompshare.txt` via authenticated `gh` (5 MB sealed budget, 10 MB raw fetch cap) with share-server fallback; prints `<share.serverUrl>/<id>#<base64url key>`. Works for in-memory sessions.

features.name: custom-share-handler
features.what: In the TUI only, `loadCustomShare()` picks the first existing of ~/.omp/agent/share.{ts,js,mjs}, requiring a default-exported `(htmlPath) => Promise<CustomShareResult|string|undefined>`; the session is exported to `${os.tmpdir()}/${Snowflake.next()}.html`, the handler receives the path, and the temp file is removed afterwards; a string result is treated as a URL (shown and opened), an object may supply `url` and/or `message`, falsy yields `Session shared`. Load or execution failure errors out and explicitly does NOT fall back to the default encrypted flow; headless/ACP never loads custom share scripts.

features.name: compaction-entry-and-boundary
features.what: `CompactionEntry{summary,shortSummary?,firstKeptEntryId,tokensBefore,details?,preserveData?,fromExtension?}` is appended on the leaf; `prepareCompaction()` considers only entries after the previous compaction (`boundaryStart = prevCompactionIndex+1`), adapts `keepRecentTokens` (default 20000) by measured usage ratio, and runs `findCutPoint()`; valid cut points are message entries with roles user/assistant/bashExecution/hookMessage/branchSummary/compactionSummary, `custom_message` entries, and `branch_summary` entries — never a `toolResult`; non-message metadata entries immediately before the cut are pulled into the kept region by moving the cut index backward until a message or compaction boundary.

features.name: compaction-triggers
features.what: Six paths: manual `/compact [instructions]`; overflow recovery (same-model assistant error detected as context overflow and not older than the latest compaction — remove the failing message, try context promotion first, else compact with reason `overflow`, willRetry true, then schedule `agent.continue()`); incomplete-output recovery (`stopReason==="length"`, reason `incomplete`, willRetry true, handoff strategy allowed); post-turn threshold maintenance (`resolveThresholdTokens`, reason `threshold`, willRetry false); mid-turn threshold maintenance at safe tool-loop boundaries when `compaction.midTurnEnabled!==false`; and idle maintenance (`runIdleCompaction()`, reason `idle`, no auto-continue) when not streaming or already compacting.
features.surface: /compact; compaction.thresholdPercent=-1 / thresholdTokens=-1 / midTurnEnabled=true / idleEnabled=false / idleThresholdTokens=200000 / idleTimeoutSeconds=300

features.name: compaction-strategies
features.what: `compaction.strategy` ∈ `snapcompact` (default) | `context-full` | `handoff` | `shake` | `off`: context-full generates an LLM summary; shake mechanically replaces eligible tool results and large fenced/XML blocks with recoverable `artifact://` refs under a protected recent-token window and minimum-savings threshold, falling through to context-full when it cannot reach the recovery band (idle shake excepted); snapcompact deterministically renders discarded history onto model-aware bitmap PNG frames with no model/API/network, requiring a vision-capable model (`model.input` includes `image`) or falling back to context-full with a warning; handoff creates a new session instead of writing a compaction entry.

features.name: snapcompact-archive-replay
features.what: The snapcompact archive persists under `CompactionEntry.preserveData.snapcompact` as bounded source text plus rendered frames and is reconstructed on every context rebuild into ordered blocks: verbatim text at the oldest edge, imaged middle, verbatim text at the newest edge; later compactions re-render from `Archive.text` rather than carrying old PNGs forward; `maxFrames` (MAX_FRAMES_DEFAULT=80) is only an upper limit and a large middle foveates internally (HQ/LQ/HQ); serialization truncates tool results head+tail (2000 chars, 0.6 head ratio), caps tool-call args per value (500) and per call (2000), and dims tool output.

features.name: split-turn-compaction
features.what:
When the cut point is not at a user-turn start (turn starts are `message.role==="user"`, `bashExecution`, `custom_message`, or `branch_summary`), generate two summaries — history (`messagesToSummarize`) and turn prefix (`turnPrefixMessages`) — and store them merged as `<history>

---

**Turn Context (split turn):**

<turn prefix>`.

features.name: summary-generation-prompts
features.what: Build summaries by converting via `convertToLlm()`, serializing with `serializeConversation()`, wrapping in `<conversation>`, optionally adding `<previous-summary>` and `<additional-context>` (extension hook context + active memory-backend context), and executing with SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT; prompt selection is compaction-summary.md (first), compaction-update-summary.md (iterative), compaction-turn-prefix.md (split second pass), compaction-short-summary.md (short UI summary), handoff-document.md (handoff).

features.name: remote-and-native-compaction
features.what: When `compaction.remoteEndpoint` is set and remote compaction enabled, POST either `{systemPrompt,prompt}` (custom omp summarizer, must return JSON with at least `{summary}`) or, for paths ending `/chat/completions`, `{model,messages:[system,user],stream:false}` reading `choices[0].message.content`; eligible OpenAI/Azure Responses and Codex models first try V2 streaming compaction (append a `compaction_trigger` to a normal Responses stream, keep the returned compaction item plus retained real user messages as replacement history bounded by `compaction.v2RetainedMessageBudget`, persisted under `preserveData.openaiRemoteCompaction`), then the provider-native `/responses/compact` path, then local summarization.

features.name: tool-output-pruning
features.what: `pruneToolOutputs` runs before compaction checks: protect the newest 40,000 tool-output tokens, require ≥20,000 total estimated savings, never blank a result below MIN_PRUNE_TOKENS=50 (the `[Output truncated - N tokens]` placeholder costs ~8 tokens), and never prune `skill` results, `read` results of `skill://` paths, or reads of the active plan reference file; superseded reads prune regardless of size for correctness. If pruning changed entries, rewrite session storage and refresh agent message state before compaction decisions.

features.name: useless-result-elision
