features.what: Tools may flag a finished result `useless` (`ToolResultBuilder.useless()`), copied by the agent loop onto the persisted ToolResultMessage but never together with `isError`; the per-turn stale pass (`pruneSupersededToolResults`, gated by `compaction.dropUseless`) blanks flagged results to exactly `[Uneventful result elided]` only when the suffix after the candidate is ≤~8k tokens or the session idled past the provider prompt-cache lifetime, the threshold prune bypasses the protect-recent window for them, and summary/archive serialization drops the whole call/result pair; the flag never reaches provider wire formats and pairs are blanked in place, never removed.

features.name: file-operation-summary-context
features.what: Track cumulative file activity from assistant tool calls (`read`→read set, `write`/`edit`→modified set), including prior compaction details only when the prior entry is pi-generated (`fromExtension!==true`) and turn-prefix ops for split turns; `details.readFiles` excludes modified files and `details.modifiedFiles` holds the rest; render a grouped prefix-folded directory tree with per-file markers `(Read)`/`(Write)`/`(RW)`, capped at 20 files with an `[…N files elided…]` line, appended as a `<files>` tag via `upsertFileOperations` (snapcompact renders a FILES section instead), stripping legacy `<read-files>`/`<modified-files>`/`<files>` tags first so old summaries self-heal.

features.name: compaction-persist-and-rebuild
features.what: After summary generation (or a hook-supplied summary): append the CompactionEntry, rebuild display context from the active leaf, replace live agent messages with the rebuilt context, synchronize active todo phases from the rebuilt branch, close provider sessions whose history was rewritten, and emit `session_compact`.

features.name: compaction-display-divider
features.what: The TUI renders the display transcript rather than restarting the conversation: every path entry appears chronologically with each compaction shown inline as a slim divider `── 📷 compacted · ctrl+o ──` that expands to the summary on ctrl+o; only the LLM context resets at the boundary, and scrollback above the divider survives session resume.

features.name: auto-continue-after-compaction
features.what: When `compaction.autoContinue!==false`, post-turn threshold maintenance schedules an agent-authored developer auto-continue prompt from `prompts/system/auto-continue.md`; mid-turn maintenance never schedules a separate continuation because the core loop already owns the next request, and idle maintenance never auto-continues.

features.name: compaction-failure-semantics
features.what: Manual compaction aborts the current agent operation first; `abortCompaction()` cancels manual, auto, and handoff controllers; auto compaction emits start/end session events, may try multiple model candidates and retry transient failures (preferring the next candidate over long retry delays), excludes overflow errors from the generic retry path, and reports `Context overflow recovery failed: ...` / `Incomplete response recovery failed: ...` / `Auto-compaction failed: ...` per path.

features.name: handoff-pipeline
features.what: `/handoff [focus instructions]` refuses while streaming and requires ≥2 `type==="message"` entries (UI warns `Nothing to hand off (no messages yet)`, the session layer throws); it renders the handoff prompt after secret obfuscation, appends it as an agent-attributed trailing `user` message to a snapshot of agent.state.messages, converts via `convertMessagesToLlm`, builds provider Context with `agent.buildSideRequestContext(...)` pinned to the base system prompt, uses the live provider cache key with a unique side sessionId `<sid>:side:<snowflake>`, `preferWebsockets:false`, `initiatorOverride:"agent"`, then issues one `generateHandoffFromContext(...)` oneshot with clamped compaction reasoning and `toolChoice:"none"` (one-time retry with `"auto"` when the provider rejects explicit tool choice), joins only text blocks with `\n`, discards tool-call blocks, deobfuscates, and throws on `stopReason==="error"` after retry.

features.name: handoff-session-transition
features.what: On generated text: emit cancellable `session_before_switch{reason:"handoff"}` → flush bash + session writer → drain/detach advisor recorders while still pointing at the old session → begin bash transition and cancel session-owned async jobs → start a brand-new session with `parentSession` = previous session file → clear advisor cost, session-scoped tool/checkpoint state and stale provider-session state → preserve steering and follow-up queues across `agent.reset()` → rebind agent session id, rekey memory, clear queued next-turn context, reset the todo cycle → append `custom_message` with customType `handoff`, display true, attribution `agent`, content wrapped in `<handoff-context>…</handoff-context>` plus the trailing usage sentence → rebuild display context, `agent.replaceMessages(...)`, reset advisors/todos → emit `session_switch{reason:"handoff",previousSessionFile}` → return `{document, savedPath?}`. The old session receives nothing.

features.name: handoff-cancellation-classification
features.what: `abortHandoff()` aborts `#handoffAbortController` (cleared in `finally`), `isGeneratingHandoff` gates the global Escape handler; a direct abort or an unreasoned caller signal normalizes to `Error("Handoff cancelled")` → UI `Handoff cancelled`, while a harness abort reason, empty manual generation (`Handoff generation produced no content`), or any provider/transition error → `Handoff failed: <message>`; `AgentSession.abort()` aborts handoff first with its harness reason so compaction cancellation cannot mask the failure; auto-handoff returns undefined on empty generation so maintenance falls back to context-full, and an extension-cancelled switch reports as cancelled without triggering that fallback.

features.name: handoff-disk-artifact
features.what: When `compaction.handoffSaveToDisk` is enabled, only an automatically triggered handoff writes `handoff-<ISO timestamp>.md` into the NEW persisted session's artifact directory; manual `/handoff` never writes it and non-persisted sessions have no artifact directory; write failure is logged and never fails the already-created handoff session.

features.name: checkpoint-tool
features.what: `checkpoint({goal})` (approval `read`, strict, loadMode `discoverable`, gated by `checkpoint.enabled` default false) throws `ToolError("Checkpoint already active.")` when a checkpoint exists, otherwise returns text `Checkpoint created.` / `Goal: <goal>` / `Run your investigation, then call rewind with a concise report.` plus `details{goal,startedAt:ISO}`; on the successful tool-result event the session captures `{checkpointMessageCount: agent.state.messages.length, checkpointEntryId: last persisted entry id, startedAt}`, clears pending/last-completed rewind state, and writes no dedicated marker entry.

features.name: rewind-tool
features.what: `rewind({report})` trims the report and rejects empty (`Report cannot be empty.`), errors with `Checkpoint already completed; continue from the retained rewind report instead of calling rewind again.` or `No active checkpoint. Create a checkpoint before calling rewind.` as appropriate, and returns `Rewind requested.` / `Report captured for context replacement.` with `details{report,rewound:true}`; the actual rewind is deferred to `turn_end`, where `#applyRewind()` calls `branchWithSummary(checkpointEntryId, report, {startedAt})` (logging `Rewind branch checkpoint missing, falling back to root` and branching from root when the id no longer resolves), appends a hidden `rewind-report` custom message rendered from `prompts/system/rewind-report.md` with `details{report,startedAt,rewoundAt}`, rebuilds display+LLM context from the new branch and replaces both the turn's message array and agent.state.messages, resets advisors preserving cost, syncs todos, closes rewritten provider sessions, and clears checkpoint/pending state.

features.name: checkpoint-rewind-rehydration
features.what: On resume, session switch, or tree navigation, `#rehydrateCheckpointRewindState()` scans the current persisted branch: the most recent successful checkpoint tool result with no later retained rewind report reconstructs the active checkpoint boundary and guard, and a retained report rehydrates `#lastCompletedRewind`; while a checkpoint is active with no pending report, `#enforceRewindBeforeYield()` injects a developer-role `<system-warning>` demanding rewind before yield and schedules another turn.

features.name: artifact-manager
features.what: Derive the artifact directory by stripping `.jsonl` from the session file path; lazily create it and, on first directory-backed allocation, scan existing `*.log` files for the max numeric id setting `nextId = max+1` (concurrent first allocations share one initialization promise so IDs cannot be reissued); allocate files `{id}.{sanitizedToolType}.log` where the tool type collapses characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` to `_`, trims surrounding underscores, caps at 64 chars and falls back to `tool`; missing directory → start at `0`; non-persistent sessions without an adopted manager keep `saveArtifact` content in an in-memory map.

features.name: artifact-url-protocol
features.what: `artifact://<id>` requires a numeric id (`artifact:// ID must be numeric, got: <id>`), searches registered active session artifact directories preferring the calling session's pinned directory first (ids are session-local), matches filename prefix `<id>.`, returns raw `text/plain`, lists available numeric ids when missing, throws `No session - artifacts unavailable` with no registered dirs and `No artifacts directory found` when registered dirs are absent on disk, and refuses inline materialization above 8 MiB while still allowing bounded `read` selectors and path-only resolution at any size.

features.name: agent-output-manager-protocol
features.what: `AgentOutputManager` allocates ids from the requested name verbatim first and suffixes `-2`,`-3`… on repeats, dot-qualifies nested outputs (`Parent.Child`), and scans both `.md` outputs and `.jsonl` child sessions at init so resume cannot clobber either (the reserved advisor transcript stem is never allocated unchanged); `agent://<id>` returns `<artifactsDir>/<id>.md` as markdown, `agent://Parent/Child` first tries nested `Parent.Child.md` and only then falls back to JSON extraction from the base output, `?q=` always extracts JSON, path and query extraction cannot be combined, extraction requires valid JSON and returns `application/json`, and line selectors are rejected for extraction URLs.

features.name: subagent-session-sidecars
features.what: Task execution writes subagent session JSONL sidecars `<outputId>.jsonl` inside the parent session's artifact directory (recursively for nested spawns); a subagent may adopt the parent ArtifactManager, sharing one directory and numeric id space; HTML export collects these recursively as `subSessions` (disable via `includeSubSessions:false`) and renders agent ids in task cards as breadcrumbed sub-session overlays.

features.name: output-sink-spill
features.what: `OutputSink` sanitizes every chunk (with optional sixel passthrough), feeds optionally-throttled live `onChunk` with pre-column-cap chunks, applies a per-line column cap that starts artifact mirroring when it drops bytes, marks output truncated and starts mirroring when the in-memory tail would exceed DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES=50KB, writes the current buffer first when opening a file sink then all queued/subsequent chunks, trims memory to a tail window (or head + elision marker + tail when head retention is configured), and returns `artifactId` from `dump()` only when file sink creation succeeded — falling back to in-memory truncation only on sink failure.

features.name: session-lifecycle-hooks
features.what: Emit `session_before_switch{reason: new|fork|resume|handoff, targetSessionFile, previousSessionFile}` (cancellable via `{cancel:true}`, `ExtensionRunner.emit()` returns early on the first cancelling result) and `session_switch` with the same reason set; plus `session_before_branch`/`session_branch`, `session_before_tree`/`session_tree`, `session_before_compact` (may cancel or supply a full `CompactionResult`), `session.compacting` (may return `prompt`, `context`, `preserveData`), `session_compact`, `session_start`, `session_shutdown`. SDK bridges these to custom-tool `onSession({reason: switch|branch|start|tree|shutdown, previousSessionFile})` callbacks, which are observational and cannot cancel.

features.name: extension-session-actions
features.what: `ExtensionCommandContext` exposes `branch(entryId)` → `{cancelled}` (creates a branched session file) and `navigateTree(targetId,{summarize?})` → `{cancelled}` (in-file leaf move); `HookCommandContext` exposes the same two actions but intentionally omits extension-only session switching/reload/compaction actions.

features.name: prompt-history-storage
features.what: A separate SQLite subsystem at ~/.omp/agent/history.db with table `history(id,prompt,created_at,cwd,session_id)` and an FTS5 index `history_fts` kept in sync by triggers; consecutive identical prompts are deduplicated via an in-memory last-prompt cache and inserts are batched through an async drain queue (~100 ms delay) so prompt capture never blocks turn execution; used for prompt recall/search in pickers, never for conversation replay.

features.name: in-memory-session-mode
features.what: `SessionManager.inMemory()` (`--no-session`) sets persist=false with `MemorySessionStorage`, has no session file path, makes `fork()` return undefined and `/fork` return false with `Fork failed (session not persisted or cancelled)`, fails `/export` with `Cannot export in-memory session to HTML`, returns undefined from `createBranchedSession` while still replacing in-memory entries, bypasses CLI resume/continue resolution entirely, and still supports `/dump` and `/share`.

features.name: Provider catalog descriptor table
features.what: A single static table maps each provider id to `defaultModel`, ordered `envVars` for API-key fallback, a model-manager factory, `allowUnauthenticated`, `dynamicModelsAuthoritative`, `catalogDiscovery` metadata, and `specialModelManager`; the `KnownProvider` union, default-model map, and provider descriptor list are all derived from it (never hand-maintained).

features.name: Provider auth-registry definitions
features.what: One declarative `ProviderDefinition` per provider (`id`, `name`, `available`, `showInLoginList`, `envKeys`, `allowsMissingApiKey`, `prepareRequest`, `mapSimpleOptions`, `prepareModelDiscovery`, `login`, `refreshToken`, `getApiKey`, `storeCredentialsAs`, `callbackPort`, `pasteCodeFlow`) registered in an ordered `ALL` array; array order is the `/login` list order, and the `OAuthProvider` union, env-key map, refresh dispatch, and callback-port map derive from it.

features.name: Model registry assembly pipeline
features.what: On refresh, load bundled catalog → load `models.yml`/`models.yaml` → apply provider overrides (`baseUrl`,`headers`,`disableStrictTools`) to built-ins → apply `modelOverrides` per provider+model id → merge custom `models` (same provider+id replaces, else append) → merge cached/runtime-discovered models, then re-apply model overrides; `getAll()` returns everything loaded, `getAvailable()` filters to selectable.
depends_on: models.yml custom provider schema and validation

features.name: Model availability rule
features.what: A model is selectable iff its provider id is NOT in the effective `disabledProviders` list AND (the provider is keyless — implicit local engine or `auth: none` — OR credentials resolve); disabled is checked strictly before credentials so no key, OAuth session, env var, or `models.yml` `apiKey` can re-enable a disabled provider.

features.name: Credential resolution ladder
features.what: Resolve a provider key by first match: (1) runtime override (`--api-key`, never persisted), (2) `models.yml` `providers.<id>.apiKey` config key, (3) stored OAuth credential (refreshed on demand), (4) login-sourced stored API key, (5) provider env var incl. `.env`-loaded values, (6) other stored API key (e.g. broker-migrated), (7) `models.yml` fallback resolver; keyless providers return a `kNoAuth` sentinel.

features.name: Provider→environment-variable map with ordered fallbacks
features.what: Each provider declares one or more env var names checked in order (e.g. `anthropic`: `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN` then `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; `moonshot`: `MOONSHOT_API_KEY` then `KIMI_API_KEY`; `coreweave`: `COREWEAVE_API_KEY` then `WANDB_API_KEY`), with computed resolvers (`envKeys`) overriding the plain list for probe-based providers (Vertex ADC, Bedrock chain, Anthropic Foundry).

features.name: .env discovery, precedence, and parsing
features.what: Eagerly load four `.env` files before any provider lookup — `<cwd>/.env` > `~/.omp/agent/.env` > `~/.omp/.env` > `~/.env` — never overwriting an already-set process env var; parsing ignores blanks and `#` lines, requires `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` keys, strips wrapping single/double quotes, drops NUL-containing values, and mirrors each `OMP_`-prefixed key to the matching `PI_` name.

features.name: models.yml custom provider schema and validation
features.what: Root accepts only `providers:`; a provider with non-empty `models` requires `baseUrl`, `apiKey` (unless `auth: none`), and `api` at provider or every model level; an override-only provider (no models) requires at least one of `baseUrl`,`apiKey`,`auth: none`,`headers`,`compat`,`disableStrictTools`,`modelOverrides`,`discovery`,`remoteCompaction`; models require `id` with positive `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` if present; a schema/YAML failure keeps built-in models running and exposes the error via `ModelRegistry.getError()` surfaced in UI.

features.name: Secret-valued config resolution (`!command`, env-name-or-literal)
features.what: `apiKey` and provider/model `headers` values resolve as: value naming an existing env var → that var's value; value starting with `!` → run as shell command with a 10 s timeout and use trimmed stdout (empty/failing output omitted); otherwise use the literal string. Successful command outputs are cached for the process lifetime so the command runs once, not per model.
depends_on: models.yml custom provider schema and validation

features.name: disabledProviders with path scoping
features.what: An exact-match provider-id list that uniformly removes bundled, custom, discovered, extension-registered, and implicit-local providers from availability without deleting credentials; entries may be bare strings (apply everywhere) or scoped objects keyed `path`/`paths`/`pathPrefix`/`pathPrefixes` with values under `providers`/`values`/`items`, applying when cwd is at or under the path (`~` expanded). Settings arrays are replaced wholesale by higher-precedence layers, and path scopes are resolved after the merge.

features.name: Model selector parsing and initial-model resolution
features.what: Parse exact `provider/modelId`, bare model id (provider inferred), fuzzy/substring, glob scope patterns in `--models` (`openai/*`, `*sonnet*`), and an optional `:thinkingLevel` suffix (`off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max`); initial model picks in order: explicit CLI provider+model → first scoped model (when not resuming) → saved default → known provider defaults among available → first available.

features.name: Model role aliases
features.what: Named roles `default, smol, slow, vision, plan, designer, commit, tiny, task, advisor` map to selectors via `settings.modelRoles`; `@role` aliases expand (must be quoted in YAML), `*` selects `@default`, each value may append a thinking selector (`:low`), a role pointing at another role inherits the target model while an explicit suffix on the referring role wins, and `tiny` (falling back to `@smol`) drives titles, memory, auto-thinking classification, and unexpected-stop detection.
depends_on: Model selector parsing and initial-model resolution

features.name: Provider-model cache with static fingerprint
features.what: Per-provider discovered model lists persist in a versioned SQLite model cache with a `static_fingerprint` column hashing the static catalog slice merged into the row; when the network fetch is skipped and the in-memory static fingerprint matches, cached rows are returned verbatim and the static+dynamic merge is bypassed. Fingerprints are memoized per process via a symbol tag on the static-models array. Cache keys are partitioned per endpoint (e.g. `vllm:<hash(baseUrl)>`, `cursor:max-mode-v3`, hashed apiKey+baseUrl+namespace+cwd for scoped gateways).

features.name: Runtime model discovery
features.what: Per-provider discovery types `ollama` (`/api/tags` + `/api/show`), `llama.cpp`, `lm-studio` (`/v1/models` + native `/api/v0/models`), `openai-models-list` (`/v1/models`, envelope keys `data|models|result|items`, dedup by id, schema-validated), `litellm` (probe `/model_group/info` → `/v2/model/info` → `/model/info` → `/v1/model/info`, else `/models`), and `proxy`; `discovery.timeoutMs` (positive finite) overrides the HTTP probe timeout, and `discovery` requires provider-level `api` except for `proxy`.
depends_on: models.yml custom provider schema and validation

features.name: Proxy discovery with per-model wire detection
features.what: `discovery.type: proxy` hits `GET /v1/models` (10 s timeout, OpenAI-style payload) and derives each model's `api` from `supported_endpoint_types`: contains `anthropic` → `anthropic-messages`; contains `openai` → `openai-completions`; otherwise fall back to provider-level `api` or drop the model. Provider-level `api` is optional here, and one `baseUrl` ending in `/v1` round-trips to both wires because the Anthropic client strips a trailing `/v1` before appending `/v1/messages`.

features.name: Implicit local engine registration
features.what: Register `ollama` (`OLLAMA_BASE_URL` → normalized `OLLAMA_HOST` → `http://127.0.0.1:11434`, api `openai-responses`), `llama.cpp` (`LLAMA_CPP_BASE_URL` → `http://127.0.0.1:8080`, api `openai-responses`), and `lm-studio` (`LM_STUDIO_BASE_URL` → `http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1`, api `openai-completions`) as keyless discoverable providers, skipped when the same id is explicitly configured in `models.yml` or appears in `disabledProviders`; Ollama context window resolves `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` → `/api/show` metadata → 128000.

features.name: Authoritative dynamic model replacement
features.what: When a descriptor sets `dynamicModelsAuthoritative: true`, a successful discovery response replaces the bundled/static seed models for that provider entirely (pruning ids not enabled for the account) instead of merging; static seeds still supply reference costs/limits via bundled-reference merge, and stale cached ids are dropped when the static seed set changes.

features.name: Offline catalog generation with pricing backfill
features.what: A build-time generator materializes `models.json` from upstream sources (models.dev descriptors, per-provider discovery using `catalogDiscovery` credentials), applies drop/override policies (exclude local `DISCOVERY_ONLY_PROVIDERS`, prune unsupported geo ids, strip internal wire ids, cap per-family max tokens), and backfills $0 upstream prices from peer providers via alias maps (Antigravity → google/vertex/anthropic; Codex → openai).

features.name: Effort-tier variant collapsing
features.what: Discovery-time collapse of upstream effort-tier model variants into one logical model with `effortRouting` mapping each effort (or `off`) to a wire model id — e.g. Gemini 3.5-flash collapses extra-low/low/agent with budget mapping minimal/low→1000, medium→4000, high→10000; `gemini-3.1-pro` routes high→`gemini-pro-agent` because the upstream high deployment 400s; `claude-*` bare/`-thinking` pairs collapse preserving absent-effort routes.

features.name: Interactive login/logout slash commands
features.what: `/login` opens the OAuth/key provider selector (ordered by registry `ALL`, filtered by `available` and `showInLoginList`), `/login <provider>` jumps directly, `/login <redirect-url>` completes a paste-code flow; `/logout` opens a selector that deletes stored credentials for a provider. Logins are provider-scoped — authenticating one provider never authenticates another — and a disabled provider stays disabled with valid stored auth.

features.name: OAuth flow infrastructure
features.what: Shared PKCE S256 helpers, a localhost callback HTTP server on per-provider fixed ports (`anthropic:54545`, `openai-codex:1455`, `google-gemini-cli:8085`, `google-antigravity:51121`, `gitlab-duo:8080`, `gitlab-duo-agent:8080`, `devin:59653`, `zai-coding-plan:54548`, `cursor` deep-link poll), RFC 8628 device-code flows with `authorization_pending`/`slow_down` backoff (GitHub Copilot, Kimi, xAI, Kilo, OpenAI Codex headless), and paste-code fallback for providers marked `pasteCodeFlow`.

features.name: OAuth token refresh and expiry handling
features.what: `refreshToken` per provider (omit for static tokens → credentials returned unchanged), refresh triggered by a per-provider skew before expiry (e.g. 60 s for Gemini CLI/Antigravity/Vertex, 5 min broker default), single-flighted per credential id so a slow refresh cannot re-trigger, with definitive failures (`invalid_grant`, `invalid_token`, `revoked`, non-blip 401/403) disabling the credential and transient failures (timeout/ECONNREFUSED/fetch failed) left for the next sweep. Anthropic additionally enforces an absolute 30-day grant TTL requiring interactive re-login regardless of refresh rotation.

features.name: Multi-account credential rotation and ranking
features.what: Multiple stored credentials per provider are ranked and rotated automatically; for Anthropic and ChatGPT/Codex each organization or workspace counts as a separate account (one email can hold both a Team seat and a personal plan). Provider-specific ranking strategies scope quota by meter so exhaustion of one meter does not block others — Codex isolates 5h/7d chat limits from `-spark` meter limits, Antigravity scopes by model family counter (`claude-`→Anthropic, `gemini-`/`gemma-`→Google, `gpt-`/`openai/`→OpenAI), Z.AI ranks 5h primary vs weekly secondary.

features.name: Per-provider usage and quota providers
features.what: Pluggable `usageProviderFor(provider)` returning `UsageReport[]` with named `UsageLimit` rows, windows, reset times, and status (`ok`/`warning ≥80%`/`exhausted ≥100%`) — e.g. Anthropic `/api/oauth/usage` (five_hour, seven_day, weekly_scoped) plus `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*` headers, Codex `/wham/usage` plus `x-codex-*-percent/window-minutes/reset-at` response headers, Copilot `quota_snapshots`, Kimi `/coding/v1/usages`, Umans `/v1/usage` (weighted soft cap vs hard burst cap vs concurrency), MiniMax `/v1/token_plan/remains`, Z.AI quota-limit, xAI billing proxy, OpenCode rolling spend windows.
depends_on: OAuth token refresh and expiry handling

features.name: Codex rate-limit reset credits
features.what: Read `rate_limit_reset_credits` from usage, list available credits (`GET /wham/rate-limit-reset-credits`), pick the soonest-expiring one, and redeem it (`POST .../consume` with a client-generated UUID `redeem_request_id`) to clear a rate-limit block immediately rather than waiting out the window.

features.name: Local SQLite auth store
features.what: Stored OAuth and API-key credentials live in `~/.omp/agent/agent.db` (relocated with `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`), with schema-versioned tables, per-credential disable with recorded cause, provider/scope rate-limit blocks, credential dedup by parsed inner token for compound JSON credentials, and a `shared`-scope compatibility mirror maintained by triggers for pre-meter binaries that current APIs must not double-count.

features.name: Auth broker service
features.what: `omp auth-broker serve` binds an HTTP listener (default `127.0.0.1:8765`), owns the canonical SQLite vault, ensures a bearer token at `<config-dir>/auth-broker.token` (mode 0600 in a 0700 dir), and exposes `/v1/healthz` (unauth) plus bearer-protected `/v1/snapshot`, `/v1/snapshot/stream` (SSE deltas + keepalive), `/v1/credential`, `/v1/credential/:id/{refresh,disable,block}`, `DELETE /v1/credential/:id/blocks`, `/v1/credentials/disabled`, `/v1/usage`, `/v1/usage/{history,observed,clients,stale}`. A background refresher sweeps every `refreshIntervalMs` (60 s) refreshing credentials within `refreshSkewMs` (5 min) of expiry.
depends_on: OAuth token refresh and expiry handling

features.name: Broker conditional snapshot long polling
features.what: `GET /v1/snapshot?wait=<ms>` supports generation-based polling: `If-None-Match` accepts a bare integer, quoted `"42"`, or weak `W/"42"` tag; `wait` is truncated to whole ms and clamped to 0–30000 (absent/non-numeric = 0). Absent/invalid/differing tag or `wait<=0` returns 200 immediately; matching tag with `wait>0` blocks and returns 200 on change, empty 304 on expiry, empty 499 on caller disconnect. Every 200/304/499 carries the current generation as a quoted `ETag` plus `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Vary: OMP-Auth-Broker-Capabilities`.

features.name: Remote auth credential store (broker client mode)
features.what: When `OMP_AUTH_BROKER_URL` (or `auth.broker.url`) is set, the local SQLite store is replaced by `RemoteAuthCredentialStore`: ladder layers 3/4/6 come from a broker snapshot whose `refresh` fields are replaced by `REMOTE_REFRESH_SENTINEL`, expiry triggers `POST /v1/credential/:id/refresh` instead of a local refresh, and local replace/upsert/delete-by-provider mutations are rejected with errors pointing at `omp auth-broker login|logout`. `AuthStorage.setConfigApiKey` still lets a `models.yml` key shadow a broker OAuth token without overriding `--api-key`.

features.name: Encrypted broker snapshot cache
features.what: Persist the broker snapshot to `~/.omp/cache/auth-broker-snapshot.enc` (override `OMP_AUTH_BROKER_SNAPSHOT_CACHE`), AES-256-GCM encrypted with `SHA-256(OMP_AUTH_BROKER_TOKEN)` and authenticated with the broker URL as AAD, written atomically mode 0600. Freshness anchors to broker-stamped `snapshot.generatedAt` with a 1 h default TTL (`OMP_AUTH_BROKER_SNAPSHOT_TTL_MS`, `0` disables); a fresh cache is revalidated against the broker with a 500 ms startup budget, 401/403 are never masked by the cache, transient 5xx fall back to it, and a new cache format version invalidates older files.
depends_on: Remote auth credential store (broker client mode)

features.name: Broker capability negotiation for meter scopes
features.what: Clients send `OMP-Auth-Broker-Capabilities: codex-meter-block-scopes` to receive canonical `chat` and `spark` block scopes; without it the broker projects those rows to the legacy `shared` scope on the wire. All capability-dependent responses carry `Vary: OMP-Auth-Broker-Capabilities` so intermediaries never reuse one representation for another client version.

features.name: Client account pools
features.what: `OMP_AUTH_BROKER_ACCOUNT_POOL_FILE` (or programmatic `accountPool`, which wins) maps provider ids to exact snapshot `identityKey` values: a missing provider is unrestricted, an empty array hides every OAuth credential for that provider, a non-empty array exposes only exact identity matches including org/workspace qualifiers, and API-key credentials are always visible. Parsed once at startup; unreadable/malformed files abort initialization rather than broadening the pool. Filtering applies consistently to full snapshots, SSE updates, refresh responses, and aggregate usage (usage attributable only to an API key or lacking identity metadata fails closed).
depends_on: Remote auth credential store (broker client mode)

features.name: Auth gateway forward proxy
features.what: `omp auth-gateway serve` (default `127.0.0.1:4000`, requires `OMP_AUTH_BROKER_URL`, token at `<config-dir>/auth-gateway.token`, `--no-auth` for loopback) exposes `GET /healthz` (unauth) and bearer-protected `GET /v1/{usage,models,credentials/check}` plus `POST /v1/{chat/completions,messages,responses,pi/stream}`; it reads the model id from the body, picks the first bundled model matching it, parses the inbound wire format into a canonical `Context`, resolves the credential from broker-backed `AuthStorage`, dispatches through the shared stream entrypoint, and re-encodes to the inbound format as SSE. There is no raw provider passthrough. `Bun.serve` `idleTimeout` is 255 s.
depends_on: Remote auth credential store (broker client mode)

features.name: Two-layer usage cache
features.what: The broker's `AuthStorage` caches each credential's `UsageReport` in SQLite with a 5-minute TTL plus ±25 % jitter (decorrelating fan-out that otherwise trips provider `/usage` 429s) and keeps the last-good report for up to 24 h on fetch failure; `RemoteAuthCredentialStore` separately coalesces concurrent `fetchUsageReports()` into one shared in-flight `GET /v1/usage` cached 15 s, with each caller's `AbortSignal` raced against the shared promise (never threaded into it) and a failed fetch yielding `null` treated as "no usage signal this cycle".
depends_on: Remote auth credential store (broker client mode)

features.name: CLIProxyAPI credential import and local→broker migration
features.what: `omp auth-broker import <file|dir>` imports CLIProxyAPI-style JSON credentials, mapping `type` to provider ids (`claude→anthropic`, `codex→openai-codex`, `gemini`/`gemini-cli→google-gemini-cli`, `antigravity→google-antigravity`); `omp auth-broker migrate --from-local` uploads local credentials via `POST /v1/credential`, including API keys by default, skipping local OAuth rows unless `--include-oauth` and env-derived keys unless `--include-env`, idempotent across re-runs.

features.name: Remote broker login over SSH tunnel
features.what: `omp auth-broker login <provider> --via=user@host` shells out `ssh -L <callback-port>:127.0.0.1:<callback-port> user@host omp auth-broker login <provider>` so the OAuth callback reaches the local browser while the credential is written on the broker host; `--via` requires an explicit provider, and the OAuth dance runs in-process via `AuthStorage.login()` (no spawned helper binary).

features.name: AWS credential chain and SigV4 signing
features.what: Five-tier resolution — env keys → web identity/OIDC (`AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`) → shared config profile (static keys with 5-min TTL on file session creds, SSO cached-token federation, `credential_process` with POSIX tokenization and `cmd.exe /c` for `.cmd`/`.bat`, Version 1 JSON envelope) → ECS/container relative or full URI → EC2 IMDSv2 (1 s token timeout) — cached per `profile\0region\0config` with 60 s refresh skew and single-flight bounded at 30 s. Requests are signed with WebCrypto SigV4 (`x-amz-content-sha256`, `x-amz-date`, `x-amz-security-token`, HMAC key chain) unless a bearer token is present, which takes precedence; HTTP 401/403 invalidates the cached credentials.

features.name: Google Application Default Credentials ladder
features.what: Resolve Vertex credentials by `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` JSON (service_account via RS256 JWT assertion signed with WebCrypto exchanged at the Google token endpoint, authorized_user refresh exchange, impersonated_service_account via IAM `generateAccessToken`) → `~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json` → GCE/Cloud Run metadata server; `GOOGLE_CLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN`/`CLOUDSDK_AUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN` bypass files and caching. Tokens cache per source with a 60 s refresh skew, share one in-flight promise bounded at 30 s, and per-caller aborts are raced rather than cancelling the shared resolve.

features.name: Unified stream event contract
features.what: Every provider emits the same `AssistantMessageEvent` sequence: `start`, block triplets `text_start/text_delta*/text_end`, `thinking_start/thinking_delta*/thinking_end`, `toolcall_start/toolcall_delta*/toolcall_end`, complete `image_end`, and exactly one terminal `done{reason: stop|length|toolUse}` or `error{reason: aborted|error}`. The event stream delivers events immediately in push order with no batching or merging; `done`/`error` resolves `result()` to the final assistant message, `fail(error)` rejects iteration and `result()`, and `end()` without a final result rejects `result()` rather than hanging.

features.name: Streaming tool-argument JSON accumulation
features.what: Providers append argument fragments to an internal `partialJson` buffer and re-parse via a throttled parser that skips re-parsing until ≥256 new bytes have arrived (bounding mid-stream cost from quadratic to linear); parsing tries `JSON.parse`, falls back to a relaxed/repairing parser for incomplete fragments, and returns `{}` on total failure so malformed deltas never crash the stream. The parse at `toolcall_end` is unconditional and authoritative, after which `partialJson` is stripped.

features.name: Stream watchdogs and terminal grace window
features.what: Wrap each provider stream with a first-event timeout and an inter-event idle timeout (per-model floors from compat: 0 = unbounded for local backends, 300 s for MiMo/Kimi/DeepSeek reasoning/local, 600 s for GLM and Alibaba coding plans, 900 s for Bedrock adaptive thinking); the synthetic `start` event does not count as first progress, providers may call `trackLocalWork()` so server-requested local work is not seen as a stall, keepalive/role-only/empty-`choices` chunks are not progress, ping events reset the idle multiplier, and a 2500 ms post-finish grace window admits trailing usage-only chunks with cache-read details.

features.name: Layered cancellation
features.what: Cancellation propagates as: `options.signal` into the provider client call → provider wrapper forcing the error path with `stopReason: "aborted"` after the stream loop → agent loop checking `signal.aborted` before each provider event and synthesizing an aborted assistant message from the latest partial → `AgentSession.abort()` → `agent.abort()`. Tool execution cancellation is separate: runners use `AbortSignal.any([agentSignal, steeringAbortSignal])` so steering interrupts can abort remaining tools while preserving already-produced results.

features.name: OpenAI Chat Completions transport
features.what: POST JSON + SSE against `/chat/completions` using in-repo HTTP/SSE transport (no vendor SDK): decode `ChatCompletionChunk` frames, normalize `delta.content` whether string or array of text parts, take the first non-empty of `reasoning_content`/`reasoning`/`reasoning_text` per chunk, track `tool_calls[].index` for parallel calls, attach `reasoning_details` encrypted signatures to `toolCall.thoughtSignature`, promote `finish_reason: "stop"` to `toolUse` when structural or healed tool calls exist, and parse usage from `chunk.usage` or `choice.usage`.

features.name: OpenAI Responses transport
features.what: POST `/v1/responses` with `input` items, `instructions`, `store`, `prompt_cache_key`, optional `previous_response_id`, `max_output_tokens`; consume `response.*` lifecycle events routing parallel items by `output_index`, `item_id`, call-id aliases and prefixed `fc_` aliases, tolerate missing `content_part.added`/`output_item.added`, finalize pending tool calls at the terminal event, and treat the stream as authoritative only after `response.completed` or `response.incomplete` (a close before either is a failure, not partial success). Supports function, freeform custom-grammar, and native computer tools, schema quarantine for invalid enum/const contradictions, orphan tool-output repair, and one bounded transient stream retry (500 ms) only before replay-unsafe output.

features.name: OpenAI Responses stateful chaining
features.what: For official OpenAI endpoints, default to `store: true` plus a delta payload anchored to `previous_response_id`; reset to a full replay when history mutates, options change, or prompt-cache breakpoint policy changes; on a stale-id error increment `staleFailures`, replay full context, and disable chaining for the session after 3 consecutive failures; a Zero Data Retention org error disables chaining immediately and forces `store: false`. Third-party Responses proxies must not chain by default.

features.name: OpenAI Codex transport
features.what: ChatGPT-subscription Responses surface over SSE or WebSocket (`OpenAI-Beta: responses_websockets=...`, socket reuse capped at 30 s idle, 10 s ping / 60 s pong, queue 4096, instant SSE fallback on handshake/fatal patterns), with Codex account and beta headers, `x-codex-turn-state`, `x-models-etag`, session affinity headers (`session_id`, `x-codex-installation-id`, `x-codex-window-id`, `x-codex-turn-metadata`, `x-codex-parent-thread-id`, `x-openai-subagent`), optional DeviceCheck attestation header, optional zstd body compression, mandatory stripping of all sampling params (backend 400s), tool-call/output pair repair into assistant notes and synthetic outputs, and `responsesLite` shaping (tools into a leading `additional_tools` developer item, system prompt as developer message, image `detail` stripped, parallel tool calls off, `reasoning.context: "all_turns"`, lite header).

features.name: Codex stream recovery policies
features.what: Bounded recovery: up to 5 retries on transient event errors (`model_error`,`server_error`,`internal_error`), HTTP 429 backoff honoring server delays within a 5-minute budget, 300 s first-event and idle timeouts, stale `previous_response_id` handled as a chain break with full-context retry (websocket only — SSE never chains), websocket→SSE fallback only before replay-unsafe output, and a whitespace tool-call loop breaker capping degenerate argument deltas (256 events / 16 KB) that drops the partial call and retries at most twice.

features.name: Azure OpenAI Responses transport
features.what: Resolve base URL from `options.azureBaseUrl` → `AZURE_OPENAI_BASE_URL` → `https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1` from `azureResourceName`/`AZURE_OPENAI_RESOURCE_NAME` → `model.baseUrl` (else ConfigurationError), strip trailing slashes, append `/responses?api-version=<v>` (default `v1`) as a query param not a header, authenticate with the `api-key` header (never Bearer), send the deployment name as the request body `model` resolved via `options.azureDeploymentName` → `AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_MAP` (`modelId:deployment` comma pairs) → `model.id`, force stateless `store: false`, reject explicit prompt caching, and disable native computer use when the host is not a recognized Azure endpoint.

features.name: Anthropic Messages transport
features.what: POST `/v1/messages` over SSE with an in-repo HTTP client (retry + timeout, honoring `retry-after-ms`/`retry-after`): handle `message_start` (usage init), `content_block_start` (text/thinking/tool_use/redacted_thinking), `content_block_delta` (`text_delta`, `thinking_delta`, `signature_delta` updating the signature with no event, `input_json_delta`), `content_block_stop`, `message_delta` (stop reason + final output tokens), `message_stop`, `ping`. OAuth requests send `Authorization: Bearer` with client-fingerprint headers, beta flags, and an injected `system[0]` agent instruction; API-key requests send `X-Api-Key` only. Errors classify into QUOTA_EXHAUSTED (30 m / rotate), RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (30 s), CONCURRENT_LIMIT (5 s), MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED (45 s ±15 s).

features.name: Anthropic message-shape invariants
features.what: Assistant turns are stably partitioned `[...non_tool_use, ...tool_use]` so `tool_use` blocks sit at the tail (otherwise 400 "tool_use ids without tool_result blocks immediately after"); tool results are a `user` message of `tool_result` blocks keyed by `tool_use_id`, with images embedded except on error results where images are hoisted after the `tool_result` run; thinking blocks replay with intact signatures (unsigned/modified replay 400s) including `redacted_thinking` passthrough; custom tool names are `_`-prefixed under OAuth to avoid collision with server built-ins and decoded on return.

features.name: Anthropic prompt-cache breakpoints
features.what: Attach `cache_control: { type: "ephemeral", scope: ... }` breakpoints to system prompt prefixes, tool definitions, and historical user turns, enforcing a hard cap of 4 breakpoints per request; Anthropic-style cache control requires the marker to sit on a text part, and OpenRouter `anthropic/*` chat-completions models get the same markers via `cacheControlFormat: "anthropic"`.

features.name: Google Generative AI and Vertex transports
features.what: REST/SSE `:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` with system prompt lifted into `systemInstruction`, tools as `tools[].functionDeclarations` with `parametersJsonSchema` (Gemini/Vertex) or `parameters` (Cloud Code Assist), `part.functionCall` treated as a complete tool call emitted start/delta/end at once (no fragment streaming) with synthesized ids, thought parts split by `part.thought === true`, `thoughtSignature` retained only when `msg.provider`/`msg.model` match the target and the value is valid base64, safety block reasons mapped to a content-blocked provider error, and usage computed as input = `promptTokenCount - cachedContentTokenCount`, output = `candidatesTokenCount + thoughtsTokenCount`. Vertex adds ADC/Express-mode auth, location→endpoint-host mapping (global, `eu`/`us` multi-region `.rep.`, regional prefix), default safety thresholds `OFF`, and `X-Vertex-AI-LLM-Shared-Request-Type: priority` for the priority tier.

features.name: Google Cloud Code Assist transport (Gemini CLI / Antigravity)
features.what: `POST /v1internal:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` with CCA-normalized tool schemas (strip `propertyNames`, `additionalProperties`, `patternProperties`, `$schema`, `title`, `description`, tracking nesting inside a literal `properties` key), `functionCallingConfig.mode: "VALIDATED"` default, provider-specific user-agent/version gating of newer models, endpoint auto-failover with a persisted `lastGoodEndpoint`, an Antigravity request envelope (`project`, structured `requestId`, `userAgent`, `requestType`, monotonic `stepIndex` labels, `trajectoryId`, signed-decimal `sessionId`), per-wire-id `maxOutputTokens` profiles (Claude ids capped at 64000), planning-leak filtering of raw JSON blocks streamed into visible text, and OAuth project discovery/onboarding via `loadCodeAssist`/`onboardUser` with bounded operation polling and VPC-SC detection.
depends_on: Google Generative AI and Vertex transports

features.name: Amazon Bedrock Converse transport
features.what: Direct HTTPS POST to `/model/{modelId}/converse-stream` decoding `application/vnd.amazon.eventstream` binary frames (`[total len u32][headers len u32][prelude CRC][headers][payload][message CRC]`, minimum 16 bytes, CRC32 verified for prelude and whole message, typed header parser) without AWS SDK deps; map `messageStart`/`contentBlockStart`/`contentBlockDelta`/`contentBlockStop`/`messageStop`/`metadata` events, throw on `:message-type` `exception`/`error`, merge consecutive tool results into one `user` message with a `toolResult` array, filter empty text blocks, resolve region from explicit option → ARN-embedded → ambient, and map geo-prefixed cross-region inference profiles to geo-default regions when ambient region is incompatible.
depends_on: AWS credential chain and SigV4 signing

features.name: Bedrock no-tools sentinel
features.what: Converse rejects any request whose history contains `toolUse`/`toolResult` without a `toolConfig`; when tools are absent or `toolChoice: "none"`, inject a placeholder tool `__no_tools__` ("do not call" description) with `toolChoice: { auto: {} }`, track a per-request `sentinelInjected` flag so a caller-defined tool of the same name still works, ignore synthetic sentinel tool-use start events, and demote `stopReason: "tool_use"` to `"stop"`.

features.name: Ollama native chat transport
features.what: NDJSON/JSONL streaming from the native `ollama-chat` protocol: `chunk.message.thinking` → thinking events, `chunk.message.content` → text, `chunk.message.tool_calls` → structured calls; reasoning mapped via a native `think` field (`minimal/low→low`, `medium→medium`, `high/xhigh→high`, `max→max`, `false` when disabled); `done_reason` mapping `length→length`, `tool_calls→toolUse`, `load→error`, undefined-with-tool-calls→`toolUse`; developer prompts stay on `system` only for initial/agent-attributed turns and the last system turn demotes to `user` when no user turn exists (otherwise Ollama returns `done_reason: "load"` with no output); `ollama-cloud` strips `thinking` from assistant history (400s otherwise) and clamps `num_predict` to 65536.

features.name: Pi-native gateway transport
features.what: When a model sets `transport: "pi-native"`, bypass local provider resolution and POST `{ modelId: "provider/id", context, options, stream: true }` to `<baseUrl>/v1/pi/stream` with `Authorization: Bearer <gateway token>`; the server validates only shapes, filters `options` against a fixed allow-list dropping unknown keys for cross-version compatibility while the client strips runtime/function-valued keys, and streams canonical `AssistantMessageEvent`s verbatim as SSE terminated by `data: [DONE]`. A stream closing without a terminal event synthesizes `error{aborted}` when the caller aborted or `done{stop}` otherwise; a server iterator throw emits a terminal error frame plus `[DONE]` so clients never hang. `transport` takes precedence over extension-registered custom APIs.

features.name: Dual-surface OpenAI/Anthropic shim
features.what: A runtime surface selector (not a one-way migration) that rebuilds a model spec for the other wire: `anthropic` format strips the trailing `/v1` from `baseUrl`, injects vendor common headers, maps internal reasoning to Anthropic thinking budgets/adaptive effort, and delegates to the Anthropic streamer; `openai` format keeps the `/v1` base URL and delegates to Chat Completions. Selected via `compat.kimiApiFormat`, `providers.kimiApiFormat`, or a per-request `format`/`syntheticApiFormat` option, sharing a `prompt_cache_key` across the transport switch to preserve cache affinity.

features.name: OpenAI compat flag resolution
features.what: Two-phase compat: at catalog build time detect defaults from provider, baseUrl, model id/name, and reasoning support, merge explicit `spec.compat` overrides, and pre-build a complete alternate resolved compat as `compat.whenThinking` when applicable; at request time combine resolved compat with per-request options (`reasoning`, `disableReasoning`, `toolChoice`) into a policy with `reasoning`/`tools`/`messages`/`stream` sub-policies, pointer-swapping to the pre-built `whenThinking` variant when thinking is active rather than spreading per request. Provider-level `compat` is the baseline; per-model `compat` deep-merges with `openRouterRouting`, `vercelGatewayRouting`, `extraBody`, and `whenThinking` merged as nested objects.
depends_on: models.yml custom provider schema and validation

features.name: Request-shaping compat flags
features.what: User-overridable flags controlling wire output: `supportsStore` (emit `store:false` only where accepted), `supportsDeveloperRole`, `supportsMultipleSystemMessages` (else coalesce leading system messages joined by blank lines), `supportsUsageInStreaming` (`stream_options.include_usage`), `maxTokensField` (`max_tokens` vs `max_completion_tokens`), `alwaysSendMaxTokens`, `supportsSamplingParams`, `extraBody`, `wireModelIdMode`, `promptCacheSessionHeader`, `supportsPromptCacheBreakpoints`/`promptCacheBreakpointTtl`, `supportsLongPromptCacheRetention`, `supportsImageDetailOriginal`, `supportsObfuscationOptOut`, `strictResponsesPairing`, `usesOpenAIToolCallIdLimit`, `streamFirstEventTimeoutMs`, `streamIdleTimeoutMs`.

features.name: Thinking capability model
features.what: A canonical `Effort` scale (`minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max`) with per-model `ThinkingConfig`: `mode` (`effort`, `budget`, `google-level`, `anthropic-adaptive`, `anthropic-budget-effort`), supported `efforts` in canonical order, `effortMap` remapping to upstream wire strings, `effortRouting` mapping effort (or `off`) to dynamic wire model ids, pre-computed `effortBudgets` for collapsed tiers, `requiresEffort` (thinking cannot be disabled), and `suppressWhenOff` (off must be sent explicitly as `includeThoughts:false`/`thinkingBudget:0`, not merely omitted). Runtime clamps a requested effort to what the model supports.

features.name: Per-provider reasoning wire encoding
features.what: `thinkingFormat` selects the enable encoding — `openai` (`reasoning_effort`), `openrouter` (`reasoning: { effort }`), `zai` (`thinking: { type: "enabled" }`), `qwen` (top-level `enable_thinking`), `qwen-chat-template` (`chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`) — with a derived `reasoningDisableMode` emitting the correct off-signal (`thinking:{type:"disabled"}`, `enable_thinking:false`, `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking:false`, `reasoning:{enabled:false}`, lowest-effort, or omit); `omitReasoningEffort` suppresses the effort field while keeping the toggle, `supportsReasoningParams:false` suppresses all reasoning params, and `reasoningEffortMap` remaps values. Anthropic uses adaptive (`thinking:{type:"adaptive"}` + `output_config.effort` behind a beta) or budget (`thinking:{type:"enabled", budget_tokens}`); Responses uses `reasoning:{effort, summary}`; Google uses `thinkingConfig:{includeThoughts, thinkingLevel, thinkingBudget}`.

features.name: Reasoning-content history replay policy
features.what: `reasoningContentField` (`reasoning_content`|`reasoning`|`reasoning_text`) names the assistant field carrying replayed thinking; `requiresReasoningContentForToolCalls` forces it on tool-call turns, `requiresReasoningContentForAllAssistantTurns` extends that to every assistant turn, `allowsSyntheticReasoningContentForToolCalls` decides whether a `"."` placeholder may substitute for stripped content (true for Kimi/OpenRouter, false for DeepSeek-reasoning and MiMo which validate exact values), `replayReasoningContent` replays preserved thinking on every assistant turn for local backends to rebuild `<think>` blocks and keep prefix KV-cache hits, `qwenPreserveThinking` emits `preserve_thinking: true`, `requiresThinkingAsText` converts thinking into `<thinking>`-wrapped text, and `filterReasoningHistory`/`includeEncryptedReasoning` control native Responses reasoning-item replay.

features.name: Message transform pipeline
features.what: A shared pre-flight pass before provider-specific conversion performing tool-call dedup, sanitization, and id normalization, plus role/content normalization: developer→user downgrade where unsupported, multi-system coalescing, assistant array content normalized to a string for backends that mirror arrays literally, `content: ""`/`"."` instead of `null` on tool-call replay, synthetic assistant bridging after tool results, tool-result `name` injection, vision partitioning to placeholders when the model cannot accept images, and foreign reasoning-signature stripping/hashing when replaying native history across models.

features.name: Tool schema normalization dispatchers
features.what: All providers start from one neutral wire schema and diverge through named normalizers: OpenAI strict-mode sanitize+enforce (local `$ref` inlining, single-item `allOf` collapse, `anyOf`-wrapper description hoist, enum/const primitive-type inference), Google `parametersJsonSchema` normalization (strip `$schema`/`additionalProperties`, type arrays→nullable), Cloud Code Assist keyword stripping, Anthropic strict-schema normalization (`additionalProperties:false`, keeping open maps non-strict), grammar sanitization for local GBNF backends (widen bare `true`/`{}` subschemas into primitive unions), and Moonshot MFJS (collapse single-value `const` into one-element `enum`, infer `type` on bare enums, strip unsupported keywords).

features.name: Strict tool schemas and scoped fallback
features.what: `supportsStrictMode` gates the per-tool `strict` field, `toolStrictMode` (`all_strict`|`mixed`|`none`) forces or suppresses it globally, and provider-level `disableStrictTools: true` opts out for the allowlisted built-in tools Omp would otherwise mark strict (Anthropic enables strict only for a small allowlist with no incompatible keywords — `oneOf`/`allOf`/`$ref`/`patternProperties`/`propertyNames` — and within strict-tool-count and optional/union parameter budgets). A 400/422 strict rejection disables strict for the scope `${provider}:${baseUrl}:${modelId}` (and a per-session flag on Anthropic) and retries once non-strict, remembering the decision so subsequent requests skip the 400 tax; it must not disable unrelated capabilities.

features.name: Unified tool choice with per-provider mapping and emulation
features.what: One `ToolChoice` type (`auto|none|any|required`, `{type:"function",name}`, nested `{type:"function",function:{name}}`, `{type:"tool",name}`, `{type:"computer"}`) mapped per wire: Completions strings + nested function object, Responses strings + flat function/custom/computer objects, Anthropic `{type: auto|none|any|tool}` (`required`→`any`), Google `toolConfig.functionCallingConfig.mode AUTO|NONE|ANY` with `allowedFunctionNames`, Bedrock `{auto|any|tool}`. `toolChoice` is one-shot per request with no stickiness. Guards: `supportsNamedToolChoice:false` emulates a pin by filtering `tools` to the target and sending `required`; `supportsForcedToolChoice:false` downgrades to `auto`; `supportsToolChoice:false` omits the field; a pin on a tool filtered out by active-tool selection or schema quarantine is silently deleted; `"none"` with no tools is dropped; `{type:"computer"}` without native support degrades to a named function pin.

features.name: Reasoning×tool-choice suppression policies
features.what: Two independent flags because backends differ: `disableReasoningOnForcedToolChoice` drops reasoning fields only when the choice is forced (Kimi, Anthropic-fronted endpoints), `disableReasoningOnToolChoice` drops them whenever any `tool_choice` is present (DeepSeek reasoning). Anthropic additionally deletes `params.thinking` on forced choice and pins adaptive-only models to `output_config.effort = "low"`; Bedrock clears `additionalModelRequestFields` on forced `any`/named choice. Named exceptions (e.g. Kimi K3 with forced `required`) must keep reasoning effort.
depends_on: Unified tool choice with per-provider mapping and emulation

features.name: Soft tool requirement escalation
features.what: Forcing `tool_choice` every turn churns the provider prompt cache, so a `SoftToolRequirement { soft: true, toolName, reminder }` first injects reminder text with `toolChoice` left at `auto`; only if the model fails to call `toolName` does the next turn escalate to a hard `{ type: "tool", name }` for exactly one turn. A queued forced choice whose tool leaves the active set is dropped before dispatch.
depends_on: Unified tool choice with per-provider mapping and emulation

features.name: Tool-call id normalization
features.what: Per-provider id rules enforced consistently across calls and results: Mistral exactly 9 alphanumeric chars (pad from a fixed alphabet or truncate), official OpenAI truncated to 40 chars, Responses composite `${callId}|${itemId}` split into a `call_`-prefixed callId (64 chars) and an `fc_`/`ctc_`-prefixed itemId with hash-derived synthesis when absent, Google synthesized (`name_timestamp_counter`) and stripped entirely for Vertex, and a deterministic SHA-256→UUID generator backing every place a provider omits or mangles ids.

features.name: Text-based tool-call dialects
features.what: In-band tool calling for models without native tool APIs: render the tool inventory into the prompt and scan streamed text back into structured calls, with dialects `harmony`, `gemini`, `qwen3`, `deepseek`, `kimi`, `glm`, `gemma`, `hermes`, `minimax`, `xml`, `anthropic`; also used for cross-model history replay, re-rendering prior thinking/tool turns into the target model's preferred dialect when the model changes mid-session. Harmony control tokens must be escaped when replayed through non-Harmony endpoints.

features.name: Stream markup healing
features.what: When `streamMarkupHealingPattern` (`kimi`, `dsml`, `thinking`) is configured, inspect visible text for leaked XML/markdown-wrapped tool calls and thinking markup, buffer across chunk boundaries (markers can split across chunks), reconstruct `toolcall_start/delta/end` events, promote `stop` finish reasons to `toolUse`, and suppress healed thinking when the provider already delivered native thinking so blocks are not double-counted. A separate wrapper converts in-band ```thinking / `<think>` fences into structured thinking blocks live.

features.name: Thinking loop guard
features.what: Monitor reasoning streams for Gemini/DeepSeek/Grok families before tool calls and kill runaways with a retryable error flagged `ThinkingLoop`: verbatim tail repetition (250-char window, ≥180 repeated chars), near-duplicate segments (trigram Jaccard ≥0.8 over the last 16 segments), progress-lexicon stalls (novelty ≤0.2 with no new concrete anchors over 8 consecutive segments), and excessive titled reasoning summaries without action (threshold 24 on Gemini).

features.name: Repeated tool-call loop guard
features.what: Canonicalize each tool call's arguments (sorted keys, `intent` stripped), hash `${name}:${canonicalArgs}`, and on repeated identical calls return a repeated-call detection used to steer the model out of the loop instead of re-executing the same side effect.

features.name: Empty-completion retry
features.what: Wrap provider streams so an attempt that finishes cleanly with `finish_reason: "stop"` but produces no visible assistant content (no text, thinking, image, or tool calls) and ≤1 output token is retried up to 2 times with exponential backoff from 500 ms; Google variants retry up to 2–3 times from a 1000 ms base after resetting accumulated stream output. Applied to OpenAI Responses/Completions, Anthropic, Google native/Vertex, Gemini CLI, and Ollama.

features.name: Reasoning-effort 400 fallback
features.what: Intercept 400/422 responses caused by an unsupported `reasoning_effort` value, parse the accepted levels from the error text (or resolve the nearest supported level, or drop the parameter), remember the fallback under a key derived from endpoint+model in provider session state, and transparently retry so the turn does not fail; applies to Chat Completions and Azure Responses independently.

features.name: Usage accounting and cost calculation
features.what: Reconcile provider usage into a canonical `Usage` (input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, reasoningTokens, cost, premiumRequests) and compute cost from model pricing, with provider-specific corrections: OpenRouter `prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` is subtracted from input and emitted as cache-write, plus authoritative reported `cost` rescales the estimated per-bucket costs; DeepSeek `prompt_cache_miss_tokens` is the billed input portion with cacheWrite forced to 0 (never double-counted); Google computes input as prompt minus cached and output as candidates plus thoughts; Copilot `premiumRequests` must survive usage population and replacement; Responses and Codex adjust cost by resolved service tier with different multipliers.

features.name: Gateway routing and wire model-id rewriting
features.what: Apply routing only when the baseUrl matches the gateway: OpenRouter `provider: { only, order }` plus variant suffixes (`:nitro`, `:floor`, `:online`, `:exacto`, `:extended`) appended only when the id has no explicit suffix after the last path segment, and Vercel AI Gateway `providerOptions.gateway.{only,order}` (never reusing OpenRouter's `provider` object). `wireModelIdMode` rewrites the dispatched model id per gateway (Fireworks `accounts/fireworks/models/<id>` with dots→`p`, Firepass `accounts/fireworks/routers/<id>`, OpenRouter, raw). OpenRouter must omit catalog-default max-token fields unless the caller set an explicit cap, since optional fields act as routing hints.

features.name: Provider-specific stream decode quirks
features.what: Decoder-level policies rather than business logic: MiniMax streams `function.arguments` as JSON objects that must be deep-merged across deltas and emitted as one concat-safe final string delta; MiniMax reasoning deltas are cumulative snapshots deduplicated by reasoning signature (`reasoningDeltasMayBeCumulative`); DeepSeek endpoints leak `<｜…｜>` chat-template markers that must be buffered and stripped across chunk boundaries (`stripDeepseekSpecialTokens`); Mistral `delta.content` can be an array/object of text parts; Ollama `finish_reason: length` with no visible content maps to a context-window error (`emptyLengthFinishIsContextError`); Chat Completions may break after `finish_reason` plus usage while Responses breaks only on `completed`/`incomplete`; Codex/Responses `end_turn:false` maps to `pause_turn`.
features.surface: provider stream decoders + compat stream flags

features.name: Image input handling and decoder hints
features.what: Convert image input and tool-result images to placeholders when the model/provider cannot accept them (including modes that are text-only despite a multimodal parent model); embed tool-result images inline where supported, buffer and flush as a trailing user turn where not (Gemini <3); clamp Responses image `detail: "original"` to `"auto"` on hosts that reject it; and honor `imageInputDecoder: stb` on a model or `modelOverrides` entry by converting attached and historical WebP images before provider dispatch.

features.name: Context promotion (model-level overflow fallback)
features.what: On a context-overflow error, before falling back to compaction: if enabled, resolve `currentModel.contextPromotionTarget` (accepting `provider/model-id` or bare `model-id` resolved within the current provider), verify credentials resolve for it, switch temporarily via `setModelTemporary` (recorded as a temporary `model_change`, saved role mapping untouched) and retry; no automatic sibling selection occurs, and if no target is available fall through to auto-compaction. Switching from/to the Codex Responses API closes that provider's session state first so websocket transport state is dropped.

features.name: Non-compaction retry engine
features.what: On `agent_end`, classify the last assistant error before ordinary compaction recovery: retry requires `stopReason === "error"`, not context overflow, and either a classifier refusal (`stopDetails.type` `refusal`/`sensitive`), a stale Responses replay failure, or a retryable normalized error classification (transient transport/envelope, overloaded, rate/usage limit, 429/500/502/503/504, service unavailable, provider retry wording, network/socket/timeout/fetch failures). Backoff is `min(baseDelayMs * 2^(attempt-1), 8000) * 75–100% jitter`; parsed `retry-after-ms`/`retry-after`/`x-ratelimit-reset-ms`/`x-ratelimit-reset` hints can extend it, credential/model switches set delay 0, stale-replay resets provider session state with delay 0, and a computed delay exceeding `retry.maxDelayMs` with no switch ends the chain immediately without sleeping.

features.name: Retry replay-safety gate
features.what: Retrying is only permitted before replay-unsafe output has been emitted: non-empty visible text, images, tool calls, and server-tool blocks block retry; thinking-only and whitespace-only partials are safe to discard. Empty generic aborts may enter the retry engine when no user/dispose/streaming-edit-guard abort is in progress, and an interrupted turn whose tool calls already have matching results is continued with the failed assistant/tool-result sequence preserved so completed side effects are never replayed (also used for resolved stream stalls and HTTP/2 resets `NGHTTP2_INTERNAL_ERROR`/`NGHTTP2_REFUSED_STREAM`/`HTTP2StreamReset`).

features.name: Retry credential rotation and model fallback
features.what: On usage limits apply a successful credential switch or banked reset credit immediately, otherwise wait for the earlier of the provider hint and the next temporarily blocked sibling credential; when allowed, consult configured fallback chains (a switch uses delay 0 and grants a fresh retry budget; classifier refusals only continue when a fallback applies), append a temporary `model_change`, and later restore the primary per `retry.fallbackRevertPolicy` (`cooldown-expiry` default, `never` disables). Usage-aware preflight runs before a request when `retry.modelFallback` and `retry.usageAwareFallback` are both on: unknown usage fails open, at `retry.usageReservePct` the `confirm` policy asks interactive sessions (auto-applying in non-interactive ones), `auto` applies silently, `fail-closed` rejects.

features.name: Retry lifecycle events and controls
features.what: Emit `auto_retry_start { attempt, maxAttempts, delayMs, errorMessage, errorId? }`, `auto_retry_end { success, attempt, finalError?, recoveredErrors? }`, `retry_fallback_applied { from, to, role }`, `retry_fallback_succeeded { model, role }` through session subscribe, extension events, and RPC stdout; expose `set_auto_retry` / `abort_retry` RPC commands with client helpers, `setAutoRetryEnabled`/`autoRetryEnabled`/`isRetrying` accessors, and a TUI retry loader (`Retrying (n/max) in Ns… (esc to cancel)`) whose Esc dispatches against live session state. `prompt()` does not resolve until any started retry chain finishes.

features.name: Provider in-flight concurrency limit
features.what: Wrap provider streams with a per-provider in-flight request limiter (bypassed only for transports that own their own concurrency, e.g. the GitLab Duo Agent websocket path) so parallel subagents cannot fan out unbounded concurrent provider requests.

features.name: Lazy provider registration and dispatch
features.what: Dispatch keys on `model.api` (not `model.provider`), so adding a provider that reuses an existing wire needs no dispatch change; heavy built-in transports are reached through lazy import wrappers registered at startup while thin routing wrappers stay eager, keeping heavy OAuth and transport modules out of the cold-start graph. Heavy provider-local OAuth flows must be reached through dynamic-import thunks from the definition file.

features.name: Extension provider registration
features.what: Extensions can register at runtime: additional or replacement models for a provider, a custom stream handler bound to a new API id (dispatched through the same path as built-ins, though a `transport: pi-native` model takes precedence), and a custom OAuth `ProviderDefinition` via `registerOAuthProvider` which flows through the same `AuthStorage.login` dispatcher, `/login` list, and broker provider enumeration as built-ins.

features.name: Secret obfuscation before provider dispatch
features.what: When `secrets.enabled` is true, collect secrets from env vars whose names match `KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|PASS|AUTH|CREDENTIAL|PRIVATE|OAUTH` with values ≥8 chars, then `~/.omp/agent/secrets.yml` and `<cwd>/.omp/secrets.yml` (project overrides global by matching `content`), then a built-in credential-token regex last; replace matches in provider-visible text with deterministic placeholders `$$HASH$$` / `$$HASH:hint$$` / `$$FRIENDLY_HASH:hint$$` whose 12-char base is an HMAC of the exact secret under a per-install key at `~/.omp/agent/secret-placeholder.key` (never sent to a model). Model-authored tool arguments are deep-walked and restored before execution; session context is restored for display/resume and re-obfuscated before provider replay; `replace` mode is one-way.

features.name: Local tiny-model inference path
features.what: Optional on-device models for session titles, memory extraction/consolidation, and auto-thinking difficulty classification, all defaulting to `online` so no downloads or on-device cost occur unless opted in; inference runs in a worker off the main thread with weights cached on disk and downloaded on first use, defaulting to CPU with `q4` quantization, configurable device (`providers.tinyModelDevice`, overridden per-run by `PI_TINY_DEVICE`) and dtype (`providers.tinyModelDtype`, overridden by `PI_TINY_DTYPE`), with unrecognized dtype failing loudly at worker startup and Darwin GPU/WebGPU/auto requests forced back to CPU in the production worker.

features.name: dialect-registry-and-selection
features.what: Resolves exactly one active tool wire format per session from `tools.format` ∈ {auto, native, glm, hermes, kimi, xml, anthropic, deepseek, harmony, qwen3, gemini, gemma, minimax} (default `auto`); `native` always uses provider-native tool calls; `auto` uses native unless the model has `supportsTools: false`, then picks the model-family owned dialect, falling back to `glm` when no family affinity matches (never `xml`); any other value force-selects that owned dialect. Applies at session start only. `PI_DIALECT=<name>` env is an equivalent selector, with legacy `PI_DIALECT=1`/`true` resolving to `glm`.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: owned-dialect-request-conversion
features.what: When an owned dialect is active, performs 4 steps per request in order: (1) delete the native structured `tools`/`tool_choice` fields from the provider payload, (2) append the compact `<tools>` catalog plus that dialect's format guide to the system prompt, (3) rewrite prior structured assistant tool calls and tool-result messages into the dialect's text protocol (results become a synthesized `user` message), (4) wrap the response stream so assistant text is scanned back into canonical tool-call events.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: inband-tool-catalog-injection
features.what: Emits a shared `# Tools` prompt section stating calls are text (not native tool messages), then `<tools>` … `</tools>` containing exactly one compact OpenAI-style function object per line — `{"type":"function","function":{"name","description","parameters"}}` using each tool's normalized wire schema — followed by the dialect-specific guide markdown.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: verbose-tool-inventory-renderer
features.what: Separate, verbose inventory used by the system prompt and `/dump`: one `## functions` block containing a TypeScript `namespace functions { … }`, with tool descriptions as `//` comments above `type NAME = (_: PARAMS);` declarations and configured examples as JSDoc-style `// @example` entries written in Python keyword-argument syntax. Emits no per-tool Markdown sections and no native call examples.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: inband-scanner-framework
features.what: Stateful, chunk-boundary-safe streaming scanner interface producing `InbandScanEvent`s: `text`, `thinkingStart`/`thinkingDelta`/`thinkingEnd`, `toolStart`, `toolArgDelta` (keyed by parameter name), `toolEnd` (complete coerced arguments + exact raw block for diagnostics), plus a `flush()` terminal pass. Constructed via `createInbandScanner(dialect, options)` with options `parseThinking` (default true on the owned path) and `xmlTagset`. Holds back trailing text that partially matches a marker so split markers never leak into visible text.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: owned-stream-projector
features.what: Projects scanner events onto the canonical assistant stream: materializes a canonical tool call at `toolStart` (before `toolEnd`), streams `toolArgDelta` text onto it, and on a normal provider `stop` promotes the turn to `toolUse` and may dispatch even calls that never received `toolEnd`. A provider `length` stop must remain non-runnable `length`. Unterminated calls retain uncoerced accumulated argument text, or `{}` when the scanner emitted no deltas.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: repairing-json-parser
features.what: Shared JSON parser with repair used at every scanner close for non-string argument bodies: trims surrounding whitespace, attempts repair-tolerant parse, and on failure retains the original raw text as a string rather than dropping the argument. Dialect-specific normalization on top: qwen3/kimi/deepseek/harmony normalize an invalid or non-object completed argument set to `{}`; glm uses strict `JSON.parse` after trim and falls back to the raw text.
features.surface: shared repairing JSON parser used by every dialect scanner close path
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: synthetic-call-id-minting
features.what: Mints an internal id (`ptc_…`) per parsed call for every wire format that carries none (xml, anthropic-xml, minimax, glm, qwen3/hermes, deepseek V3.1/legacy/DSML, harmony, gemini, gemma); Kimi is the exception — a pre-existing id beginning with `functions.` is preserved, otherwise `functions.{name}:{batchIndex}` is generated. Deterministic id derivation (`deterministicUuid(seed)` → UUID shape) backs `ensureToolCallId` wherever a provider omits or mangles wire ids.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: parameter-size-cap
features.what: Caps a single parameter/argument body at 1,000,000 JavaScript string code units; on overflow keeps the accepted prefix and appends an explicit truncation marker rather than throwing or silently dropping.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: fabricated-result-guard
features.what: Detects the model fabricating its own tool output: the first model-authored `<tool_response>` (xml) or `<function_results>`/`<tool_response>` (minimax) is a hard projection boundary — calls and text before it are preserved, projection stops there. With `tools.abortOnFabricatedResult: true` (default) provider generation is aborted immediately; when disabled the stream is drained but the fabricated continuation is discarded. GLM's scanner separately drops a hallucinated `<tool_response>` tag and the remainder of the current buffered chunk.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: cross-model-history-reencoding
features.what: On mid-session model switch, re-renders all prior thinking and tool-call/tool-result turns into the new model's `preferredDialect(modelId)` so replayed history is valid for the target family.
