features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: thinking-parse-and-render
features.what: Per-dialect in-band reasoning: parsing is enabled by default on the owned path and excludes reasoning from visible text. Tag sets — anthropic/xml/minimax: `<thinking>`, `<think>`, `<scratchpad>` (plus `antml:`-prefixed forms); qwen3/hermes/glm/kimi/deepseek: `<think>…</think>`; harmony: `analysis`-channel body; gemma: `<|channel>thought…<channel|>`; gemini: OMP-only sibling fenced ```` ```thinking ```` block. `parseThinking: false` leaves the markup as ordinary visible text. An unterminated thinking block is logically closed at flush with its content retained.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: demoted-thinking-rendering
features.what: Renders thinking blocks that the target provider cannot accept natively (missing/foreign signature, non-Claude Bedrock models) as plain text instead, marked via `isDemotedThinking`; tracks `lastCumulativeReasoningBySignature` so cumulative-reasoning providers (MiniMax-M3) do not re-emit reasoning as duplicate blocks after visible text has started.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: tool-result-rendering
features.what: Renders executed results into the active dialect and places them in one synthesized `user` message: xml → newline-separated `<tool_response>` blocks; minimax/anthropic → one `<function_results>` block with `<result><tool_name><stdout>` for success and `<error><tool_name><stderr>` for `isError`; glm → `<observation>` wrapping one `<tool_response>` per result (native transcript uses the `<|observation|>` role marker); qwen3/hermes → newline-delimited `<tool_response>`; kimi → consecutive `<|im_system|>{name}<|im_middle|>## Return of {id}…<|im_end|>` turns; deepseek → singular `<｜tool▁output▁begin｜>…<｜tool▁output▁end｜>` blocks newline-separated; harmony → canonical `<|start|>{toolname} to=assistant<|channel|>commentary<|message|>…<|end|>`; gemma → `<|tool_response>response:NAME{output:VALUE}<tool_response|>` with the text `JSON.parse`d first; gemini → one ```` ```tool_outputs ```` block per result. Result text is inserted verbatim; image blocks from a tool result are retained after the rendered text in the same message.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: transcript-renderer
features.what: Reconstructs a full model-native prompt for dialects that own a turn envelope: harmony (`<|start|>{header}<|message|>{content}<|end|>` with system/developer/user/assistant/tool roles), glm (`[gMASK]<sop>` + `<|system|>/<|user|>/<|assistant|>/<|observation|>`), kimi (`<|im_{class}|>{name}<|im_middle|>…<|im_end|>` with `tool_declare`), gemma (`<bos>` + `<|turn>{role}\n…<turn|>`), gemini (`<bos>` + Gemma-style `<start_of_turn>user|model`). Role folding rules: `developer` text is prepended to the next user turn (or becomes its own user turn if none follows) for gemini/gemma; consecutive tool results become one user turn holding their separate result blocks.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: stream-markup-healing
features.what: Activated when `policy.stream.markupHealingPattern` is configured for a provider/model: reuses the dialect scanners to reconstruct tool calls and thinking from markup a hosted model leaked into visible `content`, emits `toolcall_start`/`toolcall_delta`/`toolcall_end`, strips the markers from user-visible text, and promotes a `stop` finish reason to `toolUse`. Known patterns: DSML (`modelMayLeakDsmlToolCalls` → DeepSeek API, NanoGPT, NVIDIA, Ollama/Ollama Cloud, Fireworks, OpenRouter, OpenCode), `kimi` (truncated/split `<|tool_call*|>` markers across chunk boundaries), and inline `<thinking>` tags.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: harmony-leak-escape-and-detect
features.what: Two-sided defense against GPT-5/Codex emitting the bracket-less plain-text shadow of Harmony routing headers as tool-argument content. Outbound: escape reserved `<|...|>` spellings in untrusted text, tool results, and serialized tool arguments before replay to Harmony-dialect models. Inbound: enable detection for every model whose provider is `openai-codex`; a bare `to=functions.NAME` marker is NOT sufficient — require a co-signal (channel adjacency, glitch token, script mismatch, cascade, fake-result framing, or trusted trailing-parse boundary), and ignore fenced examples. On a hit the agent loop discards the partial response and retries up to 2 times, then escalates with an error; audit callbacks get action/signal metadata plus a hash and redacted preview. Tool-argument detection stays inert unless the caller supplies the byte offset where a structurally valid tool parse ended. Recovery (truncate at the contaminated line + append `*** Abort`) is supported only for bounded free-form `eval` input and the hashline `edit` DSL (input beginning with `@`).
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: anthropic-native-messages-protocol
features.what: Native Messages API tool calling: flat `tools[]` entries `{name (^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$), description, input_schema}` (no `{type:"function"}` wrapper, key is `input_schema` not `parameters`), assistant `tool_use` blocks `{id: toolu_…, name, input: <parsed object>}` with top-level `stop_reason: "tool_use"`, and `tool_result` blocks `{tool_use_id, content: string|block[], is_error?}` returned inside a `user` message. Streaming: `content_block_start` opens `tool_use` with `input:{}`, arguments arrive as `input_json_delta.partial_json` fragments buffered per block `index` and parsed at `content_block_stop`; final `stop_reason` lands in `message_delta` with cumulative `usage`. Handles `server_tool_use`/`web_search_tool_result` (never synthesize a result), `thinking`/`redacted_thinking` blocks with `signature`, and stop reasons `end_turn`, `max_tokens`, `stop_sequence`, `pause_turn`, `refusal`, `sensitive`, `model_context_window_exceeded`.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: anthropic-schema-whitelist-normalizer
features.what: Per-provider schema whitelist applied before placing a tool schema in `input_schema`. Keeps on every node: `$ref`, `$defs`, `$schema`, `definitions`, `type`, `enum`, `const`, `description`, `title`, `default`, `nullable`; keeps nested `anyOf`/`allOf` (root combinators not retained, `oneOf` never retained); on objects `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties`; on arrays `items`, `prefixItems`, and `minItems` only when 0 or 1; on strings `format` only for date-time|time|date|duration|email|hostname|uri|ipv4|ipv6|uuid. Every other constraint (`pattern`, length limits, numeric ranges, `maxItems`, unsupported formats/combinators) is appended to that node's `description` as model-visible guidance. Object nodes default to `additionalProperties: false`; an explicit `true` or schema value stays open (an empty schema normalizes to `true`).
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: anthropic-strict-tool-budgets
features.what: Sends `strict: true` only for eligible built-in tools (`bash`, `python`, `edit`, `find`) and only when: neither `PI_NO_STRICT` nor provider-compat/runtime fallback disabled strict tools, the tool has not opted out, the raw schema avoids `oneOf`/`allOf`/`$ref`/`patternProperties`/`propertyNames`, and every object is closed. Selection is capped at 20 strict tools per request, sharing budgets of 24 optional properties and 16 union uses; once the optional budget is exhausted another optional property must convert to required-and-nullable using union budget or the tool falls back to non-strict. Sends `eager_input_streaming: true` only when model compat data and the effective endpoint support it (first-party Anthropic endpoints, or custom endpoints explicitly configured for the capability; a canonical model rerouted to an unqualified non-Anthropic endpoint does not qualify).
features.surface: provider key `disableStrictTools`; compat `supportsStrictMode`/`toolStrictMode`; env `PI_NO_STRICT`; tool fields `strict`, `eager_input_streaming`
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: unified-schema-normalizer
features.what: One option-driven walker that upgrades any input to JSON Schema 2020-12, dereferences the tree, then per node: (1) renames snake_case combinator/property keys to camelCase (`any_of`→`anyOf`) with snake_case winning collisions, (2) applies the `handle_null_fields` nullable-union collapse before recursing, (3) strips unsupported keys and optionally spills human-meaningful ones (`pattern`, `format`, min/max, `default`, `examples`) into the sibling `description` — structural/meta keys (`$ref`, `$defs`, `additionalProperties`) are never spilled, (4) normalizes type unions (`["T","null"]` → `type:"T"` + nullable marker on Google, plain `type:"T"` on CCA), (5) collapses object-only/same-type combiners, optionally lossy-collapses mixed-type combiners (CCA only), then runs a residual-combiner fixpoint, (6) with `validateAndFallback` (CCA path) validates structurally and emits `{"type":"object","properties":{}}` per tool on residual incompatibility (`type` array, `type:"null"`, `nullable` key, or any remaining `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf`).
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: openai-strict-mode-pipeline
features.what: Two-pass sanitize→enforce composed by `adaptSchemaForStrict(schema, strict)`/`tryEnforceStrictSchema`. Sanitize strips non-structural keywords (`format`, `pattern`, min/max, `examples`, `default`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `not`, `unevaluated*`, `patternProperties`, `dependent*`, `content*`, `min/maxProperties`, `$dynamicRef`), inlining `default` into the sibling `description` as ` (default: X)` unless the description already contains `(default:` or is absent; inlines local `#/…` refs with SIBLING KEYS WINNING; collapses single-item `allOf` with the INLINED ENTRY winning; expands type-array branches into one variant per type with type-specific keyword pruning and the shared `description` HOISTED ONTO THE `anyOf` WRAPPER; infers primitive `type` from `enum`/`const`. Enforce sets `additionalProperties:false` on every object, moves every property into `required`, and wraps optional properties as `anyOf:[<original>,{type:"null"}]`, strictifying tuple `prefixItems` recursively. Both passes use cache/cycle epoch guards. Fail-open: any throw returns `{strict:false, schema: upgraded}`.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: provider-schema-dispatchers
features.what: Fixed transport→dispatcher mapping applied before tools hit the wire: `openai-completions`→`adaptSchemaForStrict`; `openai-responses`/`openai-codex-responses`→`sanitizeSchemaForOpenAIResponses` then strict adaptation; `azure-openai-responses`→`sanitizeSchemaForOpenAIResponses` and emits `strict:false` without adaptation; Moonshot/Kimi MFJS→`normalizeSchemaForMoonshot`; grammar-flavored OpenAI-compatible hosts→`sanitizeSchemaForGrammar` (widens boolean subschemas while preserving boolean `additionalProperties`/`unevaluatedProperties`); `ollama`→`sanitizeSchemaForOllama` (rewrites boolean subschemas, type arrays, boolean object-openness keywords); `google-generative-ai`/`google-vertex`/Gemini CLI→`normalizeSchemaForGoogle`; Cloud Code Assist Claude→`normalizeSchemaForCCA` (full pipeline, not just keyword stripping); MCP `inputSchema` ingestion→`normalizeSchemaForMCP`; native `anthropic-messages`→the per-provider whitelist. `sanitizeSchemaForOpenAIResponses` additionally rewrites `oneOf`→`anyOf`, adds empty `properties` to object schemas, and removes regex lookarounds.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: tool-choice-unified-mapping
features.what: One canonical `ToolChoice` type — `"auto" | "none" | "any" | "required" | {type:"function", name} | {type:"function", function:{name}} | {type:"tool", name} | {type:"computer"}` — mapped per provider: Anthropic `{type:auto|any|tool|none}` (+ `disable_parallel_tool_use`), OpenAI `tool_choice:"required"`/named function (+ top-level `parallel_tool_calls:false`), Ollama emulated by filtering `context.tools` down to the named tool and mapping none→none, required/any/named→required, auto→undefined. `toolChoice` is one-shot per request with no stickiness — the caller decides each turn.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: tool-call-loop-guard
features.what: Canonicalizes tool arguments (sorted keys, `intent` field stripped), hashes `${name}:${canonicalArgs}`, and on repeated identical calls returns a `RepeatedToolCallDetection` used to steer the model out of the loop.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: dialect-anthropic-xml
features.what: Prompt-driven Anthropic XML dialect. Renderer: always the unprefixed attribute form, all calls of a batch wrapped in one `<function_calls>` block, each argument a `<parameter name="…">` child; schema-declared string arguments inserted as literal text, all other values JSON-serialized. Results render as `<function_results>` with `<result><tool_name><stdout>` / `<error><tool_name><stderr>` (tool name in both; `isError` encoded nowhere else; correlation by call order). Scanner additionally accepts `antml:`-prefixed tags, `<tool_calls>` as a wrapper alias, and a bare `<invoke>` outside any wrapper; emits `toolArgDelta` while each parameter body arrives and publishes coerced arguments at `</invoke>`.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: dialect-xml-generic
features.what: Generic XML dialect: renderer emits bare consecutive `<invoke name="TOOL"><parameter name="ARG">VALUE</parameter></invoke>` separated by newlines with NO outer wrapper; results are one `<tool_response>` block per result, newline-separated, in a single synthesized user message with no success/error marker. Scanner (default `xmlTagset: anthropic`) also accepts `<tool_calls>`/`<function_calls>` wrappers and `antml:` variants; non-call text inside a recognized wrapper is discarded, text outside wrappers stays visible. Per-parameter `string` attribute override: `string="true"` (or any value except `false`/`0`/`no`) forces raw string; `string="false"|"0"|"no"` forces JSON parsing even for a schema-declared string. `xmlTagset: "dsml"` swaps in the DeepSeek DSML scanner (scanner-only; renderer unaffected), where parameters default to strings and only `string="false"` requests JSON coercion.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: dialect-minimax
features.what: MiniMax dialect: one `<minimax:tool_call>` envelope per assistant batch containing sibling `<invoke name="TOOL">` elements with `<parameter name="ARG">` children. Renderer XML-escapes tool/argument names in attributes but never escapes parameter bodies. Results batch into one `<function_results>` block with `<result>/<stdout>` for success and `<error>/<stderr>` for `isError`, `<tool_name>` XML-text-escaped, correlated by call order. Scanner also accepts an unprefixed `<tool_call>` wrapper or a bare `<invoke>`; supports the same `string="true|false|0|no"` coercion override.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: dialect-glm
features.what:
GLM-4.5/4.6 dialect: renderer emits the newline layout `<tool_call>NAME
<arg_key>k</arg_key>
<arg_value>v</arg_value>…
</tool_call>`, parallel calls newline-separated, with schema-driven value typing (string-only properties raw/unquoted, every other value JSON-serialized). Scanner accepts newline, `<arg_key>`, OR `</tool_call>` as the name delimiter (so both GLM-4.5 and the newline-less GLM-4.7/5 layouts parse), emits `toolStart` at the name delimiter, streams each argument body as keyed `toolArgDelta`, and heals three narrowly recognizable model mistakes: `</arg_key>` used in place of `</arg_value>`, a stray wrong closer before the real closer, and a missing value closer immediately before the next argument or the call close. Owned history renders results as `<observation>` with one `<tool_response>` per result; the native transcript uses `<|observation|>`.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: dialect-qwen3-hermes
features.what: Hermes/ChatML convention: each call is `<tool_call>\n{"name":…,"arguments":{…}}\n</tool_call>`, parallel calls newline-separated, `arguments` ALWAYS a nested object in the renderer. Scanner emits `toolStart` as soon as the leading JSON contains a complete string `name`, emits NO argument deltas, and waits for `</tool_call>` to emit `toolEnd` using the repairing parser; for compatibility it also accepts a stringified `arguments` value and parses it once more. A completed parse failure or non-object arguments normalizes to `{}`; a completed outer object whose name cannot be recovered is consumed without creating a call. Results become newline-delimited `<tool_response>` blocks in a synthetic user message. `hermes` is a separately selectable dialect emitting the same basic convention.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: dialect-kimi
features.what: Kimi K2 dialect: one `<|tool_calls_section_begin|>…<|tool_calls_section_end|>` section per assistant batch, each call `<|tool_call_begin|>functions.{name}:{idx}<|tool_call_argument_begin|>{json}<|tool_call_end|>` with `{idx}` a per-turn 0-based counter. Scanner recognizes calls ONLY inside a section, preserves the raw header verbatim as the call id, derives the name from the last dot-separated segment before the first colon, emits `toolStart` at the argument marker, buffers the body until `<|tool_call_end|>` with no argument deltas, then repairs/parses (invalid or non-object → `{}`). Section markers are suppressed from visible text; an isolated call marker outside a section stays ordinary text. Results render as consecutive `<|im_system|>{name}<|im_middle|>## Return of {id}\n{content}<|im_end|>` turns collapsed into one synthetic user message.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: dialect-deepseek
features.what: DeepSeek dialect accepting three grammars in one scanner: (a) V3.1 `<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜><｜tool▁call▁begin｜>{name}<｜tool▁sep｜>{json}<｜tool▁call▁end｜>…<｜tool▁calls▁end｜>`, (b) legacy V3-0324/R1-0528 `function<｜tool▁sep｜>{name}\n```json…```
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: dialect-harmony
features.what: OpenAI Harmony dialect over `<|start|>{header}<|message|>{content}<|end|>` envelopes with mandatory assistant channels (`analysis`/`commentary`/`final`) and stop tokens `<|return|>`/`<|call|>`. OMP renderer emits recipient in the CHANNEL section with no `<|constrain|>` marker and compact JSON arguments: `<|start|>assistant<|channel|>commentary to=functions.NAME<|message|>{json}<|call|>`. Scanner accepts the recipient in EITHER header section, strips a leading `functions.` from the exposed name, and treats any non-empty recipient other than `assistant` as a tool call (including built-ins like `browser.search`); accumulates arguments until `<|call|>`, `<|end|>`, or `<|return|>` and repairs (empty/unrepairable → `{}`); emits `toolStart` at header completion and `toolEnd` only at the terminator, with NO argument deltas. `analysis` bodies stream as thinking deltas; `commentary`/`final` bodies stream as text; non-assistant envelopes are skipped by the output scanner. Transcript renders assistant turns in order: complete `analysis` message, complete `final` message, then one `commentary` call message per tool call. Results render as `<|start|>{toolname} to=assistant<|channel|>commentary<|message|>{text}<|end|>` with `result.text` passed through verbatim and no error bit.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: dialect-gemini-pythonic
features.what: Gemini/Gemma-3 Pythonic dialect using fenced ```` ```tool_code ```` blocks (closed by a bare fence) whose body is a Python call expression. Renderer emits `default_api.NAME(kwargs)` WITHOUT `print`, and for two or more calls a Python LIST of call expressions. Scanner normalizes away `print(...)`, any `module.` prefix, and an `LHS =` assignment; extracts top-level call expressions in source order from either the list form or one-statement-per-line form; decodes Python literals (single/double quotes, `True`/`False`/`None`, lists, dicts) including raw/byte/unicode prefixes, triple quotes, octal escapes, and `\x`/`\u`/`\U`; skips string contents so `(` inside a literal is not a call opener; skips positional args and malformed keyword segments. It buffers the ENTIRE `tool_code` body and emits events only after the closing fence — no partial-argument streaming — and DISCARDS an unterminated block on flush rather than exposing it as text. Results are ```` ```tool_outputs ```` blocks, one per result in call order, with no `isError` encoding.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: dialect-gemma4
features.what: Gemma 4 token-delimited dialect: one call per `<|tool_call>call:NAME{k:v,…}<tool_call|>` block, results as `<|tool_response>response:NAME{output:VALUE}<tool_response|>` with the result text `JSON.parse`d first (JSON becomes a nested brace structure, plain strings are wrapped in `<|"|>…<|"|>`). Scanner is a state machine, not a flat regex: it (1) finds the matching `<tool_call|>` while skipping `<|"|>…<|"|>` string spans so a closer inside a string does not end the block early, (2) matches the `call:NAME{` head and takes the brace body to its depth-matched `}`, (3) splits into `key:value` pairs at top-level commas honoring `[]`/`{}` depth and string spans, decoding strings via `<|"|>` delimiters and bare scalars as `true`/`false`→bool, `null`/`none`→null, numeric→number, else bare string. Events are emitted only after the complete close marker (adjacent `toolStart`/`toolEnd`, no partial args); an unterminated block is dropped at flush, while a syntactically closed block missing its final argument brace is still parsed from the available body. Thinking round-trips through `<|channel>thought\n…<channel|>`.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: pi-native-transport
features.what: Lossless canonical transport to an `omp auth-gateway`, opted into with `transport: pi-native` + required `baseUrl` in models.yml (missing `baseUrl` fails with a specific error naming the model id). Bypasses per-API provider implementations: strips trailing slashes and POSTs `{modelId: "${provider}/${id}", context:{systemPrompt,messages,tools}, options, stream:true}` to `/v1/pi/stream` with `Accept: text/event-stream`, bearer = resolved model/API key in `Authorization` (never in JSON options; explicit `model.headers.Authorization` wins). Canonical `ToolCall` blocks cross the wire unchanged — no textual dialect, no tool conversion, no partial-content reconstruction. Server allow-lists a fixed `SimpleStreamOptions` subset and silently drops unknown/null/undefined values; the client strips runtime-owned fields (`signal`, `apiKey`, `fetch`, `onPayload`, `onResponse`, `onSseEvent`, `execHandlers`, `cursorExecHandlers`, `cursorOnToolResult`, `providerSessionState`). SSE frames each `AssistantMessageEvent` verbatim, ends after a canonical `done`/`error`, then writes `[DONE]`. Errors use `{"error":{"type","message"}}` converted to `AuthGatewayError` preserving status/headers/type; a bearer failure returns `{"error":"unauthorized"}` instead and falls back to `auth-gateway STATUS: BODY_OR_STATUS_TEXT`. `transport` changes dispatch ONLY — pricing, context window, max tokens, and thinking metadata still resolve locally from the model catalog.
features.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing

features.name: component-protocol
features.what: Every UI unit implements `render(width): readonly string[]` returning width-safe lines, plus optional `handleInput(data)`, `wantsKeyRelease`, `invalidate()`, `setIgnoreTight(ignore)`, `dispose()`; an unchanged component MUST return the *same array reference* as last frame and a *new* array whenever content changes (reference equality drives container memoization); a component that mutates a previously returned array in place MUST also implement `RenderStablePrefix` and report surviving leading row count.

features.name: focus-and-cursor-marker
features.what: `Focusable { focused: boolean; setUseTerminalCursor?(b) }` is separate from `Component`; `TUI.setFocus(c)` routes input and toggles `focused`; focused components embed `CURSOR_MARKER` inside their rendered text and the engine extracts/strips it and positions the hardware cursor there — there is no `getCursorPosition()` API. Cursor is parked at real content bottom (not padded window bottom) and clamped before movement.

features.name: append-only-scrollback-ledger
features.what: Transcript lives on the NORMAL screen (native scrollback/selection/persistence). Engine keeps `committedRows` C (rows `[0,C)` are in terminal history and are never rewritten by ordinary emitters), `windowTopRow` W (frame row mapped to grid row 0; visible window = `[W, W+height)`), and live-region boundary B. For an ordinary unpinned frame `W = max(C, L - height)` and new commit end = `max(C, W)` clamped to frame; only the chunk between old and new commit index is emitted into history. The renderer NEVER probes terminal scroll position on any platform (win32 == POSIX).

features.name: committed-prefix-resync-audit
features.what: Per frame (skipped on geometry frames) audit the committed exact prefix via `findCommittedPrefixResync`: sample up to 8 non-blank rows within the last 24 committed rows with SGR stripped; a single in-place mismatch is accepted as stale history, a structural shift re-anchors commits at the first changed row (duplication in history is preferred over content loss). An in-place width change does not audit or re-slice the prior epoch's physical coordinates.

features.name: frame-emitter-classifier
features.what: Each frame is classified and routed to exactly one of four byte shapes: (1) `#emitFullPaint` = home + committed chunk + window rows (+optional ED3) for initial paint / explicit geometry-session-reset gestures / rebuild; (2) scroll-append = new bottom rows + changed-row range, used only when rows leaving the screen are exactly the commit chunk; (3) in-window diff = relative cursor move + changed-row rewrite when nothing scrolls or commits; (4) seam rewrite = commit chunk + full window rewrite on commit/window re-anchor or hidden-gap backfill. The ordinary update path NEVER emits ED2/ED3 or an absolute cursor home (several terminal families snap scrolled readers to bottom on those).

features.name: ed3-clear-scrollback-gesture
features.what: `CSI 3 J` is emitted from exactly ONE callsite, `#emitFullPaint({ clearScrollback: true })`. Legitimate callers are explicit user gestures: session replace/branch/resume (`requestRender(true, { clearScrollback: true })`), resize outside a multiplexer, and `resetDisplay()` (default chord `Alt+L` / `app.display.reset`). ED3 is emitted WITHOUT a preceding ED2 and the replay overwrites every row from home so terminals lacking synchronized output never expose a blank viewport. Multiplexers never receive ED3.

features.name: scrollback-divergence-rebuild
features.what: Opt-in repair for committed-prefix divergence: when the committed prefix structurally resynchronizes or the frame collapses into already-committed rows, a DIRECT (non-multiplexer) session clears scrollback with ED3 and replays the current frame so stale preview and final form do not both persist. Disabled by default; guarded off on the first paint, on explicit replacement/geometry frames, and inside multiplexers (which keep the append/repair-below fallback). `PI_TUI_SCROLLBACK_REBUILD=1` only initializes the low-level `TUI` flag; `InteractiveMode` then applies the `tui.scrollbackRebuild` setting (default `false`), which is the effective control.

features.name: live-region-seam-contract
features.what: `NativeScrollbackLiveRegion.getNativeScrollbackLiveRegionStart()` returns the first local row that may still mutate; rows before it are declared byte-stable at the current width and are eligible for exactness auditing. `isNativeScrollbackLiveRegionPinned()` keeps the mutable suffix viewport-local (clipped, never snapshotted) instead of committing frozen snapshots as it scrolls off — for replacing dashboards, not append-shaped transcript. Reporting no seam yields shell semantics (whatever scrolls off is final). When multiple root children report a seam the TOPMOST wins, because commits are prefix-only. Companion interfaces: `NativeScrollbackCommittedRows` (container passes committed count to children) and `NativeScrollbackReplay` (component releases layout locks before a destructive replay).

features.name: width-epoch-cross-resize-contract
features.what: `NativeScrollbackWidthEpoch` is the cross-width source contract: capture reads only the state that produced the last EMITTED frame (Markdown snapshots its last rendered source text so a streaming update arriving before SIGWINCH cannot masquerade as already-emitted output); resolve projects that logical source boundary into the newly rendered width; the current-boundary method identifies the logical suffix queued during settlement. Containers propagate the marker through nested sources. Inside multiplexers a width change terminates the physical-row coordinate epoch: old committed physical coordinates become opaque, host-reflowed history stays immutable, old/new row counts are never compared, no old viewport row is recommitted, and only the slice from resolved-old-boundary to current-source-boundary is emitted at the terminal-owned viewport bottom before an in-place viewport repaint. Components without the contract fall back to the conservative physical-row path.

features.name: render-stable-prefix-memoization
features.what: `RenderStablePrefix` lets assembly report how many leading rows are byte-identical (unchanged component array references at unchanged offsets), so the engine skips diff work over that prefix. Required for any component that mutates a previously returned array in place.

features.name: transcript-container-seam
features.what: The application-side seam implementation: scan for the first UNFINALIZED transcript block; finalized blocks before it are exact; the live block may extend the exact boundary via `getTranscriptBlockSettledRows()`. Assistant messages derive settled rows from completed content blocks plus markdown's frozen-token prefix; constructs that can re-layout asynchronously (e.g. Mermaid) defer settling. Pinning is propagated from the first live block; tool execution uses pinning for replacing preview/dashboard states. Freezing/settling is a correctness contract, not a terminal optimization.

features.name: overlay-system
features.what: `TUI.showOverlay(...)` returns an `OverlayHandle`; overlays are composited ONLY into the screen-coordinate window slice (never into the commit chunk) and while any overlay is visible commits are frozen — overlay exit backfills the exact hidden slice. `OverlayOptions.visible` may depend on terminal dimensions, so overlay visibility is re-evaluated on resize and focus is reassigned (next visible overlay, else saved pre-overlay focus) when the focused overlay becomes hidden. Extension `custom(..., { overlay: true })` mounts bottom-center at full terminal width and max height.

features.name: render-scheduler
features.what: `requestRender()` coalesces repeated requests into one pending frame; ordinary frames run at a 30fps base cadence with adaptive backpressure derived from the previous frame's cost. `requestRender(true, ...)` forces an immediate full-window rewrite (and `{clearScrollback:true}` selects the destructive replay). `requestComponentRender(component)` scopes composition to affected root subtrees when geometry/renderer state is safe, otherwise downgrades to full compose. `requestDirectWrite(component)` immediately rewrites one quiet, visible, fixed-height segment (loader animation); overlays, images, cursor markers, geometry changes, committed segments or any unsafe state fall back to `requestComponentRender`.

features.name: width-model-primitives
features.what: One shared UAX#11 width model for measuring, slicing, truncating and wrapping: `visibleWidth()`, `truncateToWidth()`, `sliceByColumn()`, `wrapTextWithAnsi()`, `replaceTabs()`. Slicing/truncation/wrapping run on the native Rust `unicode-width` engine while `visibleWidth` measures via `Bun.stringWidth` pinned to the SAME options (`countAnsiEscapeCodes: false`, `ambiguousIsNarrow: true`). Fast path: printable ASCII = 1 cell per code unit; beyond the ASCII prefix CSI/OSC strip to zero; tabs re-added at fixed `DEFAULT_TAB_WIDTH`; OSC 66 sized spans re-added as `scale × (explicit w ?? payload width)`. The hot path CLAMPS over-wide lines and never throws.

features.name: terminal-capability-profile
features.what: `TERMINAL` is resolved once at import from `TERMINAL_ID` + environment sniffing; all detection helpers are pure over `(env, platform)` and unit-testable. `shouldEnableSynchronizedOutputByDefault(env,id)` precedence: user opt-out (`PI_NO_SYNC_OUTPUT`/`PI_TUI_SYNC_OUTPUT=0`) → user force-on (`PI_FORCE_SYNC_OUTPUT=1`/`PI_TUI_SYNC_OUTPUT=1`) → `TERM_FEATURES` advertising `Sy` → `WT_SESSION` → known direct terminals → off for risky multiplexers/unknowns, reconciled at runtime by the DECRQM mode-2026 report (user override still wins). `detectRectangularSgrSupport` = kitty only, off in multiplexers and under `PI_NO_DECCARA`. `supportsScreenToScrollback` = kitty ED22, used exactly once on the initial paint to preserve the pre-existing shell screen. Env sniffing selects OPTIMIZATIONS ONLY; there is no terminal-brand risk classifier.

features.name: synchronized-output-bracketing
features.what: Render writes are wrapped in DEC 2026 BSU/ESU (`CSI ? 2026 h/l`) when enabled; cursor writes MUST occur inside the synchronized frame before ESU, never as a second frame after it. Autowrap discipline remains enabled even when sync-output wrappers are disabled.

features.name: deccara-rect-fill
features.what: Kitty-only DECCARA rectangular-SGR background fill optimizer replaces padded-string background rendering; disabled inside multiplexers and by `PI_NO_DECCARA` (forces padded-string rendering).

features.name: capability-probe-sentinels
features.what: `ProcessTerminal` fuses every capability query with a bare DA1 (`CSI c`) sentinel so a non-answering terminal is detected when DA1 returns first. `#da1SentinelOwners` is a TYPED FIFO discriminated by `kind` so a keyboard DA1 cannot be mistaken for an OSC 11 / DECRQM / graphics probe. `#privateCsiResponseBuffer` accumulates `\x1b[?…` partials while a sentinel is outstanding, rejoins on the terminator byte and runs handlers only on the COMPLETE reply; a new `\x1b` mid-reassembly or >256 buffered bytes abandons the partial so real keys still reach input. DECRQM probes for modes 2026/2048/2031 drive runtime feature gating.

features.name: stdin-escape-reassembly
features.what: `StdinBuffer` buffers fragmented CSI/OSC/DCS/APC/SS3 sequences and emits a `data` event only when a sequence is complete or a flush timeout expires, preventing partial escape chunks from being decoded as ordinary keypresses. It detects bracketed paste and emits a separate `paste` event carrying the raw pasted text.

features.name: kitty-keyboard-protocol
features.what: On start, query Kitty keyboard protocol support with `CSI ? u` and enable protocol flags if supported; otherwise enable the modifyOtherKeys fallback after a short timeout. Key RELEASE events are filtered out before component dispatch unless the focused component sets `wantsKeyRelease = true`, which then also exposes `isKeyRelease()` / `isKeyRepeat()`. On shutdown, drain in-flight Kitty input for up to one second so release sequences do not leak into the parent shell.

features.name: inline-image-pipeline
features.what: Kitty images are transmit-once / place-many: base64 payloads are NEVER re-emitted per frame. `ImageBudget` keeps only the most-recent N images live (`tui.maxInlineImages`); exceeding the cap deletes the demoted image's pixels by id (`a=d,d=I`) and re-renders its visible rows as text fallback through the ORDINARY window diff (no destructive replay). The text fallback is height-preserving once a graphic has rendered (reserved rows + fallback line) so demotion never shrinks the block or shifts committed content below it; a demoted placement already committed simply loses its pixels. Kitty Unicode placeholders default on only for kitty/ghostty. Protocol detection is overridable.

features.name: terminal-lifecycle
features.what: `ProcessTerminal.start()` in fixed order: (1) raw mode + bracketed paste, (2) resize handler + dimension refresh, (3) Windows VT input mode on win32, (4) create `StdinBuffer`, (5) Kitty keyboard query then flags-or-modifyOtherKeys fallback, (6) OSC 11 background-color + mode 2031 appearance-notification queries for dark/light detection, (7) OSC 99 notification capability query, (8) periodic OSC 11 polling only where safe, then DECRQM probes for 2026/2048/2031. `stop()` restores real stderr and terminal modes, disables keyboard/mouse/appearance protocols, clears probes and timers, destroys `StdinBuffer`, removes stdin/stdout listeners, pauses stdin, and restores the previous raw-mode state. A dead/disconnected terminal stops interactive rendering and suppresses raw-mode restoration errors for that case only.

features.name: resize-policy
features.what: Resize is event-driven from `ProcessTerminal` into `requestRender()`, with a settle debounce. Width changes force repaint/rebuild planning because wrapping semantics change. Non-multiplexer fast path borrows the ALTERNATE screen for drag frames; `resizeRepaintsInPlace()` routes ED3-unsafe multiplexers (tmux/screen/Zellij/cmux, incl. nested inside HerdR), direct HerdR panes, and terminals that re-report size on alt-screen toggles (Warp reports a height one row different for the alt buffer) through an in-place repaint that never touches the alt buffer — otherwise alt enter/leave self-triggers a resize loop that floods ED3 repaints at stable geometry. Height-only resizes retain the existing ledger and repaint in place; during a height shrink only OCCUPIED old-frame rows actually moved into history by the host are excluded from the append-owned seam (empty viewport rows do not consume content-driven movement).

features.name: tui-env-escape-hatches
features.what: Documented environment overrides a clone must honor: `PI_NO_SYNC_OUTPUT`, `PI_TUI_SYNC_OUTPUT=0|1`, `PI_FORCE_SYNC_OUTPUT=1`, `PI_NO_DECCARA`, `PI_FORCE_IMAGE_PROTOCOL`, `PI_KITTY_PLACEHOLDERS`/`PI_NO_KITTY_PLACEHOLDERS` (the NO- form wins), `PI_HARDWARE_CURSOR=1`, `PI_NOTIFICATIONS=off|0|false`, `PI_DEBUG_REDRAW=1` (logs chosen render intent + ledger state per frame), `PI_TUI_WRITE_LOG` (logs TUI writes to file), `PI_TUI_RESIZE_IN_PLACE`, `PI_TUI_SCROLLBACK_REBUILD`, `PI_TUI_RAW_BACKSPACE_IS_CTRL=1` (raw `0x08` means Ctrl+Backspace, for SSH/container hops hiding a Windows Terminal client). Removed and NOT to be reintroduced: `PI_TUI_ED3_SAFE`, `PI_CLEAR_ON_SHRINK`, `PI_TUI_DEBUG`.

features.name: render-fidelity-stress-harness
features.what: A test harness drives the renderer's REAL emitted ANSI into a ghostty-web `VirtualTerminal` across randomized op sequences and parameterized terminal shapes, validating against an independent shadow commit ledger fed only by observed frames (`render` wrap) and observed bytes (`write` wrap). Per op it asserts: whole tape (scrollback+grid) == `shadowTape + window slice` row-for-row including across resizes; scrolled readers stay pinned and visible history rows are never rewritten; multiplexer pane history grows by exactly the committed chunk; sync-output/autowrap bracket discipline, cursor parking, background columns, duplicate accounting. Combining-mark drift is tolerated via `sameLinesAllowingMarkDrift`.

features.name: key-matching-primitives
features.what: `matchesKey(data, "...")` matches a raw input chunk against a chord string for navigation keys and combos; chord notation is the same one shown in the UI (`Ctrl+P`, `Alt+Shift+P`, `Shift+Enter`, `Ctrl+Backspace`) and is case-insensitive.

features.name: keybindings-manager
features.what: `KeybindingsManager.matches(data, actionId)` maps input to semantic action IDs so components match actions, not hardcoded keys. User remaps live in `~/.omp/agent/keybindings.yml` — a flat YAML mapping of action ID → one chord string or array of chord strings (NOT inside `config.yml`, no nested `keybindings` object). An empty array disables an action. With a named profile, the default profile's agent-dir bindings load first and the active profile's file overrides action-by-action (the inherited file is read-only during startup). `keybindings.json` and `keybindings.yaml` are accepted and migrated; older unqualified action names are migrated to namespaced IDs on load. Extension UI factories receive an in-memory manager carrying DEFAULT bindings, not the user's file.

features.name: default-action-map
features.what: Ships this default action table, discoverable at runtime via `/hotkeys` (which reflects disk remaps and extension-added bindings): `app.model.cycleForward` Ctrl+P; `app.model.cycleBackward` Shift+Ctrl+P; `app.model.selectTemporary` Alt+P; `app.model.select` Alt+M; `app.plan.toggle` Alt+Shift+P; `app.history.search` Ctrl+R; `app.tools.expand` Ctrl+O; `app.tools.toggleVisibility` Ctrl+Shift+O; `app.thinking.toggle` Ctrl+T; `app.thinking.cycle` Shift+Tab; `app.editor.external` Ctrl+G; `app.message.followUp` Ctrl+Q + Ctrl+Enter; `app.message.dequeue` Alt+Up + Shift+Up; `app.retry` Alt+R; `app.display.reset` Alt+L; `app.clipboard.copyLine` Alt+Shift+L; `app.clipboard.copyPrompt` Alt+Shift+C; `app.clipboard.pasteTextRaw` Ctrl+Shift+V + Alt+Shift+V; `app.clipboard.pasteImage` (Linux Ctrl+V; macOS Ctrl+V/Cmd+V; Windows Ctrl+V/Alt+V); `app.stt.toggle` unbound (hold Space = push-to-talk); `app.live.toggle` Ctrl+L; `app.agents.hub` Alt+A; `app.session.observe` Ctrl+S; `app.session.tree`; `app.interrupt`.

features.name: input-dispatch-pipeline
features.what: Fixed routing order `stdin → ProcessTerminal → StdinBuffer → TUI.#handleInput → focusedComponent.handleInput`: (1) run registered `addInputListener` handlers first, allowing consume/transform; (2) handle the global debug shortcut (`Shift+Ctrl+D`) before component dispatch; (3) if the focused component belongs to an overlay now hidden/invisible, reassign focus to the next visible overlay or the saved pre-overlay focus; (4) filter key-release events unless `wantsKeyRelease`; (5) dispatch to the focused component; (6) schedule a render.

features.name: custom-editor-key-interception
features.what: `CustomEditor` intercepts high-priority combos FIRST (escape, Ctrl+C/D/Z, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+P variants, Ctrl+T, Alt+Up, extension-registered custom keys) and delegates everything else to the base `Editor` (text editing, history, autocomplete, cursor movement); `InputController.setupKeyHandlers()` then binds editor callbacks to mode semantics. Key parsing and editor mechanics stay in the TUI package; mode semantics stay in coding-agent controllers.

features.name: editor-autocomplete
features.what: Debounced autocomplete inside `Editor` (debounce timers reduce recompute churn while typing). Interactive mode installs exactly ONE provider — `createPromptActionAutocompleteProvider`, a `PromptActionAutocompleteProvider` wrapping a `CombinedAutocompleteProvider` — containing built-in commands (with argument completion and inline hints for selected commands), extension commands, TypeScript custom commands, optional `/skill:<name>` commands, discovered file commands, and prompt-template commands whose names are not already taken.

features.name: editor-border-modes
features.what: Leading editor text toggles border mode: `!` → bash mode, `$` (when not a template-literal prefix) → python mode, each with its own border color token (`bashMode`, `pythonMode`). The border also encodes the current thinking level (`thinkingOff|Minimal|Low|Medium|High|Xhigh|Max`) and, when `statusLine.sessionAccent` is true, is tinted with the session color. Escape on an INACTIVE mode clears editor text and restores border color; while execution is active Escape aborts the running task instead.

features.name: draft-persistence
features.what: Editor text is snapshotted and restored around lifecycle transitions: the shutdown path snapshots the draft before disposal and attempts to save it (a save failure is logged but never skips disposal), and non-overlay custom-UI mounts save editor text before replacing the editor component and restore it on `done(...)`.

features.name: external-editor
features.what: `app.editor.external` (default `Ctrl+G`) opens the current draft in `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR` and returns the edited buffer to the prompt.

features.name: clipboard-and-paste
features.what: Four clipboard actions: copy current line (`Alt+Shift+L`), copy whole prompt (`Alt+Shift+C`), paste text RAW without collapsing (`Ctrl+Shift+V`/`Alt+Shift+V`), and paste image-preferred-with-text-fallback (`Ctrl+V`, plus `Cmd+V` on macOS / `Alt+V` on Windows). Terminals implementing OSC 5522 enhanced paste deliver clipboard MIME data directly: image pastes attach as `[Image #N]` while `text/plain` events keep normal paste behavior. Without OSC 5522, bracketed paste handles text and a pasted single image-file path is loaded as an image when readable from the host.

features.name: prompt-history-search
features.what: `app.history.search` (default `Ctrl+R`) opens interactive search over prompt history; the base `Editor` also provides plain history navigation.

features.name: message-queue-and-dequeue
features.what: `app.message.followUp` (`Ctrl+Q`, `Ctrl+Enter`) queues a follow-up message; `app.message.dequeue` (`Alt+Up`, `Shift+Up`) pulls a queued message back into the editor. Queued messages are rendered in a dedicated `pendingMessagesContainer`, and Escape during an active stream restores queued messages to the editor before aborting the agent.

features.name: interactive-component-tree
features.what: `InteractiveMode` constructs `TUI(new ProcessTerminal(), settings.get("showHardwareCursor"))`, applies `tui.maxInlineImages` and Kitty text-sizing settings, then wires persistent containers in this exact order: `chatContainer`, `pendingMessagesContainer`, `statusContainer`, `todoContainer`, `subagentContainer`, `btwContainer`, `omfgContainer`, `errorBannerContainer`, `modelCycleContainer`, `statusLine`, `hookWidgetContainerAbove`, `editorContainer` (holds `CustomEditor`), `hookWidgetContainerBelow`. `init()` wires them after startup warnings/welcome/changelog, focuses the editor, registers `InputController` handlers, starts the TUI, pushes terminal title state, updates the editor border, and requests a forced render.

features.name: event-controller-streaming
features.what: Subscribes to `AgentSessionEvent` and mutates UI incrementally: `agent_start` starts the loader in `statusContainer`; assistant `message_start` creates and mounts a streaming component; `message_update` updates streaming content and creates/updates tool-execution components as tool calls appear; `tool_execution_update`/`end` update tool result components and completion state; `message_end` finalizes the stream, applies aborted/error annotations and marks pending tool args complete on a normal stop; `agent_end` stops loaders, clears transient stream state, flushes any deferred model switch, and issues a completion notification if backgrounded. Consecutive read-tool calls are coalesced into one visual block via stateful `#lastReadGroup` until a non-read break occurs.

features.name: loader-orchestration
features.what: `statusContainer` owns transient loaders (`loadingAnimation`, `autoCompactionLoader`, `retryLoader`); `Loader` advances its spinner every 80ms (animated message colorizers redraw at ~30fps) and uses `requestDirectWrite` for quiet fixed-height frames with automatic fallback to component-scoped render when direct rewriting is unsafe. `CancellableLoader` pairs with an `AbortSignal` and exposes `onAbort` for cancellable long-running UI. End/cancel paths stop and clear loader components.

features.name: status-line
features.what: Persistent status/hooks/plan indicator lane that also drives editor top-border updates, configured by `statusLine.preset` (`default|minimal|compact|full|nerd|ascii|custom`, default `default`), `statusLine.separator` (`powerline|powerline-thin|slash|pipe|block|none|ascii`, default `powerline-thin`), `statusLine.transparent` (default `false`, uses terminal background), `statusLine.showHookStatus` (default `true`), `statusLine.sessionAccent` (default `true`). `preset: custom` enables `statusLine.leftSegments`, `statusLine.rightSegments`, `statusLine.segmentOptions`. Segments are colored by the 13 dedicated `statusLine*` theme tokens. Mode indicators (e.g. `Vibe`, plan mode) render here.

features.name: cancellation-matrix
features.what: State-conditional cancellation — the same key means different things by runtime state. Escape: during an active stream restores queued messages to the editor and aborts the agent; during bash/python execution aborts the running command; during auto-compaction / handoff generation / auto-retry the editor's SINGLE `onEscape` handler dispatches on live session state (`isCompacting`/`isGeneratingHandoff`/`isRetrying`) and calls `abortCompaction`/`abortHandoff`/`abortRetry` — handlers are never swapped; on an inactive bash/python mode it clears editor text and restores border. Ctrl+C single press clears the editor, double press within 500ms shuts down. Ctrl+D on an empty editor shuts down.

features.name: session-teardown
features.what: Exit from double `Ctrl+C`, empty-editor `Ctrl+D`, `/exit`, and postmortem signals converges on ONE promise-memoized teardown; the first caller wins — it snapshots the editor draft, calls `beginDispose()` synchronously, attempts the draft save, then disposes the session; later keypress/signal callers await the same promise and cannot double-run. Interactive shutdown ownership order: stop live commands and transient controllers → show closing status → await session disposal → drain in-flight Kitty input (≤1s) → dispose run-state title/spinner and restore the prior terminal title → `TUI.stop()` (leave alternate-screen/resize state, purge image and probe state, stop watchdog and render/resize timers, position and forcibly restore the cursor) → `ProcessTerminal.stop()`.

features.name: suspend-resume
features.what: `Ctrl+Z` is distinct from exit: `InputController.handleCtrlZ()` registers a ONE-SHOT `SIGCONT` handler that restarts the TUI and forces a repaint, stops the TUI to release terminal modes, then sends `SIGTSTP` to the process group. The session is retained; no session teardown or terminal handoff runs.

features.name: terminal-title-and-notifications
features.what: Interactive init pushes terminal title state (run-state title + spinner) and shutdown restores the prior title. OSC 99 notification capability is probed at start; a completion notification is issued at `agent_end` when the session is backgrounded. `PI_NOTIFICATIONS=off|0|false` suppresses terminal/desktop notifications.
features.surface: terminal title escape sequences, OSC 99; env `PI_NOTIFICATIONS`

features.name: mode-transitions-and-deferred-model-switch
features.what: Plan mode tracks flags, status-line state, active tools, and model switching; enter/exit updates session mode entries and status/UI state. A model switch requested while streaming is DEFERRED and flushed at `agent_end`. `app.plan.toggle` (`Alt+Shift+P`) toggles plan mode.

features.name: model-selector-and-cycle-chips
features.what: Four model surfaces: `app.model.cycleForward` (`Ctrl+P`) / `app.model.cycleBackward` (`Shift+Ctrl+P`) cycle role models and render a chip track in the dedicated `modelCycleContainer`; `app.model.selectTemporary` (`Alt+P`) picks a model for this session only; `app.model.select` (`Alt+M`) opens the full model selector that assigns roles.

features.name: hook-widget-containers
features.what: Two mount points for hook-provided widgets, `hookWidgetContainerAbove` (between the status line and the editor) and `hookWidgetContainerBelow` (after the editor), rendered as part of the persistent component tree.

features.name: theme-schema-and-tokens
features.what: Theme files are JSON validated by an ArkType runtime schema (`themeJsonSchema`, mirrored by `theme-schema.json`; a `$schema` key is informational only). Top level: `name` (required), `colors` (required), optional `vars`, `export`, `symbols`. `colors` requires 66 tokens — core text/borders (11: accent, border, borderAccent, borderMuted, success, error, warning, muted, dim, text, thinkingText), background blocks (7), message/tool text (5), markdown (10), diff+syntax (12), mode/thinking borders (8) — plus 13 statusLine segment tokens; `thinkingMax` is the ONLY optional color and falls back to `thinkingXhigh`. Values accept `"#RRGGBB"`, a 256-color index `0..255`, a `vars` reference string, or `""` meaning terminal default (`\x1b[39m` fg / `\x1b[49m` bg). Missing required tokens produce a grouped error; bad types produce validation errors with a JSON path; unknown name → `Theme not found: <name>`.

features.name: theme-var-resolution
features.what: `vars` are reusable named colors resolved recursively before ANSI conversion; nested references are supported, a missing variable reference THROWS, and a circular reference THROWS.

features.name: theme-sources-and-lookup
features.what: `loadThemeJson` resolves in order: (1) built-in embedded themes (`dark.json`, `light.json`, all `defaults/*.json` compiled into `defaultThemes`), then (2) `<customThemesDir>/<name>.json`. `getCustomThemesDir()` defaults to `~/.omp/agent/themes`, overridden to `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/themes`. `getAvailableThemes()` returns merged built-in + custom names sorted, with built-ins winning name collisions.

features.name: color-mode-detection-and-conversion
features.what: `detectColorMode()`: `COLORTERM=truecolor|24bit` → truecolor; `WT_SESSION` → truecolor; `TERM` in {`dumb`,`linux`,empty} → 256color; otherwise truecolor. Conversion: hex → `Bun.color(..., "ansi-16m"|"ansi-256")`; numeric index → `38;5`/`48;5`; `""` → default fg/bg reset.

features.name: auto-dark-light-slot-selection
features.what: `initTheme` reads `symbolPreset`, `colorBlindMode`, `theme.dark`, `theme.light` and picks the active slot in this order: (1) terminal-reported OSC 11 background luminance unless the known-broken macOS/Zellij fallback path is active, (2) `COLORFGBG` background index (`<8` dark, `>=8` light), (3) macOS appearance fallback only on that broken path, (4) dark slot. Auto mode re-evaluates the slot on terminal appearance changes, `SIGWINCH`, and the macOS fallback observer. Defaults: `theme.dark = titanium`, `theme.light = light`.

features.name: theme-switch-preview-and-watch
features.what: `setTheme(name, watch?)` loads the theme, updates the global `theme` singleton, optionally starts the watcher, and fires `onThemeChange`; on failure it falls back to built-in `dark` and returns `{success:false, error}`. `previewTheme(name)` applies a temporary theme to the global singleton WITHOUT persisting and, on failure, does NOT replace the current theme (settings UI uses it for live preview and restores on cancel). The watcher watches `<customThemesDir>/<currentTheme>.json` only when that file exists (built-ins are effectively unwatched), debounces reloads, and keeps the last successfully loaded theme on reload error or temporary absence — there is no delete/rename fallback.

features.name: colorblind-mode
features.what: `colorBlindMode` (default `false`) changes exactly ONE token at runtime: `toolDiffAdded` is HSV-adjusted (green shifted toward blue), and only when the resolved value is a hex string. All other tokens are unchanged.

features.name: symbol-presets-and-spinners
features.what: Three symbol presets (`unicode`, `nerd`, `ascii`) selected with precedence: settings `symbolPreset` override → theme JSON `symbols.preset` → fallback `"unicode"`. `symbols.overrides` overrides individual `SymbolKey` values; invalid override keys are IGNORED and logged at debug level. `symbols.spinnerFrames` accepts either a flat `string[]` (applied to both spinner types) or `{ status?: string[], activity?: string[] }`; unspecified types fall back to the preset's defaults. `status` drives the ~12.5fps spinner used by loaders and tool-execution indicators; `activity` drives the ~30fps spinner used by markdown progress bars and similar high-frequency UI.

features.name: box-drawing-token-split
features.what: All outlined chrome (tool-result frames, overlays, code fences, editor, welcome banner) draws with `boxRound.{topLeft,topRight,bottomLeft,bottomRight,horizontal,vertical}`; junction glyphs have no rounded Unicode form so `boxSharp.{cross,teeDown,teeUp,teeRight,teeLeft}` supply dividers everywhere (rounded frames AND tables). Markdown tables are the sole fully-sharp surface, so `boxSharp.{topLeft,topRight,bottomLeft,bottomRight}` affect markdown table corners only.

features.name: theme-adapters
features.what: The theme exposes typed adapters consumed by widgets rather than raw token lookups: `getMarkdownTheme()`, `getSelectListTheme()`, `getEditorTheme()`, `getSettingsListTheme()`, plus `theme.fg(token, text?)` for foreground styling and syntax colors consumed by the native highlighter.

features.name: theme-settings-persistence
features.what: Theme settings persist to global config YAML at `<agentDir>/config.yml` (default `~/.omp/agent/config.yml`): `theme.dark`, `theme.light`, `symbolPreset`, `colorBlindMode`. A legacy flat `theme: "name"` value is migrated into `theme.dark` or `theme.light` based on luminance detection.

features.name: extension-custom-ui-mount
features.what: `ctx.ui.custom<T>(factory, { overlay? }): Promise<T>` where factory is `(tui, theme, keybindings: KeybindingsManager, done: (result:T)=>void) => Component|Promise<Component>`. Interactive flow: save editor text → without `overlay` replace the editor component with yours, with `overlay` mount bottom-centered via `TUI.showOverlay` → focus your component; on `done(result)` call `component.dispose?.()`, hide the overlay if present, restore editor + text for non-overlay flows, refocus the editor, resolve the promise. `done(...)` is MANDATORY and must be called exactly once or the flow never resolves.

features.name: ui-availability-guards
features.what: UI availability is mode-dependent and must be guarded with `ctx.hasUI` / `pi.hasUI`: interactive TUI supports `custom()`; background/headless supplies a no-op UI context with `hasUI === false`; RPC mode does not mount components and implements `custom()` as unsupported returning `undefined as never`. `ctx.ui.notify(message, level)` is the non-interactive-safe messaging path.

features.name: custom-tool-renderers
features.what: Custom/extension tools may return components from `renderCall(args, options, theme)` and `renderResult(result, options, theme, args?)`; `options` carries `{ expanded: boolean; isPartial: boolean; spinnerFrame?: number }`. These are mounted by `ToolExecutionComponent`, which also drives partial-state options and uses live-region pinning for replacing preview/dashboard states.

features.name: selectlist-widget
features.what: Reusable `SelectList(items, visibleRows, theme)` widget with `onSelect(item)` / `onCancel()` callbacks, `handleInput(data)`, `render(width)` and `invalidate()`; item labels may carry theme styling. Shared by pickers across extension UI and built-in selectors.

features.name: agent-hub-surface
features.what: Full-screen live roster and control surface for subagents, opened/closed by `Alt+A` (`app.agents.hub`), `Ctrl+S` (legacy `app.session.observe`), or double-tap `←` from an empty main-session editor; opens even when empty. Rows show status (`running|idle|parked|aborted`), identity, parent, unread IRC count, model role and resolved model, age, task/activity, cost, active/elapsed time, request and tool-call counts, tokens; the header aggregates across measured agents and missing data renders as `usage —` (never estimated). Controls: `j`/`k`/arrows/wheel select, `Enter`/click open (focusing a parked agent revives it), `t` toggle flat/tree, `Tab` toggle inspector on narrow terminals, `PageUp`/`PageDown` scroll inspector, `r` revive (parked only), `x` abort-then-kill immediately, `Esc` closes inspector first on narrow terminals then the Hub. On wide terminals the inspector renders beside the roster. Focusing a subagent rebinds transcript/status line/editor to it; `Esc` with an empty editor or double-`←` returns to the main session WITHOUT interrupting it. Contexts without a local focusable session (collab guests, advisor rows) use the file-backed full-screen transcript viewer, which BORROWS THE ALTERNATE SCREEN while open and restores the Hub beneath it on close, incrementally tailing the file and offering an input line only when the agent is messageable. Advisor rows (`__advisor*.jsonl`) are read-only: not messageable, not revivable, not killable.

features.name: session-tree-selector
features.what: `/tree` opens `TreeSelectorComponent` over `SessionManager.getTree()`; also reachable via `app.session.tree`, double-Escape on an empty editor when `doubleEscapeAction = "tree"` (default), and `/branch` under that same setting. Children sort by timestamp ascending, the active-leaf branch is ordered first, the active root-to-leaf path is bulleted, labels render as `[label]` before node text, and orphan/self-parent/null-parent entries become roots sharing a virtual branching root. Viewport recenters on selection showing up to `max(5, floor(terminalHeight/2))` rows. Keys: Up/Down move (wrapping), Alt+Up/Down jump user/assistant turns, PageUp/PageDown or Left/Right page, Home/End first/last visible, Enter select, Shift+Enter summarize-and-switch, Esc clears search else closes, Ctrl+C closes, typing appends to search, Backspace deletes, Shift+L edits/clears label when search is empty, Ctrl+O / Shift+Ctrl+O cycle filters, Alt+D/T/U/L/A jump to a filter. Filters cycle `default → no-tools → user-only → labeled-only → all` (initial from `treeFilterMode`, default `default`); `default` hides `label`/`custom`/`model_change`/`thinking_level_change`; tool-only assistant nodes are hidden in EVERY mode including `all` unless error/aborted or the current leaf. Search tokenizes on spaces with case-insensitive fuzzy subsequence matching and AND semantics across tokens.

features.name: tree-selection-and-summary-flow
features.what: Selection outcomes: a `user` message sets the new leaf to its `parentId` (root user message resets to root) and reconstructs text+image attachments as an editable draft, written ONLY when the editor is currently empty; ordinary `custom_message` follows the same rule while `skill-prompt` customs are non-editable; a past `ask` tool result reopens the ORIGINAL question UI (cancel = no change; a new answer is appended as a SIBLING tool result preserving the old branch, then the agent resumes) with fallback to a plain leaf move if questions are unrecoverable; any other node sets leaf = node id with no prefill; selecting the current leaf closes with `Already at this point` except for a current-leaf `ask` result. Summary-on-switch is gated by `branchSummary.enabled` (default `false`) offering `No summary` / `Summarize` / `Summarize with custom prompt`; Shift+Enter summarizes regardless of the setting (requires a model + provider credential); Escape in the summary prompt reopens the tree, custom-prompt cancel returns to the summary choice, during summarization a loader shows and Esc binds to `abortBranchSummary()`, and an abort reopens the tree applying NO move. Labels are append-only `label` entries via `appendLabelChange(targetId, label)` — empty clears; nodes display resolved label state, not raw history.

features.name: pause-screen
features.what: `/pause` (interactive TUI only) engages a process-global gate for the main agent, in-process subagents, and the advisor; each agent parks at its next safe boundary — in-flight calls FINISH, nothing is aborted, no new work starts until release. From the pause screen `Esc`, `Enter`, `Space`, or `Ctrl+C` resumes; Ctrl+C resumes rather than aborting.

features.name: settings-ui
features.what: Interactive settings surface (`/settings`) with categorized sections (e.g. `Appearance → Dark Theme` / `Light Theme`, `Interaction → Magic Keywords`) using `getSettingsListTheme()`, applying `previewTheme` for live theme preview and restoring the prior theme on cancel.

features.name: slash-command-registry
features.what: Slash commands are a capability (`id: "slash-commands"`, `key: cmd => cmd.name`). The registry loads all registered providers sorted by provider priority DESCENDING and deduplicates by key with FIRST-WINS semantics: the highest-precedence item lands in `result.items` while lower-precedence duplicates remain only in `result.all` marked `_shadowed = true` (also within a single provider returning duplicate names). Priorities: `native` 100, `omp-plugins` 90, `claude` 80, `claude-plugins` 70, `agents` 70, `codex` 70, `opencode` 55; equal priorities keep registration order, and current import order registers `claude-plugins` before `agents` before `codex`. Provider load failures are isolated (registry collects warnings and continues); items missing name/path/content or with an invalid level are dropped by validation.

features.name: slash-command-providers
features.what: Seven discovery providers with per-provider local precedence: `native` scans `<cwd>/.omp/commands/*.md` then the profile agent dir `commands/*.md` (project beats user); `omp-plugins` scans `commands/*.md` in extension-package roots and enabled npm/link plugins ordered invocation/CLI → project settings → user settings → installed plugins (marketplace roots excluded); `claude` recursively scans `~/.claude/commands/**/*.md` then `<cwd>/.claude/commands/**/*.md` (USER beats project) and registers subdirectory commands under both `bar` and `foo:bar`, gated by `commands.enableClaudeUser`/`commands.enableClaudeProject`; `codex` loads `~/.codex/commands/*.md` and `<cwd>/.codex/commands/*.md` user-first; `opencode` loads `~/.config/opencode/commands/*.md` and `<cwd>/.opencode/commands/*.md` user-first, gated by `commands.enableOpencodeUser`/`commands.enableOpencodeProject`; `claude-plugins` reads `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`, `~/.omp/plugins/installed_plugins.json` and the nearest project-scoped registry, scans `<pluginRoot>/commands/*.md` (remappable via plugin config keys `commands`/`slash-commands`) and prefixes names `<plugin>:<command>`, merging roots as `--plugin-dir` → project-scoped (shadowing user for the same plugin id) → user with the OMP registry authoritative over Claude's, preserving per-registry JSON entry order with no extra sort; `agents` scans non-recursive `commands/*.md` under `.agent/` and `.agents/` from cwd up to repo root then `~/.agent/commands` and `~/.agents/commands` (nearest root first, `.agent` before `.agents`, project before user). `loadFilesFromDir` defaults to non-recursive `*.md` with native glob `gitignore: true`, `hidden: false`, `fileType: File`, reading matches in parallel in glob order.

features.name: file-command-materialization
features.what: `loadSlashCommands()` converts capability items to runtime `FileSlashCommand`: parse frontmatter/body (`parseFrontmatter`); description = `frontmatter.description` if present else the first non-empty body line truncated to 60 chars with `...`; the parsed body becomes the executable template; a display source string (e.g. `via Claude Code Project`) is computed. Frontmatter parse severity is level-dependent — discovered user/project commands use warning-level parsing with fallback key/value parsing, items marked `native` and bundled fallback templates use FATAL parsing. Codex and OpenCode commands may override the command name via frontmatter `name`, otherwise the filename is used. After provider commands, `EMBEDDED_COMMAND_TEMPLATES` are appended with `source: "bundled"` only for names not already present.

features.name: slash-routing-pipeline
features.what: The unified built-in registry is dispatched BEFORE `AgentSession.prompt(...)` in both TUI and ACP/RPC modes (a built-in may consume input or return residual prompt text). After that boundary, when `expandPromptTemplates !== false`, `prompt()` processes in strict order: (1) extension commands — handler executes immediately and prompt returns; (2) TypeScript custom + MCP prompt commands — returning a `string` replaces the prompt text, returning `void/undefined` means handled with no LLM call; (3) file-based `expandSlashCommand` if the text still starts with `/`; (4) `expandPromptTemplate`; (5) delivery — idle sends immediately, streaming queues per `streamingBehavior`. Unknown `/...` is NOT rejected: it falls through unchanged into prompt-template expansion and LLM delivery. TUI-only built-ins are omitted from ACP availability and dispatch.

features.name: slash-argument-expansion
features.what: `expandSlashCommand(text, fileCommands)` runs only when text begins with `/`: parse the command name from the first token, parse args from the remainder with `parseCommandArgs`, match the name exactly, then apply positional `$1`,`$2`,…; slice `$@[start]` / `$@[start:length]` using 1-BASED positions; aggregate `$ARGUMENTS` and `$@`; render via `prompt.render` with `{ args, ARGUMENTS, arguments }`; append the inline argument fallback when the template used no inline placeholder. `parseCommandArgs` is quote-aware splitting supporting `'single'` and `"double"` quoting with delimiters stripped; it does NOT implement backslash escaping and an unmatched quote is not an error (it consumes to end of input).

features.name: slash-command-refresh-lifecycle
features.what: Interactive mode builds a pending command list at construction from built-ins (`BUILTIN_SLASH_COMMANDS`), extension-registered commands, TypeScript custom commands mapped to labels, and optional `/skill:<name>` commands when `skills.enableSkillCommands` is set; `init()` then calls `refreshSlashCommandState(...)` which loads file commands, installs the single autocomplete provider, and calls `session.setSlashCommands(...)` so expansion and autocomplete share one set. Refresh occurs at init, after `/move` changes cwd (`applyCwdChange` resets capabilities and refreshes against the new cwd), when the editor component is swapped, and on explicit reload flows such as `/reload-plugins`. There is NO continuous file watcher for command directories. The Extensions dashboard surfaces active and `_shadowed` entries.

features.name: slash-streaming-and-acp-availability
features.what: While `session.isStreaming`, `prompt()` still runs extension/custom/file/template transforms then REQUIRES `streamingBehavior`: `"steer"` queues an interrupt message (`agent.steer`), `"followUp"` queues a post-turn message (`agent.followUp`); omitting it THROWS. Extension commands execute immediately even during streaming rather than being queued as text, and the `steer(...)`/`followUp(...)` helpers reject extension commands via `#throwIfExtensionCommand`. Compaction queue replay uses `isKnownSlashCommand(...)` to route entries through `session.prompt(...)` versus raw steer/follow-up. `buildAvailableSlashCommands(...)` publishes first-wins in order: text-capable built-ins → optional skill commands → extension commands → TypeScript/MCP custom commands → discovered file commands, reserving built-in primary names AND aliases first and filtering extension names like `model:foo` whose prefix parses as a built-in.

features.name: magic-keywords
features.what: Standalone lowercase prose words in a user prompt inject hidden, user-attributed instructions for THAT TURN ONLY: `ultrathink` (careful multi-step reasoning notice; when automatic thinking is active it also selects the highest reasoning effort the current model supports for that turn), `orchestrate` (multi-agent orchestration contract), `workflowz` (deterministic multi-subagent workflow contract around the persistent `eval` kernel's `agent()`/`parallel()`/`pipeline()`/`completion()` helpers — injected only when BOTH `eval` and `task` are active). Matching rules: exact lowercase only (`Ultrathink` does not trigger); the word must be standalone prose — sentence punctuation and quotes may touch it (`orchestrate,` matches) but letters, digits, underscores, slashes, backslashes, hyphens, file extensions, symbol references and call syntax do not (`orchestrated`, `orchestrate.ts`, `foo::orchestrate`, `orchestrate()` all fail); fenced code blocks (backticks or tildes), inline code spans, and HTML/XML comments/tags/elements and their contents are ignored. Multiple enabled keywords may each add a notice; the visible word REMAINS in the user message and notices are non-displayed custom messages attributed to the user. The TUI highlights recognized words with ANIMATED gradients while editing and STATIC gradients in sent messages; that highlighting persists even when notice injection is disabled.

features.name: vibe-mode
features.what: `/vibe` toggles the top-level interactive session into a director for persistent background worker sessions; `/vibe <prompt>` enters and submits that prompt as the first directive. Entering activates a parent-session worker scope, installs the vibe tools, reduces the active toolset to `read` + optional parent-owned `todo` + the five vibe tools, and injects director instructions; the status line shows a `Vibe` indicator. Exiting restores the prior toolset, cancels in-flight worker turns, KILLS every worker in the scope, and persists terminal lifecycle records — a worker never outlives an intentional mode exit. Vibe mode is mutually exclusive with both ACTIVE and PAUSED plan/goal modes, and starting/forking/moving/handing off the session is rejected while it is active. Interactive-TUI only. Resuming a session whose current mode is `vibe` rehydrates completed workers as idle/parked sessions with their child transcripts; a turn interrupted by process restart is not auto-resumed and killed/mode-exit workers stay terminal.

features.name: vibe-worker-tools
features.what: Five worker-control tools over two tiers (`fast` → bundled `sonic` agent, default role `@smol`; `good` → bundled `task` agent, default role `@task`; the tier ALWAYS selects the bundled definition, never a same-named discovered custom agent, with `task.agentModelOverrides.sonic`/`.task` beating the bundled model and role aliases resolving through `modelRoles` with the parent active/default model as fallback): `vibe_spawn {cli, prompt, name?}` starts a blank worker with a self-contained first brief (`name` sanitized and capped at 48 chars; id generated when omitted); `vibe_send {session, message}` steers a streaming turn at its next step, else queues an automatic next turn, else starts the next turn immediately when idle/parked; `vibe_wait {sessions?, timeout?}` waits for the first watched turn to settle (all in-flight when omitted, default 30s) and ACKNOWLEDGES settled jobs so results are not delivered twice; `vibe_kill {session}` cancels the in-flight turn, clears queued messages, releases the worker and retains any initialized transcript at `history://<id>`; `vibe_list {}` lists sessions in SPAWN ORDER with tier, state, turn/queue counts, resolved model and recent activity. Spawn and send return immediately; each worker-turn result self-delivers into the director conversation through the async job manager with preview-capped text and full output at `agent://<id>`.
