Worker ids are scoped to the owning agent + parent session (out-of-scope ids report unknown); spawning requires the session async job manager; spawn failure tears down the partial record; a recoverable keep-alive worker returns to `idle`, and one whose child session cannot be resolved becomes `dead`.

features.name: extension-module-loader
features.what: Imports each candidate entry path via realpath + dynamic import with a `?mtime` cache-buster, picks the factory (`module` itself if it is a function, else `module.default`), requires it to be a function, awaits a returned promise before moving to the next path, and captures per-path `{path, error}` failures without aborting the remaining loads.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: extension-factory-contract
features.what: An extension is a TS/JS module whose default export is `(pi: ExtensionAPI) => void | Promise<void>`; during factory execution only registration methods are legal, and every runtime action method (`sendMessage`, `setActiveTools`, …) throws `ExtensionRuntimeNotInitializedError` until `ExtensionRunner.initialize()` wires live actions.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: extension-runner-lifecycle
features.what: `ExtensionRunner.initialize(mode/session/tool-registry)` binds live actions and per-mode contexts after load, then emits session/agent/tool events to handlers; handler exceptions are caught and routed to an extension error channel instead of crashing the dispatch loop.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: extension-event-bus
features.what: `pi.on(event, handler)` registers handlers on one shared `EventBus`/`ExtensionRuntime` instance for all extensions; dispatch order is deterministic — extension load order first, then registration order per extension per event — and `pi.events` exposes the bus directly.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: extension-discovery-roots
features.what: Native `extension-module` auto-discovery scans `<cwd>/.omp/extensions` (cwd-only, no ancestor walk) and the active agent dir's `extensions/` (default `~/.omp/agent/extensions`, `~/.omp/profiles/<name>/agent/extensions` under `--profile`, overridable by `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`), plus legacy JSON lists in `<cwd>/.omp/settings.json#extensions` and `<agentDir>/settings.json#extensions`; native globbing uses `gitignore: true`, `hidden: false`.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: extension-entry-resolution
features.what: A configured file path is used directly (`.ts`/`.js`/`.mjs`/`.cjs`); a directory resolves in order `package.json#omp.extensions` (legacy `pi.extensions`) → `index.ts` → `index.js` → one-level scan of direct `*.ts`/`*.js`, `<sub>/index.ts|index.js`, and `<sub>/package.json` manifests; TS beats JS in `index.{ts,js}` pairs, symlinks are eligible, manifest entries resolve relative to the package dir and are included only if they exist.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: extension-path-normalization
features.what: Configured paths are normalized (Unicode spaces, `file://`, `@/absolute/path`, stray leading `:`), `~` is expanded, relative paths resolve against cwd, and the internal `local://` scheme is rejected as a filesystem path.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: extension-load-order-dedupe
features.what: One ordered candidate list is built as native auto-discovered → discovered `.ts`/`.js` hook-capability factories → installed-plugin `omp.extensions` entries → explicit configured paths (CLI `-e/--extension`/`--hook` first, then settings `extensions`), then de-duplicated by resolved absolute path with first-seen-wins.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: extension-disable-controls
features.what: `--no-extensions` / SDK `disableExtensionDiscovery` drops ambient factories while still resolving explicit `-e/--extension`/`--hook` paths and their sibling capability roots; `disabledExtensions: [extension-module:<derivedName>]` disables a single module where `derivedName` is the file stem (`/x/foo.ts`→`foo`) or directory name (`/x/bar/index.ts`→`bar`).
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: legacy-pi-module-compat
features.what: A scoped Bun `onLoad` hook rewrites legacy host-package specifiers (`@mariozechner/*`, `@earendil-works/*`) and bare `@sinclair/typebox` onto the host-bundled copies before the extension module evaluates, so third-party extensions resolve to the running harness's singletons.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: tool-interception-wrapper
features.what: Every tool in the registry (built-ins, extension tools, bridged custom tools, MCP tools) is wrapped so each execution emits `tool_call` pre-exec and `tool_result` post-exec, including on the error path.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: tool-call-block-and-revise
features.what: `tool_call` handlers may return `{block: true, reason}` (first block short-circuits and `reason` becomes the tool error text the model sees) or `{input}` to replace the raw execution arguments (last non-blocking return wins, handlers do not observe each other's revisions, ignored when blocking and for `computer` calls); a throwing handler blocks the call fail-closed. For model-issued calls the event fires at arg-prep time so a revision is revalidated and observed by concurrency scheduling, execution events, the persisted assistant message, and the approval gate.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: tool-result-middleware
features.what: `tool_result` handlers run in extension order as a middleware chain where each handler sees prior modifications and may patch `{content, details, isError}`; on tool failure the event is still emitted with `isError: true` and error-text content.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: context-transform-chain
features.what: The `context` event fires before each LLM API call with the accumulated message list; handlers run in order, each receiving the previous handler's output, and returning `{messages}` replaces the context for that single call only (returning nothing passes through).
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: provider-request-interception
features.what: `before_provider_request` may replace the outgoing provider request payload and `after_provider_response` observes the response, giving extensions a wire-level hook distinct from message-level `context`.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: session-lifecycle-events
features.what: Emits `session_start`, `session_before_switch`/`session_switch`, `session_before_branch`/`session_branch`, `session_before_compact`/`session.compacting`/`session_compact`, `session_before_tree`/`session_tree`, `session_shutdown`; the `*_before_*` events are cancelable (`{cancel: true}` short-circuits) and additionally accept `skipConversationRestore` (branch), `compaction: CompactionResult` (compact), `summary` (tree), while `session.compacting` accepts `{context?, prompt?, preserveData?}` with latest-return-wins.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: session-stop-continuation
features.what: `session_stop` is awaited before the main session settles and may return `{continue: true, additionalContext}` to keep the loop running or `{decision: "block", reason}`; consecutive continuations are capped at 8, the payload carries `stop_hook_active`/`turn_id`, and it never fires for task/subagent sessions.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: turn-and-message-events
features.what: Emits `input` (pre-prompt, runs before the built-in first-message auto-title check), `before_agent_start` (may inject one message; first returned message wins), `agent_start`/`agent_end` (notification-only), `turn_start`/`turn_end`, and `message_start`/`message_update`/`message_end` where `message_end` receives a detached snapshot.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: reliability-signal-events
features.what: Emits `auto_compaction_start`/`auto_compaction_end`, `auto_retry_start`/`auto_retry_end`, `ttsr_triggered`, `todo_reminder`, `goal_updated`, and `credential_disabled` as notification-only runtime signals.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: tool-observability-events
features.what: Emits `tool_execution_start`/`tool_execution_update`/`tool_execution_end` for every wrapped execution, and `tool_approval_requested`/`tool_approval_resolved` only when a tool requires approval AND an approval handler is registered.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: mcp-notification-bridge
features.what: `mcp_notification` fires with `{server, method, params}` for every JSON-RPC notification from a connected MCP server AFTER the manager handles known list/update methods, including unknown/server-custom methods; frames arriving before any listener attaches are buffered in a bounded drop-oldest FIFO (cap 100) and drained into the first subscriber, and a throwing handler does not prevent other handlers from firing.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: user-command-interception
features.what: `user_bash` and `user_python` let an extension override user-issued local shell/Python execution by returning `{result}`.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: extension-tool-registration
features.what: `pi.registerTool(def)` adds a model-callable tool with `name`/`label`/`description`/`parameters` (omptype/zod/typebox schema) and optional `hidden`, `defaultInactive`, `loadMode` (`"discoverable"` default; canonical essentials default `"essential"`), `deferrable`, `approval` (`"read"|"write"|"exec"`, default `"exec"`), `strict`, `mcpServerName`, `mcpToolName`, `onSession`, `renderCall`, `renderResult`; `execute(toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx)` returns `{content, details}` and may stream partials via `onUpdate`.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: native-tool-delegation
features.what: When a registered tool shadows a built-in of the same name, `ctx.invokeTool(params, {signal, onUpdate})` runs the native built-in (same-name only, no arbitrary target, not re-gated by approval, self-recursion depth-guarded) and returns its result including native side effects; the method is `undefined` for net-new tools.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: tool-activation-control
features.what: `pi.getAllTools()`, `pi.getActiveTools()`, and `pi.setActiveTools(names)` let an extension read and mutate which tools are exposed to the model for subsequent requests.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: extension-slash-commands
features.what: `pi.registerCommand(name, {description, handler(args, ctx)})` adds a `/name` slash command receiving the raw trailing argument string; names colliding with built-ins are skipped with a diagnostic, and `pi.getCommands()` enumerates registrations.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: extension-command-context
features.what: Command handlers get an `ExtensionCommandContext` superset with session-control methods unavailable to event handlers: `waitForIdle()`, `newSession(opts)`, `switchSession(path)`, `branch(entryId)`, `navigateTree(id, {summarize})`, `compact(opts)`, and `reload()`.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: message-injection-api
features.what: `pi.sendMessage(message, {deliverAs, triggerTurn})` supports `"steer"` (default, interrupts the current run), `"followUp"` (queued after the run), `"nextTurn"` (injected on the next user prompt), with `triggerTurn: true` starting a turn when idle or scheduling an internal continuation while streaming; `pi.sendUserMessage(content, {deliverAs})` always goes through prompt flow (omitted `deliverAs` = normal prompt when idle, steer while streaming).
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: custom-session-entries
features.what: `pi.appendEntry(customType, data)` persists non-LLM state into session history under a globally-namespaced `customType`, and extensions rebuild state by scanning `ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()` for matching `type === "custom"` entries on `session_start`/`session_branch`/`session_tree`.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: managed-timers
features.what: `ctx.setInterval(fn, ms, …)` / `ctx.setTimeout(fn, ms, …)` mirror platform signatures but run callbacks under handler-dispatch isolation (sync throw or rejected promise is logged to the extension error channel), return handles for `ctx.clearTimer(handle)`, are `unref`'d, and are cleared automatically on `session_shutdown`.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: extension-ui-context
features.what: `ctx.ui` (`ExtensionUIContext`) exposes `select`/`confirm`/`input`/`editor` dialogs, `notify`, `setStatus`, `custom` overlays, `setEditorText`/`getEditorText`/`pasteToEditor`, `setTitle`, `setWorkingMessage`, theme listing/`setTheme(name)`, tools-expanded toggle, and `onTerminalInput`, with `ctx.hasUI` signalling availability.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: ui-context-mode-backends
features.what: Four interchangeable `ctx.ui` backends with documented capability gaps: interactive (`extension-ui-controller.ts`, full surface except no-op `setFooter`/`setHeader`), RPC (`extension_ui_request` round-trip for dialogs, fire-and-forget for notify/setStatus/setWidget-string-arrays/setEditorText, `setTitle` only when `PI_RPC_EMIT_TITLE=1`, `setTheme` returns failure, terminal input/custom/editor-component/autocomplete/working-message inert), ACP (elicitation-bridged dialogs with capability-gated defaults when the client lacks `elicitation.form`; rest stubbed), and print/headless/subagent (`hasUI=false`, all methods no-op/default-returning).
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: status-line-aggregation
features.what: `ctx.ui.setStatus(key, text)` stores text per key, renders keys sorted by name, and sanitizes each value (ANSI/VT escapes stripped, control chars → spaces, repeated spaces collapsed, trimmed) before joining and width-truncating for the footer.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: editor-surface-injection
features.what: Interactive mode lets extensions mount real UI into the editor region: `ctx.setEditorComponent(factory)` replaces the live editor, `ctx.ui.setWidget(...)` renders components above or below the editor (`placement: "aboveEditor"|"belowEditor"`; string-array content capped at 10 lines), and `ctx.ui.addAutocompleteProvider(factory)` stacks wrappers around the built-in editor completion provider in registration order, re-applied on every slash-command refresh.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: custom-message-renderer
features.what: `pi.registerMessageRenderer(customType, (message, {expanded}, theme) => Component)` supplies the TUI renderer for custom messages of that type; the first registered match for a `customType` wins.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: assistant-thinking-renderer
features.what: `pi.registerAssistantThinkingRenderer((context, theme) => Component|undefined)` appends display-only supplemental UI beneath each visible assistant thinking block; the callback receives the visible thinking text, content/thinking indexes, theme and a `requestRender()` callback, all returning renderers are appended in registration order, and renderers must not mutate messages.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: tool-render-hooks
features.what: `renderCall(args, options, theme)` and `renderResult(result, options, theme, args?)` on a tool definition replace default TUI output (wrapped in a `Box`), with `options` carrying `{expanded, isPartial, spinnerFrame?}`; renderer errors are caught, logged, and fall back to default text rendering.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: shortcut-and-flag-registration
features.what: `pi.registerShortcut(...)` binds keyboard chords (a fixed reserved list is silently ignored) and `pi.registerFlag(...)`/`pi.getFlag(...)` declare and read extension-owned CLI flags; `pi.setLabel(text)` names the extension in UI/diagnostics.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: provider-registration
features.what: `pi.registerProvider(...)` lets an extension add a model provider to the session's registry — an extension-only capability with no hook/custom-tool equivalent.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: session-name-control
features.what: `pi.getSessionName()`/`pi.setSessionName(name)` read and persist the session title; calling `await pi.setSessionName(...)` from an `input` handler suppresses the built-in first-message auto-title generation for that session.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: model-selection-facade
features.what: `ctx.models` provides `list()` (authenticated models this session), `current()` (read lazily so it reflects `/model` switches), `resolve(spec)` honoring settings-backed aliases/role aliases (`provider/id`, bare id, `@slow`) exactly like `--model` (returns `undefined` on no match), and `family(model)` returning an opaque non-persistable lineage token for same-family comparisons; `pi.setModel`, `pi.getThinkingLevel`, `pi.setThinkingLevel` mutate live session settings.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: service-tier-control
features.what: `pi.getServiceTiers()` returns a detached snapshot of the live per-family tier map and `pi.setServiceTier(family, tier)` overrides one family for subsequent requests (`undefined` clears it); accepted values are OpenAI `auto|default|flex|scale|priority`, Anthropic `priority`, Google `flex|priority`, and changes never affect an in-flight streaming request.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: extension-runtime-facade
features.what: Handler/tool `ctx` exposes read-only runtime state and control: `cwd`, `sessionManager`, `modelRegistry`, `model`, `getContextUsage()`, `getAsyncJobSnapshot()` (null when no session owns the context), `getSystemPrompt()`, `compact(...)`, `isIdle()`, `hasPendingMessages()`, `abort()`, `shutdown()`, optional `memory` runtime (status/search/save) and `localProtocolOptions` for external tool bridges; `pi.exec(...)` and `pi.logger` are available on the API object.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: schema-builder-injection
features.what: The API object injects the host's schema builders so extensions need no dependencies: `pi.arktype` (native omptype `type(...)`), `pi.zod` (Zod-compatible builder backed by omptype), `pi.typebox` (legacy TypeBox shim), and `pi.pi` (the host package exports); all three feed the same validation/JSON-Schema wire pipeline and typed `Static<TParams>` params.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: legacy-hook-subsystem
features.what: A separate `HookAPI` subsystem (`types.ts`/`loader.ts`/`runner.ts`/`tool-wrapper.ts`) exported at `@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent/extensibility/hooks` with `discoverAndLoadHooks`/`loadHooks`, `HookRunner`, `HookToolWrapper`: a subset event catalog, `getCommand`/`getMessageRenderer` first-match-wins lookups, `getRegisteredCommands()` without dedupe, `emit()` catching handler errors into `HookError{hookPath,event,error}` while `emitToolCall()` deliberately propagates so the wrapper fails closed.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: custom-tools-loader
features.what: `discoverAndLoadCustomTools(configuredPaths, cwd, builtInToolNames)` merges tool-capability providers (native `~/.omp/agent/tools` + `.omp/tools`, `~/.claude/tools` + `.claude/tools`, `~/.codex/tools` + `.codex/tools`, Claude marketplace plugin cache), installed-plugin manifest tool entries, and explicit paths; it de-duplicates resolved paths, rejects name conflicts against built-ins and already-loaded custom tools, rejects `.md`/`.json` files as executable modules, expands `~` and resolves relative paths from cwd, and starts with a no-op UI context until the host calls `setUIContext(...)`.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: custom-tool-contract
features.what: A custom-tool module exports a factory `(pi: CustomToolAPI) => CustomTool | CustomTool[] | Promise<…>` whose tools implement `execute(toolCallId, params, onUpdate, ctx, signal)` and optional `onSession(event, ctx)` (reasons `start|switch|branch|tree|shutdown` plus `auto_compaction_*`, `auto_retry_*`, `ttsr_triggered`, `todo_reminder`, errors logged as warnings only); `CustomToolAPI` supplies `cwd`, `exec`, `ui`, `hasUI`, `logger`, `arktype`/`zod`/`typebox`, `pi`, and `pushPendingAction(action)` for preview actions finalized via `xd://resolve` / `xd://reject`.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: custom-tool-extension-bridge
features.what: Session bootstrap converts SDK-provided and filesystem-discovered custom tools into extension `ToolDefinition`s registered through a generated extension (forwarding the differing argument order), so they pass through the same interception wrappers; `CustomToolAdapter` remains available for direct library consumers.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: restricted-session-tool-gating
features.what: In unrestricted SDK bootstrap custom and extension-registered tools are force-included in the initial active set; with `restrictToolNames: true` SDK-provided custom tools are excluded unless `allowRestrictedCustomTools: true`, and opted-in tools are active only when their names also appear in `toolNames`.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: capability-provider-registry
features.what: A registry aggregates capability items (`skills`, `extensions`, `extension-module`, `hook`, `tool`, `commands`, `rules`, `prompts`, MCP, agents) from priority-sorted providers (higher wins; ties by registration order), de-duplicates by a per-capability key (`ext.name` for extensions, `${type}:${tool}:${name}` for hooks), keeps shadowed duplicates in `result.all` with `_shadowed = true`, and stamps each item with `_source {provider, providerName, path (absolutized), level: "user"|"project"}`.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: skills-discovery-pipeline
features.what: `loadSkills()` runs three passes — capability providers (`native` 100, `omp-plugins` 90, `claude` 80, `claude-plugins`/`agents`/`codex` 70, `opencode` 55, `github` 30), then `skills.customDirectories` via non-recursive `*/SKILL.md` scan (overrides same-named provider skills; first custom dir wins), then `omp-managed` auto-learn skills (priority 5) dead-last — de-duplicating by skill name and by `realpath` (symlink-safe) and emitting collision warnings; returns nothing when `skills.enabled` is false.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: skill-frontmatter-contract
features.what: `SKILL.md` frontmatter supports `name` (defaults to directory name), `description`, `globs`, `alwaysApply`, `hide`, `disableModelInvocation` (normalized from kebab-case `disable-model-invocation`), preserving unknown keys; `description` is mandatory for the `native`, `omp-plugins`, `github`, and custom-directory scans (`requireDescription: true`) but optional for claude/codex/agents/opencode/claude-plugins providers.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: skill-filtering-toggles
features.what: Skill filtering applies in fixed order: (1) not disabled by `disabledExtensions: skill:<name>`, (2) source toggle enabled (`enableCodexUser`, `enableClaudeUser`, `enableClaudeProject`, `enablePiUser`, `enablePiProject`, `enableAgentsUser`, `enableAgentsProject`; untoggled providers pass if ANY named third-party toggle is on), (3) not matched by `ignoredSkills` globs, (4) matched by `includeSkills` globs when that allowlist is non-empty.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: skill-prompt-exposure
features.what: When the `read` tool is available the system prompt lists discovered skills (name + description) excluding `hide: true` entries; without `read` the list is omitted entirely, and task subagents inherit the session's skill list with no per-task pinning.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: skill-url-protocol
features.what: `skill://<name>` resolves to that skill's `SKILL.md` and `skill://<name>/<relative-path>` resolves inside its `baseDir` after URL-decoding, rejecting absolute paths, `..` traversal, and any resolved path escaping `baseDir`; missing files return an explicit `File not found` error with no fallback search, and content type is `text/markdown` for `.md` else `text/plain`.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: skill-slash-commands
features.what: With `skills.enableSkillCommands`, interactive mode registers one `/skill:<name> [args]` command per discovered skill that recognizes both a leading token and a whitespace-delimited token embedded in prose (removing the token and passing surrounding prose as args, but not when the draft starts with another slash command or a local bash/Python sigil), reads `filePath` directly, strips frontmatter, wraps the body with skill name + base dir + user args, and injects it as a custom message whose delivery follows the submission keybinding (Enter → steer while streaming, Ctrl+Enter/`app.message.followUp` → followUp; normal idle prompt otherwise).
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: gemini-manifest-extensions
features.what: A `gemini` provider (priority 60) scans `~/.gemini/extensions` then `<cwd>/.gemini/extensions` (cwd-only, one directory level, dot-prefixed dirs NOT filtered) for `<name>/gemini-extension.json`, gates on `tryParseJson()` truthiness (warning `Invalid JSON in <manifestPath>`; missing/unreadable/empty files skipped silently), performs no schema validation of `{name?, description?, mcpServers?, tools?, context?}`, and emits an `extensions` capability item `{name: manifest.name ?? dirName, path, manifest, level}`; the same roots separately feed `extension-module` records for `.ts`/`.js` files, `index.*`, and `omp`/`pi` manifests.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: plugin-manifest-model
features.what: A plugin's manifest resolves as `package.json.omp` → fallback `package.json.pi` → fallback `{version: package.version}`, with `manifest.version` always overwritten from the package version and no strict schema validation; a package lacking `omp`/`pi` is installable and listable but skipped by runtime enabled-plugin discovery, and malformed `package.json` JSON is a hard read-time failure.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: plugin-install-npm-git
features.what: `PluginManager.install` parses feature brackets (`pkg` → `null`, `pkg[*]` → all, `pkg[]` → none, `pkg[a,b]` → named, `@scope/pkg@1.2.3[feat]`), validates npm specs against a package-name regex plus a shell-metacharacter denylist (applied after bracket stripping) or git specs via `validateGitSpec` (`github:`/`gitlab:`/`bitbucket:`/`codeberg:`/`sourcehut:`/`srht:` shorthands and full git/ssh URLs, rejecting only `SHELL_METACHARS`), ensures the plugins `package.json` skeleton, runs `bun install` in the plugins root, resolves the installed package name (npm: strip version; git: diff `dependencies` before/after), computes `enabledFeatures`, validates every declared extension entry by importing it into a throwaway registration surface, and upserts `{version, enabledFeatures, enabled: true}` into the lockfile.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: plugin-install-rollback
features.what: Install snapshots the prior package tree, `plugins/package.json`, and `bun.lock` before `bun install`; any post-install failure (feature validation, extension validation, runtime-config save) restores all three and aborts, appending any rollback failure to the reported error — while `bun uninstall` succeeding but a lockfile write failing leaves stale runtime state, and a failed `link` does not restore the removed target.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: plugin-link-dev
features.what: `omp plugin link <localPath>` resolves the path against the manager cwd, requires a local `package.json` with `name`, creates scope directories for scoped names, removes any existing target, symlinks into `~/.omp/plugins/node_modules/<pkg.name>`, and adds an enabled lockfile entry with default features (`null`).
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: plugin-runtime-state-and-overrides
features.what: Plugin state lives in the plugins data root (`~/.omp/plugins` or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/omp/plugins`) as `package.json` + `node_modules/` + `omp-plugins.lock.json` (per-plugin enabled flag, selected feature set, persisted settings), mirrored per project at `<anchor>/.omp/plugins/{node_modules,omp-plugins.lock.json}` where the anchor is the nearest `.omp/` or `.git/`; read-only `plugin-overrides.json` in project config dirs can disable plugins or override features/settings, effective enablement is `runtimeEnabled && !projectDisabled`, a missing lockfile reads as empty, and every mutation rewrites the whole pretty-printed JSON with no cross-process locking.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: plugin-capability-path-resolution
features.what: `getEnabledPlugins(cwd)` unions dependency-manifest packages with lockfile entries (so link-only plugins are found), skips packages with no plugin `package.json`, no `omp`/`pi` manifest, globally disabled, or project-disabled; per plugin, `resolvePlugin{Extension,Tool,Hook,Command}Paths` return base entries plus feature entries (explicit list → only selected, `enabledFeatures === null` → features marked `default: true`), accepting a file or a directory containing `index.{ts,js,mjs,cjs}`, silently skipping missing paths and de-duplicating by resolved absolute path first-wins.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: plugin-conventional-content-discovery
features.what: The `omp-plugins` capability provider scans enabled npm/link plugin roots (and extension packages loaded via `extensions:`/`-e`/`--extension`) for conventional `skills/`, `hooks/pre|post/`, `tools/`, `commands/`, `rules/`, `prompts/`, and `.mcp.json`, with task-agent discovery scanning the same roots' `agents/`; marketplace roots are excluded here and handled by the `claude-plugins` provider plus marketplace task-agent discovery.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: marketplace-registry
features.what: `/marketplace add|remove|update [name]|list` maintains `marketplaces.json` in the user data root: `add` classifies the source (`owner/repo` GitHub shorthand, `https://…*.json` direct catalog, other `http(s)://` as git unless the path ends in `.json`, `git@`/`ssh://` git, `./`|`~/`|`/` local dir), fetches the catalog from `.omp-plugin/marketplace.json` preferred over `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, and caches under `<plugins-root>/cache/marketplaces/<name>/`; `update` refreshes catalogs only (never reinstalls) and `remove` drops the registry entry and catalog cache without uninstalling plugins.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: marketplace-catalog-schema
features.what: Catalog parsing requires `name`, `owner.name`, and `plugins[]` (invalid JSON or invalid required top-level fields reject the whole catalog; an invalid plugin entry is logged and skipped), supports optional `metadata.{description,version,pluginRoot}` (pluginRoot prepended to relative sources), preserves unknown top-level fields, and enforces naming rules: lowercase letters/digits/hyphens/dots, must start and end alphanumeric, ≤64 chars, with `name@marketplace` IDs ≤128 chars.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: marketplace-source-fetching
features.what: Plugin `source` supports a `./`-prefixed relative path resolved inside the marketplace root after `pluginRoot` (traversal outside the root rejected; unavailable for URL-sourced catalogs), `{source:"url", url, ref?, sha?}`, `{source:"github", repo, ref?, sha?}`, `{source:"git-subdir", url, path, ref?, sha?}` (path must resolve inside the clone), and `{source:"npm", package, version?}` which parses but fails install with `npm plugin sources are not yet supported`; the install version falls back entry `version` → plugin manifest (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`/`package.json`) → source SHA → `0.0.0`, caching to `<plugins-root>/cache/plugins/<marketplace>___<plugin>___<version>/`.
features.surface: `source` field of a catalog plugin entry
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: marketplace-install-scopes
features.what: `/marketplace install|uninstall|upgrade [--force] [--scope user|project] name@marketplace` records installs in `installed_plugins.json` (version 2) at user (`~/.omp/plugins/`) or project (`<project>/.omp/plugins/`) scope, symlinks the cached plugin into that scope's `node_modules/<package>` and records it in that scope's `omp-plugins.lock.json`; an enabled project install shadows an enabled user install of the same ID while a disabled project install does not, and `--scope` is required for uninstall/enable/disable/`/marketplace upgrade` when the plugin exists in both scopes.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: marketplace-content-materialization
features.what: Installation materializes catalog `lspServers` (inline map or in-plugin path) to `.lsp.json` and `dapAdapters` to `.dap.json|.dap.yaml|.dap.yml`, reads `.omp-plugin/plugin.json` then `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` for path remapping (declared skill paths add to the default except when the catalog source is exactly `"./"` where they replace it; declared `commands`/`slash-commands` replace the default unless `./commands` is listed explicitly; paths outside the plugin root are ignored with a warning), and a manifest `mcpServers` declaration (inline map or path) replaces rather than merges with the default `.mcp.json`.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: marketplace-upgrade-autoupdate
features.what: `upgrade` without a name upgrades all plugins, comparing only catalog entries that declare `version` (semver must be strictly newer; non-semver counts as changed when unequal) and skipping per-plugin failures so the batch can partially succeed; `marketplace.autoUpdate` (`off` | `notify` default | `auto`) drives startup checks that best-effort refresh catalogs older than 24 hours first, and `omp plugin upgrade` without `--scope` reinstalls every installed scope.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: plugin-cli-surface
features.what: Every plugin operation is exposed twice with matching semantics — slash commands (`/marketplace …`, `/plugins list|enable|disable`, interactive browser when `/marketplace` has no args in TUI, marketplace list in ACP/RPC, TUI selector for argument-less uninstall) and CLI (`omp plugin install|uninstall|list|link|doctor|features|config|enable|disable|discover|upgrade|marketplace …`, plus `omp install name@marketplace`), with `--json` affecting output formatting only and `--dry-run` on install skipping `bun install`, network, and all state writes while still ensuring the plugins `package.json` skeleton; `doctor --fix` best-effort repairs drift (re-`bun install`, orphaned-config and invalid-feature cleanup) and there is no npm-plugin `update` action.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: reload-plugins-refresh
features.what: `/reload-plugins` re-discovers skills, slash commands, and MCP servers in the live session; TUI marketplace mutations update disk state and invalidate discovery caches but do not refresh the session, ACP/RPC marketplace handlers auto-refresh skills and slash commands only, and newly installed tools, hooks, or extension modules require a session restart.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: extension-diagnostics-logging
features.what: Structured logs land under the active state root's `logs/` (default `~/.omp/logs/omp.<date>.<pid>.log`) with debug level always on and nothing written to the console (which would corrupt the TUI); failed extension loads are logged with path and error, and extensions emit their own entries via `pi.logger`.
features.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)

features.name: config-root-resolution
features.what: `getConfigDirs(subpath, {user=true, project=true, cwd=getProjectDir(), existingOnly=false})` returns ordered candidate dirs: ALL user-level bases first, then ALL project-level bases, each group in the fixed source priority `.omp` → `.claude` → `.codex` → `.gemini`; user OMP base is `~/<PI_CONFIG_DIR>/agent` (default `~/.omp/agent`), project bases are `<cwd>/.omp`, `<cwd>/.claude`, `<cwd>/.codex`, `<cwd>/.gemini`; `.pi` is deliberately not in the order.

features.name: config-file-lookup
features.what: `findConfigFile(subpath, opts)` / `findConfigFileWithMeta(...)` scan the ordered bases from `getConfigDirs` and return the FIRST existing file (path only, or path + source/level metadata); used for single-file lookups such as `SYSTEM.md`, `APPEND_SYSTEM.md`, `TITLE_SYSTEM.md`.

features.name: nearest-ancestor-config-dirs
features.what: `findAllNearestProjectConfigDirs(subpath, cwd)` walks parent directories upward and returns the NEAREST existing directory per source base (one each for `.omp`, `.claude`, `.codex`, `.gemini`), then sorts the results by source priority; used where project config must be inherited from ancestors (monorepo/nested workspaces).

features.name: named-profiles
features.what: `omp --profile <name>`, `OMP_PROFILE`, or legacy `PI_PROFILE` relocates the OMP user base from `~/.omp/agent/...` to `~/.omp/profiles/<name>/agent/...` uniformly across native discovery and the generic helpers (commands, rules, prompts, instructions, hooks, tools, extensions, settings, skills, MCP, `SYSTEM.md`/`RULES.md`/`AGENTS.md`) plus runtime state (sessions, blobs, `agent.db`); `OMP_PROFILE` wins even when explicitly empty; `default`/empty/whitespace selects the default profile; a profile never sees the default profile's agent config; named profiles ignore `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`; external (`~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.gemini`) and project bases are not profile-scoped; `--alias <command>` paired with `--profile` creates a shell shortcut and does not by itself select a profile.

features.name: keybindings-profile-merge
features.what: Keybindings are the single profile-inheritance exception: a named profile loads the default profile's `~/.omp/agent/keybindings.yml` first and overrides it action-by-action from `~/.omp/profiles/<name>/agent/keybindings.yml`; the inherited default file is read-only during profile startup (legacy-format migration of it only runs when the default profile itself runs). File is a flat YAML mapping of action ID → chord string or array of chord strings; `keybindings.json` is accepted and migrated to `.yml`, `.yaml` accepted; unqualified legacy action names are migrated on load; bindings are never read from `config.yml`.

features.name: agent-dir-env-overrides
features.what: `PI_CONFIG_DIR` changes the config-root dirname under home (default `.omp`) and therefore the OMP base used by the generic helpers; `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` fully relocates the agent directory for the DEFAULT PROFILE ONLY — it moves `getAgentDir()` consumers (native discovery, settings, `config.yml`, `agent.db`, runtime state) but does NOT change the generic `getConfigDirs()`/`findConfigFile()` OMP base; `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` overrides the initial session directory at launch-argument parse time; `omp config path` prints the active agent directory.

features.name: xdg-path-relocation
features.what: On macOS/Linux an existing `$XDG_DATA_HOME/omp`, `$XDG_STATE_HOME/omp`, or `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/omp` relocates the corresponding data/state/cache paths; for a named profile a category is used only when it already contains `omp/profiles/<name>`, otherwise that category stays under `~/.omp/profiles/<name>`. `omp config init-xdg` creates the `omp` directories under the effective XDG homes; it does not move existing files and does not set the env vars; non-Linux/macOS exits non-zero.

features.name: config-file-loader
features.what: `ConfigFile<T>` is the schema-validated single-file loader: accepts `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.json`, `.jsonc`; validates parsed data against an omptype schema; caches the load result until `invalidate()`; `tryLoad()` returns a tri-state result `ok` | `not-found` | `error` where error is a `ConfigError` carrying schema/parse context.

features.name: json-to-yaml-migration
features.what: When a `.yml`/`.yaml` path is requested and only a sibling `.json` exists, the loader auto-migrates it to YAML once (idempotent, once per process, `migrateJsonToYml`); explicitly-requested `.json`/`.jsonc` configs are read as-is with no migration.

features.name: settings-layer-precedence
features.what: Effective settings are built as `schema defaults <- global config <- project config <- PI_CONFIG_FILES overlays <- --config overlays <- runtime overrides`; within either overlay list later files override earlier ones; a key unset at every layer resolves to its schema default at read time.

features.name: deep-merge-semantics
features.what: Layer combination is a deep merge: objects merge key-by-key (lower-layer-only keys survive); scalars AND arrays are replaced wholesale by the higher-precedence layer — a higher layer's array never appends to a lower layer's array (`disabledProviders`, `enabledModels`, `cycleOrder`, `extensions`, every array key).

features.name: global-settings-store
features.what: Global settings are the first present of `~/.omp/agent/config.yml` and `config.yaml`; `config.yml` is the canonical write target while an existing `config.yaml` is loaded and updated in place; the file must be a YAML mapping at top level; a missing file is treated as empty configuration.

features.name: project-settings-discovery
features.what: Project settings come from the settings capability: native `<cwd>/.omp/settings.json` first, then `<cwd>/.omp/config.yml` merged on top, admitted only when `<cwd>/.omp/` exists and is non-empty; discovery does NOT walk ancestor directories; other discovery providers (claude, codex, gemini, cursor, opencode) may also contribute project-level settings; only capability items with `level === "project"` are merged into the project layer; all project settings are read-only from the settings API.

features.name: settings-capability-merge-order
features.what: The settings capability performs NO dedup (all provider items are preserved); `Settings.#loadProjectSettings()` deep-merges the returned items in order and providers are visited highest→lowest priority, so a LOWER-priority provider's project settings override a higher-priority provider's; afterwards native `.omp/config.yml` model roles are reapplied as the authoritative project model-role layer.

features.name: cli-config-overlays
features.what: Repeatable `--config <file>` overlays and the `PI_CONFIG_FILES` platform path-list (`:` on Unix, `;` on Windows) are loaded as `config.yml`-style YAML for one process only and never persisted; env-list overlays load in listed order BEFORE explicit `--config` overlays; paths are `~`-expanded and resolved relative to the active project/working directory; each overlay is strict — a missing file, invalid YAML, or a non-mapping (array/scalar) document root is a hard startup error with no fallback, and overlay files are never quarantined; `--config` is accepted by the default launch command, `acp`, and `models`.

features.name: runtime-override-layer
features.what: Highest-precedence in-memory, non-persistent layer fed by dedicated CLI flags and feature env vars: `--model`, `--smol`, `--slow`, `--plan`, `--approval-mode`, `--auto-approve`/`--yolo`, `--hide-thinking`, `--advisor`, `--no-pty`, `--api-key`, `--thinking`, `--service-tier`, `--no-lsp`, and protocol-mode defaults; never written back to `config.yml`.

features.name: broken-settings-quarantine
features.what: Invalid global or native-project settings YAML is moved to a unique `.broken-<timestamp>-<pid>-<uuid>` sibling under a file lock and startup then fails reporting BOTH the original and backup paths; a file that cannot be read fails without being moved; a missing file is empty config; `--config`/`PI_CONFIG_FILES` overlays are never quarantined.

features.name: debounced-locked-settings-write
features.what: `settings.set(...)` writes only to the global layer (the global YAML file selected at startup) and queues a debounced background save; the save re-reads the file under a lock before writing so external edits made while a session is open are preserved; project settings and config overlays are not writable through the settings API.

features.name: model-role-project-storage
features.what: `modelRoleStorage: global|project` (default `global`) selects where model-selector role assignments are persisted; `project` writes ONLY the changed role under `modelRoles` in `<cwd>/.omp/config.yml` (no other keys), and roles missing from the project file continue to fall back to global roles.

features.name: settings-schema
features.what: A single `SETTINGS_SCHEMA` declares every setting's dotted path, type (boolean/number/string/enum/array/record), default, enum values, description, tab grouping, and optional UI metadata; it is the sole source of defaults, of `omp config` validation, and of the `/settings` panel entries; keys must be matched exactly with no shorthand (`theme.dark`, never `theme`); groups include `modelRoles`/`modelTags`/`cycleOrder`/`enabledModels`/`disabledProviders`, `thinkingBudgets.*`, sampling (`temperature`/`topP`/`topK`/`minP`/`presencePenalty`/`repetitionPenalty` with `-1` = omit the parameter), `tier.*`, `retry.*`, `tools.*`, `bash.*`, `eval.*`, `python.*`, `lsp.*`, `edit.*`, `read.*`, `compaction.*`, `memory.*`, `autolearn.*`, `theme.*`, `statusLine.*`, `terminal.*`/`images.*`/`tui.*`, `steeringMode`/`followUpMode`/`interruptMode`/`ask.*`, `providers.*`, `advisor.*`, `task.*`, `skills.*`, `commands.*`, `mcp.*`, `ttsr.*`, `startup.*`, `secrets.*`, `bashInterceptor.*`, `computer.*`.

features.name: omp-config-cli
features.what: `omp config list|get <key>|set <key> <value>|reset <key>|path|init-xdg`; bare `omp config`, `--help`, `-h` list settings; `--json` accepted by list/get/set/reset; `list` prints every setting grouped by tab with value and type (JSON form: object keyed by setting path with `{value,type,description}`); `get` prints one effective value and exits non-zero on an unknown key (JSON `{key,value,type,description}`); `set` parses and writes to the global YAML; `reset` writes the schema default; `path` prints the active agent directory.

features.name: config-value-parsing
features.what: `omp config set` trims the value string and parses it against the target key's schema type: boolean accepts `true|false|yes|no|on|off|1|0` case-insensitively and rejects anything else; number accepts any finite JS number and rejects `Infinity`/`NaN`; enum must match a listed value exactly and the error enumerates valid values; array must parse as a JSON array; record must parse as a non-array JSON object; string is stored as given with multi-word values joined by spaces. Individual keys may add extra validation (e.g. `providers.maxInFlightRequests` rejects non-positive/non-numeric values).

features.name: credential-redaction-in-config-output
features.what: Configured credential-typed fields are masked as `********` in human `omp config list` output and in `--json` list output their `value` is omitted while `redacted: true` is emitted; `omp config get <key>` is an explicit single-key request and returns the credential unmasked.

features.name: legacy-settings-migration
features.what: Startup migration runs only when NEITHER `config.yml` nor `config.yaml` exists: read `~/.omp/agent/settings.json` (renamed to `settings.json.bak` after a successful parse), merge with legacy settings persisted in `agent.db` (DB values win conflicts), write the merged result to `config.yml`; afterwards legacy sources are never consulted. Field-level migrations in `#migrateRawSettings()` run on EVERY raw settings load (global, project, overlays, runtime overrides): `queueMode`→`steeringMode`; `ask.timeout` ms→seconds when the value looks like ms (`>1000`); flat `theme: "<name>"`→`theme.dark`/`theme.light` chosen by luminance (built-in `light`/`dark` dropped to defaults); `inspect_image.enabled` bool→`inspect_image.mode` (`on`/`off`); `task.isolation.enabled`→`task.isolation.mode: auto|none`; `task.simple` removed; legacy isolation modes `worktree|fuse-overlay|fuse-projfs`→`rcopy|overlayfs|projfs`; `lastChangelogVersion`→marker file (stripped from `config.yml`); plus removed edit/compaction modes, `inlineToolDescriptors`, status-line segments, provider/search settings (`providers.webSearch`→head of `providers.webSearchOrder`, `providers.image`→head of `providers.imageOrder`), memories/hindsight settings, and nested-leaf renames. Legacy names `skills.enablePiUser`/`skills.enablePiProject` remain live gates for the `native` skill source.

features.name: path-scoped-array-settings
features.what: Only `enabledModels` and `disabledProviders` accept path-scoped entries alongside bare strings; a scoped entry accepts any combination of the path keys `path`, `paths`, `pathPrefix`, `pathPrefixes` and the value keys `models` (enabledModels) / `providers` (disabledProviders) / `values` / `items`; the entry applies when the cwd IS the configured path or is under it, with `~` expanded and relative paths resolved before matching; only string values are kept and malformed scoped entries are silently ignored; scoping is resolved AFTER the layer merge against the final effective array.

features.name: disabled-providers-namespace
features.what: `disabledProviders` is one shared id namespace gating two subsystems before any credential check: model-provider ids (`anthropic`, `openai`, `google`, `groq`, `ollama`, `openrouter`, …) remove the backend from model selection even with valid credentials; discovery-source ids (`native`, `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `github`, `opencode`, `cursor`, `agents`, `agents-md`) remove the ENTIRE config source — context files, MCP servers, slash commands, skills, hooks, tools, prompts and settings. Ids are exact and the namespaces do not collide (`google` = model backend, `gemini` = Gemini CLI discovery). Default `[]`.

features.name: capability-provider-registry
features.what: All non-core config loading flows through a capability registry: providers auto-register with a numeric priority and are sorted descending (native 100, omp-plugins 90, claude 80, agents/codex/claude-marketplace 70, gemini 60, opencode 55, cursor 50, windsurf 50, cline 40, github 30, agents-md 10, builtin-defaults 1); equal priority preserves registration order (cursor before windsurf); each capability defines `key(item)` and dedup is first-wins (skills `name`, tools `name`, hooks `${type}:${tool}:${name}`, extension modules `name`, extensions `name`, settings `undefined` = no dedup); shadowed items stay in `all` marked `_shadowed` and are excluded from `items`; `loadCapability(id, { cwd })` also returns `warnings`.

features.name: native-provider-admission-rules
features.what: The `native` provider (id `native`, priority 100) reads project `<cwd>/.omp/...` and user `~/.omp/agent/...` with per-scope admission: slash commands, directory rules, prompts, instructions, hooks, tools, extensions, extension modules and settings require the root directory to exist AND be non-empty; skills bypass that rule and scan `<ancestor>/.omp/skills/*/SKILL.md` for every ancestor from cwd up to repo-root/home plus `~/.omp/agent/skills/*/SKILL.md`; MCP bypasses it and reads project `.omp/mcp.json` then `.omp/.mcp.json` then user `mcp.json` then `.mcp.json` directly; `SYSTEM.md`, `RULES.md` and `.omp/AGENTS.md` read the user file directly and take the project file from the NEAREST non-empty ancestor `.omp` directory. Scope globs: `commands/*.md`, `rules/*.{md,mdc}`, `prompts/*.md`, `instructions/*.md`, `hooks/pre/*`, `hooks/post/*`, `tools/*.{json,md,ts,js,sh,bash,py}` and `tools/<name>/index.ts`, `extensions/` modules (+ legacy `settings.json.extensions` string array), `extensions/<name>/gemini-extension.json`, `settings.json` then `config.yml`.

features.name: dotenv-cascade
features.what: `$env` resolves a key in order: existing process env (`Bun.env`) → project `.env` in the launch cwd → active agent `.env` (`~/.omp/agent/.env`) → active config-root `.env` (`~/.omp/.env`) → home `~/.env`; each dotenv source fills ONLY keys whose current value is empty/unset; agent/root locations respect profiles, `PI_CONFIG_DIR`, and (default profile only) `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`; dotenv names must be shell identifiers `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` and unsafe names/values are discarded; the parser keeps values literal with no expansion.

features.name: omp-pi-env-alias-mirroring
features.what: Within each PARSED dotenv file every `OMP_*` key is mirrored to its `PI_*` alias and that mirrored value replaces a same-file `PI_*` value; the mirroring never applies to variables inherited from the parent process.

features.name: env-feature-overrides
features.what: Environment variables are NOT a settings layer: each is read by the owning feature as a per-machine override/fallback and is never written back to `config.yml`. Direct setting overrides: `PI_SMOL_MODEL`/`PI_SLOW_MODEL`/`PI_PLAN_MODEL` (`modelRoles.*`, CLI flag wins), `PI_NO_PTY=1` (`--no-pty`), `PI_PY`/`PI_JS`/`PI_RB`/`PI_JL` (`eval.*`), `PI_TINY_DEVICE`/`PI_TINY_DTYPE` (`providers.tinyModel*`), `OMP_AUTH_BROKER_URL`/`OMP_AUTH_BROKER_TOKEN` (`auth.broker.*`, env wins), `PI_INTENT_TRACING` (`tools.intentTracing`), `PI_EDIT_VARIANT`/`PI_STRICT_EDIT_MODE` (`edit.mode`), `OMP_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS`, `GEMINI_SEARCH_MODEL` (`providers.webSearchGeminiModel`), `SEARXNG_*` (`searxng.*` are primary, env is fallback), and the full `HINDSIGHT_*` table (env over `hindsight.*` over built-in default; strings trimmed with empty ignored, booleans true only for `true`/`1`/`yes` case-insensitively, integers base-10 `parseInt` unclamped with non-numeric ignored, enums exact-match with invalid ignored).
features.surface: env vars listed in environment-variables.md §5 and §2

features.name: system-prompt-file-customization
features.what: `SYSTEM.md` and `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` are discovered project-scope-first then user-scope, each scope ordered `.omp`, `.claude`, `.codex`, `.gemini`, with NO ancestor walk; `--system-prompt` and `--append-system-prompt` beat every discovered file. A single-line value is first tried as a file path and used literally when the path does not exist or is too long; a value containing a newline is always literal; other read failures log and fall back to literal. `SYSTEM.md` sets `customSystemPrompt`, which switches the rendered template from `system-prompt.md` to `custom-system-prompt.md` — keeping custom+append text, context files, skills, always-apply rules, rulebook listing, secret-redaction guidance, the project/environment footer and conditional extra blocks, while dropping the default template's role text, tool inventory/policy, internal-URL catalog and workflow rules. Append placement: without `SYSTEM.md` at the end of `project-prompt.md`; with it, immediately after the custom text. SDK-generated append content is combined before user append text. All four inputs are plain text inserted into Handlebars templates and are never recursively compiled.

features.name: title-prompt-override
features.what: `TITLE_SYSTEM.md` in any generic config base overrides ONLY the automatic session-title system prompt (initial titles and replan-driven refreshes), leaving `SYSTEM.md`/`APPEND_SYSTEM.md` untouched; discovery checks the cwd project bases first then the user bases in generic order with no ancestor walk; missing file keeps the bundled title prompts; the online path appends a wrap-in-`<title>...</title>` instruction after the override and parses leniently (plain sentence, truncated/unclosed tag, stray `{"title": "..."}` echo); the local tiny-title path keeps the `<title>` prefill/stop wrapper and uses the file as its system turn. Output normalization is enforced regardless of prompt: only the first trimmed line, strip surrounding quotes, `<title>` markers and terminal punctuation, treat `none`/`<title/>` as no-title, and REJECT (never truncate) results over 80 characters or 12 words — empty/deferred/rejected leaves the session unnamed so a later attempt can name it.

features.name: context-file-discovery
features.what: Markdown instruction files are auto-discovered per provider convention and injected as project context: `native` `~/.omp/agent/AGENTS.md` (user) + `<nearest-non-empty-ancestor>/.omp/AGENTS.md` (project); `claude` `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` + `<cwd>/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (no walk-up); `codex` `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (user only); `gemini` `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` + `<cwd>/.gemini/GEMINI.md` (no walk-up); `opencode` `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` (user only); `github` `<cwd>/.github/copilot-instructions.md` + `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` (relocatable via `COPILOT_HOME`) plus `AGENTS.md` candidates from `COPILOT_CUSTOM_INSTRUCTIONS_DIRS` at user scope; `agents` `~/.agent`/`~/.agents` plus project `.agent`/`.agents` walking to repo root; `agents-md` standalone `AGENTS.md` walking cwd→repo root and, for repos under home, through enclosing workspace dirs up to but not including home (with no repo root, home is the boundary and its file is included), ignoring files whose parent directory name starts with `.`. Native project discovery stops at the FIRST non-empty `.omp/` found walking upward; a missing file there does not continue the walk; empty directories and empty files contribute nothing.

features.name: context-file-dedup-ordering
features.what: Discovered context files are deduplicated by scope: exactly ONE user-level file survives across all providers (native wins, so `~/.omp/agent/AGENTS.md` shadows every other user file); ONE project file per directory depth measured from cwd (cwd = depth 0, parent = 1; an ancestor's config subdirectory counts as that ancestor's depth); at equal depth the higher-priority provider shadows the rest; across depths multiple files survive; byte-identical files are collapsed AFTER ordering with the project copy closest to cwd surviving, and the single user file sorts after project files so it survives ties on identical content. Final injection order is farther project ancestors → nearer project files → surviving user file.

features.name: context-file-injection
features.what: With the default prompt template, surviving context files are injected as one `<repo-rules>` block containing one `<file path="/abs/path">…</file>` element per file in sort order, with fully expanded Markdown; when `SYSTEM.md` selects the custom template the same files render in its `<project>`/`<instructions>` section; deeper-directory `AGENTS.md` files that were not auto-loaded are surfaced separately in a `<dir-context>` block that lists their paths as pointers (not content) and instructs the model to read them before editing those directories.

features.name: at-import-expansion
features.what: Inside any context file an `@path` token expands inline to the target's content before injection: relative paths resolve from the IMPORTING FILE's directory (not cwd), `~`/`~/` resolve to home, absolute paths used as-is; tokens inside fenced code blocks and inline code spans are left literal; a token only counts when `@` is at line start or preceded by a space/tab, so `git@github.com:org/repo.git` and `user@example.com` are never imports; trailing sentence punctuation `. , ; : ! ? ) ] } " '` is trimmed from the path; imports recurse up to five hops; files already in the current expansion tree are skipped so cycles terminate; a missing or unreadable target leaves the original `@token` text in place rather than erroring.

features.name: sticky-rules-file
features.what: A top-level native `RULES.md` — read ONLY from the active user agent directory and from the nearest non-empty project `.omp/` selected by the cwd→repo-root walk — is synthesized as a rule named `RULES` with `alwaysApply: true` forced (frontmatter cannot make it non-sticky), so its full content is re-attached near the current turn instead of loading as a context file; because rule dedup is name-based, user sticky content normally shadows project sticky content (never concatenated) and a regular `rules/RULES.md` loaded earlier can shadow both.

features.name: rule-frontmatter-parsing
features.what: `parseFrontmatter` parses YAML frontmatter only when content starts with `---` and has a closing `\n---`, then trims the body; if whole-document YAML parsing fails it logs a warning and falls back to a simple line parser `^([\w-]+):\s*(.*)$`, re-parsing each captured value independently as YAML so one-line flow values (`[text, thinking]`) still survive while individually malformed values remain raw trimmed strings; multiline arrays and nested objects are NOT reconstructed by the fallback; hyphenated keys are normalized to camelCase (`thinking-level`→`thinkingLevel`) on both the YAML and fallback paths; files without valid frontmatter still load as rules with empty metadata and the full body.

features.name: rule-provider-normalization
features.what: Every rule source normalizes into the canonical `Rule { name, path, content, globs?, alwaysApply?, description?, condition?, astCondition?, scope?, interruptMode?, _source }` via `buildRuleFromMarkdown`, with `name` = filename minus `.md`/`.mdc`. Sources: `native` (project `<cwd>/.omp/rules/*.{md,mdc}` when `.omp/` non-empty, user `<agent-dir>/rules/*.{md,mdc}`, user `RULES.md`, nearest project `RULES.md`, appended in that order); `omp-plugins` (`rules/*.{md,mdc}` per configured extension package root); `agents` (project walk `<ancestor>/.agent(s)/rules/*` then user `~/.agent(s)/rules/*`); `cursor` (user `~/.cursor/rules/*.{mdc,md}` then project `<cwd>/.cursor/rules/*`, `alwaysApply` true only for literal `alwaysApply: true`, `description` kept only if a string, `globs` from string-element array or single string); `windsurf` (user `~/.codeium/windsurf/memories/global_rules.md` fixed name `global_rules`, then project `<cwd>/.windsurf/rules/*.md`); `cline` (nearest `.clinerules` upward — directory → `*.md`, file → single rule named `clinerules`); `github` (`*.instructions.md` recursively from `<cwd>/.github/instructions/` then each comma-separated `COPILOT_CUSTOM_INSTRUCTIONS_DIRS` entry, name = filename minus `.instructions.md`, `applyTo` comma-string/YAML array → `globs`, `*`/`**`/`**/*` → always-apply with globs cleared, any other glob → non-always with a generated description when missing, missing `applyTo` → rulebook description plus a discovery warning); `builtin-defaults` (embedded source order).

features.name: rule-bucketing
features.what: After discovery, `bucketRules(...)` filters and assigns in fixed order: (1) drop rules listed in `ttsr.disabledRules`; (2) drop `builtin-defaults` rules when `ttsr.builtinRules === false`; (3) register rules with a non-empty `condition` or `astCondition` into `TtsrManager` — if registration is accepted the rule is TTSR-ONLY; (4) remaining `alwaysApply === true` → always-apply bucket (full content injected into the system prompt); (5) remaining rules with a `description` → rulebook bucket (name+description listed, content read on demand). A rule with both a condition and `alwaysApply` falls through to always-apply only if TTSR registration was rejected; a rule with both `alwaysApply` and `description` goes to always-apply only.

features.name: ttsr-trigger-metadata-parsing
features.what: `condition` is the regex TTSR trigger (legacy `ttsr_trigger`/`ttsrTrigger` accepted) and a leading `(?i)`, `(?m)`, or `(?s)` inline flag group is translated into the equivalent JS `RegExp` flags; `astCondition` is a string or YAML sequence of ast-grep structural patterns kept verbatim, matching only edit/write tool streams with the language inferred from the file path; a rule may set either or both. `scope` accepts a comma-separated YAML string or a YAML sequence with tokens `text`, `thinking`, `tool`/`toolcall`, and `tool:<name>(<path-glob>)`; omitting it watches assistant prose and all tool arguments but NOT thinking; the parser tolerates the malformed fallback spelling `scope: "text","thinking"`. A `condition` token that looks like a file glob is rewritten into `tool:edit(<glob>)` + `tool:write(<glob>)` scope entries plus catch-all condition `.*` (never applied to `astCondition`). `globs` acts as a global path gate for TTSR matching. `interruptMode` (`never|prose-only|tool-only|always`) overrides the global TTSR interrupt mode per rule.

features.name: rule-protocol-url
features.what: `setActiveRules([...rulebookRules, ...alwaysApplyRules, ...ttsrManager.getRules()])` installs a process-global active-rule snapshot once per top-level session; `rule://<name>` resolves by EXACT name match against that union and returns raw `rule.content` (frontmatter stripped) as `text/markdown`; an unknown name errors with a list of available rule names; a rule with no description, no `alwaysApply`, and no accepted TTSR condition is not addressable.

features.name: always-apply-injection-dedup
features.what: Always-apply rule bodies are deduped against the effective system/custom/append prompt sources and the loaded context-file bodies — a rule whose normalized content already appears there is omitted from automatic injection; the rest render before the rulebook listing (inside `<generic-rules>` in the default template, directly in the custom template). Rulebook rules render as `- <name> (<globs>): <description>` inside `<domain-rules>` in the default template and as `<rule name="…"><glob>…</glob></rule>` entries under an explicit "You MUST read `rule://<name>`" instruction in the custom template. Glob applicability is advisory prompt text and is not code-enforced.

features.name: approval-tiers-and-modes
features.what: Every tool may declare an approval tier `read` (reads data / UI-only session metadata), `write` (mutates workspace/session state without executing arbitrary code) or `exec` (executes code, shells out, drives a browser, spawns agents); tools with no declaration and malformed decisions are treated as `exec`; MCP server tools declare `write`. `tools.approvalMode` (default `yolo`) selects the tier matrix: `always-ask` auto-approves `read` and prompts for `write`/`exec`; `write` auto-approves `read`+`write` and prompts for `exec`; `yolo` auto-approves all tiers. `--approval-mode <mode>`, `--auto-approve` and `--yolo` override for the session.

features.name: approval-resolution-algorithm
features.what: Per tool call: (1) evaluate `tool.approval(args)` — omitted/malformed decisions default to tier `exec`; (2) a tool-declared `policy: deny` always denies, then a user `tools.approval.<tool>: deny` always denies; (3) in `yolo` an explicit tool `allow`/`prompt` policy wins, otherwise a valid user policy wins, otherwise allow — a bare `override: true` alone does NOT force a prompt in yolo; (4) in non-yolo modes an `override: true` decision allows only when accompanied by tool `policy: allow`, every other non-denied case prompts; (5) without an override an explicit tool `allow`/`prompt` wins, then a valid user policy; (6) with no explicit policy the active mode decides by tier. Policy strings are trimmed and case-normalized and invalid user values are ignored.

features.name: bash-approval-patterns
features.what: `bash.patterns` is an ordered list of `{ match, approval }` rules (literal text plus `*` wildcard, approvals `allow|prompt|deny`) evaluated first-match-wins for bash calls: `deny` and `prompt` rules fire when the glob matches the whole command OR any single segment of a compound line (split on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, a single `&`, subshells and newlines) so `rm -rf *` still denies `cd /tmp && rm -rf build`; `allow` rules must match the ENTIRE command and never apply to a compound line, so `git *` cannot vouch for `git status && rm -rf /`; an `allow` match explicitly allows at the `write` tier. The built-in critical-command guard (`rm -rf /`, fork bombs, remote-fetch-then-execute, writes to `/etc/passwd`, host shutdown) still forces confirmation unless a matching rule explicitly denies, and broad `match: "*"` allow rules do not bypass it.

features.name: bash-interceptor-config
features.what: `bashInterceptor.enabled` (opt-in) plus `bashInterceptor.patterns[{ pattern, tool, message }]` redirects matching Bash commands to a dedicated tool instead of governing whether they may run: `pattern` is a regular expression, `tool` names the replacement tool and `message` is shown to the model; if the named replacement tool is not available in the current session the interceptor does not block the Bash call. This is orthogonal to `bash.patterns` permission policy.

features.name: tool-approval-declaration-api
features.what: Built-in and custom tools share one shape: `approval?: ToolApprovalDecision | ((args:unknown)=>ToolApprovalDecision)` where a decision is a `ToolTier` string or `{ tier, reason?, override?, policy? }` with `policy: allow|deny|prompt`; `formatApprovalDetails?: (args)=>string|string[]|undefined` adds prompt body lines. The standard prompt renders `Allow tool: <name>`, `Origin: MCP server tool` for unannotated `mcp__...` tools, `Reason: <reason>` when supplied, and tool-specific details (command, path, code, browser action, subagent assignment).

features.name: computer-approval-safety
features.what: The disabled-by-default `computer` tool derives its tier from the call's `read_only` argument: `true` → `read`; `false`, a missing field, malformed arguments, or any other value → `exec`; the prompt shows `read-only` when applicable followed by the submitted JavaScript truncated to 2,000 characters. Separately, provider-originated computer-use calls carrying `pendingSafetyChecks` force an interactive prompt regardless of yolo, per-tool `allow`, or an already-approved `xd://` dispatch, listing each check's code, message and sanitized/truncated data; with no interactive UI the call fails closed with `pending provider safety checks but no interactive UI is available`.

features.name: acp-approval-routing
features.what: `omp acp` uses the identical settings resolver — global `~/.omp/agent/config.yml`, project config for the ACP session cwd, and `--config` overlays passed to the ACP process — with normal precedence (runtime flags > overlays > project > global) and supports `--yolo`/`--auto-approve`/`--approval-mode`; ACP defines no per-session approval field. Explicitly-configured or flag-supplied `tools.approvalMode: yolo` skips OMP prompts AND the ACP client permission gate for `bash`, `edit`, `delete`, `move` unless `tools.approval.<tool>` is `prompt`/`deny`, while the schema-default yolo still keeps the client gate. Required approvals route through the ACP client: client-gated tools use `session/request_permission`, generic prompts use form elicitation when the client advertises `elicitation.form`, and a rejected/cancelled/unsupported prompt rejects or cancels the tool call rather than silently allowing it.

features.name: subagent-approval-policy
features.what: Subagents run headless with `tools.approvalMode: yolo` so tier-based prompts cannot stall them, and the parent `task` tool approval is the authorization boundary; user `tools.approval.<tool>` settings remain authoritative inside the subagent — `deny` blocks the tool, `allow` permits it, and `prompt` cannot be satisfied headlessly and therefore rejects the call.

features.name: install-id
features.what: `getInstallId()` returns a persistent per-install lowercase RFC 4122 UUID stored as a single line (trailing `\n`) at `<base-config-root>/install-id` (`~/.omp/install-id`, honoring `PI_CONFIG_DIR`) resolved against the base config root regardless of active profile so every profile shares one ID; file mode `0o600`; existing values are accepted case-insensitively against `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`/i and returned exactly as stored; a new value comes from `crypto.randomUUID()` and is written with `open(O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL, 0o600)` so a concurrent loser sees `EEXIST`, re-reads and adopts the winner's ID; non-empty garbage is `unlink`ed before the exclusive create; any other write failure is swallowed while the generated UUID is still cached in memory; the value is cached in-process for the runtime lifetime; `__resetInstallIdCacheForTests()` is test-only. Lifecycle is independent of `~/.omp/agent/` — wiping agent state does not regenerate it.

features.name: settings-ui-panel
features.what: The in-session `/settings` panel reads merged effective settings and exposes the subset of schema entries that carry UI metadata (grouped by tab), writing changes through the same global-layer write path as `omp config set`.

features.name: mcp-server-config-model
features.what: Defines the authoring/runtime server shape: top-level `$schema`, `mcpServers` map, `disabledServers`, `enabledServers`; per-server `type` (`stdio` default when omitted | `http` | `sse`), stdio `command`/`args`/`env`/`cwd`, remote `url`/`headers`, shared `enabled`, `timeout` (ms, `0` = no client timeout), `requestIdFormat` (`number`|`string`), `auth`, `oauth`.

features.name: mcp-config-validation
features.what: `validateServerConfig()` rejects: both `command` and `url` set, stdio without `command`, http/sse without `url`, unknown `type`; emits `Server "<name>": stdio server requires "command" field` / `both "command" and "url" are set`; validation is structural only (no reachability check).

features.name: mcp-config-json-schema
features.what: Ships a published JSON Schema for editor autocomplete/validation, referenced via `$schema: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/.../mcp-schema.json`; its `propertyNames` pattern omits `:` even though the runtime accepts it.

features.name: mcp-config-writer
