features.what: Atomic add/update/remove of servers in OMP-owned files (temp file + rename), validating server names (non-empty, ≤100 chars, `[a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]` where `:` allows namespaced plugin names) and re-running `validateServerConfig()`; auto-injects the `$schema` line on any write; errors `Invalid server config: ...` and `Server "<name>" already exists in <path>`.

features.name: native-mcp-config-discovery
features.what: Reads OMP-native MCP config directly (no non-empty-root admission helper) in fixed order: project `.omp/mcp.json`, `.omp/.mcp.json`, then user `mcp.json`, `.mcp.json`; writes always target the primary `mcp.json` paths.

features.name: profile-scoped-user-mcp-config
features.what: When a named profile is active (`omp --profile <name>`, `--alias`, `OMP_PROFILE`/`PI_PROFILE`), the user scope resolves to `~/.omp/profiles/<name>/agent/mcp.json` and the default `~/.omp/agent/mcp.json` becomes invisible; discovery, `/mcp` commands, and the writer all follow it. Project config and foreign-tool configs stay profile-independent.

features.name: standalone-mcp-json-fallback-provider
features.what: Lowest-priority provider reading project-root `mcp.json` then `.mcp.json`; expands `${...}` placeholders and type-checks `enabled`/`timeout` without coercing string forms; applies the same `requestIdFormat` validation.

features.name: foreign-tool-mcp-config-import
features.what: Translates third-party MCP configs into canonical servers: Claude Code (`~/.claude.json`, `~/.claude/mcp.json`, `.claude/.mcp.json`, `.claude/mcp.json`), Codex TOML `[mcp_servers.*]` (`~/.codex/config.toml`, `.codex/config.toml`), Gemini CLI (`~/.gemini/settings.json`, `.gemini/settings.json`), OpenCode (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `opencode.json`), Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`), Windsurf (`~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`, `.windsurf/mcp_config.json`), VS Code project-only `.vscode/mcp.json` via `mcp.servers`. `requestIdFormat` is ignored from these sources; each source is individually suppressible via the discovery-source disable list.

features.name: capability-provider-priority-dedupe
features.what: Loads MCP providers in descending priority (native → OMP extension packages → Claude Code → Claude marketplace plugins & Codex → Gemini CLI → OpenCode → Cursor & Windsurf → VS Code → root `mcp.json`/`.mcp.json`), dedupes by `server.name` first-win (never merges), then validates; also shadows a differently-named definition whose transport, endpoint/command inputs, auth, and request-id mode are equivalent to a higher-priority one.

features.name: mcp-env-placeholder-expansion
features.what: At discovery time expands `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` recursively over string values in `command`, `args`, `env`, `cwd`, `url`, `headers`, `auth`, and `oauth`; unresolved placeholders stay literal. Applies to OMP-native files, root fallback files, and OMP extension packages only.

features.name: mcp-field-coercion-and-warnings
features.what: Native config accepts boolean/string `enabled` (`true`/`false`/`1`/`0`) and numeric-string `timeout`; `requestIdFormat` accepts only `"number"`/`"string"` and other values warn and fall back to numeric ids; invalid `enabled`/`timeout` values are warned and ignored rather than failing the file.

features.name: user-enable-disable-overrides
features.what: Active-profile user file supplies cross-source `disabledServers` (highest-precedence denylist, hides a same-named server from any source regardless of its `enabled`) and `enabledServers` (force-enables a source entry with `enabled: false`); `disabledServers` wins when a name is in both.

features.name: mcp-project-config-toggle
features.what: `mcp.enableProjectConfig: false` drops every entry whose `_source.level === "project"` before deduplication, letting a same-named user entry survive.

features.name: builtin-overlap-server-filtering
features.what: `loadAllMCPConfigs({ filterExa: true, filterBrowser })` removes Exa MCP servers and extracts their API keys for the native Exa integration — unless the config requests Exa tools the native path lacks (`web_fetch_exa`, `web_search_advanced_exa`) — and removes browser-automation MCP servers when the built-in browser tool is enabled (`browser.enabled`).

features.name: pre-connect-value-resolution
features.what: Resolves stdio `env` and http/sse `headers` values immediately before connect: value starting with `!` runs as a shell command with a 10s timeout using trimmed stdout (successful results cached process-wide); failed/timed-out/whitespace-only commands omit that entry entirely; otherwise the whole value is treated as an env-var name and, if set non-empty, replaced by the env value, else used literally.

features.name: mcp-oauth-credential-binding
features.what: Resolves managed OAuth per server: honors an explicit/legacy `auth.credentialId` when it resolves; accepts a managed `mcp_oauth:profile:<profile>:<url>` id only when that profile is active and the URL matches the expanded or literal server URL; otherwise falls back to profile-scoped URL-keyed credential ids derived from expanded and literal URLs. Injects `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` for http/sse and `OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN` env for stdio. A case-insensitive explicitly configured `Authorization` header suppresses the URL-keyed fallback; stdio ignores URL-keyed ids; no credential means connect without injection.

features.name: mcp-oauth-authorization-flow
features.what: Runs an OAuth authorization-code flow for http/sse servers with endpoint discovery, a loopback callback listener defaulting to port `3000` and path `/callback` (overridable by `oauth.callbackPort`/`callbackPath`; an HTTP loopback `redirectUri` supplies its own port/path; an HTTPS loopback redirect needs a distinct `callbackPort`), `oauth.clientId`/`clientSecret`, and a `prompt` parameter that is omitted by default except when `offline_access` is requested (then `"consent"`); `""` forces omission. Stores refresh material in profile auth storage (local `agent.db` or auth broker) without touching the config file. Errors: `Authentication required ... OAuth endpoints could not be discovered`, `OAuth flow timed out. Please try again.`, `OAuth authentication failed: ...`.
features.surface: `/mcp reauth <name>` / `/mcp unauth <name>`; `oauth` block in server config

features.name: mcp-oauth-refresh-retry
features.what: For manager-managed HTTP-like OAuth servers, an outbound request (and best-effort server-request response) that returns HTTP 401/403 triggers one token refresh and, when refresh yields replacement headers, exactly one retry; refresh/resolution failures are logged and the existing access token is kept.
features.surface: `onAuthError` hook wired by `MCPManager` into HTTP/SSE transports

features.name: transport-abstraction
features.what: `MCPTransport` exposes `request(method, params, options?)`, `notify(method, params?)`, `close()`, `connected`, plus optional `onClose`/`onError`/`onNotification`/`onRequest`; `createTransport()` picks stdio when `type` is omitted or `"stdio"`, Streamable HTTP for `"http"`, legacy HTTP+SSE for `"sse"`.

features.name: request-id-allocator
features.what: Each transport owns a `RequestIdAllocator` producing monotonically increasing integers starting at `1` by default; `requestIdFormat: "string"` switches to collision-resistant snowflake strings. IDs are transport-local correlation tokens only.

features.name: mcp-timeout-resolution
features.what: Per-request timeout precedence is `OMP_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS` (process-wide) → per-server `timeout` → `30000` ms; `0` disables client-side timeouts entirely (AbortSignal never fires); invalid env values are logged and ignored. Caller `AbortSignal`s are merged with `AbortSignal.any([...])` and AbortError handling distinguishes caller abort from timeout.

features.name: stdio-transport
features.what: Spawns the configured `command`/`args`/`env`/`cwd`, frames newline-delimited JSON on stdin/stdout, correlates via `#pendingRequests: Map<id,{resolve,reject}>`, reads stdout with a JSONL loop, reads and discards stderr, drops malformed lines and continues, ignores unknown response ids silently, and on close/exit marks disconnected, rejects all pending with `Transport closed`, fires `onClose`, kills the subprocess, and detaches the read loop without awaiting.

features.name: streamable-http-transport
features.what: POSTs JSON-RPC with a generated id; parses either a single JSON response or a `text/event-stream` response (returning the first event whose id matches and carries `result`/`error`, then draining the rest in background); stores and re-sends `Mcp-Session-Id`; `close()` best-effort `DELETE`s the session and ignores failures; `notify()` POSTs without `id` and accepts any 2xx including `202`; non-OK responses throw `HTTP <status>: <text>` with `WWW-Authenticate`/`Mcp-Auth-Server` hints appended; JSON-RPC errors throw `MCP error <code>: <message>`; unmatched SSE termination throws `No response received for request ID ...`.

features.name: http-background-sse-listener
features.what: Optional GET SSE listener for server-initiated notifications and server-to-client requests, started after `initialize` (so it inherits the session id) and before `notifications/initialized`; startup waits up to 1s (less for very small request timeouts, disabled entirely when timeout is `0`); a `405`, other non-OK status, missing body, or startup timeout silently disables it; listener errors fire `onError` (except AbortError) and an established listener ending while connected fires `onClose` so the manager can reconnect. The transport never restarts it itself.

features.name: legacy-sse-transport
features.what: Implements protocol revision 2024-11-05 HTTP+SSE: `GET` the configured URL with `Accept: text/event-stream`, treat the first `endpoint` event's plain-text data as a URL/path resolved against the configured URL, POST all JSON-RPC frames there, and read responses/notifications/server-requests from `event: message`; when the stream ends, pending requests fail with `Legacy SSE stream closed`.

features.name: server-to-client-request-handling
features.what: Inbound frames carrying both `method` and `id` are answered as server-to-client requests via `onRequest`; `connectToServer()` always installs a handler serving `ping` and `roots/list`; any other method (or a transport with no handler) is answered with JSON-RPC `-32601 Method not found`. Frames with `method` and no `id` are notifications.

features.name: mcp-initialize-handshake
features.what: `connectToServer()` creates the transport, sends `initialize` with protocol version `2025-03-26` advertising the `roots` capability, then (HTTP/SSE only) starts the background SSE listener, then sends `notifications/initialized`, and only then issues method calls; init failure closes the transport.

features.name: mcp-client-operations
features.what: Client-side MCP method wrappers over a live connection: `tools/list`, `tools/call`, plus best-effort post-connect `resources/list`, resource-templates list, `prompts/list`, and optional resource subscriptions; failures here are logged, never fatal.

features.name: direct-jsonrpc-helper
features.what: Standalone `callMCP()`/`parseSSE()` helpers for one-off HTTP MCP calls (used by Exa/web-search paths): parse the whole response text then extract the first `data: ` line with a JSON fallback, optional caller `AbortSignal` with a hard 60s `AbortSignal.timeout` default, no session-id or lifecycle handling, returning the raw JSON-RPC envelope.

features.name: manager-state-registries
features.what: `MCPManager` keeps `#connections`, `#pendingConnections`, `#pendingToolLoads`, `#pendingReconnections`, `#tools` (stable name order), `#sources`, `#serverConfigs` (unresolved), `#reconnectHistory` + `#epoch`, notification listener state; `getConnectionStatus(name)` returns `connected` when in `#connections`, `connecting` for any pending connect/tool-load/reconnect, else `disconnected`.

features.name: parallel-connect-fast-startup-gate
features.what: `connectServers()` starts every server's connect + `tools/list` in parallel and races completion against `STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 250`; after the gate it returns live tools for fulfilled tasks, a per-server `errors` map for rejected ones, and leaves still-pending servers in flight instead of blocking startup.

features.name: mcp-tool-definition-cache
features.what: Persists per-server tool definitions (`MCPToolCache.set` after each successful list, best-effort) so a still-pending server at the startup gate can expose `DeferredMCPTool`s immediately; those tools call `waitForConnection(server)` before dispatching `tools/call`.

features.name: late-background-tool-registration
features.what: Each pending tool-load promise carries a background continuation that replaces that server's tool slice, restores stable name ordering, writes cache, and fires `#onToolsChanged` so a live session rebinds late tools; late failures are logged only after the startup gate (`allowBackgroundLogging`).

features.name: transport-close-reconnect
features.what: Managed connections wire `transport.onClose` to `reconnectServer(name)`, which tears down the stale connection, re-resolves auth/env/header values from the saved unresolved config, retries with backoff `500, 1000, 2000, 4000` ms, reloads tools, keeps stale tools visible while reconnecting, and notifies tool/prompt consumers on success; also reachable explicitly via `/mcp reconnect <name>`.

features.name: reconnect-circuit-breaker
features.what: Per-server crash-window accounting suspends automatic reconnects after more than 5 reconnect invocations within 30s — the stale connection is closed/removed but its tools stay registered; a manual `/mcp reconnect` resets the history.

features.name: notification-fanout-and-buffer
features.what: Server notifications are first handled internally (`notifications/tools/list_changed` → refresh tools, `notifications/resources/list_changed` → refresh resources, `notifications/resources/updated` → only for currently subscribed URIs, `notifications/prompts/list_changed` → refresh prompts) and then fanned out to every listener registered via `addNotificationListener()` (returns an unsubscribe fn, per-listener error isolation). With no listener attached the manager buffers up to 100 frames dropping the oldest, then drains the FIFO into the first listener that attaches.

features.name: disconnect-teardown-ownership
features.what: `disconnectServer(name)` clears pending connect/tool-load/reconnect entries, source metadata, saved config, reconnect history and subscription/refresh state, detaches `onClose` before closing, removes tools by exact `mcpServerName` owner, and notifies tool/prompt consumers. `disconnectAll()` bumps the lifecycle epoch, detaches all `onClose` handlers, closes with `Promise.allSettled`, and clears every registry. Sessions own managers they create (disconnected on `AgentSession.dispose()` with a 3s bounded cleanup); a session given `options.mcpManager` borrows and never disconnects it.

features.name: mcp-tool-name-mapping
features.what: Generates agent tool names as `mcp__<sanitized_server>_<sanitized_tool>`: lowercase, non-`[a-z_]` → `_`, repeated underscores collapsed, and a redundant leading `<server>_` inside the tool name stripped once.

features.name: mcp-tool-name-collision-dedupe
features.what: `deduplicateMCPToolsByName()` runs before registry insertion; when distinct origins sanitize to the same runtime name it picks the winner by lexicographic comparison of the original `<server-name>\0<tool-name>` origin key, logs the collision, and omits the loser — so reconnect/discovery order can never change ownership.

features.name: mcp-input-schema-normalization
features.what: Every MCP `inputSchema` is passed through `normalizeSchemaForMCP()` (shared option-driven JSON Schema 2020-12 upgrade/deref/walk: snake_case→camelCase combinator keys, nullable-union collapse, unsupported-key stripping with human-meaningful keys spilled into `description`, combiner collapsing) before it is registered as a `CustomTool` schema.

features.name: outbound-argument-normalization
features.what: Before any `tools/call`, arguments are normalized in strict order: (1) non-object/`null`/array top-level values become `{}`; (2) the harness-injected `i` field is removed unless the MCP schema's `inputSchema.properties` declares `i`; (3) a schema-declared but non-`required` property whose value is `undefined`, empty string, or empty non-array object is omitted, while required props, undeclared props, `0`, `false`, `null`, and arrays (including `[]`) are preserved; (4) strings are walked recursively through nested objects/arrays and a resolvable `local://` file URL is rewritten to the real filesystem path (left as-is with no resolver or when it denotes a directory/root; invalid/missing/escaping URLs fail normalization instead of reaching the server).

features.name: mcp-tool-execution-mapping
features.what: `MCPTool.execute()`/`DeferredMCPTool.execute()` call `tools/call`, flatten MCP content into displayable text, return structured details (`serverName`, `mcpToolName`, provider metadata), map server `isError: true` to an `Error: ...` text result, attempt reconnect + exactly one retry on retriable connection errors, map remaining transport/runtime failures to `MCP error: ...` content, and translate AbortError into `ToolAbortError`.

features.name: mcp-tool-auth-challenge-handler
features.what: A structured auth challenge inside a tool result invokes the configured auth handler, then reconnects and retries the call once; interactive mode wires this to the `/mcp` OAuth controller, and with no handler installed the challenge surfaces as an ordinary MCP error.

features.name: mcp-tool-approval-integration
features.what: MCP server tools declare `approval: "write"`; approval prompts show `Origin: MCP server tool` for unannotated `mcp__...` tools, and per-tool rules can allow/deny by exact generated name (e.g. `mcp__filesystem__delete: deny`).

features.name: sdk-mcp-startup-wiring
features.what: `createAgentSession()` runs MCP startup when `enableMCP` is true (default): headless/SDK awaits `discoverAndLoadMCPTools(cwd, ...)` and merges results into `customTools`; interactive (`hasUI: true`) constructs the manager up front, defers `discoverAndConnect()` to a background task, then binds via `session.refreshMCPTools(...)` (disposing the manager if the session died mid-connect). Both pass `authStorage`, cache storage, `mcp.enableProjectConfig`, `filterExa: true` and browser filtering, log per-server errors, and store the manager on `toolSession.mcpManager`. `discoverMCPServers()` wraps this and returns `{ manager, tools, errors, connectedServers, exaApiKeys }`; loaded tools get path `mcp:<server> via <providerName>`. Restricted sessions (`restrictToolNames: true`) disable ambient MCP by default.

features.name: live-mcp-tool-rebinding
features.what: `session.refreshMCPTools(mcpTools)` removes every `mcp__` registry entry, re-wraps the latest MCP tools, and re-activates the tool set (rebuilding the system prompt) so tool changes apply without restarting; it is driven by `/mcp reload`, late initial connects, `tools/list_changed`, reconnects, and disconnects through `setOnToolsChanged`.

features.name: discovery-failure-isolation
features.what: A hard discovery exception yields an empty tool set plus one synthetic error `{ path: ".mcp.json", error }`; invalid configs, connect/init timeouts, tool-list failures, cache writes, resource/prompt loads, and subscriptions are all per-server best-effort with entries in the `errors` map, so no MCP failure aborts session startup.

features.name: mcp-command-controller
features.what: Interactive `/mcp` with subcommands `list` (shows originating config file), `add` (wizard + quick-add flags; `Use either --url or -- <command...>, not both.`, `--token requires --url (HTTP/SSE transport).`), `remove`/`rm`, `enable`, `disable`, `test <name>`, `reauth`/`unauth`, `reconnect <name>`, `reload`, `resources`, `prompts`, `notifications`. `enable`/`disable` edit `enabled` directly in OMP-owned writable files and otherwise maintain the user allow/denylist (removing conflicting stale overrides). `#reloadMCP()` = `disconnectAll()` → clear stale MCP prompt commands → `discoverAndConnect()` with the same project/Exa/browser filters → `refreshMCPTools()`; `/mcp reconnect` does one final refresh after the per-server reconnect.

features.name: mcp-prompt-slash-commands
features.what: MCP server prompts are published as slash commands resolved in the TypeScript/MCP custom-command stage (after built-ins/skills/extension commands, before file commands, first-wins), and stale prompt commands are cleared on reload and on server disconnect.

features.name: smithery-registry-integration
features.what: `/mcp` exposes Smithery search/login/logout for discovering and installing hosted MCP servers, using `SMITHERY_URL` (default `https://smithery.ai`), `SMITHERY_API_URL` (default `https://api.smithery.ai`), and `SMITHERY_API_KEY` for managed MCP auth lookup.

features.name: subagent-mcp-proxy-tools
features.what: When a parent passes `mcpManager` into a child session, the child skips standalone MCP discovery and receives proxy tools that dispatch through the parent's existing connections with `MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000`; the child never disconnects the borrowed manager.

features.name: extension-mcp-notification-event
features.what: A per-session listener bridges every MCP notification to the extension runner's `mcp_notification` event with payload `{ server, method, params }`, delivered after the manager's internal handling of known list/update methods and including unknown/server-custom methods; multiple extension handlers are supported and a throwing handler does not block the others. The runner has its own bounded startup buffer, and the listener/debounce timers are released in session postmortem cleanup.

features.name: mcp-internal-url-scheme
features.what: `read` routes `mcp://` (alongside the other built-in internal schemes) through `InternalUrlRouter`, and MCP servers may advertise additional URL schemes that the router then resolves for reads.

features.name: plugin-extension-mcp-contribution
features.what: Installed marketplace plugins, npm/linked plugins, and OMP extension packages contribute MCP servers: the `omp-plugins`/`claude-plugins` providers scan `.mcp.json` under enabled plugin roots, and a manifest `mcpServers` field (inline map or in-plugin path, read from `.omp-plugin/plugin.json` first then `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`) replaces the default `.mcp.json` rather than merging. Catalog-level `mcpServers` metadata is preserved but is not runtime config; refreshing after install requires `/reload-plugins`.

features.name: native-addon-loader
features.what: loadNative() computes mode/platformTag/variant/filenames, builds an ordered de-duplicated candidate list (first occurrence wins), require()s each in order, and returns the first validated binding; no JS memoization (relies on require cache), post-load setup is idempotent/best-effort.

features.name: platform-tag-and-target-matrix
features.what: Platform tag is `${process.platform}-${process.arch}`; supported publish tags are linux-x64, linux-arm64, darwin-x64, darwin-arm64, win32-x64; an unsupported tag is only reported after candidate probing fails.

features.name: x64-cpu-variant-selection
features.what: x64 only: PI_NATIVE_VARIANT=modern|baseline wins (invalid values ignored), else valid inherited __PI_NATIVE_VARIANT_CACHE, else AVX2 detection (Linux /proc/cpuinfo; macOS /usr/sbin/sysctl then sysctl on machdep.cpu.leaf7_features/machdep.cpu.features; Windows non-interactive PowerShell System.Runtime.Intrinsics.X86.Avx2) via Bun.spawnSync then node:child_process; result written back to the private env cache. Non-x64 neither uses nor populates a variant.

features.name: addon-filename-fallback-chain
features.what: getAddonFilenames() returns modern x64: `-modern.node`,`-baseline.node`,unsuffixed; baseline x64: `-baseline.node`,unsuffixed; non-x64: unsuffixed only. Each filename is probed across every candidate directory.

features.name: version-sentinel-validation
features.what: Install/compiled candidates must export a sentinel function named `__piNativesV<version_with_dots_as_underscores>` (e.g. __piNativesV17_2_5) derived from package.json#version; workspace-development candidates skip the check. The loader validates only this sentinel, never the full export set.

features.name: loader-failure-diagnostics
features.what: Unsupported tag throws `Unsupported platform: <tag>` + supported list + issue guidance; supported tag throws `Failed to load pi_natives native addon for <tag>` (incl. x64 variant) plus every candidate/preparation error and mode-specific help (compiled: cache paths, delete versioned dir, release curl commands; installed: reinstall + local Bazel build commands). Sentinel mismatch is diagnosed as 'restart' when the resident exports are older but the candidate bytes contain the expected sentinel, otherwise 'reinstall'.

features.name: post-load-runtime-install-hook
features.what: After require + sentinel validation the loader calls addon `__ompInstallTokioRuntime()` when present, which installs bounded Windows Tokio/Rayon pools; absent hook or hook failure falls back to napi-rs defaults and is best-effort (surfaced only in startup markers).

features.name: platform-leaf-optional-packages
features.what: Installed non-compiled loads probe `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives-<platform>-<arch>` for every selected filename before package-local native/ and the process.execPath directory; workspace loads deliberately skip leaf resolution so local artifacts win.

features.name: compiled-mode-detection
features.what: Compiled mode is true when a populated embedded manifest exists, PI_COMPILED is set, or import.meta.url contains a Bun embedded marker ($bunfs, ~BUN, %7EBUN). A non-compiled nativeDir outside any node_modules path segment is workspace mode (Windows path matching case-insensitive, elsewhere case-sensitive).
features.surface: env PI_COMPILED; embedded-addon.js manifest; import.meta.url markers

features.name: natives-cache-directory-resolution
features.what: getNativesDir() is `$XDG_DATA_HOME/omp/natives` only when `$XDG_DATA_HOME/omp` already exists, otherwise `~/.omp/natives`; versionedDir = `<nativesDir>/<packageVersion>`; legacy compiled dir = `%LOCALAPPDATA%/omp` (or ~/AppData/Local/omp) on Windows and `~/.local/bin` elsewhere. Compiled candidate order is versionedDir, legacy dir, package nativeDir, execPath dir (per filename).

features.name: embedded-addon-manifest-extraction
features.what: In compiled mode with matching platformTag+version, the loader selects a file (non-x64: `default` then first; modern x64: modern then baseline; baseline x64: baseline only), reuses already-correct-size regular files, else gunzips/parses `embedded-addons.<tag>.tar.gz` accepting only manifest-allowlisted basename-only regular entries with declared sizes, writing temp-file+rename into versionedDir; a successful extraction is prepended to the candidate list and errors are accumulated without aborting.

features.name: windows-node-modules-addon-staging
features.what: On win32, non-compiled, with a node_modules segment in nativeDir, maybeStageNodeModulesAddon() copies each available filename from leafPackageDir ?? nativeDir into versionedDir when missing (existing cache files retained), then probes versionedDir first, then leaf, then package/exec dirs; copy/mkdir failures are recorded and probing continues. Disabled in compiled mode.

features.name: stale-version-cache-gc
features.what: After a successful load, best-effort delete cache directories under nativesDir whose name parses as a semantic version strictly older than the current package version; current, future, prerelease/non-semver names and ordinary files are preserved and all read/delete failures ignored.

features.name: startup-debug-markers
features.what: PI_DEBUG_STARTUP emits synchronous `[startup] native:…` markers to stderr around loader entry, embedded extraction, each candidate load, and Tokio runtime installation (including hook success/failure).

features.name: eager-root-and-lazy-subpath-entrypoints
features.what: Three exports: `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives` (native/index.js, loads addon at module evaluation and binds every generated class/function/enum), `/desktop` (createDesktopSession(options), addon load deferred to invocation), `/clipboard` (copyToClipboard/readImageFromClipboard + ClipboardImage type, deferred). Unexported native/* paths are not package API; lazy wrappers exist only for deferred loading, never for renaming.

features.name: binding-declaration-and-enum-codegen
features.what: `build:bindings` runs the napi CLI against crates/pi-natives, installs the host addon + generated native/index.d.ts, then gen-enums.ts rewrites napi-rs `const enum` declarations to runtime-usable form and replaces the marked block in native/index.js with explicit class/function exports and literal enum runtime objects (AstMatchStrictness, Ellipsis, Encoding, FileType, GrepOutputMode, IsoBackendKind, IsoChangeKind, KeyEventType, MacOSAppearance, ProcessStatus). Only top-level `export declare class|function|enum` items become root ESM exports; index.js/index.d.ts are committed.

features.name: bazel-native-addon-build
features.what: Eight //:natives-<target> addon targets built by a `native_addon` rule whose configuration transition pins --platforms, --compilation_mode=opt, thin LTO, -Ccodegen-units=16 -Cstrip=symbols, then symlinks the rust_shared_library to the canonical pi_natives.<tag>[-variant].node under bazel-bin/natives-<t>/; per-target rustc_flags selects supply -Ctarget-cpu=x86-64-v2|v3, napi link args, musl -crt-static and win32 +crt-static/static_link_msvcrt. Hermetic toolchains: zig cc glibc 2.17 floor, zig musl, host Xcode for darwin, clang-cl+lld-link+xwin for win32.

features.name: bazel-natives-driver-script
features.what: Single driver: accepts //:natives-* names plus pseudo-targets host/linux-all/darwin-all, runs one bazel build, locates outputs via `bazel cquery --output=files` (falling back to the bazel-bin/natives-<t>/ path convention), copies dereferenced into --dest (default packages/natives/native), forwards args after `--` to bazel, resolves bazelisk|bazel from PATH, honors OMP_BAZEL_RC as --bazelrc, streams stderr with a 40-line failure tail, and hard-errors on a basename collision within one run (gnu vs musl).
features.surface: bun scripts/bazel-natives.ts <target>... [--dest <dir>] [--source <dir>] [-- <bazel args>]; bun --cwd=packages/natives run build

features.name: embedded-archive-generation
features.what: embed-native.ts computes the platform tag (overridable for cross-target archives), collects modern+baseline (x64) or the single default file from packages/natives/native, requires at least one to exist, writes native/embedded-addons.<tag>.tar.gz plus native/embedded-addon.js carrying version, archive metadata and per-file sizes; `--reset` writes `embeddedAddon = null` without validation and deletes existing archives.
features.surface: bun run gen:native / bun run gen:native:reset; scripts/embed-native.ts

features.name: platform-leaf-package-generation
features.what: Release publishing generates `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives-<platform>-<arch>` leaf packages from the authoritative LEAF_TARGETS list, strips .node files from the published core package, and injects the leaves as lockstep same-version optionalDependencies.

features.name: orchestrator-natives-build-cache
features.what: Content-addressed cross-worktree cache of built addons keyed by sha256 over ordered (path, git-tree-hash) pairs for crates, Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml, rust-toolchain.toml, packages/natives plus the target triple (<platform>-<arch>[-TARGET_VARIANT|host] on x64); hit requires the pi_natives.*.node glob AND index.d.ts/index.js/embedded-addon.js/manifest.json; populate hardlinks the .node and copies companions, capture copies under a per-repo flock into an atomically renamed staging dir, and a periodic GC drops oldest-by-captured_at beyond entry/byte caps.

features.name: native-task-scheduling
features.what: Two schedulers: task::blocking(tag, cancel_token, work) wraps napi AsyncTask/Task so compute() runs on libuv workers and returns Promise<T>, catching panics before they cross the async-work FFI boundary; task::future(env, tag, work) wraps env.spawn_future returning PromiseRaw for Tokio async orchestration. Both record a profile_region(tag) sample. CPU/blocking work uses blocking; awaiting I/O uses future.

features.name: cancel-token-and-abort-bridge
features.what: CancelToken::new(timeoutMs, AbortSignal) wraps pi_shell::cancel::CancelToken and bridges a JS AbortSignal to AbortReason::Signal via emplace_abort_token(); heartbeat() is the cooperative check for blocking loops, wait() awaits signal-or-deadline for futures, aborted() is a non-blocking check, into_core() transfers ownership to pi-shell, abort_token() returns a live handle only when a flag already exists (otherwise inert). AbortReason ∈ {Unknown, Timeout, Signal, User}.

features.name: cancellation-reporting-contract
features.what: Two mutually exclusive per-family contracts: blocking exports reject with `Aborted: Timeout` / `Aborted: Signal` from heartbeat()?, while shell/PTY command APIs resolve a typed result with exitCode omitted and cancelled|timedOut set. Domain errors are prefixed by stage (spawn/decode/wait) via Error::from_reason.
features.surface: rejected Error message vs `{ exitCode?, cancelled, timedOut }`

features.name: work-profiling-ring-buffer
features.what: profile_region(tag) guards inside task::blocking/task::future record stack path, duration and timestamp into a fixed 10,000-sample circular buffer on guard drop; getWorkProfile(lastSeconds) returns { folded, summary, svg?, totalMs, sampleCount } where folded is flamegraph input and summary is a markdown table; SVG failure is soft (omitted) and an empty window returns empty folded data, not an error.

features.name: crash-handler-init
features.what: Rust module initialization installs crash diagnostics only; it must not create Tokio runtimes, Rayon pools or any worker threads because it runs while the dynamic-loader lock is held.

features.name: filesystem-grep
features.what: grep(options, onMatch?) returns Promise<GrepResult> and streams shaped GrepMatch objects; branches to in-memory-free single-file (path resolved, metadata must be a file) or directory discovery via pi-walker with .cache(false); directory entries are filtered file-only plus optional glob filter and optional type filter (js, ts, rust, …); rejects on hard errors such as invalid path, timeout or abort.
features.surface: grep(options: GrepOptions, onMatch?: (err, match) => void): Promise<GrepResult>

features.name: in-memory-search-and-has-match
features.what: search(content, options) runs the regex over a provided string/Uint8Array and returns SearchResult with an `error` field instead of throwing; hasMatch(content, pattern, ignoreCase?, multiline?) returns a boolean and returns false on matcher failure. Neither touches the filesystem or the scan cache.
features.surface: search(content, options), hasMatch(content, pattern, ignoreCase?, multiline?)

features.name: regex-engine-selection-and-pcre2
features.what: Matcher construction tries the Rust regex engine first, then PCRE2 for lookaround/backreferences; OMP_PCRE2_JIT=0|false disables PCRE2 JIT, 1 enables it, and when unset JIT is enabled everywhere except macOS.

features.name: malformed-pattern-tolerance
features.what: Before compiling, braces that cannot form {N}/{N,}/{N,M} are escaped to \{ \} (so `${platform}` works); a compile failure for an unclosed/unopened group triggers one targeted retry escaping unmatched parentheses while preserving the rest; if both engines still reject, the entire original pattern is escaped and searched literally so grep never surfaces a regex compile error.

features.name: grep-output-modes-and-budgets
features.what: GrepOutputMode content emits one GrepMatch per hit; count and filesWithMatches emit count-style entries with lineNumber=0, line="" and matchCount set. contextBefore/contextAfter override legacy `context` and are not collected in non-content modes; maxColumns truncates matched lines at character boundaries with `...` (not ANSI- or cell-width aware); offset and maxCount apply globally across sorted per-file results while maxCountPerFile caps one hot file; limitReached is emitted only when true and skippedOversized counts files skipped above the 4 MiB limit; unreadable/non-regular files are silently skipped. Small ordered callback streams may stop early, larger ones use a bounded ordered window.
features.surface: GrepOptions{ ignoreCase, maxCount, maxCountPerFile, contextBefore, contextAfter, maxColumns, offset, timeoutMs }, GrepResult{ limitReached?, skippedOversized }

features.name: glob-file-discovery
features.what: glob(options, onMatch?) with required pattern and path resolves the root, compiles the pattern via glob_util, sources entries from a fresh scan (cache=false default) or the shared walker cache, always skips .git, skips node_modules unless includeNodeModules or the pattern mentions node_modules, applies the glob match and a file-type filter (symlink file/dir filters resolve target metadata), optionally sorts by mtime descending, then truncates to maxResults.
features.surface: glob(options: GlobOptions{ pattern, path, cache?, includeNodeModules?, sortByMtime?, maxResults?, timeoutMs?, signal? }, onMatch?)

features.name: fuzzy-path-find
features.what: fuzzyFind(options) walks with the same opt-in cache policy (default false), scores exact / starts-with / contains / subsequence plus a separator-and-punctuation-normalized path, adds a directory bonus, sorts deterministically by score desc then path asc, and excludes symlink entries entirely.

features.name: glob-pattern-normalization
features.what: glob_util::build_glob_pattern normalizes `\` to `/`, auto-prefixes simple recursive patterns with `**/` when recursive=true, and auto-closes unbalanced `{...` alternation groups before compile_glob; a still-invalid pattern returns a compile error.

features.name: parallel-ignore-aware-walker
features.what: pi-walker resolves relative roots against cwd, requires an existing directory and canonicalizes it, then collects normalized forward-slash relative CollectedEntry values (path, fileType, plus mtime and regular-file size at WalkDetail::Full) under WalkOptions (hidden/gitignore, .git and node_modules pruning, symlink policy, metadata detail, per-directory order, root emission, min/max depth, contents-first, directory-error policy, same-filesystem) with cancellation delivered through the caller-supplied heartbeat; WalkRequest applies WalkFilter, ranking and limits after collection. Rayon pool size is PI_WALK_WORKERS (default 4, 0 = auto-detect, 1 = serial) and helper operations parallelize only at >=256 items.

features.name: fs-scan-cache
features.what: Process-local DashMap of owned CollectedEntry lists keyed by canonicalized root plus the complete effective WalkOptions with only the `cache` bit cleared (follow_links IS in the key; post-collection filters, ranking and limits are NOT, though size-hint/max-file-size policy can promote detail to Full and thereby repartition). TTL=0 bypasses and reports cache_age_ms=0; a hit younger than FS_SCAN_CACHE_TTL_MS clones the stored vector and reports its age; expired entries are removed and refreshed; after insertion entries beyond FS_SCAN_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES are evicted oldest-first by creation time; cache=false scans fresh without reading, populating or evicting.

features.name: empty-result-revalidation
features.what: EmptyRecheck::Configured retries a walk exactly once when (1) the first collection was a nonzero-age cache hit, (2) the post-WalkFilter result is empty, and (3) cache age >= FS_SCAN_EMPTY_RECHECK_MS (threshold 0 disables); the retry runs uncached and never replaces or evicts the existing entry. EmptyRecheck::Never disables it and AfterMillis(n) supplies a per-request threshold. Only WalkFilter-stage emptiness triggers it, so fuzzyFind's post-collection scoring cannot.

features.name: fs-scan-cache-invalidation
features.what: invalidateFsScanCache() clears all entries; invalidateFsScanCache(path) removes every entry whose cached root is a prefix of the target, resolving relative paths against cwd and canonicalizing the target (falling back to canonicalizing the parent and reattaching the filename when the path no longer exists, so create/delete/rename all work). Consumer helpers invalidateFsScanAfterWrite/Delete/Rename wrap it; rename invalidates both sides when different.

features.name: workspace-listing
features.what: listWorkspace(options) enumerates the workspace inside task::blocking("listWorkspace", ct, …) with CancelToken from timeoutMs+signal and heartbeat checks during traversal.

features.name: ast-search-match-edit
features.what: astGrep(options) returns matches with byte/line/column coordinates and optional metavariable bindings; astMatch(options) runs the same patterns against an in-memory `source` with required `lang` and returns matches/totalMatches/limitReached/parse errors but no file-count fields; astEdit(options) returns replacement changes, per-file counts, searched/touched file counts, parse errors and whether edits were applied, with dryRun defaulting to true. Options cover language override, path/glob/selector, strictness, limits, parse-error policy, signal and timeoutMs; a directory path always uses the shared scan cache for discovery while a direct file path bypasses traversal and the cache entirely.

features.name: block-boundary-analysis
features.what: blockRangeAt and enclosingBlockBoundaries synchronously compute syntactic block ranges/boundaries for a position in source.

features.name: code-summarization
features.what: summarizeCode produces a structural code summary (declaration-level outline) for supported languages.

features.name: language-registry
features.what: pi-ast owns the tree-sitter/ast-grep grammar registry, matching/editing and block/summary support across the workspace grammar set; its language metadata is re-exported from crates/pi-natives/src/lib.rs.

features.name: ansi-text-layout-utilities
features.what: Synchronous terminal-cell utilities with an explicit tabWidth parameter on every width-sensitive call: wrapTextWithAnsi(text, width, tabWidth) wraps by visible width carrying active SGR codes across lines; truncateToWidth(text, maxWidth, ellipsis, pad, tabWidth) truncates by visible cells with Ellipsis ∈ {Unicode, Ascii, Omit} and optional right padding; sliceWithWidth(line, startCol, length, strict, tabWidth); extractSegments(line, beforeEnd, afterStart, afterLen, strictAfter, tabWidth) restores ANSI state for the after segment; visibleWidth(text, tabWidth). All are grapheme-aware and ANSI-sequence aware.
features.surface: wrapTextWithAnsi, truncateToWidth, sliceWithWidth, extractSegments, visibleWidth; Ellipsis enum

features.name: hangul-jamo-width-override
features.what: setHangulCompatJamoWidthOverride(value) controls U+3131–U+318E width for client-terminal compatibility: 0 = platform fallback, 1 = force one cell, 2 = force two cells, 3 = follow Unicode width; it is process-global state affecting all subsequent width calculations.

features.name: syntax-highlighting
features.what: highlightCode(code, lang, colors) resolves a syntect syntax by token/name lookup, then extension lookup, then alias table, then plain-text fallback, parses each line with ParseState + scope stack, maps scopes to semantic color categories and injects/resets ANSI codes; a per-line parse failure appends that line unhighlighted and continues. supportsLanguage(lang) and getSupportedLanguages() expose the registry. Pure in-memory, no filesystem access.

features.name: token-counting
features.what: countTokens(input, encoding?) accepts a single string or an array of strings and returns ONE aggregate count (array elements encoded in parallel via rayon); default encoding is O200kBase with Cl100kBase also available; uses encode_ordinary (no special-token handling) with BPE tables initialized once via LazyLock.

features.name: structured-diff
features.what: Synchronous diff family: diffLines, diffWords, diffLineRuns and structuredPatchHunks producing structured hunk data for rendering and patch application.

features.name: vector-ranking
features.what: Synchronous typed-array vector primitives: cosineSimilarityPairs, mmrRerankIndices and vectorIndexTopK consuming/producing Float32Array/Float64Array/Uint32Array rather than ordinary arrays.

features.name: one-shot-and-persistent-shell
features.what: executeShell(options, onChunk?) creates and drops a fresh embedded-brush session per call; new Shell(options?) plus repeated shell.run(options, onChunk?) reuses a lazily created session. Both stream merged stdout/stderr text through a threadsafe callback and resolve `{ exitCode?, cancelled, timedOut, minimized?, workingDir? }`. shell.abort() aborts the instance's running command via the stored AbortToken and resolves successfully even when nothing is running.
features.surface: executeShell(options, onChunk?), new Shell(options?), shell.run(options, onChunk?), shell.abort()

features.name: shell-session-environment-model
features.what: brush_core::Shell is created with do_not_inherit_env:true followed by explicit reconstruction from host env, profile/rc loading skipped, bash-mode builtins with exec and suspend disabled, native sleep/timeout/nohup registered, a skip-list for shell-sensitive vars (PS1, PWD, SHLVL, bash function exports, …), and a non-exported `env="$env"` fallback so PowerShell-style `$env:NAME` survives parameter expansion unless shadowed. sessionEnv applies at session creation; ShellRunOptions.env is EnvironmentScope::Command and is popped after the command; PATH is merged with case-insensitive dedupe on Windows and enriched with discovered Git-for-Windows paths; snapshotPath is sourced at creation with stdout/stderr/stdin wired to null files.
features.surface: ShellOptions{ sessionEnv, snapshotPath, minimizer }, ShellExecuteOptions/ShellRunOptions{ command, cwd, env, timeoutMs, signal }; crates/pi-shell/src/windows.rs

features.name: shell-output-streaming-and-drain
features.what: stdout/stderr are routed into one shared pipe read concurrently, decoded as incremental UTF-8 emitting U+FFFD for invalid byte sequences, and forwarded as text chunks; the command runs under ProcessGroupPolicy::NewProcessGroup; after the foreground command completes the reader drains until EOF, 250ms of idle output, or 2s maximum, then reader shutdown gets a 250ms timeout. A successful result may carry workingDir reflecting the shell cwd after execution.

features.name: shell-output-minimizer
features.what: An optional minimizer configuration captures and rewrites command output; when minimization occurs the result carries `minimized` with filter name, replacement text, original text and byte counts. The native layer only carries the data — persisting or displaying artifacts is consumer policy.

features.name: shell-cancellation-and-descendant-cleanup
features.what: On timeout/abort the Tokio cancellation token fires, descendants started after the baseline process snapshot receive termination waves, the command task gets a 2-second graceful window before forced abort, and the persistent session is dropped if the lock can be acquired. Timeout resolves { timedOut: true } with exitCode omitted; abort signal or shell.abort() resolves { cancelled: true } with exitCode omitted. Session state machine: normal control flow keeps the session for reuse; loop/script/shell-exit control flow, cancellation, timeout and errors drop it.

features.name: background-job-accounting
features.what: shell.liveBackgroundJobCount() silently reaps completed jobs and returns the number of live `&`/`nohup` children, letting a host keep a per-call shell alive while background children run.

features.name: embedded-shell-builtins
features.what: Every builtin the embedded shell installs: a patched fork of brush's POSIX/bash builtins plus one module per in-process command-line utility (cat, grep/rg, sed, ls, find, jq, fd, diff, ps, top, kill, the moreutils set, …) implementing a common `Utility` trait against a `Host` view exposing stdio, working directory, exported environment and cancellation; utility_builtins() and process_builtins() are the authoritative registries and pi-shell decides which to register.

features.name: pty-session
features.what: new PtySession() exposes start(options, onChunk?, onStart?) running a command string through a shell and startArgv(options, onChunk?, onStart?) running application+args with no shell parsing, both resolving { exitCode?, cancelled, timedOut } and invoking onStart(error, pid) after spawn (pid 0 only when unavailable); plus write(data), resize(cols, rows) and kill(). PtyStartOptions supports command, cwd?, env, timeoutMs, signal, cols, rows and shell (default `sh`); shell arg mapping is cmd|cmd.exe -> /c, powershell|pwsh -> -Command, otherwise -lc. Default size 120x40, clamped cols 20..400 and rows 5..200 on both start and resize. Starting while running returns `PTY session already running`; write/resize/kill when not running return `PTY session is not running`; a dead control channel returns `PTY session is no longer available`.
features.surface: new PtySession(); pty.start / startArgv / write / resize / kill

features.name: pty-windows-conpty-handling
features.what: On Windows openpty() runs on a helper thread with a 5s startup timeout rejecting with `PTY creation timed out (5s). ConPTY may be unavailable on this system.`; ConPTY input is closed before dropping the master, and master drop is offloaded to a background thread awaited up to 2s to avoid deadlock. Final reader drain is 500ms on Windows versus 50ms elsewhere.

features.name: pty-termination-and-drain
features.what: terminate_pty_processes targets the PTY process group when available and the child pid when available, sending the platform TERM_SIGNAL, then child.kill(), then the platform KILL_SIGNAL. The blocking loop calls ct.heartbeat() with a 16ms maximum wait cadence and classifies timeout by the heartbeat error string containing `Timeout`; cancellation/kill opens a 300ms post-cancel drain window and normal child exit a 300ms post-exit window before the final reader drain.

features.name: process-handle-api
features.what: Process.fromPid(pid) -> Process | null and Process.fromPath(path) -> Process[]; getters pid/ppid; args(), groupId(), children() -> Process[], status() -> running|exited; killTree(signal?) signals the process and descendants children-first (Windows ignores the signal and uses TerminateProcess); terminate(options?) is async with a 1000ms graceful phase and 5000ms post-hard-kill wait by default, gracefulMs<0 skipping the graceful phase and group:true also targeting the process group where supported; waitForExit(options?) resolves true on exit and false on timeout. Aborting the signal of terminate or waitForExit rejects the promise.
features.surface: Process.fromPid/fromPath; ProcessTerminateOptions{ group?, gracefulMs?, timeoutMs?, signal? }, ProcessWaitOptions{ timeoutMs?, signal? }; ProcessStatus enum

features.name: terminal-key-parsing
features.what: parseKey(data, kittyProtocolActive) normalizes to key IDs (ctrl+c, shift+tab, pageUp, f5, …) by combining direct single-byte mappings (enter, tab, ctrl+<letter>, printable ASCII), an O(1) PHF legacy escape-sequence map, xterm modifyOtherKeys parsing and Kitty protocol parsing (CSI u, CSI ~, CSI 1;…<letter>); matchesKey(data, keyId, kittyProtocolActive), parseKittySequence(data), matchesKittySequence(data, expectedCodepoint, expectedModifier) and matchesLegacySequence(data, keyName) round out the surface. Only shift/alt/ctrl/super bits are compared with lock bits masked out, and base-layout fallback is constrained so remapped layouts cannot create false matches for ASCII letters/symbols. Parse functions return null and match functions false on malformed input; nothing throws.
features.surface: parseKey, matchesKey, parseKittySequence, matchesKittySequence, matchesLegacySequence; KeyEventType enum

features.name: filesystem-isolation-backends
features.what: isoBackend/isoProbe/isoResolve/isoIsUnavailableError are synchronous probes while isoStart/isoStop/isoDiff are promise-based lifecycle/diff operations over pi-iso backends: APFS clone, Linux/Windows clone/reflink, overlayfs, ProjFS and a recursive copy fallback, with IsoBackendKind and IsoChangeKind enums shaping results.
features.surface: isoBackend, isoProbe, isoResolve, isoIsUnavailableError, isoStart, isoStop, isoDiff; crates/pi-iso

features.name: desktop-session
features.what: createDesktopSession(options) returns a DesktopSession providing screen capture, synthetic input and accessibility queries over Tokio-backed promise APIs, loaded lazily so importing the wrapper does not pull in the addon.

features.name: clipboard-access
features.what: copyToClipboard(text) is a synchronous arboard set_text call that keeps one process-lifetime Clipboard instance alive on Linux (to retain X11/Wayland selection ownership) and uses a transient instance per call on macOS/Windows; readImageFromClipboard() runs in task::blocking, resolves null/undefined when arboard reports ContentNotAvailable, converts clipboard RGBA to PNG on success returning { data: Uint8Array, mimeType: "image/png" }, and rejects on any other error. No OSC52/Termux fallback and no failure suppression exist natively.

features.name: audio-capture-playback
features.what: new AudioCapture(sampleRate, callback) opens the default microphone and delivers low-latency mono Float32Array PCM chunks at the requested logical rate with stop() releasing capture immediately; new AudioPlayback(sampleRate) opens the default speaker where write(samples) queues mono Float32Array PCM in order, setGain(gain) changes render-time gain even for already-queued samples, end() drains then closes, and stop() discards queued audio immediately.
features.surface: new AudioCapture(sampleRate, cb), new AudioPlayback(sampleRate); crates/pi-voice

features.name: live-webrtc-peer
features.what: new LiveWebRtcPeer(onEvent, onLevel, onFailure) owns a WebRTC peer: createOffer() returns SDP, acceptAnswer(sdp) applies the remote answer, waitForOpen(timeoutMs?) waits for the `oai-events` data channel, pushAudio() queues 16 kHz mono PCM, setMuted() controls transmission, and close() tears down media, data channel, peer and playback.

features.name: sixel-encoding
features.what: encodeSixel(bytes: Uint8Array, targetWidthPx, targetHeightPx) synchronously validates that both target dimensions are > 0 (else `Target SIXEL dimensions must be greater than zero`), guesses the format with ImageReader::with_guessed_format(), decodes to DynamicImage, resizes with resize_exact + FilterType::Lanczos3 only when source dimensions differ, converts to RGBA8, and returns the icy_sixel escape string; decode failure and `Failed to encode SIXEL: …` are hard errors with no JS fallback.

features.name: snapcompact-png-rendering
features.what: renderSnapcompactPng(text, options) renders pre-normalized text on a bounded bitmap and asynchronously resolves a base64-encoded PNG carried in an N-API Latin1String (not raw bytes); options.size is required with optional font, cellWidth, cellHeight, variant, lineRepeat, stretch and columns; output height hugs used rows and overflowing input is ignored. snapcompactSupportedChars(font, chars) synchronously returns only the characters the named bundled font supports.
features.surface: renderSnapcompactPng(text, options): Promise<string>, snapcompactSupportedChars(font, chars): string

features.name: html-to-markdown
features.what: htmlToMarkdown(html, options?) schedules task::blocking("html_to_markdown", (), …) with no cancel token, no timeout and no abort option; cleanContent defaults to false and when true enables PreprocessingPreset::Aggressive with remove_navigation=true and remove_forms=true; skipImages defaults to false; remaining recursive DOM traversal is capped at depth 64 and hitting the cap rejects with `Conversion error: …` rather than returning partial Markdown.
features.surface: htmlToMarkdown(html: string, options?: { cleanContent?: boolean; skipImages?: boolean }): Promise<string>

features.name: macos-appearance-detection
features.what: detectMacOSAppearance() returns "dark", "light", or null on non-macOS; MacAppearanceObserver.start(callback) returns a handle with stop(), using distributed notifications plus a 2-second polling fallback on macOS and a no-op observer elsewhere.

features.name: macos-power-assertion
features.what: MacOSPowerAssertion.start(options?) returns a handle with stop(); on macOS it acquires one or more IOKit assertions from { reason?, idle?, system?, user?, display? } and defaults to idle behavior when every boolean is unset or omitted; on other platforms it is a no-op handle.
features.surface: MacOSPowerAssertion.start({ reason?, idle?, system?, user?, display? })

features.name: devicecheck-token
features.what: deviceCheckGenerateToken() resolves within the native helper's one-second wait with { supported, tokenBase64?, error?, latencyMs }, reporting unsupported platforms/devices and generation failures inside the result rather than rejecting or requiring a token.
features.surface: deviceCheckGenerateToken(): Promise<{ supported, tokenBase64?, error?, latencyMs }>

features.name: file-lock
features.what: FileLock exposes cross-process advisory file locking as a stateful native class for coordinating concurrent harness instances.

features.name: native-port-benchmark-convention
features.what: Every ported hot path keeps a durable in-package benchmark that runs the JS baseline and the native implementation in the same process against identical prepared input, separating reusable setup from the timed operation and awaiting every call for promise-returning APIs; a native export that is slower or behaviorally different than the JS baseline is not an acceptable port.

features.name: memory-backend-selection
features.what: `memory.backend` selects exactly one of `off` (default) | `local` | `hindsight` | `mnemopi`; legacy `memories.enabled: true` migrates to `local` only when no explicit backend key is set; changing backend/bankId/prefix/scoping rebuilds the primary session memory state so later ops use the new scope.

features.name: memory-backend-interface
features.what: One backend-agnostic interface implemented by local/hindsight/mnemopi: startup init (best-effort; on failure the session continues with memory inert and logs a warning while tools report 'not initialised'), prompt-injection payload, `preCompactionContext`, `view`/`stats`/`diagnose`/`clear`/`enqueue`, subagent aliasing of the parent state, and disposal drain.

features.name: memory-slash-command
features.what: `/memory view|stats|diagnose|clear|reset|enqueue|rebuild` routes to the active backend: view prints the current injection payload, stats/diagnose render backend-specific data when supported, clear deletes active-backend data (Hindsight: local state+recall cache only, never the server bank; Mnemopi: every scoped .db plus WAL/SHM sidecars), enqueue forces retention/consolidation work.

features.name: memory-guidance-injection
features.what: At session start the active backend injects a Memory Guidance block rendered from `read-path.md` with `{{memory_summary}}` and `{{learned}}`, capped by `memories.summaryInjectionTokenLimit` (5000, shared by summary and lessons); the block frames memory as heuristic background context that loses to repo state/user instruction and must be cited with repo evidence when it changes a plan.

features.name: memory-url-protocol
features.what: `read` resolves `memory://root` (injected summary), `memory://root/MEMORY.md`, `memory://root/learned.md`, `memory://root/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, and under Mnemopi `memory://<memory-id>` returning the full row + metadata across all scoped banks; a missing id throws `Mnemopi memory <id> not found`.

features.name: local-memory-phase1-extraction
features.what: Background startup pipeline: for each persisted session changed since last processing, a `default`-role model extracts durable signal (decisions, constraints, resolved failures, workflows) into a raw memory block + synopsis; skips sessions idle < `minRolloutIdleHours` (12), older than `maxRolloutAgeDays` (30), currently active, beyond `threadScanLimit` (300) or `maxRolloutsPerStartup` (64); `stage1Concurrency` 8, lease 120s, retry delay 120s, per-session input capped by `phase1InputTokenLimit` (4000) within `rolloutPayloadPercent` (0.7) of context (`fallbackTokenLimit` 16000 when the window is unknown).

features.name: local-memory-phase2-consolidation
features.what: After extraction a `smol`-role pass over at most `maxRawMemoriesForGlobal` (200) extractions writes three artifacts — `MEMORY.md`, `memory_summary.md`, and `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` playbooks — under the project memories dir; guarded by a 180s lease with 30s heartbeat and 180s retry delay so simultaneous process starts cannot double-run; stale skill directories from prior runs are pruned; `learned.md` is never overwritten.

features.name: local-memory-job-store
features.what: SQLite-backed job queue + thread registry recording per-session processing state, claim leases, retry-after timestamps, and `/memory enqueue` marks that the next startup consumes; the whole pipeline is skipped for subagents and for sessions with no session file.

features.name: memory-secret-redaction
features.what: All generated memory written to disk (MEMORY.md, memory_summary.md, generated skills) and every captured lesson pass a common secret/token redactor; lessons additionally get prompt-injection neutralization before length caps are applied.

features.name: memory-model-role-resolution
features.what: Memory piggybacks on model roles: extraction uses role `default`, consolidation uses `smol`; an unresolved role falls back to `default`, then the active session model, then the first model in the registry.

features.name: memory-prompt-templates
features.what: Extraction/consolidation behavior is driven by static template files with fixed variables: `stage_one_system.md`, `stage_one_input.md` (`{{thread_id}}`,`{{response_items_json}}`), `consolidation_system.md`, `consolidation.md` (`{{raw_memories}}`,`{{rollout_summaries}}`), `read-path.md` (`{{memory_summary}}`,`{{learned}}`).

features.name: learned-lessons-store
features.what: Local-backend lesson file at `<agent-dir>/memories/<encoded-cwd>/learned.md`: bullets are newest-first, deduplicated by normalized rendered line, capped at 100 entries, content ≤2000 chars and context ≤400 chars after neutralization/redaction; injected starting with the next session and never mutating the live session's prompt-cache prefix; a normalized-empty lesson stores nothing (`stored === 0` = failure).

features.name: learn-tool
features.what: `learn({memory, context?, skill?})` stores one durable lesson through the active backend, then optionally creates/updates a managed skill: Mnemopi `rememberScoped` (source `coding-agent-learn`, importance 0.8, scope bank, veracity tool, memoryType fact, extraction on; missing returned id = failure), local `save` to learned.md, Hindsight `enqueueRetain` returning 'Lesson queued for retention.'; returns `details = { skill: null | "<name>" }`; requires `autolearn.enabled: true` plus backend in {hindsight,mnemopi,local}.

features.name: manage-skill-tool
features.what: `manage_skill({action: create|update|delete, name, description?, body?})` writes/removes `<agent-dir>/managed-skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; create is exclusive-create and fails if present, update requires an existing regular single-link file, delete recursively removes the directory; on success it calls the session `refreshSkills` callback so the active session discovers the change immediately; requires `autolearn.enabled: true` and is independent of `memory.backend`.

features.name: managed-skill-writer
features.what: Shared helper that trims+lowercases names to `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}`, collapses descriptions to one line stripped of control/format chars, angle brackets, backticks and repeated tildes, generates frontmatter containing only normalized name + sanitized description (body must not include frontmatter), rejects a final file over 64000 UTF-8 bytes, verifies root/dir/file against symlink escape and rejects non-regular or multiply hard-linked update targets, and serializes same-name in-process mutations in submission order (different names run in parallel; cross-process races are unserialized).

features.name: managed-vs-authored-skill-precedence
features.what: Authored skills always win discovery over managed skills of the same normalized name; `create` against an authored name returns a normal result with `isError: true` and `details.shadowed = true` and writes nothing, while `update` still writes but stays shadowed.

features.name: recall-tool
features.what: `recall({query})` searches the active backend and returns `Found <n> relevant memory/memories (as of YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC):` plus bullets — Hindsight `- <text> [<type>] (<mentioned_at>)`, Mnemopi `- <content> (id: <id>) [<source>] (<YYYY-MM-DD>) c:<score>` with 500-char previews ending in `…` when clipped; empty result returns `No relevant memories found.` with `useless = true`; `details = {}`; runs under `untilAborted(...)`.

features.name: retain-tool
features.what: `retain({items: [{content, context?}]})` (minItems 1) stores memories: Mnemopi writes each item synchronously to the scoped retain bank (source `coding-agent-retain`, importance 0.75, scope bank, extract+extractEntities, veracity tool, memoryType fact, metadata session_id/cwd/context/tool) and reports `<n> memories stored.`; Hindsight enqueues into the per-session retain queue and reports `<n> memories queued.`; `details = { count }` reflects requested count, not durability.

features.name: reflect-tool
features.what:
`reflect({query, context?})` synthesizes over memory: Hindsight best-effort `ensureBankExists` then POST reflect with configured budget and scope tags, returning trimmed server text or `No relevant information found to reflect on.`; Mnemopi performs one scoped recall (query + `

Additional context:
<context>` when context is non-blank) and returns `Based on recalled memories:

<formatted context>` — local reflect is recall+format, not model synthesis.

features.name: memory-edit-tool
features.what: `memory_edit({op: update|forget|invalidate, id, content?, importance?, replacement_id?})`, Mnemopi-only: update replaces working-memory text and/or importance wholesale (requires at least one, importance clamped to 0..1), forget hard-deletes working rows, invalidate soft-supersedes working/episodic rows recording `replacement_id`; resolution walks deduplicated retain → recall → global targets returning first editable success, else first resolved ineligible, else not_found; `details = { status: updated|deleted|invalidated|not_found|not_editable, bank?, store?: working|episodic|fact }`.

features.name: memory-tool-registration-gating
features.what: Tool exposure is computed from backend + settings: `recall`/`retain`/`reflect` for hindsight|mnemopi, `memory_edit` for mnemopi only, `learn` for autolearn+{hindsight,mnemopi,local}, `manage_skill` for autolearn alone; memory tools are `strict`, `loadMode: discoverable`, `approval: read` (learn/manage_skill are `essential`, and learn's approval is dynamically `write` when a skill is included or backend is local); unrestricted sessions with an explicit tool list auto-include the set, restricted lists are never widened, subagents never auto-receive them (only via explicit requested-tools/frontmatter), and discoverable ones may surface as `xd://<tool>` in xdev sessions.

features.name: hindsight-http-client
features.what: HTTP client against a Hindsight server (`hindsight.apiUrl`, default http://localhost:8888, optional bearer `apiToken`): `POST /v1/default/banks/{bank}/memories/recall`, `POST /v1/default/banks/{bank}/memories` (retainBatch, async), `POST /v1/default/banks/{bank}/reflect`, `PUT /v1/default/banks/{bank}` (createBank/missions); failures map to `HindsightError` carrying statusCode and parsed details; per-op timeouts requestTimeoutMs 30000, recallTimeoutMs 30000, retainTimeoutMs 60000, reflectTimeoutMs 120000.

features.name: hindsight-bank-scoping
features.what: `hindsight.scoping` = `per-project-tagged` (default: shared bank + `project:<label>` tags on writes, recall filters with `tagsMatch: any` so tagged and untagged global memories both surface) | `per-project` (bank id suffixed `-<label>`) | `global` (one bank, no tags); the project label is the repository's primary checkout root basename lowercased (so every linked worktree folds to one scope; cwd basename outside a repo) and tags match literally; explicit `hindsight.bankId` overrides the base.

features.name: hindsight-auto-recall
features.what: With `hindsight.autoRecall: true` the primary session recalls on its first model turn using a composed query bounded by `recallContextTurns` (1) and `recallMaxQueryChars` (800) with budget `recallBudget` (mid), `recallMaxTokens` (1024), `recallTypes` [world, experience]; results are injected as background context (not instructions), update `lastRecallSnippet`, refresh the base prompt, and are offered again as extra compaction context.

features.name: hindsight-retain-queue
features.what: Per-session in-memory queue: `enqueue` flushes immediately at `RETAIN_FLUSH_BATCH_SIZE` (16) else debounces `RETAIN_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS` (5000); flush verifies session ownership (mismatch logs and drops the batch), best-effort ensures the bank, maps items with `context ?? hindsight.retainContext` (`omp`), `metadata.session_id`, and scope tags, then issues one async retainBatch; auto-retain (`autoRetain: true`, `retainEveryNTurns: 3`, `retainOverlapTurns: 2`, `retainMode: full-session`) extracts plain user/assistant turns with `<memories>`/`<mental_models>` blocks stripped; agent end schedules cadence retention and flushes, disposal drains before releasing state; enqueue on a disposed state throws `Hindsight retain queue is closed.`

features.name: hindsight-mental-models
features.what: Bank-scoped mental models seeded once per bank from `seeds.json` (built-ins `user-preferences`, `project-conventions`, `project-decisions`; `projectTagged: true` seeds inherit retain tags, untagged seeds read the whole bank), rendered into a cached `<mental_models>` developer-instruction block; defaults `mentalModelsEnabled: true`, `mentalModelAutoSeed: true`, `mentalModelRefreshIntervalMs: 300000`, `mentalModelMaxRenderChars: 16000`, first-turn load waits at most 1500ms; seeding is create-only and `ensureBankExists` tracks up to MISSION_SET_CAP 10000 bank ids per state before dropping half.

features.name: hindsight-env-overrides
features.what: 18 `HINDSIGHT_*` env vars override the matching `hindsight.*` settings which override built-in defaults; strings are trimmed and empty is ignored, booleans accept only `true|1|yes` (case-insensitive) as true and any other defined value as false, integers use base-10 parseInt with invalid values ignored and no clamping, enums must match a listed lowercase value exactly.

features.name: mnemopi-embedded-backend
features.what: Local SQLite long-term memory: shared db defaults to `<agent-dir>/memories/mnemopi/mnemopi.db` (override `mnemopi.dbPath`), project banks are sibling databases managed by BankManager; `mnemopi.scoping` = `per-project` (default; bank = cwd basename + stable hash of the absolute cwd, git-layout independent) | `per-project-tagged` (write project bank, recall project+shared merged) | `global`; startup may adopt safely identified legacy cwd-only banks, scanning at most 64 candidate bank directories.

features.name: mnemopi-scoped-recall
features.what: Scoped recall queries every resolved recall bank with `recallEnhanced(query, recallLimit, { includeFacts: true, channelId: bank })`, merges/dedupes by id and content, sorts, and truncates to `mnemopi.recallLimit` (8, clamped ≥1); in `per-project-tagged` the shared bank gets one extra fallback query with project-bank literal tokens stripped; per-target failures are logged and healthy targets still contribute, but if every target fails the single error or a multi-bank AggregateError is thrown rather than returning empty.

features.name: mnemopi-auto-recall-retain
features.what: `mnemopi.autoRecall` (true) recalls on the first turn of a session into a `<memories>` prompt block and refreshes the base prompt when triggered from the `agent_start` listener, with query composition bounded by `recallContextTurns` (3) and `recallMaxQueryChars` (4000) and injection bounded by `injectionTokenLimit` (5000); `mnemopi.autoRetain` (true) stores completed transcripts no more often than `retainEveryNTurns` (4) with source `coding-agent-transcript`, importance 0.65, veracity unknown, memoryType episode.

features.name: mnemopi-retrieval-modes
features.what: Opt-in retrieval features, each overridable by env: `polyphonicRecall` (false, 4-voice vector/graph/fact/temporal fusion via reciprocal rank fusion, `MNEMOPI_POLYPHONIC_RECALL`), `enhancedRecall` (false, tiered query-result cache, `MNEMOPI_ENHANCED_RECALL`), `proactiveLinking` (false, ingest new memories into the episodic graph and link entities at write time, `MNEMOPI_PROACTIVE_LINKING`), `noEmbeddings` (false → FTS-only recall).

features.name: mnemopi-embedding-config
features.what: Embedding selection: `embeddingVariant` `en` = BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 (768d) default or `multilingual` = intfloat/multilingual-e5-large (1024d); precedence `mnemopi.embeddingModel` > `MNEMOPI_EMBEDDING_MODEL` > variant default; changing the model/variant rebuilds stored embeddings on the next writable start; `embeddingApiUrl`/`embeddingApiKey` point at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

features.name: mnemopi-llm-modes
features.what: `mnemopi.llmMode` = `smol` (default; resolves pi-ai role `tiny` then `smol` and passes a dynamic completion function so each LLM call fetches current provider credentials at call time) | `remote` (OpenAI-compatible `llmBaseUrl`/`llmApiKey`/`llmModel`) | `none` (no LLM calls); a configured local on-device memory model (`providers.memoryModel`) takes precedence; if nothing resolves, Mnemopi continues without LLM-backed extraction/consolidation.

features.name: mnemopi-shutdown-drain
features.what: Normal interactive/print exit runs a lighter path than enqueue: retain the current transcript with new fact extraction disabled → flush already-in-flight extractions (no per-session sleep, no cross-session promotion) → only then close owned SQLite bank handles, with the embedding worker shut down after state disposal; the drain gets a 1.5s budget and on expiry is detached so handles close when it settles rather than racing writes against closed databases; aliased subagent states never own or close banks.

features.name: mnemopi-enqueue-durability-boundary
features.what: `/memory enqueue` under Mnemopi is the explicit strong boundary: force-retain the current session, flush pending fact extractions, and run full sleep/consolidation across owned banks; `/memory clear` disposes scoped instances, removes every scoped .db plus WAL/SHM sidecars, and rehydrates the backend when the session is still active.

features.name: mnemopi-standalone-cli
features.what: Public `@oh-my-pi/pi-mnemopi` ships bin `mnemopi` with `store|remember`, `recall|search`, `update|edit`, `delete|forget`, `stats`, `sleep|consolidate`, `diagnose|doctor`, JSON `export`/`import`, `scratchpad|sp {read,write,clear}`, `bank {list,create,delete}`, and `mcp` (MCP server); unknown commands/invalid args print a concise error and exit nonzero.

features.name: advisor-runtime
features.what: `advisor.enabled: true` attaches one or more reviewer agents; without a WATCHDOG.yml roster a legacy/default advisor resolves `modelRoles.advisor`, with a roster each enabled entry uses its own `model` or falls back to that role and unresolvable entries report `no_model` without blocking siblings; each update receives only the new primary transcript delta rendered with reasoning, tool intent, watched-role markers and expanded constraint context, passed through the session secret obfuscator.

features.name: advisor-delta-rendering-rules
features.what: Hidden `custom` messages collapse to one-line summaries except `plan-mode-context`/`plan-mode-reference`, which render verbatim inside XML-escaped `<primary-context kind="…">` with repeated copies deduplicated; advisors additionally get the primary's discovered project context files in a `<project-context>` system block, plus a watchdog block naming the active child repo when cwd is outside git with exactly one direct child repository; advisory messages already injected into the primary transcript are filtered out of later deltas.

features.name: advisor-reset-and-cursor
features.what: Advisor runtime resets (clears its private in-memory transcript and rewinds its cursor, replaying the current bounded primary transcript) on compaction, session switch/resume, branch/fork history replacement, and context-maintenance re-prime; enabling the advisor mid-session seeds the cursor at the current transcript length instead of replaying history.

features.name: advise-tool-severity-delivery
features.what: `advise({note, severity?})` renders XML-escaped `<advisory advisor="<name>" severity="…" guidance="weigh, don't blindly obey">` into the primary transcript; omitted/`nit` = non-interrupting aside batched at the next step boundary, `concern` = interrupting steer except when the primary is idle on a terminal text answer with no queued work (preserved as a visible card), `blocker` = interrupting steer even after a terminal answer; while reviewing in-progress work only `blocker` may route, and an equal-or-lower-severity repeat of a whitespace-normalized note returns the visible `Duplicate advice ignored.`

features.name: advisor-steering-constraints
features.what: Steering is suppressed and the note preserved as a card when the user deliberately interrupted (Esc or cancel from collab/ACP/RPC/SDK/extension), in plan mode (all would-be steers become cards even mid-stream), and under ACP `deferAgentInitiatedTurns` when the bridge has not allowed agent-initiated turns while idle; `advisor.immuneTurns` (default 3) downgrades later concerns/blockers to non-interrupting asides for that many completed primary turns after a successful steer, leaving `nit` unchanged.

features.name: advisor-emission-guard
features.what: Per-advisor guard between advise and the yield/steer channel: normalize (lowercase, NFKC, collapse non-alphanumeric runs to one space, trim), suppress content-free phrases (`stop`, `done`, `lgtm`, `nothing to add`, …), drop any normalized note already accepted this session from a FIFO history of at most 4096 entries, and accept at most one note per advisor `prompt()` cycle (suppressed noise does not consume the budget); guard suppression is invisible to the model because advise already returned `Recorded.`; full guard state clears on every advisor reset.

features.name: advisor-sync-backlog
