features.what: `advisor.syncBacklog` ∈ {off, 1, 3, 5}: on primary turn end the delta is queued and the drain loop runs in background; when not `off` the primary waits only while advisor backlog is at/above the threshold, capped at 30s, continuing immediately when the advisor catches up or when the cap expires.

features.name: advisor-failure-and-quarantine-policy
features.what: Retriable advisor failures retry up to 3 times before the backlog is dropped; 3 dropped-backlog cycles halt the runtime until explicit reset and a permanent rejection can halt after one; quota failures pause with the batch retained until `/advisor` rebuild, config reload, new session, or restart; catch-up waiters release as soon as an advisor fails. Separately, before tool dispatch the runtime quarantines a whole turn that requests non-bridge tools it lacks, that emits an output-only destructive-shell directive, that matches ≥3 output-only hazard classes (destructive shell, instruction override, denial instruction, account-deletion claim), or that pairs a new instruction override with a quoted destructive command — the first consecutive quarantine silently resets and re-primes, the second emits one deduplicated host warning, drops the batch, and resets context; any successful turn resets the counter.

features.name: watchdog-md-discovery
features.what: `discoverWatchdogFiles(cwd, agentDir)` loads every readable `<agent-dir>/WATCHDOG.md` plus `<dir>/WATCHDOG.md` and `<dir>/.omp/WATCHDOG.md` while walking cwd upward to the git root (or home when none) — unlike context files it does not stop at the nearest match; candidates in hidden owner directories are ignored unless inside `.omp`; each file is appended to the advisor system prompt as `Especially pay attention to:\n<attention>…</attention>` ordered user-level first, then farther ancestors down toward cwd.

features.name: watchdog-at-imports
features.what: WATCHDOG.md and both WATCHDOG.yml instruction fields expand `@path` imports with the context-file helper: relative paths resolve from the importing file's directory, `~/` from home, imports inside fenced code blocks and inline code spans stay literal, cycles are skipped, and missing/unreadable imports leave the original `@path` text.

features.name: watchdog-yml-roster
features.what: `WATCHDOG.yml`/`.yaml` declares `instructions` (shared prompt concatenated across all discovered files) and `advisors[]` with `name` (slugified for session id and transcript filename), `enabled` (default true; false shows as paused without building a runtime), `model` (optional selector with `:level` thinking suffix), `tools` (any `BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES` including mutating ones; omitted → read/grep/glob, `[]` → none, legacy aliases search→grep and find→glob normalized, unknown names dropped with a warning), and `instructions`; files failing parse/schema validation are logged and skipped, and a more specific file (project leaf > project ancestor > user) replaces an earlier entry with the same slug.

features.name: advisor-tool-isolation
features.what: Each advisor is a full agent with its own `Agent` and a distinct `ToolSession` whose id is suffixed `-advisor`, sharing none of the primary's file snapshots, seen-lines tracking, conflict state, or summary cache; granted tools are built against that session and wrapped with `ExtensionToolWrapper` so `tools.approvalMode`, per-tool approval policies, and `autoApprove` apply normally; only built-ins actually constructed for the session are grantable (a factory returning null, e.g. unavailable `lsp`, is absent).

features.name: advisor-slash-commands
features.what: `/advisor` toggles the subsystem for the session (never persisted), `/advisor on|off` set it explicitly, `/advisor status` shows each advisor's runtime state, model, context usage, tokens and cost, `/advisor dump` copies the compact transcript for all active advisors and `/advisor dump raw` includes system prompt, tools, thinking and calls, `/advisor configure` opens a TUI-only editor for project/user `WATCHDOG.yml`.

features.name: advisor-headless-mode
features.what: `omp -p --advisor "…"` enables advisors for one print-mode process without persisting `advisor.enabled`; concerns/blockers steer the live turn while a prompt runs, after the final prompt settles late notes are preserved without starting hidden primary turns, and disposal waits up to 10 minutes for final reviews (30s on error exits), logging reviews it will abandon when the deadline expires.

features.name: advisor-subagent-opt-in
features.what: Subagents run unadvised by default; agent frontmatter `advisor: true|"<model pattern>"` and the `task.agentAdvisor` settings record (agent name → on|off|pattern, editable from the `/agents` hub property strip) opt individual agents in, with the settings record overriding frontmatter; legacy `advisor.subagents: true` migrates to `task.agentAdvisor: { task: "on" }`; an advised subagent builds its own advisor subsystem and reruns WATCHDOG.md/.yml discovery for that session's cwd and agent dir.

features.name: advisor-transcript-persistence
features.what: Every finalized advisor turn appends to JSONL beside the owning session file — `<session>/__advisor.jsonl`, `<session>/__advisor.<slug>.jsonl`, `<session>/<SubId>/__advisor[.<slug>].jsonl` — so `omp stats` attributes advisor usage/cost and Agent Hub shows read-only `advisor`-kind transcripts; advisor 'session update' prompts persist as `synthetic` agent-attributed user messages; the recorder reopens at the new path after `/new`/resume/switch/branch and is detached+drained before a `/drop` deletes the old artifacts dir; the log is append-only and unaffected by re-prime/compaction.

features.name: advisor-non-peer-exclusion
features.what: The `advisor`-kind registry ref is excluded from every agent-facing surface — hub peer roster and broadcast targets, subagent peer prompt, and `history://` index/lookup/completions — cannot be messaged via hub send or collab chat, and cannot be revived or killed from Agent Hub or collab, regardless of granted tools.

features.name: advisor-context-maintenance
features.what: Before each advisor prompt the session estimates incoming tokens and maintains the advisor's own append-only in-memory context in order: model-level context promotion when enabled and a larger compatible model exists → compact the advisor's own history → re-prime from the current bounded primary transcript; the live context is retained while the session runs so `/advisor dump` works.

features.name: ttsr-rule-registration
features.what: At session creation rules load from the rule capability (deduped by `rule.name`, first-wins by provider priority) and `bucketRules(...)` drops names in `ttsr.disabledRules`, drops embedded `builtin-defaults` rules when `ttsr.builtinRules === false`, registers the rest with `TtsrManager`, then routes leftovers to always-apply/rulebook buckets; `addRule()` refuses when TTSR is disabled, when neither a compilable `condition` regex nor a non-empty `astCondition` exists, on duplicate name, or when the parsed scope excludes all monitored streams; invalid regexes and unreachable scopes warn and continue.

features.name: ttsr-stream-monitoring
features.what: On `turn_start` the buffer resets; during `message_update` the coordinator monitors `text_delta`, `thinking_delta` and `toolcall_delta` with buffers isolated per source or tool-call stream key, replacing file-scoped buffers with per-file `matcherEntries` digests (or a single `matcherDigest`) via `checkSnapshot` and falling back to appending raw deltas via `checkDelta`; default scope monitors assistant text and all tool arguments but not thinking, and explicit scope tokens enable text, thinking, any tool, a named tool, and per-tool path globs.

features.name: ttsr-ast-conditions
features.what: `astCondition` evaluates only on tool-argument streams whose tool exposes a reconstructed `matcherDigest` or per-file `matcherEntries` and only when a candidate path yields a usable extension for language inference; the snapshot is source-bearing payload only (replace `new_string`, added lines for JSON-patch/hashline/apply-patch, full content for create/write), multi-file calls split into `{path, digest}` entries evaluated independently, and matching runs in-memory through native `astMatch` with Smart strictness; identical consecutive snapshots per stream key are skipped and parse/match failures log and count as no match.

features.name: ttsr-interrupt-and-retry
features.what: Per-rule `interruptMode` (always|prose-only|tool-only|never) overrides `ttsr.interruptMode`; when any matched rule interrupts, matches are deduped into pending injections, the abort-pending flag and a resume gate are set, `agent.abort()` fires immediately (tool matches scope the reason to that tool-call id so siblings get `TTSR interrupt on another tool call`), `ttsr_triggered` is emitted fire-and-forget, and retry is scheduled 50ms later tagged with prompt generation + retry token; the retry re-validates token, generation, abort state and target assistant message, then applies `contextMode` (`discard` truncates messages to the target index, `keep` leaves the partial output), renders `ttsr-interrupt.md` into a hidden `custom_message` (`customType: "ttsr-injection"`, `details.rules`), persists a `ttsr_injection` entry, and calls `agent.continue()`.

features.name: ttsr-noninterrupting-injection
features.what: Non-interrupting matches split by source: tool-source rules bucket per matched tool-call id and are marked injected immediately, and when the result is produced the `afterToolCall` hook prepends one rendered `ttsr-tool-reminder.md` `<system-reminder reason="rule_violation" rule="…" path="…">` text block ahead of the tool's own content (multiple rules concatenated with a blank line) and persists the consumed rule names; prose-source rules queue a hidden `ttsr-injection` custom message via `agent.followUp()` scheduled 1ms after a successful non-error non-aborted assistant message and do not emit `ttsr_triggered`.

features.name: ttsr-repeat-policy
features.what: `ttsr.repeatMode` `once` (default) lets a rule trigger only once after it has an injection record; `after-gap` re-triggers only when `messageCount - lastInjectedAt >= ttsr.repeatGap` (default 10) where `messageCount` increments at `turn_end`, so the gap counts completed turns rather than stream chunks.

features.name: ttsr-persistence-and-restore
features.what: Injected rule state persists as `ttsr_injection` entries (`appendTtsrInjection(ruleNames)` / `getInjectedTtsrRules()`), is reconstructed into `SessionContext.injectedTtsrRules`, and restores through `TtsrManager.restoreInjected(ruleNames)` at session creation; only names are stored, so restored rules are recorded at message count zero and an `after-gap` rule becomes eligible after `repeatGap` newly completed turns regardless of elapsed history.

features.name: ttsr-event-surface
features.what: `{ type: "ttsr_triggered", rules: Rule[] }` is part of `AgentSessionEvent` and is routed to extension listeners, hook `on("ttsr_triggered")`, custom tools via `onSession({ reason: "ttsr_triggered", rules })`, and local subscribers; interactive mode uses `session.isTtsrAbortPending` to suppress rendering the aborted stop reason as a failure and shows a TTSR notification component instead.

features.name: sdk-create-agent-session
features.what: `createAgentSession(options?)` follows provide-to-override/omit-to-discover, defaulting cwd=`getProjectDir()`, agentDir=`~/.omp/agent`, authStorage=`discoverAuthStorage`, modelRegistry=new + background refresh, settings=`Settings.init`, file-backed SessionManager, skills/rules/context files/prompt templates/slash commands/extensions/custom TS commands, built-in tools, MCP (Exa folded into native integration, browser MCP filtered when the built-in browser tool is on), LSP, and a fresh EventBus; returns `{ session, extensionsResult, setToolUIContext, mcpManager?, modelFallbackMessage?, lspServers?, eventBus }`.

features.name: sdk-session-manager-modes
features.what: `SessionManager.create(cwd, dir)` persists conversation/message/state deltas to a `.jsonl` file (with `session.sessionFile` defined and resume/open/list/fork supported) while `SessionManager.inMemory()` disables persistence and leaves `sessionFile` undefined; helpers `continueRecent(cwd)`, `list(cwd)`, `open(path)` and `getDefaultSessionDir(cwd, agentDir)` complete the surface.

features.name: sdk-auth-model-resolution
features.what: When `model`/`modelPattern` are omitted, selection order is: restore from existing session (if restorable and key available) → settings `default` model role → an authenticated provider-default model in availability order → first authenticated available model, with `modelFallbackMessage` explaining any fallback; `AuthStorage.getApiKey` resolves runtime override (`--api-key`) → `models.yml` provider apiKey → stored OAuth credential (refreshing as needed) → API key persisted by `/login` → provider env vars → other stored key in `agent.db`/broker storage → custom-provider resolver.

features.name: sdk-event-subscription
features.what: `session.subscribe(listener)` returns an unsubscribe function and streams core AgentEvents plus session events (`auto_compaction_start/end`, `auto_retry_start/end`, `retry_fallback_applied/succeeded`, `model_changed`, `thinking_level_changed`, `ttsr_triggered`, `todo_reminder`, `todo_auto_clear`, `irc_message`, `notice`, `goal_updated`); `agent_end` carries `messages`, optional telemetry, and `isTerminal?: boolean` where `false` means maintenance/async delivery will resume the session and an absent field means terminal.

features.name: sdk-prompt-and-queue-api
features.what: `session.prompt(text, options?)` expands slash/custom/file commands and prompt templates, then either queues (`streamingBehavior: "steer" | "followUp"`, required while streaming) or validates model+API key, appends the user message and starts a turn; companions are `sendUserMessage(content, { deliverAs? })` (extension default steer), `steer`, `followUp`, `sendCustomMessage({ customType, content }, { deliverAs?, triggerTurn? })`, and `abort()`; queued messages are preserved rather than discarded.

features.name: sdk-two-phase-disposal
features.what: `beginDispose()` is a synchronous idempotent admission barrier that marks the session disposed, cancels memory startup, title generation and auto-learn capture, clears queued yields/asides, stops advisor runtime, detaches aside delivery and rejects new eval executions; the later idempotent `await dispose()` flushes the exit diagnostic, emits `session_shutdown` once, aborts retries/compaction/turn, gives post-prompt and auto-learn work bounded time, then concurrently tears down async jobs, eval kernels, browser tabs, native computer sessions, MCP, advisor and memory state (best-effort, failures logged), and only after entry-appending work settles cleans an empty moved session, closes SessionManager and provider session state, disconnects the agent and removes listeners.

features.name: sdk-tool-selection-options
features.what: `toolNames` requests named tools (and can enable default-disabled ones) but is not an allowlist by itself; `restrictToolNames: true` limits the session to those names and by default disables ambient MCP, extensions, custom commands and LSP; SDK-supplied `customTools` are excluded in a restricted session unless `allowRestrictedCustomTools: true` and their names also appear in `toolNames`; hidden tools such as `yield` are opt-in unless `requireYieldTool`/options demand them.

features.name: sdk-extension-loading-options
features.what: `extensions` accepts inline `ExtensionFactory[]`, `additionalExtensionPaths` loads extra files, `disableExtensionDiscovery` turns off ambient scanning while keeping explicit paths and inline factories, and `preloadedExtensions` reuses an extension set loaded early by the same session-owning process — cross-session reuse must go through `preloadedExtensionPaths` so each session binds its own `ExtensionAPI`.

features.name: sdk-runtime-tool-activation
features.what: `getActiveToolNames()`, `getAllToolNames()`, `setActiveToolsByName(names)` and `refreshMCPTools(mcpTools)` change the live tool set and rebuild the system prompt to reflect the change.

features.name: sdk-discovery-helpers-and-entrypoints
features.what: Public discovery helpers (`discoverAuthStorage`, `discoverExtensions`, `discoverSkills`, `discoverContextFiles`, `discoverPromptTemplates`, `discoverSlashCommands`, `discoverCustomTSCommands`, `discoverMCPServers`, `buildSystemPrompt`) are exported so embedders can take partial control; the package root exports the full surface while the narrower `/sdk` subpath omits `SessionManager`, `AuthStorage` and `ModelRegistry`.

features.name: sdk-subagent-orchestration-options
features.what: Orchestrator-facing options `outputSchema`, `outputSchemaMode` (permissive|strict), `requireYieldTool`, `taskDepth`, `parentTaskPrefix` feed structured-output enforcement and nested task artifact naming; concurrent top-level sessions in one process each need a private `AgentRegistry` because the process-global registry admits only one `"Main"` identity per generation.

features.name: sdk-startup-optimizations
features.what: Two background startup optimizations: best-effort `fetch.preconnect(model.baseUrl)` as soon as the model resolves (silently skipped when unavailable or throwing) in every mode; and conditional LSP warmup that runs only when `enableLsp !== false` AND `options.hasUI === true` AND `lsp.lazy` is disabled — with the default lazy mode UI sessions still get `lspServers` entries reported as status `"available"` without spawning processes, and `lspServers` is `undefined` only when LSP is off or `hasUI === false`.

features.name: rpc-stdio-loop
features.what: `omp --mode rpc` claims stdin before extension discovery and parses one non-empty JSONL line at a time, writing a `ready` frame before processing commands; malformed JSON emits a recoverable `command: "parse"` failure with `id: undefined` and keeps the loop alive; `@file` CLI args are rejected; on stdin close pending extension-UI, host-tool and host-URI requests are rejected, accepted commands drain, the session disposes and the process exits 0.

features.name: rpc-frame-protocol-v2
features.what: The ready frame advertises `protocolVersion: 1`, `supportedProtocolVersions: [1,2]`, `maxFrameBytes: 1048576`, `maxReassembledFrameBytes: 67108864`; after `negotiate_protocol` v2 succeeds, oversized stdout objects emit as an uninterrupted `rpc_chunk` sequence (`chunkId`, `index`, `count`, `byteLength`, base64 `data`) that clients MUST validate, reject when interleaved/interrupted, bound by the reassembly limit, concatenate in index order, decode as strict UTF-8 and parse as one JSON object; v1 clients ignore the extra fields and keep bounded fallback for oversized output.

features.name: rpc-command-surface
features.what: Newline-delimited `RpcCommand` set covering prompting (`prompt`, `steer`, `follow_up`, `abort`, `abort_and_prompt`, `new_session`), state (`get_state`, `set_fast_mode`, `get_available_commands`, `set_todos`, `set_host_tools`, `set_host_uri_schemes`, `set_subagent_subscription`, `get_subagents`, `get_subagent_messages`), model/thinking (`set_model`, `cycle_model`, `get_available_models`, `set_thinking_level`, `cycle_thinking_level`), queue modes, compaction, retry, `bash`/`abort_bash` (dispatched concurrently so abort is serviced mid-run), session ops (`get_session_stats`, `export_html`, `switch_session`, `branch`, `get_branch_messages`, `get_last_assistant_text`, `set_session_name`, `handoff`), messages, and login; responses are `{ id?, type: "response", command, success, data? | error, code? }`.

features.name: rpc-prompt-ack-semantics
features.what: `prompt`/`abort_and_prompt` return immediate success on acceptance, may later emit an error response with the same id if async scheduling fails, and may carry `data.agentInvoked` (`false` = completed locally with no agent turn, `true` = produced agent lifecycle events, omitted = rely on session events); a later `{ type: "prompt_result", id?, agentInvoked }` frame resolves prompts accepted immediately but resolved local-only; `abort_and_prompt` emits neither `agentInvoked` nor `prompt_result`.

features.name: rpc-get-state-and-fast-mode
features.what: `get_state` returns model, thinkingLevel, isStreaming/isCompacting, steering/followUp/interrupt modes, session file/id/name, `fastModeEnabled` (session setting) vs `fastModeActive` (computed), `tokensPerSecond` (number or null), autoCompactionEnabled, message/queued counts, todoPhases, systemPrompt, dumpTools, contextUsage; `set_fast_mode` always returns `{enabled, active}`, fails with exactly `Fast mode is unavailable for the current model.` on a model with no service-tier family, is idempotent when disabling, and an explicit enable re-arms Anthropic's sticky `speed: "fast"` rejection fallback.

features.name: rpc-message-pagination
features.what: `get_messages_page {cursor?, limit?}` returns a stable chronological page (≤256 messages) with `messages`, `totalMessages`, and an opaque `nextCursor` bound to session id, durable leaf and message count; it refuses to start a walk while streaming/compacting (`code: session_busy`) and rejects cursors whose snapshot changed (`code: stale_cursor`); bundled clients drain it after negotiating v2, keep the legacy monolithic `get_messages` for v1 servers, and on either code discard partial pages and fall back to the best-effort snapshot while direct paged calls stay strict.

features.name: rpc-host-tool-protocol
features.what: `set_host_tools` replaces the host-owned tool set (name/label/description/JSON-schema parameters, optional `hidden` and `loadMode` where an explicit mode wins, known essential built-in names stay essential and others default to discoverable) and returns `{toolNames}`; the server then emits `host_tool_call {id, toolCallId, toolName, arguments}` and `host_tool_cancel {id, targetId}`, and hosts reply with optional `host_tool_update {partialResult}` and terminal `host_tool_result {result, isError?}` where top-level `isError: true` surfaces the text content as a tool error.

features.name: rpc-host-uri-protocol
features.what: `set_host_uri_schemes` registers host-owned URL schemes (`scheme`, `description`, `writable`, `immutable`), normalized to lowercase and replacing the entire previous set (missing schemes are unregistered); reads/writes of `<scheme>://…` emit `host_uri_request {id, operation, url, content?}` with `host_uri_cancel {targetId}` on abort, and hosts answer `host_uri_result` with required `content` for reads (`contentType` default `text/plain`, else `text/markdown`/`application/json`, optional per-read `immutable` override and `notes`) or `isError: true` + `error`; the `edit` tool never targets host URIs (hosts expose `write` instead) and `security://` is reserved and cannot be shadowed.

features.name: rpc-extension-ui-protocol
features.what: Extensions round-trip UI over the same transport: outbound `extension_ui_request` with methods `select|confirm|input|editor|cancel|notify|setStatus|setWidget|setTitle|set_editor_text|open_url`, inbound `extension_ui_response` carrying `value`, `confirmed`, or `cancelled(+timedOut)`; unknown response ids are ignored, timeouts/aborts resolve to a default, and `setTitle` plus automatic session-title generation are disabled in RPC mode unless `PI_RPC_EMIT_TITLE=1`.

features.name: rpc-subagent-and-command-channels
features.what: `set_subagent_subscription` (`off` default | `progress` | `events`) gates `subagent_lifecycle`/`subagent_progress`/`subagent_event` frames; `get_subagents` returns the registry snapshot sorted by subagent index then id; `get_subagent_messages {subagentId|sessionFile, fromByte}` returns `sessionFile`, `fromByte`, `nextByte`, `reset`, raw `entries` and converted `messages`, restarting at byte zero with `reset: true` when `fromByte` exceeds file size; `available_commands_update` pushes command metadata at startup and on change, and builtin slash commands use `command_output`, `session_info_update`, `config_update` side channels.

features.name: rpc-host-defaults
features.what: RPC/ACP hosts receive built-in defaults for task isolation/execution, memory, advisor, tier, async-job and bash auto-background settings, applied only where a path is not explicitly configured; project/global config, `--config`, and isolated settings stay authoritative, and todo settings are never host-defaulted.

features.name: rpc-client-libraries
features.what: Two bundled clients wrap the wire contract: the TypeScript `RpcClient` (spawns `bun <cliPath> --mode rpc`, correlates `req_<n>` ids, dispatches core AgentEvents, `setCustomTools()` handling of host_tool frames, OAuth `getLoginProviders()`/`login()`), and the Python `omp_rpc.RpcClient` (context-manager process lifecycle, typed commands/events, v2 negotiation and chunk reassembly, message pagination, extension UI, host tools and URI schemes, `prompt_and_wait(...).require_assistant_text()`); unwrapped surfaces require raw frames.

features.name: collab-session-sharing
features.what: `/collab` starts hosting full-control, `/collab view` read-only, `/collab <relay>` targets a specific relay, `/collab status` lists link+participants, `/collab stop` ends sharing, `/join <link>`/`omp join "<link>"` joins and `/leave` leaves restoring the guest's previous session; hosting prints both the terminal join command and a click-to-join OSC 8 browser deep link with QR codes, and re-running `/collab` while hosting re-prints them.

features.name: collab-link-grammar
features.what: Links parse recursively: `<roomId>.<key>` (default relay wss://my.omp.sh), legacy `<roomId>#<key>`, `host[:port]/r/<roomId>{.|#}<key>`, `https://`/`wss://` direct URLs normalized to wss, `ws://localhost:7475/...` for plain-ws localhost only, and browser wrappers `https://host/#<link>` where a parseable fragment wins over treating the HTTP host/path as the relay (falling back to the legacy direct form otherwise); the secret is base64url and either 48 bytes (32-byte AES-256-GCM key + 16-byte write token) or a bare 32-byte view-only key, dot-joined in new links because RFC 3986 forbids a raw `#` in a fragment while `#` and `%23` legacy forms still parse.

features.name: collab-e2e-encryption
features.what: Every session payload (entries, events, state, prompts) is sealed with AES-256-GCM before hitting the socket so the relay only sees room ids, connection counts, opaque ciphertext frames with sizes, and a 4-byte routing prefix; possession of the link is the entire trust boundary and the key never leaves the URL fragment.

features.name: collab-permission-model
features.what: The host verifies the 16-byte write token at join and rejects writes from peers lacking it (shown read-only in participants and in the join notice); full-control guests can read the whole session including back-transcript, prompt (name badge is display-only, the LLM sees verbatim text), interrupt with Esc, drive Agent Hub against host subagents (table, progress, chat/steer, kill, revive, transcript fetch), and answer host `select`/`editor` requests (broadcast only to writable guests, first submitted or cancelled response settles and dismisses the rest); everything mutating host session/machine (`/model`, `/compact`, `/resume`, `/branch`, `!` bash, `$` python, skills) is host-only and guests keep a local allowlist (`/dump`, `/export`, `/copy`, `/help`, `/hotkeys`, `/theme`, `/settings`, `/leave`, `/collab`, `/exit`, `/quit`).

features.name: collab-frame-protocol
features.what: Hub topology with an authoritative host and no guest peering: host→guest `welcome` + byte-bounded `snapshot-chunk` (each arrival resets the guest progress timeout, oversized entries shrunk), `entry` (durable entries broadcast pre-blob-externalization so images stay inline, appended with ids preserved to a replica `~/.omp/collab/<roomId>.jsonl` and into the agent message array), `event` (fed to the guest's normal event controller; rendering is events-only to avoid double render), debounced `state` (streaming flag, full host model object + thinking level applied to the replica agent state, context numbers, participants), `bus` (mirrored subagent lifecycle/progress republished on the guest bus), `agents` (registry snapshots), `ui-request`/`ui-request-end`; guest→host `hello`, `prompt`, `abort`, `agent-cmd`, `fetch-transcript` (answered by targeted `transcript` frames), `ui-response`; replicas load through normal `/resume` machinery and the guest never chdirs to host paths.

features.name: collab-web-client
features.what: `packages/collab-web` is a standalone browser guest served by the relay at `/` so `https://<relay>/#<link>` auto-connects from the fragment, rendering streaming text/thinking/tool cards, a subagent panel with on-demand transcripts, and a composer with guest prompt/interrupt/hub powers; `bun run dev` (port 3000), `bun run mock-host` (offline scripted host), `bun run relay` (ws://localhost:7466 stand-in implementing only `/r/<roomId>`), `bun run build` emits a static `dist/`; non-local deployments require HTTPS for WebCrypto and the client talks only to the relay.

features.name: collab-relay-contract
features.what: The relay is a content-blind service exposing `GET /` (static guest client), `GET /r/<roomId>?role=host|guest` (WebSocket upgrade), `POST /s` + `GET /s/<id>` + `GET /s/<id>/raw` (`/share` blob upload, viewer, raw fetch), and `GET /healthz`, keeping no state beyond live connections; production relay binaries/source are not distributed for self-hosting.

features.name: collab-settings-and-share
features.what: `collab.relayUrl` (default `wss://my.omp.sh`) selects the relay when none is passed inline, `collab.webUrl` (empty) sets the browser UI base and when empty derives `http(s)://host[:port]` from the relay — explicit web URLs must be `https://` except `http://localhost`; `collab.displayName` defaults to the OS username; `share.serverUrl` (`https://my.omp.sh/s`) forms `/share` links as `<base>/<id>#<key>` and `share.redactSecrets` (true) runs the secret obfuscator over uploaded snapshots.

features.name: stats-dashboard-package
features.what: `@oh-my-pi/omp-stats` (bin `omp-stats`, main path `omp stats`) reads `~/.omp/agent/sessions/`, syncs into `~/.omp/stats.db`, and serves a dashboard on http://localhost:3847 (`--port` overrides) with `/api/stats`, `/api/stats/models`, `/api/stats/folders`, `/api/stats/timeseries`, `/api/sync`; `--summary` prints a console summary and `--json` prints JSON and exits; it scans session folders recursively so subagent and advisor turns attribute to their owning session.

features.name: snapcompact-package
features.what: Public `@oh-my-pi/snapcompact` deterministically serializes discarded conversation history and renders it to PNG for vision-model context compaction with no model call or API key, exporting `compact`, `render`, `renderMany`, `frames`, shape selection, text normalization/serialization, image budgets and file-operation helpers; rasterization/PNG encoding require `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives`.

features.name: omptype-package
features.what: Public `@oh-my-pi/omptype` provides callable ArkType-compatible schemas with interpreted startup and lazy hot-path compilation, defaults/morphs, validation errors and JSON Schema emission; surfaces are the native root plus `/typebox`, `/zod` compatibility builders and `/ark`; schema calls return the value or `type.errors`, `.assert()` returns or throws, `.allows()` is boolean.

features.name: metaharness-benchmark-manager
features.what: Private `@oh-my-pi/pi-metaharness` (bin `metaharness`) unifies Harbor (default `terminal-bench@2.0`), TypeScript-edit and SnapCompact benchmarks behind one dashboard, SQLite store at `<jobs-dir>/_manager/metaharness.sqlite`, and REST/SSE API with a normalized experiment → run → trace model; `serve -- --port 4700` plus `POST /api/runs` launch all three adapters, direct runners exist per adapter, benchmark-native artifacts remain the filesystem source of truth with historical runs auto-discovered, and deleting an experiment/run also deletes its job dirs and is rejected while running.

features.name: typescript-edit-benchmark-fixtures
features.what: Private `@oh-my-pi/typescript-edit-benchmark` generates, loads, formats and verifies TypeScript mutation fixtures (task metadata, prompt, input files, expected files) consumed by the metaharness edit adapter; the runner copies each fixture into an isolated worktree, accepts provider/model, thinking level, runs per task, timeouts, concurrency, task ids, fixture dir or `.tar.gz`, edit strategy, guided mode, retry/turn limits and output path/format, and writes Markdown or JSON results with optional conversation dumps.

features.name: robomp-triage-service
features.what: Python `robomp` (3.11+, bin `robomp` with `serve|triage|replay|status|cleanup`) receives GitHub webhooks for allowlisted repos, classifies issues, resumes an `omp --mode rpc` session per issue, comments or opens a fix PR, and handles follow-up issue/PR conversations; FastAPI serves an operator dashboard at `/` (Compose publishes http://localhost:6543/) over a SQLite-backed event queue, with config from `.env` plus mounted `models.container.yml` and per-issue worktrees/transcripts/logs persisted in the `robomp_data` volume; the default two-container deployment keeps the GitHub PAT in an HMAC-authenticated `gh-proxy` sidecar.

features.name: browser-relay-package
features.what: Private `@oh-my-pi/browser-relay` exposed as `omp browser-relay`: `install` writes the unpacked extension to `~/.omp/browser-relay/extension`, then `browser.relay` or `app.relay: true` enables it; the relay auto-starts through the global daemon broker, `app.target` picks a tab by URL/title substring otherwise the visible tab is adopted; it binds loopback with optional `--token`, and Chrome internal pages, DevTools, Web Store, extension pages and tabs with DevTools open cannot attach.

invariants.rule: Selector parsing MUST fall through for unrecognized trailing `:...` so `archive.zip:inner/file` and `db.sqlite:table:key` keep working, and an existing literal filesystem path MUST beat selector interpretation (a real POSIX filename ending in selector-looking text is read literally).
Archive detection MUST run before SQLite detection in both `read` and `write`; a path matching an archive selector is never treated as SQLite.

SQLite interpretation requires BOTH a matching extension and valid SQLite magic bytes; an existing `.db`/`.sqlite` file without the header MUST fall back to plain-file handling. `write` MUST never create a new SQLite database.

The hashline `#TAG` is a 4-uppercase-hex hash of the whole normalized file, not of the displayed range; anchors MUST be suppressed for `:raw` reads and immutable sources (artifacts, skills, memory, agent outputs) because there is no editable backing target.
In a hashline patch every line number refers to the ORIGINAL tagged snapshot, never to the state produced by earlier hunks in the same call.

Same-path sections MUST be merged before application so their original anchors apply together; clipboard operations MUST be rejected when interleaved same-path sections make authored register order ambiguous.

For multi-section edits, every section MUST be parsed and prepared before any write begins (fail-fast on syntax/anchor/no-op), and named-register session state MUST advance only for the prefix of files that actually landed.

Edits targeting lines outside the ranges the model has actually seen (elided summary spans, undisplayed regions) MUST be rejected — so summarizing reads MUST record their visible spans in the snapshot store.
A patch that applies to exactly the existing bytes is an error, and repeating the same no-op payload three times MUST escalate through the no-op loop guard.
Every filesystem mutation path MUST call the fs-scan-cache invalidation helpers after success, invalidating BOTH sides of a rename; otherwise cached walks feed stale results to glob/ast discovery.

Archive entry writes MUST rewrite the entire container to a sibling temp file and rename over the destination, resolving existing archive symlinks first so the target file is updated rather than replaced.
Archive inner paths MUST reject `..`, and PDF image members MUST be matched against extracted basenames only, so separators cannot escape the artifact cache directory.

Deterministic disk reads (plain-file line/range reads and directory listings) MUST be invoked without the abort signal so an interrupt cannot surface a misleading "Operation aborted" on a read that would have finished instantly; every other branch (URL, internal URL, archive, sqlite, conversion, image, summary, conflict scan, suffix glob) MUST honor the signal and call `throwIfAborted`.
`grep`/`glob` output MUST override `maxLines` to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` so truncation is byte-based (50 KiB), not line-based.
Native glob receives `sortByMtime: true` only so it can stop early at `maxResults`; JS MUST still re-sort mtime-descending after merging concurrent multi-target results.

Multi-root scope resolution MUST NOT collapse roots to a common ancestor that is not itself a requested scope (and MUST NOT demote a plain-file entry into a directory walk's glob union) — it must fan out per-target, or unrelated siblings get scanned.
In multi-root calls missing paths are skipped non-fatally and reported; a single missing path hard-fails; all-missing errors. Single-file searches ignore `skip`.

`ast_edit` is preview-first unconditionally: writes happen only through `write xd://resolve`, the apply pass MUST stage every changed file in memory and verify the whole pass before writing, and MUST compare replacement totals and per-file counts against the preview, erroring on mismatch instead of reporting success.

Native AST rewrite rules execute in pattern-string sort order, not `ops` array order, and accumulated per-file edits are applied from the end of the file backward after an overlap check; overlapping computed edits MUST abort the run.

A pending resolve invoker MUST be consumed exactly once by a successful apply or discard; an apply that throws MUST re-register the same preview; rejecting with nothing pending succeeds, resolving with nothing pending throws.
`write` MUST remain registered whenever a deferrable tool (e.g. `ast_edit`) is active or plan mode is enabled, because previews and plan approval ride on `write`.
Unknown URI-like schemes passed to `write` MUST be refused rather than silently creating a local file; `./scheme://...` is the only way to intentionally create such a filename.

Conflict URI scopes (`/ours`, `/theirs`, `/base`, `/both`) are read-only; bulk `conflict://*` resolution MUST apply bottom-up and be all-or-nothing per file, invalidating successful ids while retaining ids of failed files for retry.

Notebook source lines that look like cell markers MUST gain one `%` on render and lose one on parse; a non-empty editable representation MUST start with a marker (text before the first marker, including a blank line, is rejected).
`write` is not notebook-aware — the virtual `# %%` representation must never be written back through `write`; only the edit pipeline round-trips it to notebook JSON.
Hashline prefix stripping in `write` MUST only occur when the session's file display mode has hashLines enabled; otherwise content is written unchanged.

LSP aborts MUST send `$/cancelRequest` and rethrow `ToolAbortError`, while ordinary validation failures return text with `details.success: false`; a wall-clock tool timeout without a caller abort throws `ToolError` instead.
`rust-analyzer/reloadWorkspace` MUST be gated on the server binary/name — sending it to other servers (e.g. Roslyn) can crash them.

`rename_file` apply order is fixed: `workspace/willRenameFiles` -> coalesced edits applied once per URI from a single snapshot -> filesystem rename -> `textDocument/didClose` for renamed open files -> `workspace/didRenameFiles`.
For project-aware servers, `definition`, `references`, and `rename` MUST reject an omitted `symbol` when `line` is supplied instead of silently using the first non-whitespace column.
The LSP config cache is per-cwd and never auto-invalidated; only a workspace `reload` (omitted `file` or `file: "*"`) may rebuild it — a concrete-file reload MUST keep the cached configuration.
URL line-range reads MUST request `ensureArtifact: true, preferCached: true` so later paginated reads reopen the same rendered body from artifact storage instead of refetching.
The structural-summary footer MUST cite concrete re-read ranges derived from the actual elisions, not placeholder ranges.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Approval resolves BEFORE interception: a `bash.patterns` deny never reaches the interceptor, and an accepted `prompt` can still be rejected by an interceptor rule (the subprocess never starts either way).

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: `bash.patterns` allow rules must match the ENTIRE command and never approve shell-control/compound syntax, while deny/prompt rules match both the whole command and each tokenized segment — so `match: "git *"` does not approve `git status && rm -rf build`, but `match: "rm -rf *"` does catch `cd /tmp && rm -rf build`.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: The interceptor blocks only when the rule's `tool` is present in `ctx.toolNames`; invalid regexes are silently skipped; a stage consuming piped stdin from `|`/`|&` (including across blank/comment continuation lines) is never an interception candidate; heredocs, parameter expansion, command substitution, backticks, grouping, and malformed quoting get only the whole-input check. It is routing, not a security boundary.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Internal-URL expansion escapes replacements for `command` (shell text) but uses raw values (`noEscape: true`) for `env` values and `cwd`, which are filesystem/environment values — swapping these breaks quoting or corrupts paths.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Timeout clamping order is global-then-per-tool: `tools.maxTimeout` applies first, then the per-tool range, so debug's 5-second floor still wins over a smaller global ceiling.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: `timeout: 0` must disable the deadline everywhere on that path — no host timer, no native deadline, no background-job deadline — and leaves the auto-background threshold uncapped instead of `timeoutMs - 1000`.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: A native `Shell` session runs one command at a time and `Shell.abort()` kills every in-flight run on that instance; concurrent bash calls must therefore never share a cached session. Track in-flight session keys, run overlapping calls through one-shot shells, and let only the owning call clear the in-use flag or evict the cache entry.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: A shell session that timed out must be quarantined/dropped, never reused.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: The PTY path must NOT apply non-interactive hardening: it inherits the user environment with a real `TERM=xterm-256color` so editors/pagers/TUIs behave normally, whereas non-PTY layers hardening defaults UNDER caller and direnv overrides.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: direnv-provided variables merge BELOW explicit caller `env`, and safe variables direnv removed must be emitted as `unset -v ...` prefixed to the command; an unallowed `.envrc` is never executed.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: `OutputSink` must trim on UTF-8 boundaries and mirror the RAW uncapped stream (not the capped/minimized text) to the artifact; `truncated` must be set by any of tail overflow, middle elision, column-cap drops, or file spill.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Timeout error shaping is backend-specific and must stay that way: local non-PTY and interactive-PTY timeouts return an `isError` result with `details.timedOut`, while client-terminal-bridge timeouts and all non-timeout cancellations throw `ToolError`/`ToolAbortError`.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: One `eval` call is exactly one cell, the tool is `exclusive` per session, and state is isolated per language — `reset` recreates only the requested runtime and is destructive to anything else sharing that backend session id.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Reference-counted pause/resume around `agent()`/`parallel()`/`completion()` is the ONLY mechanism that suspends the eval cell budget; compute, stdout/stderr, `log()`/`phase()`, and ordinary `tool.*` calls must keep consuming it.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: The Python runner owns one persistent asyncio loop: top-level `await` works and `asyncio.run(...)` is invalid; `input()`/interactive stdin must be rejected rather than forwarded.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: SIGINT must be `SIG_IGN` between requests and only installed during execution, so a stray cancel cannot kill the kernel; if `done` does not arrive within 5s of the interrupt, escalate `exit`→SIGTERM→SIGKILL and recreate on the next call.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Retained kernels are keyed by (namespaced eval session id, normalized cwd, interpreter); a dead subprocess is replaced before execution and a mid-run death is retried exactly once; concurrent resets for a key must coalesce so queued runs land on the freshly restarted kernel.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Eval-spawned `agent()` children run with `keepAlive=false` and `shareEvalSession=false`, so their code mutations must not appear in the caller's retained VM/kernel and they must be unregistered/disposed after completion.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: A notebook editable representation MUST begin with a cell marker (any text, including a blank line, before the first marker is rejected), and source lines that look like markers must gain exactly one `%` on render and lose exactly one on parse or round-trip editing corrupts cells.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Notebook serialization must clone the original document and replace only `cells`, reusing an existing unused `cell:N` (preserving code-cell `execution_count`/`outputs`) — and the standalone `write` tool is not notebook-aware, so writing the virtual marker text destroys the file.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: DAP `continue`/`step_*` must subscribe to tree-wide stop/termination events BEFORE sending the request, or the stop event races ahead of the subscription and the action reports a false 'still running'.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: `configurationDone` must be sent during the root/child handshake and lazily before later requests if the handshake never completed; breakpoints must be bound to a new `startDebugging` child BEFORE that child's `configurationDone`.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Only one root DAP session may exist; recursive `startDebugging` children require `tcp` transport reusing the root server, and source breakpoint paths must be `path.resolve()`d before caching/synchronizing across the tree.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: `continue`/`step_*` timing out is non-fatal by contract: return `state: "running"` + `details.timedOut = true`, never throw.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Computer pixel coordinates belong to the most recent screenshot of the SAME target; input before capture, after target/layout change, or using another target's frame must throw `InvalidCoordinateFrame`. AX bounds and `desktop.elementAt()` use global logical desktop coordinates and must never be mixed with screenshot pixels.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Each window AX snapshot advances a reference generation: current and immediately previous refs remain valid, older refs must throw `StaleRef`.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: `read_only: true` blocks mutation only through the `desktop` facade and downgrades approval to `read`; it is NOT a sandbox — the evaluated code retains full Bun/Node host access.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Run-scoped state (signal, read-only policy) must be bound via AsyncLocalStorage so leaked asynchronous work from an earlier run cannot borrow a later run's cancellation or permission context.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: A browser tab name is process-global; rebinding it to a different browser kind must fail with `Tab "..." is bound to a different browser`, and a changed `dialogs` policy must force tab recreation rather than in-place mutation.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Browser handles are refcounted per browser kind: dispose only at zero, and never close/kill connected, relay, or spawned pages on `close` — `kill: true` affects spawned-app process trees only.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: ARIA refs renumber deterministically from `e1` on every snapshot (existing `_ariaRef` expandos are cleared first) and are valid only until the next snapshot; the numeric `observe()` id cache must be cleared on `goto()` and on every new `observe()`.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Per-op browser deadlines must be `min(cellBudget − 1s, ceiling)` so a stalled helper fails with a named error while cell budget remains; `goto`/`evaluate` stay uncapped.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: `app.cdp_url` must be the HTTP CDP discovery endpoint; a `ws://` URL is rejected by `normalizeConnectedCdpUrl()`.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Puppeteer probes the current working directory during module load, so `loadPuppeteer()`/`loadPuppeteerInWorker()` must temporarily redirect cwd to a safe directory containing a `{}` `package.json` before importing `puppeteer-core`.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Stealth patches apply to headless only; spawned, connected, relay, and cmux browsers must remain untouched.

invariants.subsystem: exec-tools (bash / eval / notebook-file / debug / computer / browser + native shell·PTY·process layer)
invariants.rule: Raw page request interception is run-scoped: at run end the worker must remove user `request` handlers, disable interception, and release held requests, or the tab leaks a hung network layer.
Agent ids MUST be allocated before background jobs are registered — the immediate tool text names both the agent id and job id, and the job id IS the agent id.

Agent-id uniquification (`Task`, then `Task-2`/`Task-3`; nested as `Parent.Child`) is what prevents `agent://` artifact collisions across repeated and nested invocations; skipping it silently overwrites outputs.
Discovery dedup is first-wins by EXACT, case-sensitive name (`Task` ≠ `task`), files within a directory load in lexicographic order, and bundled agents are appended last against the same seen-set.
Bundled agents parse at `level: "fatal"` — malformed bundled frontmatter throws and can fail all discovery, unlike a bad custom file which is warned-and-skipped.

Create-time discovery is memoized per cwd only for the tool description; execution MUST rediscover from disk, and blocking behavior MUST be decided after policy resolution, never from the stale description-time agent object.

The concurrency `Semaphore` must be RESIZED IN PLACE from the live setting before every acquire and every release — recreating it loses queued waiters and breaks mid-session `task.maxConcurrency` changes.
The child must terminate through `yield`; `yield` is auto-added to any explicit `tools` list, and after 3 reminders the final prompt must force `toolChoice = yield` where the provider supports it.

`hub` must be retained in child tool lists (unless the session explicitly restricts tool names) — messaging is the ONLY follow-up/resume path to a finished subagent, so stripping it strands idle agents forever.

Subagent settings inherit `async.enabled` and `bash.autoBackground.enabled` from the parent (they are NOT force-disabled), but `tools.approvalMode` MUST be forced to `yolo` because headless children have no UI to confirm prompts against.

`todo` is stripped from children as a parent-owned tool at BOTH the registry and executor layers — except for prewalk-armed spawns, where the plan nudge and todo gate require the child to commit its own list first.

End-of-run status mapping is load-bearing: hard abort/timeout → `aborted` (terminal, disposed); soft-request-budget abort on a non-isolated kept-alive agent → `idle` (resumable); isolated run → `parked` with NO reviver; everything else including failures → `idle` with live session.
Isolated agents are torn down at completion and are not revivable — their workspace is already merged and cleaned, so only `history://<id>` remains readable.
`"Main"` is never parked, and idle-TTL park timers must be unref'd so they never hold the process open.
Messaging a parked agent revives it; this is the only resume primitive — there is deliberately no `resume` parameter on `task`.
The unified `wait` must never drop a photo-finish message: a message consumed by the bus waiter is returned even if a job settles in the same tick, and the jobs keep running and still self-deliver.
A `jobs`/`wait` snapshot that observes a settled job first counts as its delivery and must suppress the duplicate async-result injection.
Smart-ladder bookkeeping (`recordPollWaitEnd`) runs only when the smart window was actually used; an explicit `timeoutMs` must not advance the ladder.
`send` with both `to` and `name` is ambiguous and must be rejected; `await: true` is invalid with `to: "all"`; self-send is rejected.
A `wait` timeout is a normal result (`waited: null` or an all-running snapshot flagged `useless`), never an error.
Launch names are unique per project directory: a live name must be stopped or restarted; starting a completed name creates a new launch and rotates its prior output log.
`detached: true` implies `persist` and forces `pty: false`, disabling stdin — process input is a single serialized stream shared by all project clients.
When both `ready.log` and `ready.port` are supplied, BOTH must pass; readiness must be observed, since process creation alone is not readiness.
A `todo` op that produces ANY error discards every mutation it made — the returned and persisted state stay at the pre-call list — and `view` never normalizes or writes.
`normalizeInProgressTask` runs exactly once after the op completes, never mid-op, so a single op may build a transient invalid state and rely on final normalization.

`todo` task lookup is exact string equality on content across all phases (first match wins); `append` enforces global task-content uniqueness and `init` rejects duplicate phase names and duplicate task contents.

`ask` runs `concurrency: "exclusive"` because the selector/editor surface is shared; concurrent asks would clobber each other. Reserved option labels `Other (type your own)`, `Chat about this`, and `Next →` must never be used by callers.
`ask` headless use and user cancellation THROW `ToolAbortError` (after aborting the context) rather than returning a structured result; only an empty `questions` array returns text.
A `web_search` response with no renderable content must be rejected as a `SearchProviderError(204)` so the chain advances — never presented as a successful empty search.
Query-constraint post-filtering relaxes any dimension that would eliminate all results and must emit a leading `Note:` — and must never rewrite answer or citation text.
`providers.webSearchTimeoutSeconds` is a per-provider transport ceiling, not a whole-chain deadline; the chain is strictly sequential with no fan-out.
`public` must never be auto-selected: its `isAvailable()` is false and only `isExplicitlyAvailable()` is true.
Aborting `web_search` must rethrow the cancellation during fallback handling instead of returning an `"Error: ..."` text result.

`pr_checkout` must serialize every git mutation under a repo lock keyed by the PRIMARY repo root, not the current worktree path, because worktrees share `.git/config`, `packed-refs`, and commit-graph state.
`pr_push` has no metadata source other than the `branch.pr-<number>.ompPr*` git-config keys written by `pr_checkout`; it must run after a checkout for that branch.
`run_watch` commit-mode success means "all observed runs succeeded AND the run-ID set is unchanged one poll later", not merely that the latest poll looked green.
`file_read` rejects a path with a leading `/` and URL-encodes every path segment independently; `search_code` rejects `since`/`until` because GitHub code search has no date qualifier.

`security_scan` `start` must recompute the plan fingerprint from current state and refuse on any mismatch; native scans require OAuth (API-key-only auth is rejected) and stay pinned to the exact credential row for execution and refresh.
`security_publish` must succeed exactly once per scan; a second call fails, no publication yields a `partial` scan, and out-of-scope/absolute/parent-traversing finding paths are rejected.
`scan.json` is written LAST as the commit marker of a completed output directory; directories are `0700` and files `0600` on non-Windows.
`cloud_pull` fails closed unless the project's `origin` remote's normalized repository identity matches the cloud configuration URL.

`generate_image` falls through to the next provider ONLY on credentialed HTTP failures; validation, parsing, local I/O, cancellation, and timeout errors must abort immediately, and `provider: "auto"` adds no provider to the order.
`inspect_image` must verify the resolved model advertises `input.includes("image")` BEFORE reading the file, and must send content parts in the order `[image, text]`.
Image format support is determined by content sniffing, never by filename extension.
`tts` codec is inferred solely from the `output_path` suffix; a local-backend MP3 request writes a sibling `.wav` and must say so in the result.
Advisor rows are observability records, not peers: they must be excluded from `hub`, `history://`, and `agent://` peer workflows and can never be messaged, revived, or killed.

Appends are strictly append-only: every append creates exactly one entry whose parentId is the current leafId, and that entry becomes the new leaf. branch() only moves the pointer; existing entries are never mutated or deleted, so rewrites must preserve logical history.
branch() must reject null — use resetLeaf() for the root-before-first-entry state; branchWithSummary(null) is legal and must persist fromId as the literal string "root".
A branch summary is attached at the NEW navigation position (as a child of the target leaf), never on the abandoned branch tail.

The logical first entry must be a valid session header (type==="session" with a string id); an invalid or missing header means the file is treated as EMPTY and re-initialized at that exact path — this is recovery, never a hard error. Only real I/O failures propagate.

If any migration ran, the session must be marked for a full rewrite and that rewrite must complete before incremental appends resume; never interleave migrated in-memory state with appends against the un-rewritten file.

The title slot is a fixed 256-byte first line. Title changes patch the slot in place and append a title_change audit entry; they must not rewrite the body, or listing loses its cheap-prefix guarantee.
titleSource:"user" blocks any automatic rename; auto-naming must check getSessionName() emptiness first.

Persistence truncation must exempt signed/encrypted provider blocks, signature fields, and complete Anthropic native web-search history blocks — these must stay byte-exact or replay breaks. Signature fields are CLEARED, not truncated.

image_url data URLs are always externalized to blobs regardless of size; other base64 image payloads only at ≥1024 chars. Persisted blob refs must be exactly `blob:sha256:` + 64 lowercase hex, and parseBlobRef must validate before any path join (path traversal).
A missing blob during rehydration must warn and keep the ref string in memory; it must never abort the session load.

Context reconstruction must stop the parentId walk on a repeated id to bound corrupt cycles, and getTree() must sort children oldest→newest by timestamp with orphan/self-parent/null-parent entries promoted to roots.

Dangling tool calls must be removed from model context (protected reasoning metadata neutralized on rewritten turns) and unsafe aborted/error assistant turns dropped with their paired tool results — except when keepDanglingToolCalls is set for a mid-turn transcript rebuild.
The latest reset_boundary on the path hides everything through it from model context and the collapsed live transcript, while the JSONL and full-transcript export must still retain pre-reset history.

Compaction must never cut at a toolResult entry, must only consider entries after the previous compaction, and must pull trailing non-message metadata entries (model_change, thinking_level_change, label…) into the kept region by walking the cut index backward.

The `useless` flag must never coexist with `isError` (errors win), must never reach provider wire formats, and must only blank results in place — flagged pairs are never removed, so tool-call/result pairing and provider-native replay stay intact.
Never blank a tool result below MIN_PRUNE_TOKENS=50: the `[Output truncated - N tokens]` placeholder costs ~8 tokens, so pruning smaller results grows the context and churns the prompt cache.

Handoff generation must append its prompt as a trailing agent-attributed USER message on a context built by the identical transform/normalization pipeline as a live turn, keep the tools array present, and reuse the live promptCacheKey — otherwise the provider cache prefix is invalidated. toolChoice must be "none" with exactly one compatibility retry at "auto".

Handoff writes nothing to the old session; the document lives only as a custom_message in the new session. Overflow recovery must never use the handoff strategy because the handoff request would carry the same oversized input.
Rewind side effects are deferred to turn_end; the tool's execute() must only record the request. Applying rewind inside execute() would rewrite history mid-turn.

At most one active checkpoint per session; checkpoint state is reconstructed from the ordinary successful checkpoint tool-result entry (there is no dedicated marker entry), so that entry must remain on the active branch.

Artifact id allocation must scan the directory for the max existing numeric id BEFORE the first allocation, and concurrent first allocations must share one initialization promise, or resume/parallel tools hand out duplicate ids and overwrite artifacts.
artifact:// ids are session-local: resolution must prefer the calling session's pinned artifacts directory before other registered directories.
session_before_* hooks are cancellable and the emitter must return early on the first cancelling result; after-events are observational only.

switchSession must snapshot manager/messages/queues/model/thinking/tier/tools/prompts/provider-cache/memory/checkpoint state before any mutation and fully restore + reconnect + re-reconcile on any throw; it must never create a new session file.
Concurrent completed appends must supersede an in-flight atomic rewrite with an authoritative full-body rewrite so a stale publication cannot clobber them.
A breadcrumb third line of `fresh` denotes a lazily-unmaterialized /new boundary: a missing target with `fresh` must start a new session, never fall back to the previous transcript.
Recent/list scans must read only the 4 KiB prefix (plus a bounded 32 KiB tail for lifecycle status) — never the full JSONL body.

Core-reserved customType strings (tool_execution_start, session_exit, user_todo_edit, vibe-session-lifecycle, autoresearch-control) must not be used by extensions; collisions cause core replay logic to interpret extension data as lifecycle state.
session_exit must be followed immediately by flushSync() so the next process can inspect the last durable turn.

The share encryption key lives only in the URL fragment and must never appear in any HTTP request; redaction must DROP opaque provider replay fields and untyped extension payloads rather than traversing them.
Export must append zero session entries.
`disabledProviders` is evaluated BEFORE credentials; a disabled provider id can never be re-enabled by any key, OAuth session, env var, or models.yml apiKey.

Settings arrays (`disabledProviders`, `enabledModels`) are replaced wholesale by the higher-precedence layer, never merged or appended; path-scoped entries are resolved AFTER the merge, so a project array silently drops global scoped entries.
A variable already present in the process environment is never overwritten by any `.env` file; among files precedence is `<cwd>/.env` > `~/.omp/agent/.env` > `~/.omp/.env` > `~/.env`.

The `models.yml` config key (ladder layer 2) must beat stored OAuth (layer 3) so a key supplied for a custom baseUrl/gateway is used instead of forwarding an upstream OAuth token the proxy would reject — but it must never override a runtime `--api-key`.
Anthropic assistant turns must be stably partitioned so all `tool_use` blocks sit at the tail; otherwise Anthropic 400s with "tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks immediately after".

All parallel Google `functionResponse` parts must be merged into a single contiguous `user` message, or Google errors that the number of function response parts does not equal the number of function call parts.
Vertex `GenerateContent` rejects `id` on `functionCall`/`functionResponse` parts; the field must be deleted for `google-vertex` even though Gemini 3 accepts it.

Bedrock Converse validates that any request whose history contains `toolUse`/`toolResult` supplies a `toolConfig`; with no active tools a `__no_tools__` sentinel must be injected and its synthetic tool-use events and `tool_use` stop reason suppressed.
When an owned in-band tool dialect is active the native tools array is stripped, so `tool_choice` MUST be `undefined` — a native `tool_choice` without native `tools` 400s.

`tool_choice: "none"` must be dropped when no tools are emitted (LiteLLM/Bedrock proxies 400), and a forced named choice must be deleted when that tool was filtered out by active-tool selection or schema quarantine.

For Anthropic through LiteLLM/Bedrock: if history contains tool calls/results and `context.tools` is undefined, send `tools: []` as a sentinel; if `context.tools` is explicitly `[]`, treat it as an opt-out and do NOT emit the sentinel.

OpenAI Responses stream completion is authoritative only after `response.completed` or `response.incomplete`; a stream close before either terminal event must fail rather than surface partial output as success.
Codex chains `previous_response_id` only over websocket — SSE never chains — so stale-id fallback logic applies to the websocket path only.

Retry (provider-level or session-level) must stop once user-visible content has been emitted: non-empty text, images, tool calls, or server-tool blocks are replay-unsafe; thinking-only and whitespace-only partials are safe to discard.

Strict-tool fallback must be scoped to the failing capability and to `${provider}:${baseUrl}:${modelId}` (or a per-session flag for Anthropic) — it must not disable unrelated features, and a stale Responses chain must reset chain state rather than disabling Responses entirely.

Synthetic `"."` reasoning placeholders are acceptable for Kimi/OpenRouter-style compat but NOT for exact-replay providers (DeepSeek reasoning, MiMo) where `allowsSyntheticReasoningContentForToolCalls` is false.
Google thought signatures may only be retained when `msg.provider === model.provider && msg.model === model.id` and the value passes a base64 validity check; foreign signatures must be stripped.

Anthropic budget thinking requires `max_tokens` to be raised to at least `budget_tokens + 1024`; forced tool choice must delete `params.thinking` and pin adaptive-only models to the lowest effort so default adaptive thinking cannot re-engage.
Anthropic prompt-cache breakpoints are capped at 4 per request and `cache_control` must sit on a text part.
OpenRouter must omit catalog-default max-token fields unless the caller set an explicit cap, because optional fields are treated as routing hints and bias upstream selection.
Codex must strip every sampling parameter (`temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `min_p`, penalties, `stop`) and must not forward caller max-token caps; the backend returns 400 for both.
The `whenThinking` compat variant is a fully pre-built alternate object that is pointer-swapped at request time — it must not be produced by per-request spreading/allocation.

The synthetic `start` event must not count as first progress for the stream watchdog, and keepalive/role-only/empty-`choices` chunks are not progress; `trackLocalWork()` must suppress stall detection for server-requested local work.
`done`/`error` resolves `result()`; `fail(error)` rejects both iteration and `result()`; `end()` without a final result must reject `result()` rather than leave it pending.
Mid-stream tool-argument re-parsing must be throttled to ≥256 new bytes of growth (linear, not quadratic), but the parse at the tool-call boundary is unconditional and authoritative.

The broker is the only writer of OAuth refresh tokens: clients receive snapshots with refresh fields replaced by a sentinel and must refresh via `POST /v1/credential/:id/refresh`; local replace/upsert/delete-by-provider mutations must be rejected.

Broker usage caching layers must nest correctly: the client's 15 s single-flight window sits strictly below the broker's 5-minute ±25 % jittered server cache, and a per-caller `AbortSignal` must be raced against the shared in-flight promise, never threaded into it.

An unreadable, malformed, or invalid account-pool file must abort initialization rather than silently broadening the visible credential set; account pools are a routing policy, not an authorization boundary.

The broker snapshot cache is keyed by both token and URL (AES-256-GCM with the URL as AAD) and anchored to broker-stamped `generatedAt`; 401/403 must never be masked by the cache, only transient server errors may fall back to it.
Retry attempt counters increment before the max check, so the max-exceeded event reports `attempt - 1`; `prompt()` must not resolve until the retry lifecycle promise settles.
Context-overflow errors are excluded from retry classification and must route to context promotion then compaction; if retry is initiated, compaction checks are skipped for that turn.

Provider `headers`/`compat`/`remoteCompaction` are baselines: model-level `headers` override provider header keys and `compat` deep-merges with `openRouterRouting`, `vercelGatewayRouting`, `extraBody`, and `whenThinking` merged as nested objects.
OAuth grant TTL is absolute for some providers (Anthropic: 30 days) regardless of refresh-token rotation, so refresh success alone does not imply a usable session.

Refreshes must be single-flighted per credential id, and definitive failures (`invalid_grant`/`invalid_token`/`revoked`/non-blip 401/403) must disable the credential while transient failures are left untouched for the next sweep.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Anthropic Messages API ordering is enforced with HTTP 400: `tool_result` blocks MUST be first in their `user` message's content array (any text after them), that user message MUST immediately follow the assistant `tool_use` message with nothing in between, and every `tool_use.id` MUST be answered by a matching `tool_result.tool_use_id` in that next message. Parallel results MUST all ship in ONE user message.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Anthropic `tool_use.input` is an ALREADY-PARSED object in non-streaming responses — never `JSON.parse` it. Only streaming `input_json_delta.partial_json` fragments are strings, and they MUST be concatenated per content-block `index` and parsed only at that block's `content_block_stop` (mid-stream fragments like `{"location":` are not valid JSON).

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Anthropic streaming `stop_reason` is `null` in `message_start` and arrives in `message_delta` (NOT `message_stop`); `usage` in `message_delta` is cumulative, not incremental.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Anthropic extended-thinking `thinking`/`redacted_thinking` blocks (with their `signature`) MUST be replayed verbatim across turns when combined with tools; forced `tool_choice` (`any`/`tool`) is rejected while thinking is on, and `any`/`tool` suppress the leading text preamble entirely.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Harmony generation MUST stop on BOTH `<|return|>` and `<|call|>`; stopping only on `<|return|>` runs past tool calls and stopping only on `<|end|>` is wrong for assistant generation.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Harmony recipients (`to=functions.NAME`) may appear in the ROLE section or the CHANNEL section of a header — a parser MUST accept both. Channel is mandatory on every assistant message.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Harmony tool-result messages are authored by the TOOL'S NAME (`functions.get_current_weather`), not the literal string `tool`; splitting `functions.x` into namespace + function is the parser's job.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Harmony CoT dropping is conditional: drop prior `analysis` messages ONLY when the last assistant turn ended in a `final` message. Dropping the `analysis` immediately preceding a `<|call|>` breaks multi-step tool reasoning.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: When persisting a Harmony assistant reply into history, normalize the trailing `<|return|>` to `<|end|>` so every stored message is a well-formed `<|start|>{header}<|message|>{content}<|end|>`.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Harmony `<|...|>` control tokens are atomic special tokens in `o200k_harmony` — encoding them as ordinary text yields different ranks and corrupts the stream.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
