invariants.rule: DeepSeek markers use U+FF5C FULLWIDTH VERTICAL LINE (`｜`) and U+2581 (`▁`), NOT ASCII `|`/`_`. Substituting ASCII produces tokens the model never trained on and silently breaks both generation and parsing. Only `<think>`/`</think>` and the rare `<|EOT|>` use ASCII brackets/pipes.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: DeepSeek V3.1 chains parallel calls with NO separator, newline, or space (`…<｜tool▁call▁end｜><｜tool▁call▁begin｜>…`); split on the call-boundary tokens, never on whitespace. Legacy V3-0324/R1-0528 prefixes each subsequent call with `\n` and uses `function<｜tool▁sep｜>{name}` + a fenced ```json block — the two grammars are mutually unparseable.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: DeepSeek emits `</think>` even in non-thinking mode; strip everything up to and including the first `</think>` before treating the remainder as the visible answer. After a `tool` message the reference V3.1 template appends NO `<｜Assistant｜>` marker — an agent loop MUST NOT double-insert one.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: GLM `<arg_value>` typing is schema-driven: a value is a literal unquoted string IFF the parameter is string-typed in the tool's JSON Schema, otherwise it is JSON-decoded. There is NO escaping mechanism — a value containing `</arg_value>` or `</tool_call>` truncates the parse.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: GLM tool calls are parsed from post-`</think>` content ONLY; a `<tool_call>` emitted inside `<think>…</think>` is ignored. GLM's `eos_token_id` is a LIST (`<|endoftext|>`, `<|user|>`, `<|observation|>`) — the tool turn ends because `<|observation|>` is an EOS id.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: For GLM, Qwen3, Kimi, and DeepSeek the structural tool/think tags are registered `special: false`; `skip_special_tokens` MUST be off (servers force it false when tools are enabled) or the literal markers vanish and no tool call is detected.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Qwen3/Hermes `arguments` is a NESTED JSON OBJECT on the wire but a JSON STRING at the OpenAI API boundary — never double-encode. Qwen3 renders `role: "tool"` messages into `<|im_start|>user` turns (not a `tool` turn), coalescing consecutive results into one turn.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Kimi call ids are `functions.{name}:{idx}` where `{idx}` is a PER-TURN 0-based counter that resets each assistant turn — ids are NOT unique across turns; disambiguate by turn when persisting. The result body must echo the exact originating id after `## Return of `.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Gemini/Gemma-3 call arguments are PYTHON literals, not JSON (`True`/`False`/`None`, single quotes, trailing commas). A JSON parser rejects valid calls. When scanning for call openers you MUST track string state so a `(` inside a string literal (e.g. `search(pattern="foo(")`) is not mis-detected.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Gemma 4 pipes are ASYMMETRIC: opener `<|tool_call>`, closer `<tool_call|>` (never `</tool_call>`). The string delimiter `<|"|>` is a TOKEN, so raw `"` and `,` inside a string span are literal data — split arguments on `,`/`}` only OUTSIDE a string span and honor `[]`/`{}` depth.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: XML-family dialects (anthropic, xml, minimax) are delimiter-matched, NOT real XML: parameter bodies MUST NOT be entity-escaped or run through an XML DOM/entity decoder. Write `a & b < c` literally; only a literal `</parameter>` is reserved. Tool and parameter NAMES in attributes are still XML-escaped by the renderer.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Formats without wire ids (xml, minimax, anthropic-xml, glm, qwen3, deepseek, gemini, gemma) correlate results to calls by ORDER ALONE — never reorder, split, or drop a result in a parallel batch.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: The stream projector materializes a canonical call at `toolStart`, BEFORE `toolEnd`. Consequently an unterminated call on a normally stopped stream stays runnable (retaining uncoerced streamed argument text, or `{}` if the scanner emits no deltas), while a provider `length` stop MUST remain non-runnable `length`. `flush()` only clears scanner-private state; it never retracts an emitted `toolStart`.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Scanner acceptance is deliberately WIDER than renderer output (wrapper aliases, `antml:` prefixes, bare invokes, stringified `arguments`). Renderers MUST still emit only the canonical form so behavior never depends on recovery paths.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: `xmlTagset` selects the SCANNER ONLY. Choosing `dsml` does not make the XML renderer emit DSML; the `xml` definition's call/result/thinking/transcript renderers always emit generic plain-XML.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Tool schemas MUST be supplied to BOTH the renderer and the scanner: schema-declared strings are what keep a value literal instead of JSON-quoted on render and JSON-coerced on parse. Without schemas even a plain JavaScript string round-trips as a quoted JSON string.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Emit `strict: true` ONLY when strict enforcement actually succeeded — `tryEnforceStrictSchema` is fail-open and returns `{strict:false, schema: upgraded}` on any throw.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Strict-mode precedence rules are load-bearing: inlining a local `$ref` merges with SIBLING KEYS WINNING over the resolved def, and collapsing a single-item `allOf` lets the INLINED ENTRY's keys win over the original siblings. A shared `description` on a type-array expansion is hoisted onto the `anyOf` WRAPPER, never duplicated onto each branch.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: In the Anthropic native whitelist, constraints that are dropped are APPENDED TO THAT NODE'S `description` — they stay model-visible guidance and must not be silently discarded. Object nodes default to `additionalProperties: false`; an explicit `true`/schema value (empty schema → `true`) stays open.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: Harmony leak detection MUST require a co-signal — a bare `to=functions.NAME` marker alone is insufficient, and fenced examples must be ignored — otherwise legitimate content discussing the protocol triggers false aborts. Tool-argument detection stays inert unless the caller supplies the byte offset where a structurally valid tool parse ended.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: pi-native reports `reason` as the TOP-LEVEL event field while `stopReason` exists only on the nested `AssistantMessage`; a cancelled stream emits `{type:"error", reason:"aborted"}` with nested `stopReason:"aborted"`, and any other clean close without a terminal event synthesizes `{type:"done", reason:"stop"}` so `.result()` cannot hang.

invariants.subsystem: toolconv — tool-call wire-format conversion: provider-native protocols, owned in-band dialects (renderers + streaming scanners), schema normalization, and leak/fabrication healing
invariants.rule: `tools.format` applies at SESSION START; it is not a per-request switch.

NEVER add a second `CSI 3 J` (ED3) callsite — ED3 flows only through `#emitFullPaint({ clearScrollback: true })`, only for explicit user gestures or the guarded opt-in divergence rebuild, and NEVER inside a multiplexer (it is a no-op there and the replay would duplicate pane history).

Ordinary emitters treat frame rows `< committedRows` as immutable and MUST NEVER rewrite them; a shrink or structural resync may re-anchor below the old commit point, but stale history remains and new bytes are appended — it is never silently skipped.
Commits are EXACTLY the chunk: any byte shape that scrolls the screen must scroll only rows accounted for by the commit advance, or the shadow ledger diverges from the real tape.

A multiplexer WIDTH resize NEVER advances history: old committed physical-row coordinates are opaque after host reflow, no old/new row counts may be compared, and no old viewport row may be recommitted. Height-only resizes do not terminate the epoch.
NEVER probe the terminal viewport/scroll position and NEVER fork on platform in the update path — win32 behaves like POSIX; ConPTY's probe lies and POSIX has no API.

Only declare a row exact when its bytes are stable. Rows before the live-region seam are under the exact-prefix audit; unpinned mutable rows commit as frozen visual snapshots and are deliberately outside the exactness claim.
Park the hardware cursor at the real content bottom, not the padded window bottom, or height shrinks scroll live rows into history and duplicate them once per resize step.
Cursor writes must live INSIDE the synchronized-output frame, before ESU — never emitted as a second frame after it.
NEVER throw in the render hot path: clamp over-wide lines with `truncateToWidth`; a width mismatch is cosmetic, not fatal.
Multiplexers get no destructive clear and no history rewrap on resize — repaint the window in place and let pane history keep its authored wrap.
When several root children report a live-region seam, the TOPMOST seam wins, because commits are prefix-only.

An unchanged component MUST return the SAME array reference; a changed component MUST return a NEW array. Mutating a previously returned array in place is only legal alongside a `RenderStablePrefix` implementation.

`done(...)` in a custom-UI factory must be called exactly once, or the mount never unwinds (editor never restored, promise never resolves). `dispose()` must be idempotent because containers propagate disposal and reset/removal paths converge.

Measuring and slicing must use ONE width model: `visibleWidth` (`Bun.stringWidth` with `countAnsiEscapeCodes:false`, `ambiguousIsNarrow:true`) and the native slice/wrap engine must never disagree — mixing unpinned width models in measure-vs-slice caused crashes.

Kitty images are transmit-once/place-many: NEVER re-emit full base64 per frame, and image demotion must use the ordinary window diff with a height-preserving text fallback — never a destructive replay, or committed rows below shift.

Every capability probe must own a TYPED sentinel (`#da1SentinelOwners` FIFO discriminated by `kind`) and survive a reply split across a stdin flush; a partial `\x1b[?…` must be abandoned on a new `\x1b` or >256 bytes so real keys still reach input.
Slash-command dedup is first-wins by name after sorting providers by priority descending; shadowed duplicates must remain visible in `result.all` with `_shadowed = true` rather than being discarded.

The prompt pipeline order is load-bearing: built-in registry → extension commands → TypeScript/MCP custom commands → file-command expansion → prompt-template expansion → delivery. Built-ins reserve their names and aliases before file commands are considered.

During streaming, `prompt()` THROWS if `streamingBehavior` is omitted; extension commands must execute immediately rather than being queued as text, and `steer`/`followUp` must reject extension commands.

Session teardown is promise-memoized with first-caller-wins semantics; a draft-save failure is logged but must NOT skip disposal, and later callers must await the same promise rather than re-running shutdown.
`Ctrl+Z` suspend must stop the TUI to release terminal modes BEFORE sending `SIGTSTP`, and register a one-shot `SIGCONT` handler; it must not run session teardown.
Escape handling must dispatch on live session state inside a single `onEscape` handler (`isCompacting`/`isGeneratingHandoff`/`isRetrying`) rather than swapping handlers per state.
New mutable UI above the editor must report (or live inside) the live-region seam, or it freezes at the first commit.
Ordinary update emitters must never emit ED2/ED3 or an absolute cursor home — several terminal families snap a scrolled reader to the bottom on those.
Theme `vars` resolution must throw on a missing or circular reference; `setTheme` failure falls back to built-in `dark`, but `previewTheme` failure must leave the current theme untouched.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Registration-only during load: any runtime action (`pi.sendMessage`, `pi.setActiveTools`, …) called during factory execution MUST throw `ExtensionRuntimeNotInitializedError`; wiring happens later in `ExtensionRunner.initialize()`.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: `tool_call` is fail-closed: a handler that throws blocks the tool, and the first `{block:true}` short-circuits remaining handlers with `reason` becoming the tool error text the model sees.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: `tool_call` non-blocking returns are last-wins and handlers never observe each other's `input` revisions; `input` replacement is ignored when blocking and MUST NOT be applied to `computer` tool calls.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: `tool_result` under the extension runner is a middleware chain (each handler sees prior modifications); under the legacy `HookRunner` it is last-wins with every handler seeing the original event. The two subsystems must not be conflated.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: `HookToolWrapper` never propagates a returned `isError`, and on tool failure it emits `tool_result(isError:true)` and then rethrows the ORIGINAL error — execution cannot be resumed from the error path.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Extension path de-duplication is by resolved absolute path, first-seen-wins, so a module that is both auto-discovered and explicitly configured loads once at the earlier (auto-discovery) position — explicit configuration cannot reorder it.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Capability dedupe is higher-priority-provider-wins, ties by registration order, first-seen-wins within a provider; shadowed items survive only in `result.all` with `_shadowed = true`. Intra-provider order direction differs: the gemini loader appends user-then-project (user wins) while native builds project-then-user (project wins).

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Native extension auto-discovery applies `gitignore: true` / `hidden: false`, but explicit configured-directory scanning in `loader.ts` uses raw `readdir` with no gitignore filtering — the same directory can yield different sets depending on how it was reached.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Auto-scanning of native/configured extension directories accepts only `.ts` and `.js`; explicitly named files and installed-plugin manifest entries additionally accept `.mjs` and `.cjs`. Directory manifest entries resolve `index.{ts,js,mjs,cjs}`; plain auto-scan resolves only `index.{ts,js}`, preferring TS.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Module import must use the entry realpath plus a `?mtime` cache-buster, otherwise edited extension sources will not reload.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Extensions are not sandboxed: one process, one `EventBus`, one `ExtensionRuntime`. A raw `setInterval`/`setTimeout`/detached-promise callback that throws escapes handler dispatch, surfaces as `uncaughtException`, and the postmortem handler tears down the entire session — background work MUST go through `ctx.setInterval`/`ctx.setTimeout` (isolated, `unref`'d, auto-cleared on `session_shutdown`).

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: `pi.appendEntry` `customType` is a single global namespace: values must be package- or reverse-domain-qualified and must avoid core-reserved custom session-entry types.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Tool names must be globally unique in the active registry; conflicts are rejected against built-ins and already-loaded custom tools.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: `loadMode` defaults to `"discoverable"` except for the canonical essential names (`read`, `write`, `bash`, `edit`, `glob`, `computer`, `eval`, `task`, `hub`, `learn`, `manage_skill`) which default to `"essential"` so wrappers/re-registrations cannot silently demote them; an explicit `loadMode` always wins.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: `ctx.invokeTool` is same-tool-only (native built-in of the identical name), is deliberately not re-gated by approval because the caller already holds approval for that tool, and must be depth-guarded against self-recursion; it is `undefined` for tools shadowing nothing.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: `message_end` delivers a detached message snapshot, so provider-context changes must be made from `tool_result` or `context` instead.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: `session_stop` continuations are capped at 8 consecutive iterations and the event never fires for task/subagent sessions.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: `mcp_notification` must fire only AFTER the MCP manager's own handling of known list/update methods, and notifications arriving before the first subscriber must be buffered in a bounded drop-oldest FIFO (cap 100) and drained into that first subscriber.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Extension `ToolDefinition.execute` is `(toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx)` but `CustomTool.execute` is `(toolCallId, params, onUpdate, ctx, signal)` — the bridge MUST reorder arguments.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Reserved shortcuts are silently ignored: `ctrl+c`, `ctrl+d`, `ctrl+z`, `ctrl+k`, `ctrl+p`, `ctrl+l`, `ctrl+o`, `ctrl+t`, `ctrl+g`, `ctrl+q`, `alt+m`, `shift+tab`, `shift+ctrl+p`, `alt+enter`, `escape`, `enter`.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Slash-command names that collide with built-ins are skipped with a diagnostic rather than overriding; `ctx.reload()` is terminal for the current command handler frame.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: `skill://` resolution must reject absolute paths and `..`, and must reject any resolved path escaping the skill's `baseDir`; there is no fallback search for missing assets.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Skill discovery is non-recursive: only `<skills-root>/<skill>/SKILL.md` is found, never `<root>/group/<skill>/SKILL.md`. Managed (auto-learn) skills resolve dead-last and always defer to a same-named authored skill.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Skill filter order is fixed: disabled → source-toggle → ignored → included; `hide: true` hides from the system prompt but does NOT disable the skill (still reachable via `skill://` and `/skill:`).

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: `disabledExtensions` is a shared list with typed ids — `extension-module:<derivedName>` for modules and `skill:<name>` for skills; the derived module name is the file stem or the directory name for `index.*` entries.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Plugin `enabledFeatures === null` means "apply the defaults policy" (features marked `default: true`), which is NOT the same as `[]` (no features).

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: The npm shell-metacharacter denylist is applied after `parsePluginSpec` strips feature brackets, so a legitimate `pkg[feat]` never trips it; git specs bypass the package-name regex and are validated only against `SHELL_METACHARS`.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Install must validate every manifest-declared extension entry by resolving, importing to a factory function, and initializing it against a throwaway registration surface, then roll back `plugins/package.json`, `bun.lock`, and the package snapshot on any failure.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Marketplace catalog validation is asymmetric: an invalid required top-level field or invalid JSON rejects the entire catalog, while an invalid plugin entry is logged and skipped so the rest stay installable.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Relative plugin sources must begin with `./`, are resolved inside the marketplace root after `metadata.pluginRoot` is prepended, and any traversal outside the root (including `git-subdir` `path`) is rejected.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: An enabled project-scoped marketplace install shadows an enabled user-scoped install of the same `name@marketplace`; a disabled project install must NOT shadow the user install.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Catalog path preference is `.omp-plugin/marketplace.json` first, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` as fallback (same shape); plugin manifests likewise read `.omp-plugin/plugin.json` before `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, and a manifest `mcpServers` declaration replaces `.mcp.json` rather than merging.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Marketplace/plugin names must match lowercase `[a-z0-9]` start/end with only lowercase letters, digits, `-`, and `.` inside, ≤64 chars; `name@marketplace` IDs ≤128 chars.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Lockfile writes rewrite the whole file with no cross-process locking or merge strategy — concurrent writers overwrite each other.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Gemini manifest validity is gated purely on `tryParseJson()` truthiness, so valid JSON literals `null`, `false`, `0`, and `""` take the same warning path as syntactically invalid JSON; there is no `ExtensionManifest` runtime validator.

invariants.subsystem: extensibility (extensions, hooks, custom tools, skills, plugins, marketplace, capability discovery)
invariants.rule: Both the native `.omp/extensions` project root and the gemini `<cwd>/.gemini/extensions` root are cwd-only — no ancestor directory walk.
Source base order is fixed and identical at both scopes: `.omp` → `.claude` → `.codex` → `.gemini`; `.pi` MUST NOT appear in generic discovery order.
`getConfigDirs()` returns ALL user-level entries before ANY project-level entry — project precedence comes from capability/subsystem merge logic, never from this ordering.

`PI_CONFIG_DIR` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` are not interchangeable: `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` moves `getAgentDir()` consumers (settings, native discovery, `agent.db`, runtime state) but NOT the generic `getConfigDirs()`/`findConfigFile()` OMP base, and named profiles ignore it entirely.
`OMP_PROFILE` wins over `PI_PROFILE` even when explicitly set to empty; `default`, empty, or whitespace selects the default profile.

Profile isolation is total for agent config — with two documented exceptions: keybindings (default profile's file merged UNDER the profile's, per-binding, inherited file read-only) and `install-id` (shared at the base config root).

Settings capability items are never deduplicated and are merged in provider-visit order highest→lowest priority, so a LOWER-priority provider's project settings override a higher-priority provider's; native `.omp/config.yml` model roles MUST be reapplied after that merge as the authoritative project model-role layer.
Deep merge applies to objects only: scalars AND arrays are replaced wholesale by the higher-precedence layer, so a project array must contain the complete desired set.
Path-scoped entries in `enabledModels`/`disabledProviders` are resolved AFTER the layer merge against the final effective array — never per layer.

Overlay strictness is asymmetric: a missing file, invalid YAML, or a non-mapping root in `PI_CONFIG_FILES`/`--config` is a hard error and the overlay is never quarantined, while invalid global or native-project YAML IS moved to a unique `.broken-<timestamp>-<pid>-<uuid>` sibling under a file lock before startup fails with both paths.

All persistent writes go to the global main YAML selected at startup (`config.yml`, or an existing `config.yaml` updated in place); the sole project write path is a model-selector role assignment under `modelRoleStorage: project`, which touches only `modelRoles`.
Settings saves MUST be debounced and MUST re-read the file under a lock before writing, or concurrent external edits made during a live session are lost.
`omp config reset <key>` persists the schema DEFAULT value; it must not delete the key.
Field-level migrations run on EVERY raw settings load — global, project, overlays, and runtime overrides — not only on the global file.

The startup legacy migration (`settings.json` + `agent.db` → `config.yml`, DB wins conflicts, `settings.json` renamed `.bak`) runs only when NEITHER `config.yml` nor `config.yaml` exists; after that the legacy sources are never consulted.
JSON→YAML auto-migration fires only when the requested path is `.yml`/`.yaml` and only a sibling `.json` exists, and must be idempotent (once per process).

Native project discovery stops at the NEAREST non-empty `.omp/` directory; a missing `AGENTS.md`/`RULES.md`/`SYSTEM.md` there must NOT cause the walk to continue upward. Empty `.omp/` directories are skipped and empty files contribute nothing.

Settings discovery, `SYSTEM.md`/`APPEND_SYSTEM.md`/`TITLE_SYSTEM.md` discovery, and `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `.gemini/GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` never walk ancestors — only `<cwd>/<base>/`.
Capability dedup is first-wins by `key(item)`; `key === undefined` disables dedup entirely; shadowed items must remain in `all` marked `_shadowed` while being excluded from `items`.
Equal-priority providers must preserve registration order (cursor before windsurf) because dedup outcomes depend on it.

Rule identity is `rule.name` only — two different files with the same name are the same logical rule; both sticky candidates are synthesized as name `RULES`, so a regular `rules/RULES.md` can shadow them.
TTSR bucketing runs BEFORE always-apply/rulebook bucketing: an accepted `condition`/`astCondition` makes the rule TTSR-only regardless of `alwaysApply` or GitHub `applyTo`.

`rule://` resolves only against rulebook ∪ always-apply ∪ registered TTSR rules, from a process-global snapshot installed exactly once per top-level session; resolution is exact-name and unknown names must list available names.
Always-apply rule content must be deduped against the effective system/custom/append prompt sources and loaded context-file bodies before injection.

Exactly one user-scope context file survives across all providers, and one project file per directory depth; byte-identical collapse happens AFTER ordering, and the user file sorts last so it wins ties against identical project content.

`@` import expansion happens before injection, resolves relative paths from the importing file's directory, stops after five hops, skips cycles, and leaves the literal `@token` when the target is missing or unreadable.
The `.env` cascade only fills keys whose current value is empty/unset — process env always wins — and OMP's parser keeps values literal with no expansion.
`OMP_*` → `PI_*` mirroring applies only within a parsed dotenv file (mirrored value replaces a same-file `PI_*` value) and must never rewrite variables inherited from the parent process.
Environment variables are not a settings layer and must never be written back to `config.yml`.
Missing or malformed tool approval declarations must default to tier `exec`, never `read`.

A tool-declared `policy: deny` and a user `deny` are absolute in every mode including `yolo`; in `yolo` a bare `override: true` is ignored but an explicit tool/user `prompt` or `deny` is still enforced.

Bash `allow` pattern rules must match the ENTIRE command and never apply to a compound line, while `deny`/`prompt` rules must also match any single segment of a compound line (split on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, single `&`, subshells, newlines).
Provider `pendingSafetyChecks` force an interactive prompt regardless of yolo/per-tool allow/prior dispatch approval, and must fail closed when no interactive UI exists.
Headless subagents run yolo, but a user `tools.approval.<tool>: prompt` must REJECT the call rather than auto-allow it.
The install ID must be written with `O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL` at mode `0o600`, and an `EEXIST` loser must re-read and adopt the winner's value; it is cached in-process for the runtime lifetime.
`SYSTEM.md` sets `customSystemPrompt` (a template switch), not the raw provider system prompt; user prompt files are inserted verbatim and are never recursively compiled as Handlebars.

Handshake order is fixed: `initialize` → (HTTP/SSE only) start the background SSE listener after the initialize response has established any `Mcp-Session-Id` → `notifications/initialized` → any other method. Starting the listener earlier loses the session id; issuing `tools/list` before `initialized` breaks spec-compliant servers.

Outbound request ids MUST default to monotonically increasing integers starting at 1 (ecosystem/`xcrun mcpbridge` compatibility); snowflake strings only when `requestIdFormat: "string"`. Ids are transport-local, so a reconnect legitimately restarts numbering.

stdio `request()` MUST NOT await `stdin.write()`/`flush()` — awaiting a full pipe strands the async function before it returns the response promise, so its timeout/abort rejection can never reach the caller. Synchronous throws and asynchronous write/flush rejections must instead reject the already-registered pending promise.
stdio `notify()` MUST detect synchronous write failure (close + throw) but neutralize asynchronous FileSink/EPIPE rejections, because a notification has no response promise to reject.
Malformed stdio JSONL lines and unknown response ids MUST be dropped silently (no reject, no `onError`); one bad frame must never terminate the connection.

Per-request SSE parsing MUST return the FIRST event whose id matches the expected request id and carries `result` or `error`, then drain remaining events in the background; interleaved notifications on the same stream must still be dispatched.
HTTP `notify()` MUST accept any 2xx, including `202 Accepted`, as success.

Timeout precedence is `OMP_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS` → per-server `timeout` → 30000 ms, and `0` means the AbortSignal never fires at all (it also disables the SSE-listener startup deadline). Invalid env values are ignored with a warning, never applied.
Cancellation is local-only: aborting a request settles the local promise but sends no protocol-level cancellation, so the server keeps executing — never assume server-side rollback.
`transport.onClose` MUST be detached before any intentional close (`disconnectServer`, `disconnectAll`), or explicit teardown will trigger the automatic reconnect path.
`disconnectAll()` MUST increment the lifecycle epoch, and reconnect attempts that settle after that epoch bump MUST NOT resurrect connections or re-register tools.
Reconnect MUST re-resolve credentials/env/headers from the preserved *unresolved* config; resolved tokens are never cached in `#serverConfigs`.
Tool removal on disconnect MUST key on the exact `mcpServerName` owner, never on a sanitized `mcp__<prefix>` string — sanitization is lossy and would delete another server's tools.
Runtime tool-name collisions MUST be resolved by lexicographic comparison of the original `<server-name>\0<tool-name>` origin key, so connect/discovery/reconnect ordering can never flip ownership.

Discovery is first-definition-wins by server name across providers in fixed priority order; duplicate names are shadowed, never merged. Equivalent definitions (same transport, endpoint/command inputs, auth, request-id mode) are shadowed even under a different name.

Project entries MUST be encountered before same-named user entries for OMP-native, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, and Windsurf, so a project `enabled: false` suppresses the user server (OpenCode is the documented exception, user-first).
`disabledServers` always beats `enabledServers`; `enabledServers` only overrides a source's `enabled: false` and can never resurrect a denylisted name.

`${VAR}`/`${VAR:-default}` expansion and the `requestIdFormat` field are honored ONLY from OMP-native files, root `mcp.json`/`.mcp.json`, and OMP extension packages; configs translated from other tools must ignore `requestIdFormat`.
A `!command` value that fails, times out (10s), or prints only whitespace MUST omit the `env`/`headers` entry entirely — never substitute an empty string.

An explicitly configured, case-insensitively matched `Authorization` header MUST suppress the URL-keyed OAuth credential fallback; stdio servers MUST ignore URL-keyed profile-scoped credential ids entirely.

A managed `mcp_oauth:profile:<profile>:<url>` credential id is accepted only when that profile is active AND the URL matches the server's expanded or literal URL; on mismatch it is ignored and the URL-keyed profile binding is used instead.

Argument normalization order is load-bearing: top-level coercion → strip injected `i` → prune optional empty declared properties → recursive string/`local://` resolution. Required properties, undeclared properties, `0`, `false`, `null`, and arrays (including `[]`) MUST survive pruning.
Abort semantics must survive the bridge: AbortError becomes `ToolAbortError` and is never rewritten into `MCP error: ...` content.

Reconnect/tool-call retry budgets are exactly one retry (tool call), one OAuth-refresh retry (HTTP 401/403), and the fixed backoff ladder 500/1000/2000/4000 ms for transport-close reconnects — no unbounded retry loops anywhere.

With no notification listener attached, frames MUST be buffered FIFO with a hard cap of 100 (oldest dropped) and drained into the first listener that attaches; internal list/update handling runs before any listener fanout.
`notifications/resources/updated` MUST be acted on only for currently subscribed URIs.
The 250 ms startup gate MUST never block or fail the session: pending servers keep loading and register later through `#onToolsChanged`.
A session that receives `options.mcpManager` borrows it and MUST NOT disconnect it; only the owning session disposes its own manager (bounded to 3s).
`/mcp reload` MUST reuse the manager object after `disconnectAll()` so installed callbacks/listeners survive into the next discovery cycle.
MCP config file writes MUST be atomic (temp file + rename) and MUST NOT mutate another tool's config file — foreign sources are toggled through the user allow/denylist instead.

Candidate resolution de-duplicates while retaining FIRST occurrence, and order is mode-specific: installed = leaf package -> package native/ -> execPath dir; Windows node_modules staging = versionedDir -> leaf -> package/exec; compiled = versionedDir -> legacy dir -> package/exec, with a successfully extracted embedded candidate prepended.

Workspace-development loads MUST skip both leaf-package resolution (so local artifacts win) and version-sentinel validation (so release-versioned addons load under a newer checkout); install and compiled loads MUST enforce the sentinel.

Rust #[module_init] MUST NOT create Tokio runtimes, Rayon pools, or any worker threads — it runs while the dynamic-loader lock is held; all pool installation happens in the optional post-load __ompInstallTokioRuntime() hook.

Embedded extraction accepts ONLY manifest-allowlisted, basename-only, regular-file tar entries with the declared size, and writes through a temporary file plus rename; missing, truncated, unsafe, wrong-type and wrong-size entries are errors.

Stale-cache GC deletes ONLY directories whose name parses as a semantic version strictly older than the current package; current, future, prerelease and non-semver names plus ordinary files must survive, and every failure is ignored.
The x64 variant decision must be written to the private __PI_NATIVE_VARIANT_CACHE env entry so workers and child processes inherit the identical choice; non-x64 must neither read nor populate it.
musl and gnu addons intentionally share the canonical `linux-<arch>` basenames — building both into a single --dest must be a hard error, not a silent overwrite.

Changing a public export between synchronous and promise-returning is a breaking change; e.g. renderSnapcompactPng is async while the adjacent snapcompactSupportedChars is sync, and native/index.d.ts is the only authority.

Cancellation is cooperative: a CancelToken that is never heartbeat()-checked never stops work; no loop over externally sized input may run longer than a short bounded interval without heartbeat (PTY uses a 16ms maximum wait cadence).

Each API family picks exactly one cancellation contract and never mixes: blocking exports reject with `Aborted: Timeout`/`Aborted: Signal`, while shell/PTY resolve typed results with exitCode omitted and cancelled|timedOut set.

The FS scan cache key is the canonicalized root plus the COMPLETE effective WalkOptions with only the `cache` bit cleared — follow_links is in the key; WalkFilter predicates, ranking and limits are not, but size-hint/max-file-size policy can promote metadata detail to Full and thereby select a different key.

Only WalkFilter-stage filtering can trigger empty-result revalidation; post-collection scoring (fuzzyFind) cannot, and the revalidation retry runs uncached and must never replace or evict the cached entry.
cache=false bypasses the shared cache without reading, populating, OR evicting the existing entry for the same key; TTL 0 bypasses and must report cache_age_ms = 0.
Every successful filesystem mutation path (write, hashline, patch, replace, delete, rename) MUST call the invalidation helper; a rename invalidates both sides when the paths differ.
grep must never surface a regex compile error: the ladder is Rust regex -> PCRE2 -> brace sanitization -> one unmatched-paren escape retry -> whole-pattern literal escape.

grep offset/maxCount are applied globally across sorted per-file results, so parallel directory results must be re-ordered before budgets are applied; maxCountPerFile exists solely to stop one hot file consuming the content-mode budget.
search returns errors in SearchResult.error while grep rejects its promise — the two error models must not be unified.
Streaming callbacks never replace the owning promise or result value, and napi-rs ThreadsafeFunction callbacks always use the error-first shape (error: Error | null, value) => void.

Runtime enum objects must be emitted as literal objects into native/index.js; napi-rs enum declarations alone provide no runtime value, and gen-enums.ts only exports top-level `export declare class|function|enum` items.
Binary APIs must be passed typed arrays (Uint8Array/Float32Array/Float64Array/Uint32Array); substituting ordinary arrays without explicit conversion breaks N-API conversion.

The embedded brush shell must not inherit environment (do_not_inherit_env: true) and must explicitly reconstruct it with a skip-list for shell-sensitive variables plus a non-exported `env="$env"` fallback so PowerShell-style $env:NAME survives parameter expansion.
Command-scoped env uses EnvironmentScope::Command and must be popped after the command; only sessionEnv persists for the session lifetime.

A persistent Shell session is reused only after normal control flow; loop/script/shell-exit control flow, cancellation, timeout and errors MUST drop the session. Dropping the Shell kills its live &/nohup children, so a host that needs them must retain the instance.
Shell and PTY output decoding must be incremental across chunk boundaries, emitting U+FFFD for invalid byte sequences rather than failing or splitting code points.

PtySession.start() must install the control channel synchronously before any async work so write/resize/kill are immediately valid, and `core` must always be reset to None after start completes, including every error path.
PTY dimensions are clamped on both start and resize (cols 20..400, rows 5..200) — never only on start.
On Windows, ConPTY input must be closed before dropping the PTY master, and the master drop must be offloaded to a background thread awaited at most 2s, or the process deadlocks.
PTY termination order is process group (when available) then child pid, sending TERM_SIGNAL, then child.kill(), then KILL_SIGNAL; killTree terminates children before the parent.
Process.terminate with gracefulMs < 0 skips the graceful phase entirely rather than clamping to zero.
Key matching compares only shift/alt/ctrl/super bits with lock bits masked out; parse functions return null and match functions false on malformed input and must never throw.
On Linux, copyToClipboard must keep a single process-lifetime arboard::Clipboard instance alive to retain X11/Wayland selection ownership; macOS/Windows use a transient instance per call.
renderSnapcompactPng returns base64 TEXT inside a Latin1String — callers must base64-decode before treating the result as PNG bytes.
readImageFromClipboard must distinguish 'no image' (null/undefined from ContentNotAvailable) from operational failure (rejection).
encodeSixel resizes only when the source dimensions differ from the target, and zero width or height is a hard error.
countTokens on an array returns ONE aggregate count, never per-element counts.

Orchestrator natives cache: populate hardlinks the .node but must COPY index.d.ts/index.js/embedded-addon.js (bindings regeneration truncates them in place, which would corrupt the cache through a hardlink), and capture must COPY (a hardlink would preserve slot UID ownership and defeat the shared-group model).

The Bazel release profile lives inside the native_addon rule's configuration transition, so a bare `bazel build //:natives-<t>` is always release-grade regardless of -c and every addon shares one cache entry per (platform, source) pair.

Memory injection is background context, never instructions: repo state, user messages and tool output outrank recalled/consolidated memory, and memory that conflicts with the repo must be treated as stale.

`learn` persists the lesson BEFORE any skill mutation and never rolls it back: a skill failure returns `<lesson result>, but the managed skill could not be written: <reason>` and an authored-name conflict returns `isError: true, details = { skill: null, shadowed: true }` with the lesson already stored/queued.

`learn` must NOT call the session `refreshSkills` callback (the skill appears on a later refresh) while `manage_skill` MUST call it after a successful mutation — swapping this breaks the documented immediate-discovery contract.
Managed skills never override authored skills; `create` against an active authored name writes no file, and `update` may write but the skill stays shadowed in discovery.

Managed-skill writes must be serialized per normalized name in submission order (different names may run in parallel) and must reject symlinked roots/dirs/files plus non-regular or multiply hard-linked update targets.
Managed `SKILL.md` frontmatter is generated from the normalized name and sanitized description; a body containing its own frontmatter is invalid input.

Always read the full row via `read memory://<id>` before `memory_edit update`: recall previews are clipped at 500 chars and copying one into `content` deletes the unseen tail because update is wholesale replacement.

`memory_edit` must resolve ids across deduplicated retain → recall → global targets in that order, returning the first successful editable result, otherwise the first resolved ineligible result, otherwise `not_found`.
Fact-store rows are immutable: every `memory_edit` op on a fact id returns `not_editable`, and `update`/`forget` on an episodic id returns `not_found` (with bank/store) rather than throwing.
Local memory consolidation must never overwrite `learned.md`, and Phase 2 must hold a lease with heartbeat so simultaneous process starts cannot double-run consolidation.
The local memory pipeline must be skipped for subagents and for sessions with no session file; `/memory enqueue` only marks work that the NEXT startup performs.
All disk-written memory (MEMORY.md, memory_summary.md, generated skills, learned.md) must pass secret redaction, and lessons must additionally be prompt-injection-neutralized before length capping.
A `learn` write must not mutate the active session's prompt-cache prefix; lessons take effect from the next session.

Subagents alias the parent memory state and must never run their own auto-recall/auto-retain loops, own bank handles, or close shared databases; the parent owns final retention, flush and handle closure.

Mnemopi shutdown ordering is mandatory: retain with new fact extraction disabled → flush in-flight extractions → close owned bank handles → shut down the embedding worker after state disposal; on the 1.5s budget expiring, detach the drain instead of racing writes against closed databases.
Hindsight retain flush must verify session ownership; a mismatch logs and drops the batch rather than writing under the wrong session, and enqueue on a disposed state throws.
`/memory clear` under Hindsight only clears local state/cache after draining the queue — it must never imply server-side bank deletion.
Hindsight bank/mission setup is best-effort, once per bank per session state, and create-only: seed definition changes never mutate existing server-side mental models.

Project scope derivation differs per backend and must not be unified: Hindsight uses the git primary checkout root basename lowercased (all worktrees fold to one scope, tags matched literally), Mnemopi uses the absolute cwd basename plus a stable hash of that absolute cwd (git-layout independent).
If every Mnemopi recall target fails, throw the single error or a multi-bank AggregateError — never convert total failure into an empty/no-results answer.
Advisor deltas must exclude advisory messages already injected into the primary transcript, or the advisor recursively reviews its own advice.

Any primary transcript rewrite (compaction, session switch/resume, branch/fork, context re-prime) must reset the advisor transcript, cursor, and emission-guard state; enabling mid-session seeds the cursor at the current transcript length.

The emission guard accepts at most one note per advisor `prompt()` cycle and suppressed noise must not consume that budget; guard suppression is invisible to the model because the tool already returned `Recorded.`

After a deliberate user interrupt, the advisor must not auto-resume: interrupting notes become visible cards that re-enter context on the next resume; plan mode and deferred-ACP turns preserve would-be steers the same way.

The advisor is never a peer: exclude the `advisor` registry kind from hub roster/broadcasts, subagent peer prompts, and `history://` index/lookup/completions, and refuse hub send, collab chat, revive and kill.

Advisor transcript paths derive from the owning session file (not the shared artifacts root); the recorder must detach and drain before `/drop` deletes an artifacts dir so a queued write cannot recreate it.

TTSR abort must fire immediately and must never await extension callbacks; the 50ms-deferred retry must re-validate retry token, prompt generation, abort-pending flag and target assistant message identity, and on any mismatch clear pending state and resolve the resume gate without retrying.
Within one TTSR match batch a rule attaches to exactly one sibling tool call (first claimed bucket wins), though several distinct rules may fold onto one call.

Non-interrupting tool-source TTSR reminders are prepended as an extra leading text block on the tool result: the tool's own content must stay verbatim, and transcript readers must scan past `<system-reminder reason="rule_violation"` blocks to find the real payload.
TTSR persistence stores rule names only; `restoreInjected()` records restored rules at message count zero, so `after-gap` eligibility restarts from the reload point.
TTSR duplicate handling has two layers: the capability loader dedupes rule names first-wins by provider priority, and `TtsrManager.addRule()` ignores a second registration of the same name.
In the SDK, when both `authStorage` and `modelRegistry` are supplied, `modelRegistry.authStorage` MUST be the same instance or session creation rejects.

`beginDispose()` must be called before the wrapper's first `await` during teardown; otherwise deferred work slips into the gap. Both `beginDispose()` and `dispose()` are idempotent and `dispose()` is still required to finish async cleanup.
Never pass loaded extension instances from a parent session to another session; use `preloadedExtensionPaths` so each session gets its own `ExtensionAPI` binding.
Each concurrent top-level SDK session needs a private `AgentRegistry`: the process-global registry admits only one `"Main"` identity per generation.

`toolNames` alone is not an allowlist — only `restrictToolNames: true` restricts the session, and restricted sessions exclude SDK `customTools` unless `allowRestrictedCustomTools` is set and the names are also listed.
Treat `agent_end` as run completion only when `isTerminal !== false`; an absent field means terminal for older runtimes.
RPC clients MUST correlate responses by `id`, never by emission order (concurrent `bash` and other commands interleave), and unknown-command/parse failures deliberately carry `id: undefined`.

RPC v2 chunk sequences must be uninterrupted and validated on `chunkId`/`index`/`count`/`byteLength`, bounded by `maxReassembledFrameBytes`, concatenated in index order, decoded as strict UTF-8, and parsed as exactly one JSON object.

`set_host_tools` and `set_host_uri_schemes` are full replacements, not merges: anything absent from the new list is unregistered; URI schemes are lowercased on registration and `security://` can never be registered or shadowed by a host.
RPC command acceptance is not run completion: hosts must resolve completion via `data.agentInvoked`, a later `prompt_result`, or terminal `agent_end`.

RPC/ACP host defaults apply only where a setting path is not explicitly configured; project/global config, `--config` and isolated settings remain authoritative, and todo settings are never host-defaulted.

Collab entry frames must be broadcast pre-blob-externalization (guests cannot resolve host blob refs) and guests must render events-only while still appending entries to the replica, or the transcript double-renders.
The collab room key lives only in the URL fragment and is never sent to the relay; the host verifies the 16-byte write token at join and rejects prompts/interrupts/agent control from view-only peers.
